# Decisions

Each decision states what was chosen and why. A decision is revisited only when
something concrete blocks progress; the reopening is recorded here. Record one
with `tools/spec/spec add decision`, and put a question to the owner with
`tools/spec/spec add proposal`.

## Accepted

### D1. Name and prefix

**Summary**: The project is named sxml (small XML implementation), with the
public symbol prefix `sxml_` and the macro prefix `SXML_`.

sxml (small XML implementation). Public prefix `sxml_`, macro prefix `SXML_`.

### D2. Core language

**Summary**: sxml is written in portable C17 with C23 features behind macros,
chosen for linking reach, with memory-safety risk mitigated by sanitizers,
fuzzing and checked arithmetic.

Portable C17 with C23 features behind macros, following `docs/C_GUIDELINES.md`.
Chosen for the widest linking reach (every platform and language can call C).
Memory-safety risk is mitigated by sanitizers, fuzzing and checked arithmetic.

### D3. Phase 0 time box

**Summary**: Phase 0 is time-boxed to two weeks (2026-10-16 to 2026-10-30);
when the box ends, open design questions become decision records or proposals
instead of extending the phase.

Recorded 2026-10-16 at the Phase 0 gate review. The original file skipped D3
(no commit ever used the number); the plan's risk table names a "Time-boxed
Phase 0" without a length, so this record fills it. Phase 0 is time-boxed to
two weeks from its start (2026-10-16 to 2026-10-30). When the box ends, open
design questions are written down as decision records or "Proposed" items and
design stops; they are not a reason to extend Phase 0. Phase 0 closed on its
first day, well inside the box.

### D4. License: MIT

**Summary**: sxml is licensed under MIT, and its vendored code is compatible:
tree-sitter (MIT), the W3C test suites (test data only) and mpdecimal
(BSD-2-Clause).

Confirmed at the Phase 0 gate (2026-10-16). Vendored code is compatible:
tree-sitter (MIT, D12, D15), the W3C test suites (test data only, D13),
mpdecimal (BSD-2-Clause, D8, D42).

### D5. Build on an existing engine?

**Summary**: sxml is written from scratch in C rather than built on an existing
engine, studying Xee's shared IR architecture while keeping the IR out of the
value model and parsing with tree-sitter.

Start from scratch in C. Study Xee (Rust, MIT, https://github.com/Paligo/xee)
closely: it implements most of XPath 3.1 with one IR and bytecode interpreter
shared by XPath and XSLT, the same architecture as this plan. Confirmed at the
Phase 0 gate: the substrate keeps the IR out of the value model (function
bodies are an interface, D38), and parsing uses tree-sitter (D12) rather than a
hand-written parser.

### D6. String representation

**Summary**: Strings are UTF-8 with a per-string ASCII-only flag for O(1)
codepoint indexing, and the codepoint count and flag are computed at validation
(refined by D25).

UTF-8, with a per-string flag for ASCII-only content so codepoint indexing is
O(1) in the common case. Codepoint count cached on first use. Confirmed at the
Phase 0 gate, refined by D25: count and flag are computed when the string is
validated, not cached later.

### D7. Ordered maps (XDM 4.0)

**Summary**: XDM 4.0 maps keep insertion order, designed after Saxon 13: a
built-once pair list with a lazy key index, a persistent layer for updates,
shared record shapes and positional entries.

XDM 4.0 maps keep insertion order. Design after Saxon 13 (Michael Kay,
"Implementing Maps for XPath 4.0", XML Prague 2026):

- a built-once list of key/value pairs plus a key-to-offset index, built lazily
  on first lookup;
- a separate persistent layer for later `map:put` / `map:remove`;
- shared key "shapes" for records;
- entries addressable by position, needed for JNode sibling navigation.
  Confirmed at the Phase 0 gate; the design is in D37. The 2026 drafts dropped
  extensible record types (`record(a, *)`) and optional field markers (`a?`); a
  field whose type allows the empty sequence may be absent from a map that
  matches, and coercion fills it, so record cells hold every field.

### D8. Decimal arithmetic

**Summary**: Decimal arithmetic uses libmpdec (mpdecimal), whose process-global
allocator hooks are wrapped (D42) to keep the no-global-state rule, and it also
backs integers beyond `int64_t`.

libmpdec (mpdecimal, BSD-2-Clause). Check whether its allocator hooks are
process-global; if so, wrap it so the no-global-state rule holds. Checked at
the Phase 0 gate: they are process-global, so the wrapping is decided in D42.
D36 uses libmpdec for integers beyond `int64_t` too.

### D9. Regular expressions

**Summary**: sxml has its own engine for the XSD and XPath regular expression
dialect, designed after Saxon HE's engine, built as a Phase 2 packet on
`sxml_string` alone.

Own engine for the XSD/XPath regex dialect, designed after Saxon HE's engine
(regexml is a Rust port that shows the approach). Check the license of any
source before porting code. Confirmed at the Phase 0 gate, unchanged; it is a
Phase 2 packet (PLAN.md, risks) and needs no substrate support beyond
`sxml_string`.

### D10. WebAssembly toolchain

**Summary**: The WebAssembly build uses WASI SDK to produce a standalone module
wrapped by a small hand-written TypeScript package, without Emscripten's
JavaScript system emulation.

WASI SDK producing a standalone module, wrapped by a small hand-written
TypeScript package. The core does no I/O of its own, so Emscripten's JavaScript
system emulation is not needed. Confirmed at the Phase 0 gate: the `wasm`
preset builds with WASI SDK 34 and runs the tests under Node.js (D14, D18). The
TypeScript package arrives with the first public API (Phase 1 onwards).

### D11. Phase gates closed by agent review

**Summary**: Work proceeds through the phases until XQuery 4.0 and XSLT 4.0
work, with each gate closed by a separate review agent and its boxes marked
"(agent review)".

Recorded 2026-10-16. The project owner chose, when asked, that work proceeds
through the phases until XQuery 4.0 and XSLT 4.0 work, with each gate closed by
a separate review agent instead of a human. The review agent checks the work
against `docs/C_GUIDELINES.md` and the gate criteria; its findings are fixed

### D12. Parsing with tree-sitter

**Summary**: All parsing, XML included, uses a vendored tree-sitter runtime and
committed generated grammars; sxml builds its own structures from the syntax
tree, and any `ERROR` or `MISSING` node is a static error.

Recorded 2026-10-16, at the owner's request ("use tree-sitter wherever you need
parsing"), confirmed for XML as well as the query languages.

- The tree-sitter runtime (MIT) is vendored under `third_party/tree-sitter/`,
  pinned to a release tag.
- Grammars live under `grammars/<language>/grammar.js`. The generated parser
  (and any external scanner) is committed so the build needs no Node.js; a
  script regenerates it with a pinned `tree-sitter-cli`.
- sxml walks the concrete syntax tree and builds its own structures (the XML
  tree arena, the XPath/XQuery abstract syntax, then the shared IR). The
  concrete syntax tree is freed before the parse function returns.
- Any `ERROR` or `MISSING` node is a static error (XML: not well-formed;
  XPath/XQuery: `XPST0003`). Error recovery never accepts input.
- What a context-free grammar cannot express (XML well-formedness constraints,
  entity expansion, namespace processing, XQuery lexical constraints) is
  checked in the tree-building step.
- Vendored third-party code is exempt from `docs/C_GUIDELINES.md` and the lint
  gates. The tree-sitter runtime allocates with `malloc` unless
  `ts_set_allocator` is called, and that hook is process-global, so sxml does
  not call it. This exemption is limited to the parse step.

The W3C QT4 test suite (`qt4cg/qt4tests`) and the XSLT 4.0 test suite

CI run. From xslt40-test, `report/`, `admin/unicode.xml`, the zipped QT3 tests
and the DocBook toolchain `.jar` files are left out, because no test reads them
(about 370 MB remain for both suites). The W3C XML conformance suite
(xmlts20130923, 17 MB) is vendored the same way under `third_party/xmlconf/`
for the XML parser (see `grammars/xml/README.md`). Pinned commits: qt4tests
`166453359bd7770fb113b6d9c9015df7f7fa5d02`, xslt40-test
`91328fbf0fed4a5d2813eb3661808ee53cb961ba` (both HEAD on 2026-10-16). Spec
applicability: a test-case `spec` dependency replaces the test-set one; no

### D14. Build layout and presets

**Summary**: The build uses CMake 3.24+ and Ninja with `debug`, `debug-gcc`,
`release`, `msvc` and `wasm` presets, one `sxml` library target, hidden
visibility with `SXML_EXPORT`, and a per-header self-containment check.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.1). CMake 3.24+, Ninja. Presets: `debug` (Clang,
ASan + UBSan), `debug-gcc`, `release` (default compiler), `msvc` (Visual Studio
2022, Windows only), `wasm` (`cmake/wasi-sdk.cmake`, wrapping the SDK's
`wasi-sdk-p1.cmake`; SDK from `WASI_SDK_PREFIX` or `/opt/wasi-sdk`; WASI SDK 34
in CI). Build trees go to `build/<preset>`.

- One library target `sxml`, static by default; `-DSXML_BUILD_SHARED=ON` builds
  it shared. Public functions are marked `SXML_EXPORT`
  (`include/sxml/export.h`); project code has hidden visibility.
- `sxml_apply_project_flags(target)` applies C17 and the guideline flags (MSVC:
  `/W4 /WX`) to project targets only; `sxml_apply_third_party_flags` builds
  vendored and generated code as C11 with warnings off.
- Sanitizers (`SXML_ENABLE_SANITIZERS`) apply to every target, third-party
  included, so instrumentation sees all memory accesses.
- Each public header is compiled alone, twice included, by the
  `sxml_header_check` target (self-containment and include guard).
- WASI test executables run under Node.js (`tools/run-wasi.mjs`, set as
  `CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR`), so `ctest --preset wasm` runs the tests.
- `sxml_version_text` returns a NUL-terminated string: an external boundary.

### D19. View types in their own header

**Summary**: `sxml_byte_view` and `sxml_memory_view` live in their own header
`include/sxml/view.h` to avoid an include cycle between `status.h` and
`memory.h`, while the view functions stay in `memory.h`.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.5). `sxml_byte_view` and `sxml_memory_view` live in
`include/sxml/view.h`, with `SXML_BYTE_VIEW_INITIALIZER` (brace form, for
static tables) and `SXML_BYTE_VIEW_FROM_LITERAL` (compound literal). `status.h`
needs byte views and `memory.h` needs `sxml_status`, so the views cannot live
in either without a cycle. `memory.h` includes `view.h`, so "memory.h provides
the views" still holds. The view functions (`sxml_byte_view_equals`,
`sxml_memory_view_slice`, ...) are in `memory.h`. The header `sxml/string.h`
shares its file name with `<string.h>`; it is only ever included as
`"sxml/string.h"` and `include/sxml/` is never put on an include path itself.

### D20. Outputs on failure are left untouched

**Summary**: A function that fails does not write its outputs, as the
project-wide default; a declaration that deviates says so, as
`sxml_utf8_validate` does.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.5). Project-wide default, chosen from the two
options in `docs/C_GUIDELINES.md` ("Ownership and lifetimes"): a function that
fails does not write its outputs. A declaration that deviates says so (the only
one so far: `sxml_utf8_validate` fills its result on both outcomes, to report
where the input stops being valid). Lifecycle functions check the configuration
and memory before writing anything.

### D21. Error records and diagnostics hold borrowed views

**Summary**: `sxml_diagnostic` and `sxml_error_record` carry an error's code,
description, value and source location as borrowed views, static for sxml's own
errors, so the common case allocates nothing.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.5). `sxml_diagnostic` (description +
`sxml_source_location`: source name, line, column in codepoints, byte offset)
receives details of any failure. `sxml_error_record` adds the error code
(`sxml_error_code`: namespace URI, local name, display prefix) and the error
value (`const sxml_sequence *`, forward-declared in `status.h`; `xdm.h` in task
0.7 must define `struct sxml_sequence`). Together they carry what an XQuery
catch clause binds: `$err:code`, `$err:description`, `$err:value`,
`$err:module`, `$err:line-number`, `$err:column-number`.

- All text is borrowed views: static text for errors sxml raises itself (so the
  common case allocates nothing), or memory owned by the object that raised the
  error (fn:error with a computed description or value). They are valid until
  that object is next used or finalized. No fixed-capacity description buffer:
  it would put a frozen size into the ABI and truncate.
- `SXML_STATUS_STATIC_ERROR`, `_DYNAMIC_ERROR`, `_TYPE_ERROR` mean "details in
  the error record" (`sxml_status_has_error_record`); every other status is a
  condition of the C interface.
- Amended by D41: computed descriptions and values are kept by the item heap,
  which a native function body can reach, rather than by "the object that
  raised the error", which a body does not have.

### D22. The allocator interface has no reallocate

**Summary**: `sxml_allocator_operations` has only `allocate` and `release`,
with no reallocate; `allocate` rejects a zero byte count, and an allocator with
no operations is the null allocator.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.5). `sxml_allocator_operations` has `allocate` and
`release` only, as in `docs/C_GUIDELINES.md`. A reallocate would need the old
size and alignment in its request, every host allocator (JavaScript, Swift,
Kotlin) would have to implement it, and the main grower, the arena, grows by
adding blocks. Growable arrays allocate anew and copy, geometrically, which is
amortized O(1). Interfaces are not extended in place, so if profiling shows a
need, a new interface type is published. `allocate` rejects `byte_count` 0
(`SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`), avoiding `malloc(0)`'s implementation-defined
result. The wrappers check every request, so implementations may trust their
arguments, and `sxml_allocator_allocate` also checks the alignment of what an
implementation returns. An allocator with `operations == NULL` is the null
allocator: "this object must not grow". The default allocator uses `malloc` up
to `alignof(max_align_t)` and `aligned_alloc` above it (size rounded up to the
alignment for C libraries that still require it); on Windows it uses
`_aligned_malloc` for everything, since `_aligned_free` cannot release `malloc`
memory.

### D23. The counting allocator is public

**Summary**: The allocator test double `sxml_counting_allocator` is public in
`memory.h`, counting allocations and failing exactly the numbered one, so
embedders can test every allocation failure path.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.6). The allocator test double,
`sxml_counting_allocator`, is in `memory.h` and the library, not in `tests/`,
so embedders can drive the failure paths of their own code. It wraps a backing
allocator, counts attempts, failures, releases, live allocations and bytes, and
fails exactly the allocation numbered `failing_allocation_number` (from 1; 0 =
none). Test pattern for every module (see
`test_arena_survives_every_allocation_failure` in `tests/memory_test.c`): run
the operation with failing number 1, 2, 3, ... until it succeeds; after each
run `live_allocation_count` must be 0.

### D24. The arena is part of the memory substrate

**Summary**: `sxml_arena` bump-allocates from caller memory and then from
blocks of a block allocator, returns memory only on reset, finalize or destroy,
and can bound its growth for untrusted input.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.5). `sxml_arena` in `memory.h`: bump allocation
from caller `initial_memory`, then from blocks of `block_byte_count` taken from
`block_allocator`; a request too large for a block gets a block of its own and
the current block keeps serving small requests. The null allocator as block
allocator gives a fixed-capacity arena (`SXML_STATUS_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`);
`maximum_block_byte_count` bounds growth for untrusted input
(`SXML_STATUS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, 0 = no bound). Memory goes back only on
`sxml_arena_reset`, `_finalize` or `_destroy`; `sxml_arena_as_allocator`
exposes it as an `sxml_allocator` whose release does nothing. Typed,
index-addressed storage for trees and XDM values (task 0.7) builds on it rather
than replacing it.

### D25. Strings validate eagerly

**Summary**: `sxml_string` is a UTF-8 byte view whose `is_ascii` flag and
codepoint count are computed in the same strict validation pass that constructs
it, and it compares by bytes.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.5). D6 holds: `sxml_string` is a UTF-8 byte view
with an `is_ascii` flag and a codepoint count. Both are computed in the same
pass that validates the bytes (`sxml_string_from_utf8`), so "cached on first
use" is "computed at construction", with no extra pass and no mutable cache in
a value type. `is_ascii == false` makes no claim, so a zero-initialized
`sxml_string` is a valid empty string. Validation is strict (Unicode 16.0 §3.9
table 3-7: no overlongs, surrogates or values above U+10FFFF). Comparison is by
codepoint, implemented as byte comparison, which gives the same order for
well-formed UTF-8. A constructor for producers that already know the count (the
XML parser) can be added later as a new function. `string.h` is designed but
not implemented in Phase 0.

### D26. Lint for byte pointers without a length

**Summary**: The ast-grep rule `pointer-parameter-without-length` flags single
byte-pointer parameters in `include/` and `src/`, and an external boundary
taking a NUL-terminated string marks itself with an ignore comment.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.6), completing D17. The ast-grep rule
`pointer-parameter-without-length` flags parameters in `include/` and `src/`
that are a single pointer to `char`, `signed char`, `unsigned char`, `uint8_t`
or `int8_t`. Object pointers, `void *` state or memory, and pointers to
pointers are allowed. An external boundary that takes a NUL-terminated string
(so far only `sxml_byte_view_from_c_string`) marks the line before with `//
ast-grep-ignore: pointer-parameter-without-length`. `tests/` is not covered:
the test runner takes `argv`. `SXML_TEST_REQUIRE` now branches on the condition
itself, so clang-analyzer knows what holds after it.

### D27. string.h implemented in Phase 0

**Summary**: `src/string.c` implements `include/sxml/string.h` unchanged in
Phase 0, fixing how decoding treats bytes that are not well-formed and when
`sxml_string_codepoint_at` reports an index out of range.

Recorded 2026-10-16, amending the last sentence of D25: `src/string.c`
implements `include/sxml/string.h` unchanged, with 29 cases in
`tests/string_test.c` (including an exhaustive check of all scalar values and
of every lead/second byte pair against table 3-7). Choices the header leaves
open: on bytes that are not well-formed, decoding stays within the view,
decodes a byte that cannot start an encoding as itself, and decodes a truncated
encoding from the bytes present; `sxml_string_codepoint_at` returns
`SXML_STATUS_INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE` when the bytes run out before the index, and
takes the ASCII fast path only when the index is also below `byte_count`.
`compare` and `equals` work on bytes (D25). Validation is a plain byte loop; a
word-at-a-time ASCII scan can come later without an interface change.

### D28. XML 1.0 grammar

**Summary**: sxml has its own tree-sitter grammar for XML 1.0 in
`grammars/xml`, with an external scanner holding element names on an interned
tag stack, and leaves the remaining well-formedness checks to the tree builder.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `grammars/xml` is written for sxml, not vendored:
tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-xml (MIT) was studied but is too lenient and
its tag-stack scanner is unsafe for deep or non-ASCII documents (reasons in
`grammars/xml/README.md`; credit in `grammars/xml/NOTICE`).

- Node names spell out the XML 1.0 production names in snake_case (`STag` is
  `start_tag`, `CharData` is `character_data`); names, values and identifiers
  are fields. Content items are direct children of `element`.
- External scanner (`src/scanner.c`): element names on a tag stack, so a
  mismatched end tag is an `ERROR` (WFC Element Type Match); character data,
  CDATA text, comment text and PI content with their delimiters and [2] Char;
  PI targets other than `xml`. The stack is a persistent, interned table of
  (parent frame, name) pairs owned by the scanner; the serialized state is one
  4-byte frame index, so depth and name length are unlimited. The scanner
  allocates through `ts_malloc`/`ts_calloc`/`ts_realloc` (D12 exemption).
- Only the document and its internal subset are parsed; parameter-entity
  references inside internal-subset declarations are a grammar error (WFC PEs
  in Internal Subset). The external subset and text declarations have no
  grammar.
- Every well-formedness check the grammar cannot make is listed in
  `grammars/xml/README.md` ("What the tree builder checks"). Entity replacement
  text is checked by parsing it wrapped in a dummy element.
- `grammars/CMakeLists.txt` registers every `grammars/<language>/src/parser.c`
  with `sxml_add_grammar`; a new grammar needs no CMake edit.
- Measured: W3C XML suite (standalone, XML 1.0 Fifth Edition) valid 601/601 and
  invalid 175/175 parse cleanly, not-wf 870/948 rejected by the grammar (the
  other 78 are builder constraints); all 3583 well-formed UTF-8 `*.xml` files
  of the QT4 and XSLT 4.0 suites parse cleanly.

### D29. Query grammars: XPath, XQuery and XSLT patterns

**Summary**: The XPath, XQuery and XSLT pattern grammars are written from the
QT4 CG drafts, with XQuery and patterns inheriting from XPath and one shared
stateless external scanner.

Recorded 2026-10-16. Grammars `grammars/xpath`, `grammars/xquery` and
`grammars/xslt_pattern`, written from the QT4 CG drafts (XPath/XQuery 4.0
Appendix A, XSLT 4.0 section 6.3 and Appendix E; drafts of 13 October 2026).
Where the test suites still use syntax the drafts have dropped (XSLT type
patterns `~T`), the drafts win. (This record was first committed as a second
"D27"; renumbered.)

- Inheritance: `xquery` and `xslt_pattern` are
  `grammar(require('../xpath/grammar'), ...)`. tree-sitter takes the first rule
  as the start rule, so a derived grammar moves its start rule (`module`,
  `pattern`) to the front of the rule table. Keyword lists and name regular
  expressions are in `grammars/xpath/lexical.js`.
- Node names are the EBNF production names in snake_case with abbreviations
  spelled out (`VarRef` is `variable_reference`, `CompElemConstructor` is
  `computed_element_constructor`); choice productions such as `ExprSingle` are
  hidden. Operands, steps, axes, clauses and bindings are named fields; binary
  operators are left-recursive nodes with `left`, `operator`, `right`. XSLT
  pattern productions ending in "P" become `..._pattern` nodes.
- Keywords are not reserved (A.3): every keyword is a tree-sitter reserved
  word, so the lexer always returns the keyword token, as the context-free
  tokenizer of A.3 would; every name position accepts each keyword aliased to
  `ncname`, except function names (A.4 reserved function names; in patterns
  also `atomic` and `empty-sequence`) and XQuery computed-constructor names
  (xgc: unreserved-name).
- One stateless external scanner, `grammars/common/query_scanner.h`, included
  by each `src/scanner.c`: nested comments, string template fixed parts, string
  constructor characters, all of direct constructor syntax (tags, attribute
  values, content, comments, PIs, CDATA) and pragmas. All grammars declare the
  same external token list. In XQuery the scanner applies the "<" rules of A.3
  without regard to context: a direct constructor is recognized even where the
  operator "<" is expected, and the parse fails.
- GLR conflicts are declared only where one token of lookahead is not enough:
  `namespace #x {}` against `namespace#1`; `element instance {}` against
  `element instance of T` (also attribute, namespace, processing-instruction);
  and the two prolog groups, where `declare` may continue either group or start
  the query body.
- In patterns, a step at the outermost level has no JNodeType test, so `jnode(`
  always starts a JNodePattern.
- Checked later, in the tree builder (XPST0003 unless noted): terminal
  delimitation (A.3.2, two non-delimiting terminals with no separator, e.g.
  `10div 3`); a prefixed name as a lookup key (accepted so that `a:b` stays one
  token); end tag name equal to start tag name (XQST0118); duplicate
  attributes, QName and namespace well-formedness; reserved PI target names in
  computed constructors.
- `tools/qt4-parse-check.py` (with `tools/qt4-parse-harness.c`, which also
  applies the A.3.2 delimitation check) parses every applicable query. Results
  on 2026-10-16: XP40 0 false rejects of 32,118 valid queries, 2 false accepts
  of 363 XPST0003 queries; XQ40 0 of 43,663 and 3 of 772; XSLT 4.0 patterns 3
  false rejects of 19,168 (invalid DocBook patterns). Details in
  `grammars/xquery/README.md`.

**Sources**: XP40, XQ40 and XSLT 4.0 pattern false rejects and false accepts,
every applicable query, on 2026-10-16 (`tools/qt4-parse-check.py`,
`tools/qt4-parse-harness.c`, from `grammars/xquery/README.md`).

### D30. Substrate headers and their order

**Summary**: The substrate is the headers `name.h`, `types.h`, `tree.h` and
`xdm.h`, each including only those before it, with the name pool, type registry
and item heap as separate objects and no processor object.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). The substrate is five headers, each including
only those before it: `name.h` (name pool) < `types.h` (type registry, sequence
types, node kinds) < `tree.h` (tree interface, node references, axes, tree
builder, arena tree) < `xdm.h` (item heap, items, sequences, atomic items, node
items, function items, maps, records, arrays, JNodes). `tree.h`
forward-declares `sxml_item_heap`; `status.h` already declares `sxml_sequence`,
which `xdm.h` defines. Accessors that produce XDM values from nodes (string
value, typed value, base URI) are in `xdm.h`; structural accessors in `tree.h`.
There is no "processor" object in the substrate: the name pool, type registry
and item heap are separate objects with stored references (heap -> registry ->
pool), and the Phase 1 processor owns them. Document and collection resolution
(`fn:doc`, `fn:collection`, `fn:unparsed-text`, module import) is a host
interface of the dynamic context, designed with it in Phase 1, not a substrate
header: what it returns (a tree made through `sxml_tree_builder`, or bytes) is
already covered here.

### D31. Name pool

**Summary**: `sxml_name_pool` interns namespace URIs, prefixes and expanded
names into dense 32-bit identifiers per processor, with constant identifiers
for well-known namespaces and prefixes kept outside a name's identity.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). Namespace URIs, prefixes and expanded names are
interned into dense 32-bit identifiers in a per-processor `sxml_name_pool`;
comparing names is comparing integers, and nodes and QName items hold no text.
URI and prefix identifier 0 mean "none"; name identifier 0 means "no name". A
fixed set of well-known namespaces (`xml`, `xs`, `fn`, `err`, ...) have
constant identifiers in every pool. Names are never removed;
`maximum_byte_count` bounds growth on untrusted input, and
`sxml_name_pool_find_name` looks up without interning. Prefixes are kept beside
names, never part of their identity (XDM 4.0, section 5.6).

### D32. Type registry and sequence types

**Summary**: `sxml_type_identifier` names schema and item types in one space,
with built-ins as constants below 70, interned item types from 512, and
sequence types as the plain value `sxml_sequence_type`.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). `sxml_type_identifier` (32-bit index) names
every type: schema types and item types share one space, since atomic types are
both (XDM 4.0, section 4.1.2). Built-in types (all XSD/XDM built-ins including
`xs:untyped`, `xs:numeric`, `xs:error`, the list types, and the generic item
types `item()`, `node()`, `element()`, `function(*)`, `map(*)`, `array(*)`,
`record(*)`, ...) have constant identifiers `SXML_TYPE_*` below 70, described
by static const data; the enum only grows. Identifiers 70-511 are reserved for
later built-ins; registered types start at 512. Item types written in queries
(node tests, function, map, array, record, enumeration, choice and JNode types)
are registered and interned, so structural equality is identifier equality;
nominative record types are declared, then defined, so they can be recursive.
Schema types (Phase 5) are registered into the same table. A sequence type is
not registered: it is the plain value `sxml_sequence_type` (item type +
occurrence), with occurrences as bit sets so occurrence subtyping is a subset
test. Predicates (`is_derived_from`, `is_subtype`) return `bool` and treat
unknown identifiers as false.

### D33. XDM values are immutable and reference counted

**Summary**: XDM values are immutable with reference counts on heap cells in an
`sxml_item_heap` and small values inline; owned outputs are released exactly
once, and node items retain their tree.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). Considered: an arena per evaluation (simple,
but garbage grows without bound in long loops and folds, and values that escape
the evaluation, such as results, global variables, XSLT keys and cached
documents, need another mechanism), tracing garbage collection (needs root
scanning of C stacks), and reference counting. Chosen: immutable values with
reference counts on heap cells, small values inline. XDM values cannot form
cycles (built bottom-up, never changed; closures capture values), so counting
reclaims everything. Rules: outputs of make/put/append/... are owned (+1) and
released exactly once; get/describe outputs are borrowed; inputs are borrowed
and functions that store an input retain it themselves. Retain and release are
no-ops on inline values and on immortal cells (static data, counts that would
overflow). Cells live in an `sxml_item_heap` and record their heap, so
`sxml_item_release(item)` needs no other argument. `sxml_item_heap_read_counts`
reports live cells, so every test can check for leaks (with D23's counting
allocator for failure paths). Trees are counted too: node items retain their
tree.

### D34. Item and sequence representation

**Summary**: `sxml_item` and `sxml_sequence` are 16-byte plain values with
private fields, small values inline and others in cells, and a sequence is
empty, one inline item, or a vector, range, concatenation or lazy cell.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). `sxml_item` and `sxml_sequence` are 16-byte
plain values with private fields; the size is frozen as ABI (static assert).
Inline: booleans, doubles, floats, integers that fit `int64_t` (any integer
type), QName/NOTATION (name identifier + prefix identifier), node references
(tree pointer + node index + namespace number). Cells: strings, decimals, big
integers, dates, durations, binary, function items, maps, arrays, JNodes. A
sequence is the empty sequence (all zero), one inline item (an item is a
singleton sequence, XDM 4.0, section 3.2), or a cell: vector, integer range
(two `int64_t` bounds), concatenation (flattened parts), or lazy (a
`sxml_sequence_generator`, memoized so every reading sees the same items). One
read interface serves all: count, get item by index, iterator. Item counts and
indices in sequences are `uint64_t`, since `1 to 10000000000` is valid on
32-bit WebAssembly; counts of things held in memory are `size_t`.

### D35. Thread confinement

**Summary**: An item heap and everything tied to it are used by one thread at a
time, separate heaps are independent, and sharing one parsed document between
threads is not supported in year one.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). Reference counts are not atomic and the name
pool, registry and lazy indexes mutate on read. Rule: an item heap and
everything tied to it (its name pool, type registry, trees and values) are used
by one thread at a time; separate heaps are fully independent. Static const
data and functions on inline values are safe from any thread. Sharing one
parsed document between threads is not supported in year one; if needed later
it becomes a new decision (an immortal, frozen tree with a read-only name pool
is the likely shape).

### D36. Numbers, dates and durations

**Summary**: `xs:integer` is inline up to `int64_t` and moves to a libmpdec
cell on overflow, `xs:decimal` is always a libmpdec cell, and dates and
durations keep nanosecond precision with `int64_t` years.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). `xs:integer` is unbounded: values that fit
`int64_t` are inline; arithmetic that overflows moves to a cell holding a
libmpdec value with exponent 0 (D8), so there is one arbitrary-precision
library, not two. `xs:decimal` is always a libmpdec cell. Date/time values keep
the seven XDM components (local values, optional timezone in minutes) with
`int64_t` year and nanosecond seconds; durations are months plus seconds plus
nanoseconds (XDM 4.0, section 5.7 note). Nine fractional digits exceed the
required three; more digits are truncated by casting. The public
`sxml_atomic_datum` reads and writes every datum; decimals are exchanged as
canonical text, cached in the cell on first read.

### D37. Maps, records, arrays and JNodes

**Summary**: Maps keep entry order with a lazy hash index and persistent
updates, records share field names in the type registry, arrays are persistent
vectors, and JNode children are made on demand.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). Maps follow D7: entry order kept, entries
addressable by position (`sxml_map_get_entry`), hash index built on first
lookup, persistent put/remove sharing structure. Keys compare by
`fn:atomic-equal` with a consistent `sxml_atomic_item_hash` (equal numeric
values of different types hash alike). Map construction takes a whole entry
list and a duplicate-key policy (reject with XQDY0137, use first, use last);
combining duplicates with a function is left to `map:build`/`map:merge`.
Records are maps whose cell holds only field values plus the record type, whose
field names and name index live once in the type registry (D7's shared shapes);
`map:put` on a record gives a plain map. Arrays are persistent vectors of
sequences with O(log n) updates. A JNode is a cell (parent, key, value, child
index, JTree identifier); roots take a fresh tree identifier so JTrees order
among XTrees; children are made on demand and are identical when parent and key
are (XDM 4.0, section 8.5).

### D38. Function items

**Summary**: A function item cell holds a name, signature, annotations,
captured values and a body behind the `sxml_function_body` interface, shared by
native C and IR functions so the substrate never sees the IR.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). A function item cell holds name (optional),
signature (a registered function type; arity is its parameter count),
annotations (borrowed from the body's owner), captured values (retained) and a
body. The body is an interface (`sxml_function_body`: state, `call`, optional
`retain`/`release`) shared by native C functions and IR functions: the
evaluator supplies the operations of IR bodies, so the substrate never sees the
IR. Bodies receive arguments already coerced, the item (for captures), the
dynamic context (opaque), the heap and an error record. Partial application and
function coercion are native bodies capturing the wrapped function. Maps and
arrays answer `sxml_function_item_call` as `map:get`/`array:get`. Function
identity is not modelled (withdrawn from XDM 4.0, section 8.1).

### D39. Trees: interface, node numbering, document order

**Summary**: `sxml_tree` wraps an implementation whose node indices are in
document order, so order is an integer comparison and descendants an index
range, with order across trees by tree identifier.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). `sxml_tree` wraps an implementation (state +
`sxml_tree_operations`) with a tree identifier and a reference count; the
built-in `sxml_arena_tree` is one implementation and hosts can supply others.
Contract for every implementation: node indices are in document order
(preorder, attributes right after their element), so document order in a tree
is an integer comparison, descendants are an index range (`last_descendant`),
and attributes are the indices after their element. Namespace nodes are not
stored: a namespace node is (element index, namespace number from 1) into the
element's in-scope namespaces, which keeps lexicographic order correct (XDM
4.0, section 6.2). Across trees, order is by tree identifier, issued in
increasing order by the item heap to XTrees and JTrees alike, so it is stable
and consistent (XDM 4.0, section 6.2). An `sxml_node_reference` is tree pointer +
node index + namespace number and does not retain; node items do. When the
count drops to zero the tree's owner is told (evaluation-built arena trees
destroy themselves; host trees are destroyed by the host). Axes, XPath 4.0's
`-or-self` axes included, are iterated by the library over the interface.

### D40. Tree builder and arena tree

**Summary**: One event interface, `sxml_tree_builder`, is fed by the XML
parser, XQuery constructors and XSLT instructions and implemented by the arena
tree and later serializers, with text merging and namespace fixup.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.7). One event interface, `sxml_tree_builder`
(start/end document and element, namespace binding, attribute, text, comment,
processing instruction, unparsed entity), is fed by the XML parser, XQuery
constructors and XSLT instructions, and implemented by the arena tree and later
by serializers, so results can stream to output. Builders merge adjacent text,
drop empty text, reject duplicate attributes and perform namespace fixup (XSLT
4.0, section 5.7.3). `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node` replays a subtree as events
(deep copy with copy-namespaces modes). The arena tree stores nodes in
index-addressed arrays and text in one store (D24), shares in-scope namespace
lists between elements that declare nothing, keeps source locations on request,
and enforces node-count, depth and text-size limits for untrusted input.

### D41. Raised errors are kept by the item heap

**Summary**: `sxml_item_heap_raise_error` copies a raised error's code,
description and source name into the item heap and retains its value, keeping
one raised error per heap.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.8, header review). An error record holds borrowed
views (D21), but fn:error and other native function bodies have no object of
their own that outlives the call to keep a computed description or `$err:value`
in. `sxml_item_heap_raise_error` copies the code, description and source name
into the heap and retains the value; the record points there until the next
error raised on that heap, `sxml_item_heap_clear_raised_error`, or
finalization. One raised error per heap is enough: a catch clause retains
`$err:value` (and makes its description an item) before evaluating anything
else, and an error that propagates is the latest one. The function returns the
error status itself so bodies can `return` it. A lazy sequence that must report
its error again keeps its own copy and raises it again.

### D42. libmpdec allocation through a scoped allocator

**Summary**: libmpdec is vendored with only `mpalloc.c` patched so its hooks
allocate through the allocator of a thread-local decimal scope, the only
thread-local in sxml, keeping the no-global-state rule in effect.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (task 0.8), completing D8. Checked in mpdecimal 2.5.1
(`mpalloc.c`, as bundled by CPython 3.12): `mpd_mallocfunc`, `mpd_callocfunc`,
`mpd_reallocfunc` and `mpd_free` are process-global function pointers without a
state argument, `MPD_MINALLOC` and `mpd_traphandler` are globals too, and the
internal resize path (`mpd_qresize`; about 90 allocation call sites in
`mpdecimal.c` alone) receives no context. Chosen, for the decimal packet of
Phase 2:

- Vendor libmpdec (mpdecimal 4.0.x, pinned like D15) under
  `third_party/mpdecimal/`. Patch only `mpalloc.c` and the matching
  declarations: the four hooks become fixed functions that allocate through the
  `sxml_allocator` of the current decimal scope.
- The scope is one thread-local pointer, set by sxml's decimal module on entry
  to every operation that may allocate and restored before it returns (so
  nesting works); it holds the item heap's allocator. Every block starts with a
  header naming its allocator, so free and resize never depend on the scope. No
  state survives between library calls, two heaps on two threads never share
  it, and nothing is visible to the host: the no-global-state rule holds in
  effect. This thread-local is the only one in sxml and is documented at its
  definition.
- sxml never calls `mpd_setminalloc` and runs contexts with no traps, so the
  other globals stay constant and `mpd_traphandler` is never called.
- Rejected: threading an allocator through every allocation site (a large,
  permanent patch against upstream), and a process-wide hook (breaks heap
  independence, D35). Fallback if the patch or the WebAssembly size budget
  fails: an own decimal module (add, subtract, multiply, divide with the
  precision rules of F&O 4.0), behind the same cell format.

### D43. Header review findings (task 0.8)

**Summary**: The Phase 0 header review adds `sxml_name_test` wildcards,
`sxml_name_pool_find_namespace_uri`, `sxml_sequence_test_emptiness` and an
arena tree duplicate attribute policy, and moves argument coercion to the
evaluator.

Recorded 2026-10-16. Changes made by the Phase 0 review agent (D11):

- `types.h`: node tests carry an `sxml_name_test` (any name, expanded name,
  `prefix:*`/`Q{uri}*`, `*:local`), because XPath 4.0 element and attribute
  tests take a NameTestUnion with wildcards (`element(p:*)`); the same struct
  serves path steps.
- `name.h`: `sxml_name_pool_find_namespace_uri`, so a name from untrusted input
  can be looked up without interning its namespace URI.
- `xdm.h`: `sxml_sequence_test_emptiness` replaces a `bool` predicate that
  swallowed generator errors (fn:empty on a lazy sequence must raise them);
  `sxml_function_item_call` does not coerce arguments, the evaluator does
  (coercion needs casting and function coercion); the borrowed-output verbs are
  get, describe, find and iterator next; iterator sizes are ABI.
- `tree.h`: `sxml_duplicate_attribute_policy` in the arena tree configuration
  (XQuery rejects with XQDY0025, XSLT 4.0 section 5.7.1 replaces); builder
  errors use XQuery codes and XSLT rewrites them; the event order is the
  caller's contract (XQTY0024 and XTDE0410 are checked by the evaluators,
  well-formedness by the XML parser).
- `status.h` and `xdm.h`: D41.

### D44. The sxml command-line program and its CLI framework

**Summary**: The `sxml` command-line program is built on a declarative CLI
framework in `apps/`, with stdio confined to one platform file, no option
abbreviations or aliases, and fixed exit codes 0 to 4.

Recorded 2026-10-16. Rules and planned commands in `docs/CLI.md`.

- Layout: `apps/cli_framework/` (static library `sxml_cli_framework`:
  declarative command tables, parser, help, "did you mean", output streams,
  dispatch); `apps/sxml/` (`sxml_program`: table and command functions;
  executable target `sxml_cli`, output name `sxml`). Option `SXML_BUILD_APPS`
  (default ON), added after `tests/`. Application code: public `include/sxml/`
  API only, memory from an `sxml_allocator`.
- I/O boundary: only `apps/sxml/platform_stdio.c` touches stdio; lint
  `input-output-outside-platform-layer` enforces it for `apps/**`, and
  `pointer-parameter-without-length` now covers `apps/` too.
- One intent, one action: no option abbreviations, no aliases beyond
  `help`/`--help`/`version`/`--version`, a repeated single option is a usage
  error, `-h`/`--help` wins over everything before `--`, no implicit stdin, no
  files written without `--output`, no network. Typos get a suggestion (optimal
  string alignment distance), never an action.
- Exit codes 0 success, 1 operation failed, 2 usage error, 3 input/output error
  (incl. failed writes to stdout), 4 internal error.
- Built-ins: `help [COMMAND]` and the program options `--help`, `--version`;
  tables cannot redeclare them (`sxml_cli_program_validate`, run at start: a
  broken table exits 4). The program name is fixed in the table, never argv[0],
  so output is identical natively and under WASI.
- Today's commands: `help`, `version [--format=text|json]`. Nothing else is
  listed until it works.
- Tests in `tests/cli/`, registered from `apps/CMakeLists.txt` so the
  `tests/*_test.c` glob (D45) never sees them: framework unit tests and golden
  end-to-end tests (stdout, stderr, exit code) under every preset, MSVC
  included (CI runs `ctest -R ^cli` there).
- The QT4 driver (packet 1.24) is a separate tool under `tests/qt4/driver/`
  built on this framework, not an `sxml` subcommand: it reads the vendored
  catalogs and is never shipped. Rejected: `sxml test-suite`, which would
  advertise a developer tool to users.

### D45. Phase 1 work packets and conflict-free registration

**Summary**: Phase 1 is split into packets of one agent session that own
disjoint files in one working tree, and the build uses globs over `src/*.c` and
`tests/<name>_test.c` so additions never conflict.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (Phase 1 planning; D44 is left to the CLI work, which cites
it). Phase 1 is split into packets of one agent session
(`docs/tasks/phase-1.md`) that run in parallel in one working tree. Each packet
names the files it owns; packets that can run together own disjoint files. To
make additions conflict-free, packet 1.0 replaces the explicit lists with
globs: `src/*.c` is the library and every `tests/<name>_test.c` is the ctest
test `<name>`; `tests/qt4/driver`, `tests/fuzz` (with `SXML_BUILD_FUZZERS`) and
`third_party/mpdecimal` join the build when their `CMakeLists.txt` exists.
`src/` stays flat; a module owns the prefix `src/<module>[_<part>].c` and
`src/<module>_internal.h`. The ledgers (DECISIONS, GLOSSARY, LOG) take one
small insertion per change, committed at once and alone; a D-number is claimed
by re-reading the file first. Rejected: one subdirectory per module (breaks the
module/header pairing of `docs/C_GUIDELINES.md` for little gain) and per-packet
branches (the brief forbids branches).

### D46. The shared IR is internal, tree-walking and ANF-like

**Summary**: The shared IR is internal to `src/ir_internal.h`, ANF-like after
Xee with the focus bound as ordinary variables, evaluated by tree walking with
bounded depth, and rewritten by IR-to-IR passes.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (Phase 1 planning; designed in packet 1.5).

- **Internal**, in `src/ir_internal.h`, not a public header. XPath, XQuery and
  XSLT front ends are all in this repository, so nothing outside needs to
  produce IR; a public IR would join the frozen ABI before XQuery and XSLT have
  tested it. Hosts extend sxml through function bodies (D38) and the resolver,
  not through IR. If a later need appears (an external front end, a persisted
  compiled form), a decision publishes a versioned copy.
- **Shape**, after Xee's `xee-ir` (D5): expressions whose operands are atoms (a
  constant or a variable slot), with `let` bindings for intermediate values;
  branches, loop bodies and function bodies are nested expressions. The focus
  is not implicit state: map, filter, quantified, sort and path-step nodes bind
  the context item, position and size as ordinary variables, so closures
  capture them like any variable and XPDY0002 is a static or dynamic check on
  an unbound slot. Variables are resolved to frame slots during lowering;
  function definitions carry their capture list. Node-construction,
  `try`/`catch` and template-rule nodes are reserved for XQuery and XSLT (XSLT
  rules lower to IR functions plus a rule table, as in Xee).
- **Evaluation** walks the IR (no bytecode: PLAN.md non-goal), with evaluation
  depth bounded so deep recursion returns a limit status.
- **Optimizer seam**: `src/ir_pass_internal.h` declares a pass as an IR-to-IR
  function over a compiled unit, run in a fixed list between lowering and
  evaluation. Phase 1 has only a verifier pass; rewrites (constant folding,
  type-based simplification) come later as new passes, each with tests that
  compare results with and without it.

### D47. Phase 1 public API headers

**Summary**: Phase 1 adds four public headers outside the substrate, `xml.h`,
`processor.h`, `xpath.h` and `serialize.h`, which become stable with the first
public release in Phase 2.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (Phase 1 planning; designed in packet 1.3). Four new public
headers, outside the substrate: `xml.h` (XML parser into any
`sxml_tree_builder`), `processor.h` (the processor of D30, owning name pool,
type registry and item heap, plus the host resolver interface for `fn:doc` and
the implicit timezone and current dateTime), `xpath.h` (static context
configuration, compile, evaluate) and `serialize.h` (adaptive method only in
Phase 1; XML, JSON and text methods arrive with XQuery in Phase 3). The CLI and
the QT4 driver use only these and the substrate headers. They are not frozen at
the Phase 1 gate; they become stable with the first public release (Phase 2).
The TypeScript package of D10 also waits for Phase 2: Phase 1 runs the slice
under Node.js WASI only.

### D48. A regular expression seed in Phase 1

**Summary**: Phase 1 has a small backtracking regular expression matcher for a
subset of the XPath dialect behind `src/regex_internal.h`, raising FORX0002 for
syntax outside the subset.

Recorded 2026-10-16. Three slice tests need `fn:tokenize`, but the D9 engine is
a Phase 2 packet. Phase 1 has a small backtracking matcher for a subset of the
XPath dialect behind `src/regex_internal.h` (compile, match at a position, step
limit), which the D9 engine later implements unchanged. Syntax outside the
subset raises FORX0002 rather than matching wrongly.

### D49. libmpdec arrives in Phase 1

**Summary**: mpdecimal is vendored and wrapped as D42 describes in Phase 1
rather than Phase 2, because the slice needs decimal arithmetic and integer
ranges beyond `int64_t`.

Recorded 2026-10-16, amending D42 ("for the decimal packet of Phase 2"). The
slice divides and multiplies decimals and builds integer ranges beyond
`int64_t` (D36), so mpdecimal is vendored and wrapped as D42 describes in Phase
1 (packet 1.2). Decimal formatting and the rest of the decimal function library
stay in Phase 2.

### D50. A status for failed input and output

**Summary**: `SXML_STATUS_INPUT_OUTPUT_FAILED` means the platform refused to
read or write bytes for a host interface while the sxml object and arguments
were fine, and it carries no error record.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (was P1, from D44; accepted by the orchestrator, added in
packet 1.0). `SXML_STATUS_INPUT_OUTPUT_FAILED` in `include/sxml/status.h` means
the platform refused to read or write bytes for a host interface (a closed
pipe, a full disk, a missing file) while the sxml object and its arguments were
fine. Host callbacks that read or write bytes return it: the CLI's output
streams and platform layer now, the serializer's output and the document
resolver of D30 later. It carries no error record; a host that maps it to a
specification error (for example `fn:doc` and FODC0002) does so itself.
Rejected: reusing `SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, which blames the caller for a
platform failure.

### D51. The Phase 1 public API (packet 1.3)

**Summary**: The Phase 1 public API defines the XML parser, the processor with
its resource resolver and clock, plain static and dynamic context structs,
compiled XPath expressions with complete results, and adaptive serialization.

Recorded 2026-10-16, completing D47. Headers: `xml.h` (needs `tree.h`) <
`processor.h` (`xdm.h`, `xml.h`) < `xpath.h`; `serialize.h` needs only `xdm.h`
(it serializes from an item heap).

- **XML parser**: a reusable object (allocator, name pool, `sxml_xml_limits`:
  depth, entity expansion bytes) that parses a whole document in memory into
  any `sxml_tree_builder`, or only checks it (`sxml check`). Failures are
  interface statuses (`MALFORMED_INPUT`, `INVALID_UTF8`, `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`
  for other encodings, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`) with a diagnostic naming the failed
  production or WFC: well-formedness errors have no QName codes; fn:doc and
  fn:parse-xml turn them into FODC0002 and FODC0006. Nothing outside the input
  is read.
- **Processor**: pool, registry and heap in its memory, one allocator for
  everything, one limits struct, a resource resolver and a clock;
  `sxml_processor_parse_document` gives an owned document node whose arena tree
  destroys itself when unreferenced.
- **Resource resolver**: one `resolve` operation with an `sxml_resource_kind`
  (only `XML_DOCUMENT` now; text, XQuery modules and XSLT stylesheet modules
  later), after Saxon's ResourceResolver, so later phases add kinds instead of
  publishing new interfaces. It answers bytes (sxml parses them with the
  processor's limits), a document node, or none. "Not available" (a missing
  file, a refused URI, a failed read) is `SXML_RESOURCE_FORM_NONE`, which
  fn:doc raises as FODC0002; a failure status (D50 included) stops the
  evaluation. The null resolver makes nothing available (the library does no
  I/O); the default implementation and test double is
  `sxml_table_resource_resolver` over in-memory entries.
- **Clock**: read at most once per evaluation, so fn:current-dateTime is
  stable; `sxml_system_clock` (C17 `timespec_get`, implicit timezone UTC) and
  `sxml_fixed_clock`.
- **Contexts**: `sxml_static_context_configuration` and
  `sxml_dynamic_context_configuration` are plain structs embedded by value in
  requests; zero means the default context. XQuery and XSLT reuse them. Names
  are name pool identifiers and types registry identifiers, as in the
  substrate. External variables are declared with a type and bound by name
  (coerced, XPTY0004; unbound XPDY0002); the context value is a sequence (XPath
  4.0) with a presence flag; available documents make `fn:doc(uri)` the very
  node bound elsewhere (QT4 sources with a `uri`). A namespace binding with
  prefix 0 is the default namespace for elements and types.
- **Expressions**: `sxml_xpath_expression` follows the lifecycle quintet;
  initialize compiles. The compiled form is allocated from the processor and
  counted, so inline function items in a result outlive the expression (D38).
  Results are complete: nothing lazy that can fail later. Evaluations may nest.
  `sxml_xpath_parse_sequence_type` turns declared types given as text (279 QT4
  `param ... as=`) into sequence types.
- **Serialization**: `sxml_output_stream` (one `write`, which returns D50's
  status when the platform refuses), the `sxml_output_buffer` as default and
  test double, and `sxml_serialize_sequence` with the adaptive method; the
  method enum and parameters struct grow in Phase 3.
- **Limits**: 0 means no bound, except `maximum_expression_depth` and
  `maximum_evaluation_depth`, where 0 means sxml's default: no bound would mean
  a C stack overflow.
- Left out until needed, each a new field that designated initializers keep
  source-compatible: host extension functions in the static context (meanwhile
  a function item bound to a variable), decimal formats, collations, default
  language, fn:trace output, cancellation, a seed for
  fn:random-number-generator.

### D52. The abstract syntax tree (packet 1.4)

**Summary**: The internal XPath abstract syntax tree in
`src/xpath_ast_internal.h` has one node kind per visible grammar production,
children tagged by grammar field, and fixed-capacity arrays sized from the
concrete syntax tree.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xpath_ast_internal.h`, internal. One node kind per
visible production of `grammars/xpath` (D29), except `comment`, and `axis` and
`occurrence_indicator`, which only hold a token and become their parent's
detail; anonymous field tokens (operator, quantifier, abbreviation) become
detail or flags. Children are linked in source order and tagged with their
grammar field, so lists are "children with field F" and code finds children by
field, never by position: XQuery and pattern grammars, which add node types and
add fields to four XPath types, only append to the kind and field enumerations.
Nodes and decoded text live in two fixed-capacity arrays (D24) sized from the
concrete syntax tree (its node count bounds the AST nodes, the source byte
count bounds decoded text), so building never grows; index 0 means "no node".
Names are kept as written (prefix, local name, braced URI); string literals and
template parts are unescaped and numeric literals lose `_` and `0x`/`0b`, while
lowering makes the atomic items. Each node has a source span (byte offset and
count, line, column in codepoints). Front-end entry points
`sxml_xpath_build_ast` and `sxml_xpath_build_sequence_type_ast` are declared
there and defined by packet 1.16 in `src/xpath_parse.c`; the lifecycle and
builder functions go in `src/xpath_ast.c`, also written by 1.16 (the AST
module's only producer in Phase 1). Identifiers use the module prefix
`sxml_ast_`, since XQuery and patterns share the tree.

### D53. Regular expressions: hand-written parser, compiled regex and matcher (packet 1.17)

**Summary**: Regular expressions are parsed by a hand-written parser in
`src/regex.c` without recursion, compiled into an immutable shareable
`sxml_regex`, and run by a per-thread `sxml_regex_matcher`.

Recorded 2026-10-16. The regex text is parsed by a hand-written
recursive-descent parser in `src/regex.c`, not by a tree-sitter grammar: an
exception to D12, for these reasons. (1) A regex is run-time data, compiled
during evaluation (`fn:tokenize($s, $p)` with a computed `$p`), and tree-sitter
allocates with `malloc` outside every sxml allocator and limit (D12 accepts
that only for the parse step of source text). (2) The flags change the lexing
before any grammar applies (F&O 4.0, section 6.2: `x` removes whitespace except
inside `[...]`, `c` removes `#...#` comments, `q` makes every character
literal), so a grammar would need a preprocessing pass that is most of a
parser. (3) Tokens are single characters whose meaning depends on context
(inside or outside `[...]`, after `\`, the hyphen rules of XSD 1.1), and
back-references need the groups closed so far; a context-free grammar plus a
tree walk adds a layer without removing any check. (4) FORX0002 needs a precise
reason, and tree-sitter `ERROR` nodes give none. (5) Saxon HE and regexml, the
models of D9, parse by hand too. The XSD dialect (Phase 5) is a flag of the
same parser. Interface (`src/regex_internal.h`), which the D9 engine keeps:
`sxml_regex_parse_flags` (FORX0001); `sxml_regex`, compiled from `regex_text`
and flags, immutable, shareable between threads, with the object lifecycle of
every type (C_GUIDELINES, "Object lifecycle and caller-provided memory")
(memory requirements found by a counting pass of the parser, so they are exact
and need no scratch memory); `sxml_regex_matcher`, the per-thread working state
(backtrack stack through an allocator, captured groups, step count), with
`match_at` (anchored), `find` (first matching segment at or after an offset)
and `find_next` (the next of the disjoint matching segments, F&O 4.0, section
6.1.1), each writing an `sxml_regex_search_result` (found or not, and the
segment: the bool outputs the lint forbids become a struct), and captured
groups as byte ranges of the regex input. Positions are byte offsets at
codepoint boundaries. A regex error is SXML_STATUS_DYNAMIC_ERROR with
err:FORX0002 in the error record the configuration points to; running out of
steps or stack is SXML_STATUS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, not a spec error. The seed (D48)
supports: literals, `.`, classes with ranges, negation and subtraction, `\s \S
\d \D \w \W` (Unicode 16.0 tables generated by
`tools/generate-regex-tables.py`), greedy and reluctant quantifiers, capturing
and non-capturing groups, alternation, `^ $`, back-references, and flags `s m i
x q c`. FORX0002 with "not supported by the regex seed": `\p \P \i \I \c \C \b
\B`, lookahead and lookbehind, named groups and `\k`; with `i`, non-ASCII
characters in the regex and back-references (case variants beyond ASCII need
Unicode case data). A public step limit in `sxml_processor_limits` is left for
the D9 packet (a new field).

**No recursion (D71)**, amended 2026-10-16: the parser reads pieces in one loop
and keeps open groups on an explicit stack of group frames, inline for
`SXML_REGEX_INLINE_GROUP_DEPTH` (16) groups, then grown through the new
`stack_allocator` of `sxml_regex_configuration` and released before the call
returns (`sxml_regex_create` uses its own allocator; without one, deeper
nesting is CAPACITY_EXCEEDED); `maximum_group_depth` (default 100) now bounds
that heap. Every atom is parsed and emitted once: a "|" inserts the split of
the branch before it, a quantifier inserts what precedes the first copy and
appends copies of the atom's instructions (targets moved, progress registers
renumbered, classes shared), so the lexical skipping and re-parsing are gone.
Class subtraction is a chain, read and matched in loops. Arrays are sized by
the most a pass wrote, which fixes a write past the arrays when an atom
quantified with {0} came last (`(ab){0}` at the end). 400,000 random regexes
compile, fail and match exactly as before.

**Sources**: 400,000 random regexes compiled, failed and matched before and
after the rewrite; configured: SXML_REGEX_INLINE_GROUP_DEPTH (16) and the
default maximum_group_depth (100) (from `src/regex_internal.h`).

### D54. Name pool internals (packet 1.1)

**Summary**: The name pool keeps URIs, prefixes and names in entry arrays with
unseeded FNV-1a open-addressing indexes and text in an arena of 1 KiB blocks,
all counted against `maximum_byte_count`.

Recorded 2026-10-16. Three tables (URIs, prefixes, names), each an entry array
in issue order plus an open-addressing index (linear probing, at most 3/4 full,
slots keep the hash so growth never reads entries); FNV-1a, not seeded: hash
flooding is bounded by `maximum_byte_count`. Interned text lives in an arena
placed in the pool's own memory, in 1 KiB blocks. `maximum_byte_count` counts
every allocation the pool holds (tables and whole text blocks, so a pool may
stop up to one block early); a replaced table gives its bytes back. A failed
intern leaves the pool's names as they were. Interned URI identifiers start at
`SXML_NAMESPACE_WELL_KNOWN_COUNT`; prefix and name identifiers at 1.
`src/name_internal.h` gives `sxml_name_pool_name_limit` (and URI, prefix) so
tables indexed by identifier can be sized.

### D55. IR, passes, evaluator and function table (packet 1.5)

**Summary**: Four internal headers define the reference-counted IR unit with
its expression kinds, the pass list holding only the verifier, the evaluator's
dynamic context, and native function rows typed by F&O-spelled text.

Recorded 2026-10-16, completing D46. Four internal headers.

- `src/ir_internal.h`: a unit holds every array (expressions, atoms, functions,
  constants, globals; reserved: catch clauses, name tests, namespace bindings,
  parameter bindings, modes, template rules), index 0 meaning none; it grows
  while built, is sealed before evaluation and is reference counted, so
  function items made from IR functions keep it alive (D38, D51). Slots number
  from 1: parameters, then captured variables, then locals. 25 expression kinds
  for XPath (MAP, FILTER, SORT, QUANTIFIED bind the focus to slots; STEP yields
  axis order and DOCUMENT_ORDER sorts; COERCE and RAISE are explicit) plus
  reserved TRY_CATCH, seven constructors, SHALLOW_COPY and APPLY_TEMPLATES. The
  header writes out the IR of `let $f := function($x){$x + .} return $f(4)`,
  `/a/b[2]`, an XQuery FLWOR with order by (tuples as arrays, no new kind) and
  an XSLT apply-templates (named extension point: modes and template rules,
  match functions from patterns). group by and windows use internal native
  rows. Globals read by an inline function are captured, so escaped closures
  need no global table of their own.
- `src/ir_pass_internal.h`: `sxml_ir_pass` (name, function over a request),
  `sxml_ir_standard_passes` = {verifier}, `sxml_ir_run_passes` optionally
  verifying after each pass; passes only add and replace.
- `src/evaluator_internal.h`: `struct sxml_dynamic_context` (heap, frames,
  clock read once, document loader, function table for fn:function-lookup,
  depth limit, globals); `sxml_evaluator_evaluate`; coercion, dynamic calls
  with coercion and the effective boolean value for native bodies; the function
  body operations of IR functions. fn:doc and fn:parse-xml go through an
  internal `sxml_document_loader` that the processor (1.23) implements, so 1.20
  and 1.22 test with doubles.
- `src/function_library_internal.h`: native rows give parameter and result
  types as F&O-spelled text ("fn(item(), xs:integer) as xs:boolean?"), resolved
  once per library through the front end and static analysis; defaults are
  required, the context value (lowering supplies it) or supplied by the body;
  properties flag dynamic-context use, nondeterminism, higher-order calls and
  position/last. One `extern const sxml_native_function_view` per part file;
  the configuration names the parts, so no file lists another's functions.
  Static analysis finds functions through the `sxml_function_table` interface
  (tests bring their own).

### D56. `memcpy` and `memset` are allowed

**Summary**: `memcpy`, `memmove` and `memset` are allowed when the byte count
comes from checked size arithmetic, and the clang-tidy check that demands Annex
K functions is switched off.

Recorded 2026-10-16 by the orchestrator. clang-tidy's
`clang-analyzer-security.insecureAPI.DeprecatedOrUnsafeBufferHandling` rejects
`memcpy`, `memset` and `snprintf` in favour of the C11 Annex K `_s` functions,
which glibc, macOS and WASI do not provide. Packets wrote byte loops instead.
The check is switched off in `.clang-tidy`; `memcpy`, `memmove` and `memset`
are allowed when the byte count comes from checked size arithmetic. Printing
functions stay banned outside the CLI platform layer (D17, D44). Existing byte
loops may stay; new code uses `memcpy`.

### D57. Decimal arithmetic over libmpdec (packet 1.2)

**Summary**: Decimal arithmetic wraps vendored mpdecimal 4.0.1 in
`sxml_decimal`, with the allocator scope in the patched `mpalloc.c`, a per-heap
digit limit, exact sums and products, and 34-digit quotients.

Recorded 2026-10-16, completing D42 and D49.

- **Vendoring**: mpdecimal 4.0.1 (`third_party/mpdecimal.version`), libmpdec
  only; patches marked "sxml patch" in `mpalloc.c`, `mpdecimal.h` and
  `context.c`. The configuration is chosen in `mpdecimal.h` from the width of
  `size_t` (CONFIG_64 or CONFIG_32 with the portable ANSI arithmetic,
  `__uint128_t` under GCC and Clang), so one header serves every target, 32-bit
  WebAssembly included; no MASM or inline assembler. WASI has no `signal.h`:
  the never-called trap handler does nothing there.
- **Scope location**: the D42 thread-local lives in the patched `mpalloc.c`,
  not in `src/`, so libmpdec does not depend on the sxml library that links it;
  `src/decimal.c` sets it with `mpd_sxml_exchange_allocator_scope`. Shrinking a
  block keeps it (never fails); growth is allocate, copy, release (D22).
- **Value type**: `sxml_decimal` wraps an `mpd_t` with a static struct and a
  dynamic coefficient: movable byte for byte, made by the functions that write
  it, released by `sxml_decimal_finalize` without a scope. No create/destroy:
  cells (1.7) embed it.
- **Limits and precision**: a configuration (allocator, `maximum_digit_count`
  default 10000, `division_digit_count` default 34) per item heap. Sums,
  differences, products, `idiv` and `mod` are exact or
  `SXML_STATUS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (FOAR0002); quotients are computed to max(34,
  digits of both operands) significant digits, half to even
  (op-numeric-dividepint2args-5 then gives its second allowed result). Division
  by zero is `SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` (callers raise FOAR0001).
- **Binary floating point**: casting uses the shortest round-trip decimal
  (`0.1e0` gives `0.1`, as XPath processors do); `fn:atomic-equal` and numeric
  comparison use the exact value. Decimal to double/float goes through
  `strtod`/`strtof` on text without a decimal point (locale-free), 780 digits
  plus a sticky digit, so rounding is exact.
- **Size**: a stripped `wasm32-wasip1` program using parse, divide, shortest
  conversion, canonical text and `to_double` grows by 89 KB (35 KB gzip) over
  one using only the allocator.

### D58. Type registry internals and the subtype search (packet 1.6)

**Summary**: The type registry interns normalized type descriptions in
open-addressing indexes and answers subtype questions by the XPath 4.0 rules on
a fixed, non-allocating stack of frames with a work budget.

Recorded 2026-10-16.

- **Storage**: built-in descriptions are static (`src/types_builtin.c`); their
  names are interned at initialization and found through a fixed 256-slot index
  inside the registry. Registered types are an entry array plus two
  open-addressing indexes (structure, names), as in D54; copied views live in
  an arena of 4 KiB blocks, released at finalize. A registration that fails
  after copying leaves its copies unused there.
- **Normal form**: registered descriptions are normalized before interning
  (name test fields its kind does not use cleared; `allows_nilled` only on
  `element(N, T)`; `map(*)`, `array(*)`, `function(*)` and `jnode(*)` carry
  their explicit equivalents, as the built-ins do), so `map(*)` with any key
  gives `SXML_TYPE_MAP` and a node test of kind any gives xnode(). node() and
  xnode() share a description; node() is told apart by identifier. A choice of
  one member is that member.
- **Rejected on registration** (INVALID_ARGUMENT): duplicate enumeration values
  and duplicate field names (the front end removes duplicate enum values
  first), empty choices and enumerations, map keys that are not atomic, union
  or enumeration types, `document-node()` around anything but element tests,
  JNode key constants outside the six key types.
- **Subtyping** follows XPath 4.0 §3.3.2 rule by rule; transitivity is built
  into the rules where it adds pairs (maps, arrays, records as functions;
  records as maps; nominative records as their structural twin). A choice as
  derived type is split first (every member), then a choice as base (some
  member, else the abstract expansion of xs:anyAtomicType, xnode(), node(),
  item()); `document-node(element(a|b))` is split per element. Two places are
  slightly more permissive than the letter of §3.3.2.2 (a derived member is
  compared with the whole base choice, so a union member may spread over
  several base members); both are sound. Without schemas (Phase 5)
  schema-element/-attribute tests are subtypes only of themselves,
  `element()`/`attribute()` and same-name `attribute(N)`. JNode key constants
  compare by type and lexical form.
- **Budget**: one question may nest 128 deep and apply 10⁶ rules. Every rule is
  monotone, so running out answers false, never a wrong true; this bounds work
  on hostile types.
- **No recursion (D71)**: the rules reduce a question to an and/or tree of
  subtype goals, evaluated left to right with short-circuiting on an explicit
  stack of subtype frames; the last sub-goal of a frame replaces it, so
  array(array(...)) and function results take one frame however deep. The
  header promises the subtype queries never allocate, so the 192 frames (about
  6 KiB under wasm, 9 KiB on 64-bit) are a fixed array in the query's own C
  frame; the 128 depth is unchanged. A goal that would need a 193rd frame is
  false: only choices nested inside choices (an enumeration value or
  document-node() searched through a base choice of choices) need frames
  without depth. Derivation tries union members depth first on a fixed stack of
  256 (the old derivation depth).

### D59. The XPath front end (packet 1.16)

**Summary**: `src/xpath_parse.c` builds the XPath AST in one iterative
tree-sitter cursor walk, applies the delimitation and lookup-key checks, and
parses sequence types as `() instance of T`.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xpath_parse.c` builds the AST of D52 in one iterative
walk of a tree-sitter cursor in source order; the current AST parent is kept
through the AST's own parent links, so nesting depth costs no C stack (20,000
nested parentheses pass under the `wasm` preset). Node types and field names
map to kinds and fields through sorted static tables; the AST capacity is
`ts_node_descendant_count` of the top node.

- Checks of D29 in the walk: A.3.2 delimitation over the terminals in order
  (non-delimiting: keywords, `ncname`, `prefixed_name`, `uri_qualified_name`
  and the numeric literals; a comment separates) and a `prefixed_name` in the
  `key` field of `lookup` or `unary_lookup`. Every failure, and the first ERROR
  or MISSING node, is XPST0003 with a static description, the source name,
  line, codepoint column and byte offset. With these, XP40 has no false rejects
  or false accepts left (32,542 valid queries build; Lookup-156 and
  MapConstructor-025a, the two D29 false accepts, now fail).
- A sequence type is parsed as the type of `() instance of T`: the prefix is
  served before the text through a `TSInput` callback (no copy), the result
  must be that instance-of expression with the type starting in the text, and
  spans are relative to the text.
- tree-sitter aliases each token of `alias(seq('(', ')'), jroot_selector)`
  separately; the front end makes one JROOT_SELECTOR spanning both.
- `maximum_expression_depth` counts AST nodes from the root (depth 1).
- The only memory taken from the request's allocator is the AST, one
  allocation; tree-sitter's parser, tree and cursors use malloc (D12).
- AST builder tests are in `tests/xpath_ast_test.c` (module prefix `xpath`,
  D45), front-end tests in `tests/xpath_parse_test.c`.

**Sources**: 20,000 nested parentheses (wasm build); XP40 valid queries that
build, and the two D29 false accepts.

### D60. Item heap, cells and atomic items (packet 1.7)

**Summary**: `src/xdm_internal.h` defines the item heap's cell header and cell
classes, frees released cells in a loop, counts every byte against the heap
limit, and stores decimals with their canonical text.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xdm_internal.h` is the shared interface of the value
model; later XDM packets add files, not edits.

- **Layout**: `sxml_item.representation` is an internal enum (inline boolean,
  integer, float, double, QName; atomic, JNode, function, map, array cells;
  from 64 the sequence cells vector, integer range, concatenation, lazy); 0 is
  "no item" and, as sequence content, the empty sequence. Atomic items keep
  their primitive type in `flags`, so type families need no registry;
  `type_or_node_index` holds the annotation (node index for XNodes).
- **Cells**: header (cell class, heap, byte count, reference count) at the
  start of a module's struct. A `sxml_cell_class` (static const) gives
  `release_contents` and, for sequence cells, count/get item/iterator next, so
  `src/xdm.c` dispatches to range, concatenation and lazy cells (1.8) without
  link-time dependencies. Releasing the last reference queues the cell on the
  heap's pending list; the outermost release frees the list in a loop, so deep
  values free in constant C stack (a 10^6 chain is tested). Count overflow
  makes a cell immortal.
- **Memory**: every byte the heap hands out counts in `live_byte_count` and
  against `maximum_byte_count`: cells, side tables
  (`sxml_item_heap_allocate_bytes`), the raised error, and decimal
  coefficients, which go through `sxml_item_heap_as_allocator` (a hidden size
  header per block) as the heap's decimal configuration.
- **Decimals**: a decimal cell stores its canonical text (made with the cell,
  not on first read), the nearest double and whether it equals it exactly.
  atomic-equal, the hash and compare therefore never allocate: doubles are
  compared through their exact decimal text, built on the stack. Numbers equal
  to some double hash as that double, others as their canonical text, so 1,
  1.0, 1.0e0 and xs:float 1 hash alike.
- **Compare** follows F&O 4.0 `fn:compare` with PR2256 (QT4 fn-compare):
  durations by months then seconds, binary by octets across hex and base64,
  QNames by namespace URI then local name. QName order needs the name pool,
  which `sxml_atomic_comparison` lacks: internal
  `sxml_atomic_item_compare_in_heap` takes the heap; the public function
  returns `SXML_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE` for distinct names (P2).
- **Making**: strings are revalidated as UTF-8 and checked against the derived
  types (NCName, token, language, ...); integer subtypes by range, beyond
  `int64_t` only where the type allows (unsignedLong up to 2^64-1).
  `sxml_atomic_item_make_taking_decimal` lets operators and casting hand over a
  computed `sxml_decimal`.
- **Node items**: `sxml_item_retain`/`_release` must retain the tree, but
  `src/tree.c` arrives with 1.11. `src/xdm.c` has two empty static functions,
  `sxml_node_item_retain_tree`/`_release_tree`; packet 1.11 fills them with
  `sxml_tree_retain`/`sxml_tree_release` (a two-line hand-off; no node item
  exists before 1.13).
- `sxml_error_record_report` fills an error record from a `sxml_static_error`
  (err namespace), for every packet's static errors.

### D61. Maps and records (packet 1.9)

**Summary**: Maps are entry blocks with a hash index above 8 entries,
persistent AVL entry and key trees for put and remove, or records whose field
keys are made on first need.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xdm_map.c`; three cell classes behind
`SXML_ITEM_REPRESENTATION_MAP_CELL`, told apart by cell class.

- **Entry block** (`sxml_map_make`): entries in one cell. Maps of more than 8
  entries get a hash index (key hash, entry index; open addressing, load at
  most 1/2). Duplicate detection needs it, so it is built while making and
  kept, not built on first lookup (a refinement of D37); maps of 8 entries or
  fewer are searched linearly.
- **Persistent map** (`sxml_map_put`, `sxml_map_remove`): an entry tree (AVL,
  ordered by entry stamp, entry counts per subtree) and a key tree (AVL,
  ordered by key hash, then stamp), both of `map_node` cells shared by path
  copying. Put and remove are O(log n), `sxml_map_get_entry` and
  `sxml_map_find` O(log n). A new key gets the next stamp, so it goes last; a
  removed and re-added key goes last too. Put on an existing key keeps the old
  key and its position and replaces the value (which key is kept is
  implementation-dependent, QT4 map-put-011). Put or remove on an entry block
  or record converts it in O(n log n) once; results of 8 entries or fewer stay
  entry blocks (copied).
- **Record**: the cell holds the record type, the field values and
  `field_key`s, made on first need (`sxml_map_get_entry`, `sxml_map_find`) in a
  side table of the cell; lookup by name goes through
  `sxml_type_registry_find_record_field`, shared by every record of the type.
  Only string-family keys (xs:string, xs:anyURI, xs:untypedAtomic) can match a
  field. Put and remove give a plain map (persistent or block). Because field
  keys are made lazily, `sxml_map_get_entry` on a record can return the heap's
  failures on its first call (P3).

### D62. Ranges, concatenations and lazy sequences (packet 1.8)

**Summary**: `src/xdm_sequence.c` adds integer range, concatenation and lazy
