sequence cells, where lazy sequences keep produced items and a generator
failure is final and raised again on later reads.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xdm_sequence.c` adds three sequence cell classes and
`sxml_sequence_test_emptiness`; xdm.h and src/xdm.c are unchanged.

- **Ranges** store the two `int64_t` bounds; an empty range is the empty
  sequence and a one-integer range an inline item, so a range cell always has
  two or more items. Members are computed in `uint64_t`; every index below 2^64
  is readable. Only the count of `INT64_MIN to INT64_MAX` (2^64 items) does not
  fit: `sxml_sequence_count` raises XPDY0130 (XPath 4.0,
  implementation-dependent limit), as for a concatenation whose total passes
  2^64 - 1.
- **Concatenations** drop empty inputs, flatten nested concatenations and
  return a lone remaining part itself (retained). Part ends (items up to and
  including each part) are a cache filled in order as reads count the parts;
  `get_item` binary-searches the counted parts and asks each further part for
  the item before counting it, so a lazy part is read only as far as needed.
  Iteration uses `part_index`/`next_index_in_part`: O(1) per item.
- **Lazy sequences** keep produced items in a doubling array (room is made
  before calling the generator, so an item is never lost and an allocation
  failure is retryable). The generator always gets the cell's own error record;
  a failure is final: its error is copied into the cell (the kept error, D41)
  and raised again through the heap by every later read that needs an item past
  the last produced one; items before it stay readable. A non-error status (out
  of memory in the generator) is kept and returned the same way. The
  generator's state is released only when the cell is freed, as xdm.h says. A
  generator that reads its own lazy sequence gets
  `SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` instead of reentry.
- **Emptiness** is `get_item(0)`: at most one item of a lazy sequence is
  produced, and its error is reported (D43).

### D63. Static analysis and lowering (packet 1.12)

**Summary**: `sxml_xpath_lower` lowers the XPath AST to ANF IR without C
recursion, resolving names, focus slots, paths, calls and literals; listed
constructs are UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE in Phase 1.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xpath_static_internal.h` (module `xpath_static`):
`sxml_xpath_static_context` (heap, allocator, namespace bindings, variable
declarations, function table); `sxml_xpath_resolve_name`,
`_resolve_sequence_type` and `_resolve_item_type` (also for the type text of
function library rows, D55); `sxml_xpath_lower` (AST to an unsealed unit) and
`sxml_xpath_compile` (parse, lower, `sxml_ir_standard_passes`, seal), which
1.23 calls.

- **Names**: the AST's namespace declarations, then the configuration, then the
  predeclared prefixes; unprefixed functions are in fn, variables, attributes
  and QName literals in no namespace, element and type names in the default
  element namespace. Function names are found with `sxml_name_pool_find_name`:
  a name never interned is XPST0017. Global variable n is variable declaration
  n, referenced or not, so the processor binds by index.
- **Shape**: ANF blocks append LETs; atoms (literals, variables) are never
  bound. Left-recursive chains (binary operators, paths, filters, lookups,
  dynamic calls, arrows) are walked in a loop; other nesting costs one frame of
  the lowering machine in allocator memory (D71; no C recursion), bounded by
  `maximum_expression_depth` (default
  `SXML_XPATH_DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EXPRESSION_DEPTH`, 10,000 levels, a few MB of
  frames at most; LIMIT_EXCEEDED beyond). The former default of 32 for the
  WebAssembly stack is gone. An inline function's free variables are found by
  walking its AST through parent links; each becomes a captured slot, except a
  constant (a `let` of a literal), which is substituted. Globals read in a
  function are captured (D55).
- **Focus**: slots made on first read (main, MAP, FILTER); absent in an inline
  function body (a RAISE of XPDY0002 where read); a focus function and `->` fix
  the value, with position and size 1.
- **Paths**: `E1/E2` is MAP then DOCUMENT_ORDER; `//` adds a MAP of
  `descendant-or-self::node()` and DOCUMENT_ORDER; a reverse-axis step is
  followed by DOCUMENT_ORDER after its predicates; default axis attribute or
  namespace for those tests; `node()` steps use the generic node type. A name
  test on a JNode origin is the evaluator's to read as a key test (XPath 4.0,
  4.6.5), since STEP carries element(N).
- **Calls**: COERCE unless the type is `item()*` or a constant already matches;
  constructor functions are CAST allowing empty; a left-out context-value
  parameter is the focus value (static calls) or captured by a closure (`f#N`);
  `position()`/`last()` read focus slots; static placeholders make a closure
  (constant arguments in its body, others coerced and captured); dynamic
  placeholders call fn:partial-apply with `xs:positiveInteger` keys; keyword
  arguments are reordered; `and`/`or` are CONDITIONALs giving
  `true()`/`false()`, `otherwise` tests `instance of item()+`, string templates
  use fn:string-join#2 and `||`. fn:root, fn:partial-apply and fn:string-join
  must be in the table.
- **Literals**: integers inline or as decimal cells (hex and binary converted);
  doubles through decimal text, rounded once (D57).
- **Not lowered in Phase 1** (UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, diagnostic filled): for
  member, for key/value, destructuring let, method calls, but with, dynamic
  node tests, the item axis, named namespace-axis tests (P4), jnode() selectors
  other than `*`, `()`, NCName, string, integer, boolean.
- **Text form**: nested expression operands start a line two columns past their
  parent's "(", except a LET's bound expression; constants print as XPath
  literals (doubles as `<shortest decimal>e0`).
- **Checks**: with a permissive function table, 29,653 of the 32,409 valid XP40
  queries lower and pass the verifier; the rest are static errors from missing
  test environments, or the constructs above.
- `sxml_native_function` now has `properties` after `function_namespace` (no
  padding; clang-tidy's padding check failed on the first file to include it).
  Field order only.
- `sxml_function_table_find` (D55) is declared but nobody defines it yet;
  static analysis uses `sxml_xpath_find_function`; 1.20 may define the wrapper
  over it.

**Sources**: XP40 valid queries that lower and pass the verifier, with a
permissive function table; configured:
SXML_XPATH_DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EXPRESSION_DEPTH, 10,000 levels (from
`src/xpath_static_internal.h`).

### D64. Arrays and function items (packet 1.10)

**Summary**: Arrays are AVL trees of `array_node` cells updated by split and
join in O(log n); function items need a registered function type; maps and
arrays act as functions through stateless bodies.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xdm_array.c`, `src/xdm_function.c`.

- **Arrays** are AVL trees of `array_node` cells (one cell class): a flat node
  holds members inline (`sxml_array_make`, so get is O(1)); a run node names a
  part of a flat node's members (splitting a leaf copies nothing); a branch
  node joins two subtrees. The array item's cell is the root; the empty array
  is a flat node of no members. Every update is split plus join (Blelloch et
  al., "Just Join", without middle keys): append, put, insert, remove and slice
  are O(log n), get O(log n). 10^5 appends are tested at most 1 + 3 x height
  allocations each; deep nesting frees through the pending list.
- **Function items**: the signature must be a registered function type other
  than function(\*) (arity = its parameter count), else INVALID_ARGUMENT.
  Annotations are kept as the borrowed view; captured values are retained; the
  body's `retain` runs once on make and `release` once when the cell is freed.
- **Maps and arrays as functions**: `sxml_function_item_describe` gives a
  stateless static body (map:get through `sxml_map_find`, array:get with
  1-based positions). The bodies check their argument although coercion is the
  caller's: not one atomic key / one integer is XPTY0004; a position out of
  range, also beyond int64_t, is FOAY0001.

### D65. WASI test runner disables V8 fast API calls

**Summary**: `tools/run-wasi.mjs` sets `--no-turbo-fast-api-calls` before
compiling the module, so Node.js calls WASI imports the ordinary way and no
longer crashes in garbage collection during fast calls.

- **Problem**: the `xpath_parse` test crashed Node.js (SIGSEGV, exit 139) about
  one run in eight on the `wasm` preset; `deep_nesting_needs_no_recursion`
  alone, after it had passed. Not a memory error in sxml: the same test is
  clean under ASan/UBSan (Clang, GCC) and valgrind, and the crash is not a wasm
  trap or a stack overflow (it happens with `--stack-size=200` too).
- **Cause**: in Node 22 the WASI imports are V8 fast API callbacks. `fd_write`
  allocates through uvwasi, which reports external memory to V8 and can start a
  full garbage collection inside the fast call; the collector then faults
  walking the optimized wasm frame (`InnerPointerToCodeCache::GetCacheEntry`).
  Whether a collection falls there depends on heap timing, hence one run in
  eight; tests that grow linear memory a lot (20,000 nested parentheses) make
  it likely. `--no-allow-allocation-in-fast-api-call` turns it into a
  deterministic V8 abort in `WASI::FdWrite`'s FastCallback (45 of 60 runs).
- **Decision**: `tools/run-wasi.mjs` sets `--no-turbo-fast-api-calls` through
  `v8.setFlagsFromString` before compiling the module, so WASI functions are
  called the ordinary way. 0 failures in 110 runs afterwards, also with
  allocation in fast calls forbidden. The test depth and the wasm stack size
  stay as they are; the library is not involved. Revisit when the runner's Node
  version no longer uses fast calls for WASI.

**Sources**: xpath_parse crash rate under Node, with
--no-allow-allocation-in-fast-api-call (45 of 60), and 0 failures in 110 runs
afterwards (`tools/run-wasi.mjs`, `ctest`, wasm build).

### D66. Casting and lexical forms (packet 1.15)

**Summary**: Casting takes the atomized operand and any atomic, list, union,
enumeration or choice target, follows XSD 1.1 lexical spaces, and casts nested
targets on an explicit stack of cast frames.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/cast_internal.h`; `src/cast.c` (casting table,
targets), `src/cast_lexical.c` (lexical forms, canonical text).

- **Interface**: `sxml_cast_make_value` and `sxml_cast_test_castability` take
  the atomized operand (atomizing is the evaluator's) and any target type:
  atomic, list, union, enumeration or choice; a target that cannot be cast to
  gives XPST0080 at run time too. `sxml_cast_make_value_from_text` casts text
  as an xs:string without making one (list tokens use it).
  `sxml_cast_write_canonical_text` borrows the text of strings and decimals,
  writes the rest to the caller's buffer and reports the size needed on
  CAPACITY_EXCEEDED (96 bytes hold every number, date and duration).
- **xs:QName**: the request carries the statically known namespaces as an
  `sxml_namespace_binding_view` (prefix 0: default namespace for elements and
  types), predeclared prefixes as fallback; no callback interface. XPTY0117
  (coercing untypedAtomic to xs:QName) stays with the evaluator.
- **Checks**: syntax here, value space in `sxml_atomic_item_make`, whose
  INVALID_ARGUMENT becomes FORG0001. XSD 1.1 lexical spaces: "+INF" accepted,
  base64 with single spaces, year of 4 to 16 digits ("-0000" refused, more is
  FODT0001), 24:00:00 is the next day, fraction digits past nine truncated
  (D36), duration parts beyond `int64_t` FODT0002; digits beyond the heap's
  limit FOCA0003 (integer targets) or FOCA0001.
- **Numbers**: xs:double and xs:float write the shortest digits (D57) as a
  decimal when the first significant digit's power of ten is -6 to 5, else as
  d.dddEn, so xs:float("1e-6") writes 0.000001. To integer types truncates
  (doubles beyond 2^63 by their exact value); to xs:decimal the shortest
  decimal. Text to float goes through `strtof` (one rounding) on locale-free
  text, as D57.
- **Unions and choices**: an instance of an atomic member is returned
  unchanged, otherwise members in order; when all fail XPTY0004 if every member
  refused the source type, else FORG0001 (xs:error: FORG0001).
  **Enumerations**: cast to xs:string, then codepoint membership; the result is
  an xs:string. **Lists**: only from the string types (XPTY0004), collapsed and
  split, no tokens is FORG0001. Targets nest at most 32 deep (LIMIT_EXCEEDED
  beyond): unions, choices and lists are cast on an explicit stack of cast
  frames in heap memory (D71), grown up to 33.
- **castable**: dynamic and type errors of the cast give false; errors reading
  the operand, XPST0080, memory and limits are returned.

### D67. Tree, axes and arena tree (packet 1.11)

**Summary**: Axes derive each step from node numbering, `copy_node` walks index
order with a constant C stack, and the arena tree keeps nodes in segments that
never move and fixes namespaces at header close.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/tree_internal.h` holds `struct sxml_tree` (the arena
tree embeds it) and node-reference helpers.

- **Wrapper**: caches node count and name pool at initialize (trees are
  immutable); the identifier is issued last, so a failed initialize uses none.
  Namespace node names are found in the pool, interned only if new.
- **Axes** keep only origin and next node and derive each step from
  descriptions (D39 numbering): descendants/following by `N + 1 +
  attribute_count(N)`; preceding scans backwards from the reference node (an
  attribute's or namespace node's element), skipping attributes and nodes whose
  subtree reaches it (ancestors). Following of an attribute or namespace node
  includes its element's descendants.
- **copy_node** walks index order and closes elements by parent links: linear,
  constant C stack. Preserve sends the bindings the copy's parent lacks plus
  undeclarations; no-preserve sends none and lets fixup bind what names use.
  Without type preservation nilled is dropped, ID flags kept.
  `inherits_namespaces` cannot be honoured for the top element (P6).
- **Arena tree**: one `sxml_arena` over initial memory and the allocator. Nodes
  in segments of 16·2^k (never moved or copied); content in a text store whose
  pending run becomes one text node; in-scope lists shared when an element
  declares nothing new (xml binding in a base list). Fixup at header close:
  names keep a bound prefix, else bind it unless the element declared it
  otherwise, else reuse a prefix bound to the URI, else `ns0`, `ns1`...; a
  no-namespace element undeclares the default. XQDY0025, XQDY0102, XQDY0101
  (xml/xmlns misuse) and XQDY0044 are raised into the configured error record.
  Duplicate checks scan up to 8 attributes, then use a hash index.
  `maximum_depth` counts open elements; the text limit counts every byte copied
  into the store. Unparsed entities only before document content. After a
  failed event only finalize/destroy is meaningful.

Recorded 2026-10-16 by packet 1.19, on the orchestrator's acceptance of P2 and

  `sxml_atomic_item_compare` now orders QNames by namespace URI, then local

  SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT. The internal `sxml_atomic_item_compare_in_heap`

### D69. No-inherit for the top element of a copy (P6)

**Summary**: `sxml_element_start_event` gains `ignores_parent_namespaces`,
which `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node` sets on a copy's top element for
copy-namespaces no-inherit, so that element starts from the xml binding alone.

Recorded 2026-10-16 by packet 1.14, on the orchestrator's acceptance of P6
(design edit to `include/sxml/tree.h`). `sxml_element_start_event` gains `bool
ignores_parent_namespaces`: true makes the element start from the xml binding
alone (plus its own bindings and fixup), not from its parent's in-scope
namespaces. Named so that zero, the default of every existing designated
initializer, keeps inheriting (P6 had proposed `inherits_namespaces` defaulting
to true, which zero cannot express). `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node` sets it on
the copy's top element when `inherits_namespaces` is false (XQuery 4.0
copy-namespaces no-inherit); descendants inherit from the top element as usual.
The arena tree honours it when it computes the header element's inherited list.

### D70. Node items, accessors and JNodes (packet 1.13)

**Summary**: Node items are inline and retain their tree; string value, typed
value and base URI follow the listed rules; a JNode cell holds parent, key,
value and child position, compared by position paths.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xdm_node.c`, `src/xdm_json_node.c`.

- **Node items** are inline (D60 layout) and retain their tree.
- **String value** of a document or element walks the index range up to
  `last_descendant` (D39) for text nodes; one text node is passed as is, more
  are joined in heap scratch memory released before returning.
- **Typed value**: derived (xs:untypedAtomic for documents, text, elements,
  attributes; xs:string for comments, PIs, namespace nodes) when the annotation
  is none, xs:untyped or xs:untypedAtomic, or the tree has no
  `get_typed_value`; otherwise the tree answers.
- **Base URI**: the xml:base values of the element and its ancestors, up to the
  first absolute one, resolved outermost-in against the tree's base URI (RFC
  3986, section 5.2.2, strict; checked on all 42 examples of section 5.4). A
  relative value with no base is kept as written. No base URI for namespace
  nodes and for parentless attributes, text and comments; a parentless PI has
  the tree's. xml:base values are not percent-encoded first (XML Base, section
  3.1).
- **JNodes**: one cell holds parent (retained), key, value, child position,
  child count (computed at make), depth and JTree identifier (issued last, so a
  failed root uses none). Under a map: one child per entry; an array: per
  member; two or more items: per item, keyed by position from 1; anything else
  is a leaf. Identity and order compare the paths of child positions from the
  root in O(depth) without memory: equal positions under one parent select the
  same key, so this is XDM's "same parent and atomic-equal key". The generic
  node functions live in `src/xdm_json_node.c`.

### D71. No C recursion

**Summary**: Project code never recurses, directly, across files or through
function pointers; every walk over nested structure is a loop over an explicit
stack in allocator memory, checked by clang-tidy and
`tools/check-call-cycles.py`.

Recorded 2026-10-16 at the owner's request ("make sure we don't use C
recursion"). Project code never recurses: not directly, not through a chain of
functions, not through function pointers or operations tables. Every walk over
nested structure (CST, AST, IR, types, regex patterns, maps, arrays, trees,
JNodes, sequences) is a loop over an explicit stack or work list in allocator
memory, bounded by a configured limit that reports `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (or the
specification's error). Consequences:

- clang-tidy `misc-no-recursion` is on (`.clang-tidy`); it sees recursion
  within one file. Review checks recursion across files and through pointers.
- The evaluator is an explicit-stack machine. Calling a function item from a
  native function (for example `fn:for-each`, `fn:sort` with a key,
  `fn:fold-left`) must not re-enter the evaluator on the C stack: native
  higher-order functions are written as resumable steps that ask the evaluator
  to make the call and resume them with the result. The same holds for lazy
  sequence generators that evaluate IR. Packets 1.18 and 1.21 follow this.
- Limits such as `maximum_expression_depth` bound heap use, not C stack, so
  their defaults no longer depend on the WebAssembly stack size (this replaces
  the 32-level lowering depth of D63).
- Existing recursive code is rewritten: `xpath_lower.c`, `xpath_static.c`,
  `ir.c`, `types.c`, `cast.c`, `regex.c`, `xdm_map.c`, `xdm_array.c`,
  `xdm_atomic.c` and two tests.
- Vendored third-party code (tree-sitter, libmpdec) is exempt; the generated
  grammar scanners are ours and have no recursion.
- `tools/check-call-cycles.py` (run by `tools/lint.sh`) links all of src/ and
  apps/ into one LLVM module and fails on any call-graph cycle, so recursion
  across files is caught too (not through function pointers).
  `tools/call-cycles-allowlist.txt` lists the cycles still being rewritten; it
  is temporary: each rewrite deletes its lines (a stale entry fails the check)
  until the file is empty and the allowlist is removed.
- Lowering (`src/xpath_lower.c`), type resolution (`src/xpath_static.c`) and
  the type text of `src/ir.c` are rewritten: lowering is a machine of frames
  allocated one by one (a procedure, a step, locals; results written into the
  frame below), type resolution and type text use stacks of at most 64 frames
  (`SXML_XPATH_MAXIMUM_TYPE_DEPTH`, the text's depth limit). Free-variable
  analysis skips AST subtrees without variable references, so nested inline
  functions cost linear time. 100,000 levels of parentheses, calls, inline
  functions and predicates compile, also on wasm. `misc-no-recursion` is on and
  the call-cycle allowlist is empty.

**Sources**: 100,000 levels of parentheses, calls, inline functions and
predicates compile, natively and on wasm; configured:
SXML_XPATH_MAXIMUM_TYPE_DEPTH, 64 frames (from `src/xpath_static_internal.h`).

### D72. Arithmetic and comparison operators (packet 1.19)

**Summary**: Arithmetic and comparison operators have their own enums, take
atomized operands, use int64 fast paths with libmpdec beyond, and follow the
listed rules for durations, dates and value, general and node comparisons.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/operator_internal.h`; `src/operator.c` (operands,
promotion, numbers, unary), `src/operator_temporal.c` (durations, dates,
times), `src/operator_compare.c` (value, general and GNode comparisons).

- **Interface**: own enums (`sxml_arithmetic_operator`,
  `sxml_comparison_operator`, `sxml_node_comparison_operator`), not the IR's,
  so the function library and later front ends share them; operands are
  atomized sequences (atomizing is the evaluator's), results owned; the
  implicit timezone and, for untyped-to-QName casts, namespace bindings travel
  in the request. Non-atomic items are INVALID_ARGUMENT.
- **Numbers**: int64 fast paths with checked arithmetic, else libmpdec; integer
  div gives xs:decimal; xs:float computed in double and rounded once; idiv and
  mod of doubles are exact (int64 within 2^53, else exact decimals; no libm).
  Decimal LIMIT_EXCEEDED (digit or heap byte limit) is FOAR0002.
- **Durations** (PR2628): any xs:duration times/div a number cast to xs:decimal
  (shortest digits, D57); months by fn:round#1, nanoseconds half to even; NaN
  FOCA0005, times INF or div 0 FODT0002, div INF zero. **Dates**: 400-year
  cycle days (Hinnant), so every int64 year works; results beyond it FODT0001,
  differences beyond int64 seconds FODT0002.
- **Comparisons**: value = NaN rule + fn:compare (`sxml_atomic_item_compare`
  with the heap's name pool, D68); general: untyped vs number cast to the
  number's primitive type, else xs:double; vs string or untyped compared as
  text; else cast to the other primitive type; left outer, first error ends.
  GNode: document order (equal only for the same node).
- **Known problem (fixed by D74)**: libmpdec's large-number multiplication
  (`six_step_fnt`/`transpose_pow2`, stack buffers of up to 128 KiB) overflowed
  the 64 KiB WebAssembly stack: 10^6000 \* 10^6000 trapped under `wasm`. D74
  moves the buffers to the heap; the operator tests may now multiply at the
  digit limit.

### D73. JNode making may fail with a lazy value's error (P7)

**Summary**: The contracts of `sxml_json_node_make_root` and
`sxml_json_node_make_child` list a lazy value's generator failures, returned
without an error record, since both count their value's items.

Recorded 2026-10-16 by packet 1.18, on the orchestrator's acceptance of P7
(option "amend contract"; design edit to `include/sxml/xdm.h`, comments only).
`sxml_json_node_make_root` and `sxml_json_node_make_child` count their value's
items, so a lazy value's generator may fail inside them; both contracts now
list those failures. They take no error record, so the status comes without
one: callers that need the error read the value first. The evaluator never
makes lazy sequences whose generator evaluates IR (D75), and it reads values
completely before fn:jtree sees them.

### D74. libmpdec keeps no large buffers on the stack

**Summary**: A patch to libmpdec's `transpose.c` moves its large transform
buffers to one heap block from `mpd_alloc`, so large products no longer trap
the 64 KiB WebAssembly stack and report OUT_OF_MEMORY instead.

Recorded 2026-10-16, amending D57. Upstream `transpose.c` holds two
`SIDE*SIDE`-word buffers in `squaretrans_pow2` (128 KiB with 32-bit words) and
two `BUFSIZE`-word buffers in `swap_halfrows_pow2` (32 KiB). Every product of
more than 1024 words (on WebAssembly 9216 digits, smaller operand above 2304)
whose transform is not a power of two up to 4096 words takes the four- or
six-step path through them and trapped on the 64 KiB WebAssembly stack; an
untrusted query could do it within the default digit limit.

- **Patch** ("sxml patch (D74)" in `transpose.c`): both pairs are one heap
  block from `mpd_alloc` (the current decimal scope, D42), sized for the actual
  block; `squaretrans_pow2` now returns 0 on failure and `transpose_pow2`
  passes it on, so the product reports `MPD_Malloc_error` (OUT_OF_MEMORY) and
  leaks nothing.
- **Audit** (`-fstack-usage`, wasm32 at `-Os`): after the patch the largest
  libmpdec frame is 1248 bytes (`mpd_qpowmod`; 2.5 KiB on x86-64 GCC); the
  `MPD_MINALLOC_MAX` (64-word) buffers in `mpdecimal.c`, `basearith.c` and
  `io.c` and the 3-word arrays in `fourstep.c`, `sixstep.c`, `crt.c`,
  `numbertheory.c` stay. Measured by painting the stack under wasm: multiply
  needs 785 bytes, divide and integer divide at most 2.9 KiB, flat from 5000 to
  16,000,000 digits.
- **Recursion** (D71 exempts libmpdec): only `_kmul_worksize`, `_karatsuba_rec`
  (operands of at most 1024 words: depth 7) and `_karatsuba_rec_fnt` recurse.
  The last runs only for products above 3 \* 2^25 words on 32-bit targets, more
  than two `MPD_MAX_PREC` (425 million digit) operands have, and above 3 \*
  2^32 words on 64-bit ones, depth log2 of the size ratio with frames under 100
  bytes. Newton division and the integer power sxml uses are loops. So no
  recursion patch and no lower cap on `maximum_digit_count` are needed.
- **Tests** (`tests/decimal_test.c`): squares and quotients at 10,000 digits
  (four-step on wasm), 10^6000 \* 10^6000 and two 10,000-digit operands refused
  with LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 60,000 digits (the plain six-step path on wasm), and
  every allocation failure of a long product reported and clean.

**Sources**: libmpdec frame sizes after the patch, wasm32 at -Os and x86-64 GCC
(`-fstack-usage`); stack painted under wasm: multiply, divide and integer
divide from 5000 to 16,000,000 digits (wasm build); test operands: 10,000, 6000
and 60,000 digits (`ctest`, from `tests/decimal_test.c`).

### D75. The evaluator: an explicit-stack machine (packet 1.18)

**Summary**: The evaluator runs every nested expression, call and native step
as a task on a stack in allocator memory, with tail calls, a depth limit,
resumable native bodies, coercion and type matching without C recursion.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/evaluator.c` (dynamic context, machine, expressions),
`src/evaluator_function.c` (atomization, effective boolean value, type
matching, coercion, function items and bodies), `src/evaluator_path.c` (steps
over XNodes and JNodes, document order, node sets, merge sort). Internal
headers changed as D71 requires.

- **Machine** (D71): every expression with a nested expression, every call and
  every native step is an `evaluator_task` on a task stack in allocator memory;
  one loop runs the top task; a finished task hands its value to the task
  below. LET bodies, CONDITIONAL branches and calls in tail position replace
  their task; a tail call reuses the caller's frame (100k-deep non-tail
  recursion and 200k tail calls with depth limit 10 are tested, also on wasm).
  Leaf work (operators, casts, axes, atomization, matching) is plain C over
  explicit stacks of its own.
- **Depth** = calls in progress (IR calls and resumable native calls);
  `maximum_evaluation_depth` 0 means 10^6 (heap, not C stack, per level);
  beyond it LIMIT_EXCEEDED. `maximum_frame_slot_count` bounds slots.
- **Reentry**: `sxml_evaluator_evaluate`, `sxml_evaluator_call_function_item`
  and the call operations of IR, coerced and resumable native bodies run the
  machine only on an idle dynamic context (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise). Inside
  a run the machine recognizes those bodies by their operations pointer and
  calls them through tasks; maps, arrays, constructor functions and host bodies
  are leaves.
- **Resumable native bodies** (`function_library_internal.h`): a row with
  `CALLS_FUNCTION_ITEMS` has a `resumable_body` (step function, state size,
  `release_state`) instead of `call`. Each `native_step` finishes with a value
  or asks for one call of a function item; the evaluator coerces the arguments,
  makes the call on its stack and runs the next step with the result (owned).
  State is evaluator memory, zeroed, released exactly once. 1.21 writes
  fn:for-each, filter, fold-\*, sort with keys, apply, partial-apply's bodies,
  map:/array:for-each this way; `sxml_native_function_body_operations` is now
  defined in `src/evaluator_function.c`, because the evaluator dispatches on
  it.
- **Lazy sequences**: the evaluator makes none whose generator evaluates IR;
  MAP, FILTER, paths and calls build complete values (Phase 1).
- **Coercion** (XPath 4.0, 3.4): atomization, untypedAtomic cast (XPTY0117 for
  QName/NOTATION), numeric and URI promotion, relabelling to a derived type of
  the same primitive only when the cast keeps the value (3 to
  xs:positiveInteger yes, 4.2 to xs:integer no), function coercion by a
  coerced-function body (lower arity allowed, extra arguments dropped), then a
  full type match. Type matching handles occurrences, atomic, union,
  enumeration, node, JNode (key and value), function, map, array, record and
  choice types on an explicit stack with backtracking for choices.
- **Paths**: STEP from a JNode reads element tests as key tests and runs every
  axis over the JTree; several origins are put in document order;
  DOCUMENT_ORDER keeps sorted input as it is. Constant numeric predicates index
  directly.
- **Errors** get the source span of the failing expression when the record has
  no location. The implicit timezone is read from the clock only when an
  operand is a date, time or duration (null clock: UTC).
- **Not yet**: TRY_CATCH, constructors, APPLY_TEMPLATES and global initializers
  return UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE; static namespaces are not available to casts to
  xs:QName at run time (predeclared prefixes only).

**Summary**: A namespace node test accepts a name: `namespace::x` resolves like
an unprefixed attribute name and matches the namespace node whose prefix is x;
a prefixed name matches nothing.

Recorded 2026-10-16 by packet 1.18, on the orchestrator's acceptance of P4
(design edit to the comment of `sxml_node_test` in `include/sxml/types.h`). The
registry's normal form accepts any name test for `SXML_NODE_KIND_NAMESPACE` (no

### D78. Function library: core (packet 1.20)

**Summary**: The core function library indexes the parts its configuration
names, sorted by interned name, assigns fn:sort and other rows to packet 1.20's
files, and follows the listed 4.0 semantics and unsupported options.

Recorded 2026-10-16; written first so packet 1.21 can rely on it.

- **Assembly**: `src/function_library.c` indexes whatever parts its
  configuration names (D55); no file lists another file's rows, and no shared
  list exists to edit. 1.21 only defines `sxml_function_library_higher_order`,
  `_map` and `_array` in its own files; the processor (1.23) names every part,
  unit tests name the parts they test (plus a test-only part of their own if
  they need one). `sxml_function_table_find` is defined in
  `src/function_library.c`.
- **fn:sort** (every arity, with or without `$key`) is one resumable row in
  `src/function_library_sequence.c` (1.20); 1.21 writes `array:sort` only.
  fn:position and fn:last are rows of `src/function_library_context.c`.
- **Files** (all under the module prefix): the six part files of D55, plus
  `src/function_library_deep_equal.c` (fn:deep-equal, a row of the sequence
  part), `src/function_library_case.c` (Unicode 16.0 full case mappings without
  conditions, generated by `tools/generate-case-tables.py` from UnicodeData.txt
  and SpecialCasing.txt) and `src/function_library_core_internal.h` (row
  macros, argument readers, heap text builder, collation check, position spans;
  defined in `src/function_library.c`). `function_library_internal.h` is
  unchanged.
- **Library**: indexed rows sorted by interned name (binary search); types
  resolved on first find and kept; variadic rows get repeated-type arrays kept
  in a chain so entry views stay valid; signatures registered per find. xs:
  constructors for atomic, union and list types (not anyAtomicType, NOTATION).
- **4.0 semantics followed** (from the QT4 tests): fn:max/min return the item
  itself, unpromoted, ordered by fn:compare (durations and QNames too), the
  first NaN wins when reached first; fn:subsequence and fn:substring take
  xs:numeric and add integers exactly (FOAR0002 past int64_t, PR2543); rounding
  of doubles uses the exact binary value; codepoints-to-string accepts XML 1.1
  characters; string-length and normalize-space accept any item; fn:index-of

  replacement, coerced by the body with `sxml_evaluator_coerce` because the
  evaluator does not apply function coercion inside a choice type, so the
  parameter is `item()?`).
- **Not supported yet**: collations other than codepoint (FOCH0002); deep-equal

  false; fn:trace does not print; the random-number-generator map is not

### D80. Higher-order, map and array functions (packet 1.21)

**Summary**: Three resumable engines (traversal, folds, sorts) serve the
higher-order, map and array functions; partial application and fn:op make
function items over hidden rows, and `$f(?)` lowers to fn:partial-apply.

Recorded 2026-10-16, completing D79.

- **Engines**: `src/function_library_higher_order_internal.h` declares three
  resumable engines defined in the higher-order part and used by all three
  parts: a traversal (one call per item, member or entry, with its position;
  for-each, filter, index-where, take-/drop-while, every, some, for-each-pair,
  array:build/for-each/filter/index-where/for-each-pair, map:for-each/filter),
  folds (fold-left/right, scan, array folds) and sorts (sort-by, sort-with,
  highest, lowest, array:sort/-by/-with). Keys are computed one call each, then
  sorted by `sxml_evaluator_sort_indices`; sort-with runs a bottom-up merge
  sort one comparator call per step. No engine calls a function item (D71).
- **Hidden rows**: partially applied functions and fn:op's functions are
  function items whose body is a row no part lists (native operations, D75):
  captured values hold the wrapped function, the bound positions and values, or
  the operator's code.
- **Types the front end lacks**: the `$keys` of sort-by are `map(*)*` (the
  grammar has no optional or extensible record fields); the engine checks
  `key`, `collation` and `order` and atomizes key values itself.
  fn:partial-apply takes `map(xs:integer, item()*)` because map coercion does
  not relabel keys (an xs:integer key is not an xs:positiveInteger); a position
  below 1 is XPTY0004.
- **Placeholders**: lowering turns `$f(?)` into fn:partial-apply with the empty
  map, so the empty map returns `$function` unchanged only for an anonymous
  function item; a map, an array or a named function is wrapped, so `$m(?)` is
  not a map (hof-920) and has no name (XPath 4.0, 4.5.2.5).
- **fn:function-lookup** uses the dynamic context's function table; a row that
  needs the focus at that arity raises XPDY0002 at lookup (F&O 4.0 allows
  raising early), IR functions (XQuery) are UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.
- **Not yet**: array:index-of (needs 1.20's deep-equal); a dynamic call on a
  sequence of functions (DynamicFunctionCall-146) is the evaluator's.

### D81. The XML parser (packet 1.14)

**Summary**: The XML parser detects and transcodes encodings, walks the
internal subset and content over explicit stacks of entity frames, bounds depth
and entity expansion, and passes the whole W3C XML suite selection.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/xml.c` (walk and checks), `src/xml_encoding.c`
(encodings, character classes, positions), `src/xml_entity.c` (buffers, DTD
tables with hash indices).

- **Decoding**: Appendix F detection; UTF-8 and US-ASCII are parsed in place,
  UTF-16 and ISO-8859-1 are transcoded to a UTF-8 copy kept by the parser.
  UCS-4, EBCDIC and other names are UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE; an 8-bit document
  declaring UTF-16, a UTF-8 mark with another declared name, or BOM-less UTF-16
  not declared UTF-16LE/BE is MALFORMED (4.3.3). U+0000 is refused before
  parsing (tree-sitter would read it as the end). Diagnostics give line, column
  (codepoints) and the input byte offset.
- **Walks** without C recursion (D71): the internal subset, then the document's
  children, each over a stack of entity frames (cursor + tree) in allocator
  memory. A general entity in content is reparsed as `<x>TEXT</x>` (4.3.2); its
  tree is cached per entity for the parse; replacement text without `<` or `&`
  is sent as text without a parse. An internal parameter entity between
  declarations is included by parsing `<!DOCTYPE d [TEXT]><d/>` (2.8);
  conditional sections in it are not supported (the grammar has none). Entities
  in attribute values are expanded with an explicit stack (4.4.5). Element
  nesting is bounded by `maximum_depth`, expansion by
  `maximum_entity_expansion_byte_count` (every replacement text counted,
  parameter entities included).
- **Choices**: line ends are normalized as text is emitted (pieces split at CR,
  the builder joins them), not in a copy; replacement text is not normalized
  again. Predefined entity names are always predefined (declarations of them
  are ignored). External parsed entities are skipped in content (4.4.3);
  undeclared ones are skipped when WFC Entity Declared does not apply. xml:id
  is an ID and collapsed; DTD types ID, IDREF(S) give is_id/is_idrefs. Element
  types and attribute names in DTD declarations must be QNames too. version 1.1
  documents are parsed by the 1.0 rules, except that `xmlns:p=""` undeclares p
  (Namespaces 1.1, section 5). Unparsed entity system identifiers are passed as
  written, not resolved against the base URI.
- **Measured**: W3C suite (Fifth Edition selection of D28) valid 601/601,
  invalid 175/175, not-wf 948/948 through the library
  (`tests/xml_conformance_test.c`, which reads `third_party/xmlconf` from the
  source tree and passes with a "skipped" line where it cannot, as under WASI).
  Of the 9 NAMESPACE="no" valid/invalid tests, 8 are refused as not
  namespace-well-formed and counted as passing. QT4 suite: 1046 of 1051 `*.xml`
  files parse; the 5 refused are not well-formed on purpose (bad bytes, U+00BC
  in names, unknown encoding "foo", `invalid-xml.xml`). XSLT 4.0 suite, the
  2541 files under 5 MB: 18 refused, 17 not well-formed on purpose and
  `xml-version-03.xml`, an XML 1.1 document with character references to
  control characters (1.0 rules apply).
- **CLI**: `sxml check` (docs/CLI.md); the framework gains
  `sxml_cli_file_reader` in the invocation, implemented over stdio in
  `apps/sxml/platform_stdio.c`; CLI golden tests run in `tests/cli/input/` so
  file names work under WASI too.

### D82. JSON texts are parsed with tree-sitter (packet 1.22)

**Summary**: JSON texts are parsed with the strict RFC 8259 tree-sitter grammar
`grammars/json` and one loop over a tree cursor, serving fn:parse-json,
json-to-xml, xml-to-json, jtree and parse-xml, plus adaptive output.

Recorded 2026-10-16. fn:parse-json and fn:json-to-xml parse with a tree-sitter
grammar, `grammars/json` (strict RFC 8259, original work), not with a
hand-written parser; D12 applies without exception. Weighed against D53's
reasons for regexes: (1) JSON is run-time data and tree-sitter allocates with
malloc outside sxml's allocators and limits, but fn:parse-xml already parses
run-time data this way (D81), so that alone is no exception; (2) unlike a
regex, JSON is context-free with context-free tokens: no flags change the
lexing, no back-references, so the grammar is complete and the walk adds only
what a grammar cannot say (surrogate pairing, permitted characters, duplicates,
numbers); (3) FOJS0001 is one code, and the walk reports the line and column of
the first ERROR or MISSING node in the description. The cost: the concrete
syntax tree is held while the walk builds values (several times the text in
memory), and U+0000 is refused before parsing (tree-sitter would read it as the
end; RFC 8259 forbids it unescaped). The walk is one loop over a tree cursor
(D71) that sends JSON events to a sink: one sink makes maps, arrays and atomic
items on explicit stacks, the other sends tree builder events.
`src/json_internal.h` is the interface.

- **Functions** (`src/function_library_json.c`, part
  `sxml_function_library_json`): fn:parse-json, json-to-xml, xml-to-json,
  jtree, parse-xml. Options follow F&O 4.0, 1.7: unknown string keys XPTY0004,
  QName keys with a namespace ignored, values coerced
  (`sxml_evaluator_coerce`), bad values FOJS0005; `liberal` accepts nothing
  beyond RFC 8259. Characters an escape gives that xs:string cannot hold
  (U+0000, unpaired surrogates, U+FFFE/FFFF) become U+FFFD; a `fallback`
  function is UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE for now (it needs a resumable body).
  json-to-xml: untyped tree in heap memory that destroys itself, default
  namespace on the outer element, `validate=true` FOJS0004. xml-to-json:
  FOJS0006 checks without a schema, duplicate normalized keys through a hash
  index, `indent` adds nothing. parse-xml: through the document loader (D55);
  xs:string as UTF-8, binary values as their octets (the string's encoding
  declaration is not ignored yet); dtd-validation, xinclude, strip-space="all"
  FODC0013, xsd-validation other than skip FODC0009.
- **Adaptive output** (`src/serialize.c`): frames on a heap stack (D71);
  strings in double quotes with quotes doubled, also at the top level;
  xs:double as mantissa and exponent (`1.0e0`), other non-string, non-decimal
  types and non-finite doubles as `xs:TYPE("value")`; QNames `#prefix:local`
  (array fn map math xs) or `#Q{uri}local`; anonymous functions
  `(anonymous-function)#N`; nodes by the XML method without a declaration, each
  element declaring the in-scope namespaces its written parent lacks; JNodes
  `jtree(V)` / `jnode(K:V)`.
- Root `CMakeLists.txt` links `sxml_grammar_json` (one line, 1.0's file).

### D83. The QT4 driver: catalog and environments (packet 1.24)

**Summary**: The QT4 driver `sxml-qt4` reads the catalog and test sets through
the public API into arena trees, resolves environments, decides applicability
by dependency tables, and lists test cases.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `tests/qt4/driver/`, the developer tool `sxml-qt4` on the
CLI framework (D44), public API only.

- **Reading**: catalog.xml and test-set files go through
  `sxml_xml_parser_parse` into an arena tree (own name pool, type registry,
  item heap) and are walked with the public node accessors; only elements in
  the catalog namespace count. One catalog object (lifecycle quintet; `load`
  makes the parts, `initialize` allocates nothing) keeps catalog.xml and one
  open test set; a test case's views and arrays live until the next
  `open_test_set` (a per-test-set arena). File paths are suite paths: relative
  to catalog.xml's directory, dot segments removed (RFC 3986 5.2.4), so output
  is the same wherever the suite is and under WASI.
- **Environments**: `ref` looks in the test set first, then the catalog; an
  environment element without `ref` is inline even with a `name` (`<environment
  name="empty"/>`); no element means absent. All children of catalog-schema.xsd
  are read (sources, params with `as`, namespaces, context item, static base
  URI with `#UNDEFINED`, resources, collections, collations, decimal formats,
  schemas, function library, sandpit, modules).
- **Applicability** (first failing rule is the skip reason): spec as
  `tools/check-test-list.py` (case spec replaces set spec; every value needs a
  matching token); every other dependency of set and case must be satisfied as
  asked, satisfied meaning one of its tokens is in a table: feature
  higherOrderFunctions and namespace-axis, xml-version 1.0 and 1.0:5+,
  xsd-version 1.1, limits big_integer and year_lt_0, language and
  default-language en; then the environment: source validation, schema,
  resource, collection, non-codepoint collation, decimal format, function
  library, sandpit; then modules. The table grows with sxml.
- **CLI**: `sxml-qt4 list [--catalog=FILE] [--spec=XP40|XQ40] [--test-set=NAME]
  [TEST-LIST]` (default catalog `third_party/qt4tests/catalog.xml`; neither
  selection means the whole catalog; both is a usage error). Text blocks per
  test case, summary line; problems on stderr, exit 1/3/4 as `sxml check`.
  Packet 1.25 adds `run` with `assertion.c` and `report.c`; the library target
  globs the directory, so it needs no CMake edit for new modules.
- **Tests**: ctest `qt4_driver` (unit tests over in-memory files,
  allocation-failure loop) and `qt4/*` golden tests over a small suite in
  `tests/qt4/driver/input/` and the slice (`qt4/list_slice`: 198/198 resolve

### D85. Evaluator follow-ups: calls, paths, coercion, namespaces (packet 1.18b)

**Summary**: The evaluator gains dynamic calls on sequences of functions, maps
and arrays as path origins, coercion on an explicit stack of coercion frames,
omitted defaults before keyword arguments, and static namespaces for casts.

Recorded 2026-10-16. Gaps reported by 1.20 and 1.21; sections are those of the
XPath 4.0 editor's draft of 13 October 2026 (vendored with QT4).

- **Dynamic calls** (4.6.3.1): the target is coerced to `function(*)*` (a JNode
  gives its jvalue); one function is called as before (tail calls kept), none
  gives (), several go through `call_each`, a resumable body of the evaluator's
  own (not a library row) that calls each in turn and concatenates. A dynamic
  partial application (4.6.4) lowers to a MAP over the target whose body is
  fn:partial-apply on the focus (golden hof-920 of D63 changed).
- **Paths** (4.7.3, 4.7.5): maps and arrays on the left of `/` and `//` and as
  the origin of a step become JNode roots as if by fn:jtree. The error codes
  stay XPTY0019 and XPTY0020 (D76); the draft's XPTY0004 (PR 2627) and its
  selector interpretation of non-navigational steps are not done.
- **Coercion** (3.4.2) runs on an explicit stack of `coercion_frame`s: choices
  and unions take the first alternative an item matches, else try each in order
  and keep the first attempt's error; typed arrays, maps and records are
  coerced part by part (records built with sxml_record_make; surplus keys and
  keys equal after coercion are XPTY0004); a JNode that does not match is
  coerced through its jvalue; the whole implicit-casting table applies when the
  required type is the "to" type exactly (so no xs:anyURI to xs:NCName); an
  enumeration accepts an xs:anyURI by its string; function coercion wraps even
  an instance of the type, except an item whose signature is that type. A value
  that matches a type whose matching items never change is returned after one
  match; an integer range is matched in O(1) (xs:integer a subtype of the item
  type).
- **fn:replace**: `$replacement` has its F&O 4.0 type again, `(xs:string |
  fn(xs:untypedAtomic, map((xs:integer | xs:string), xs:untypedAtomic)) as
  item()?)?`; the function gets untyped values (integer group keys only: the
  regex seed has no named groups), coerced by the call; D78's coercion in the
  body is gone.
- **Lowering**: a parameter whose default the body supplies, left out before a
  keyword argument, gets () when its type allows it: every such default in F&O
  4.0 is () or default-on-empty (section 1.5), except `$timezone` of
  adjust-\*-to-timezone, a last parameter. Otherwise still UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.
- **Static namespaces**: a unit keeps the statically known namespaces beyond
  the predeclared ones (`sxml_ir_unit_set_static_namespaces`,
  `_get_static_namespaces`; collected by `sxml_xpath_collect_namespaces`: the
  expression's declarations, then the configuration's); CAST, CASTABLE and xs:
  constructor calls pass them to the cast. xs:QName#1 as a function item still
  sees the predeclared prefixes only.
- **array:index-of** calls fn:deep-equal's body once per member (a leaf).
- **number(xs:integer(...)) eq integer** is false by design: comparisons are
  decimal-exact since PR 2218 (QT4 fn-numberintg1args-2a); the cases that
  expect true depend on XP20 to XP31 only.

### D86. Fuzz targets (packet 1.26)

**Summary**: Five libFuzzer targets under `tests/fuzz/` check crashes, leaks,
invalid-argument returns, invariants and timeouts, built by the `fuzz` preset
and run by `tools/fuzz.sh` with seeds from `tools/fuzz-seeds.py`.

- **Targets.** Every `tests/fuzz/<name>_fuzz.c` is a libFuzzer executable
  (glob, D45) linked with `tests/fuzz/fuzz_fixture.c`: `xml_parse_fuzz` (parse
  into an arena tree and read every node back; `check` must give the same
  status), `xpath_compile_fuzz` (both front ends, then `sxml_xpath_compile`
  against the whole function library), `xpath_evaluate_fuzz` (compile and
  evaluate with a parsed context document and small limits; the internal
  evaluator until 1.23's processor), `regex_fuzz` (flags byte, regex, NUL,
  input; every disjoint match and its groups) and `cast_fuzz` (target byte,
  text; the canonical text of an atomic result must cast back to the same
  canonical text).
- **What a finding is.** A crash or sanitizer report; a leak (the counting
  allocator's blocks and the item heap's cells are checked after every input,
  on a fixture made fresh per input); an entry point returning
  `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY`, `MISALIGNED_MEMORY` or
  `INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE` for arguments the target made valid (an error in sxml:
  for compilation, the verifier or the function table); a broken invariant
  above; a timeout (10 s per input). Deep input is not bounded in the targets:
  it must cost heap, not C stack (D71).
- **Build.** Preset `fuzz`: Clang, `RelWithDebInfo`, ASan and UBSan, the
  library built with `-fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link`, no `apps/`. `ctest --preset
  fuzz` runs each target on 2000 generated inputs.
- **Running.** `tools/fuzz.sh --seconds N` runs every target at once for N
  seconds in a kept work directory; seeds come from `tools/fuzz-seeds.py`
  (xmlconf and QT4 documents, QT4 queries, the literal arguments of
  `fn:matches`-like calls and `xs:T("...")` constructors; at most 4000 per
  target), never committed (D13); the first run merges them into a corpus. The
  script fails on any artifact, except timeouts of `xpath_evaluate_fuzz`, which
  runs in fork mode and lists them for triage until the evaluator has a step
  limit (P9).
- **CI.** Running each target for 60 s in CI is a `ci.yml` change, owned by
  1.27: a Linux job `cmake --preset fuzz && cmake --build --preset fuzz &&
  tools/fuzz.sh --no-build --build-directory build/fuzz --seconds 60`.

### D87. XML positions move back in place (P8)

**Summary**: The XML position tracker walks back from where it is when asked
for an earlier offset, instead of restarting from byte 0, so position cost is
linear in the document.

Recorded 2026-10-16. The position tracker of `src/xml_encoding.c` no longer
restarts from byte 0 when asked for an earlier offset: it walks back from where
it is, undoing line, column and input offset, and when a line end lies between
it recounts the column from the start of that line; it restarts only when the
start is nearer. The parser keeps asking for an element's position after its
attributes' (and diagnostics may ask anywhere), so the fix is in the tracker,
not in the call order. Cost is now linear in the document. Measured (release):
`sxml-qt4 list tests/qt4/torture-slice.txt` 23.3 s before, 0.76 s after, same
output; a 9.6 MB document with multi-line start tags did not finish in 600 s
before, parses in 2.7 s after (about 70% of that is `ts_parser_parse`, so D12's
tree-sitter bounds parse speed at about 3.5 MB/s here). Tests:
`xml/positions_move_back` (every pair of offsets against a fresh walk),
`xml/large_documents_parse_in_linear_time` (10000 elements, 400 KB).

**Sources**: sxml-qt4 list of the torture slice, before and after (`sxml-qt4`,
release build, from `tests/qt4/torture-slice.txt`); 9.6 MB document with
multi-line start tags, before and after, and the share of ts_parser_parse
(release build); test sizes: 10000 elements, 400 KB (`ctest`).

### D88. The processor and the XPath API (packet 1.23)

**Summary**: The processor holds name pool, type registry, item heap and the
full function library in one block; each XPath evaluation allocates its own
dynamic context and document loader; `sxml xpath` is the CLI.

Recorded 2026-10-16. `src/processor.c`, `src/processor_internal.h`,
`src/xpath.c`, `src/function_library_uri.c`; tests `processor`, `xpath`.

- **Processor**: one block holds the processor, name pool, type registry, item
  heap and the function library over every part (numeric, string, sequence,
  node, context, error, higher_order, map, array, json, uri); member
  requirements are queried with stand-in pointers (they only check for NULL). A
  null clock means `sxml_system_clock` (C17 `timespec_get`, civil date by
  Hinnant's algorithm); `sxml_clock_read` checks the whole reading contract
  (components, leap years, offsets) and the evaluator now reads through it.
  Parsed documents: arena trees from the processor's allocator with its tree
  and XML limits, no locations, destroyed with their last reference.
- **Limits** (comments in `processor.h` fixed): both depths bound heap, not C
  stack (D71); 0 means 10,000 for `maximum_expression_depth` (D63) and
  1,000,000 for `maximum_evaluation_depth` (D75); new
  `maximum_evaluation_step_count` (D89).
- **Expressions**: compile is `sxml_xpath_compile` with the processor's
  function table; identifiers of the static context are checked against the
  pool and registry (INVALID_ARGUMENT), the static base URI must have a scheme
  and is copied. Each evaluation allocates its own dynamic context, global
  slots (bound by name to the unit's globals) and document loader, and frees
  them before returning, so evaluations nest (tested through a host function
  body).
- **Document loader** (per evaluation): `fn:doc` resolves its argument against
  the static base URI (`sxml_uri_resolve`, RFC 3986 5.2, now in
  `src/xdm_internal.h` over the resolver of `src/xdm_node.c`), then looks in
  the available documents, then the documents loaded so far, then asks the
  resolver; a resource that does not parse or a non-document node is FODC0002,
  the resolver's description goes into the error. fn:parse-xml makes a new tree
  per call (FODC0006).
- **Static base URI** reaches functions through the dynamic context
  (`sxml_evaluation_request.static_base_uri`,
  `sxml_dynamic_context_get_static_base_uri`): fn:doc, fn:parse-xml (when no
  `base-uri` option), fn:json-to-xml (document base URI), and the new rows
  fn:static-base-uri and fn:resolve-uri (FONS0005, FORG0002). A function item
  called after its evaluation sees the caller's.
- **CLI**: `sxml xpath` (docs/CLI.md): file resolver over the invocation's file
  reader (paths and `file://` only), `--param` as `xs:untypedAtomic` exactly
  one, `--method=adaptive` the only choice; errors as `expression:LINE:COLUMN:
  err:CODE: description`. 19 golden tests.
- `tests/fuzz/fuzz_fixture.c` names the json and uri parts too.

**Sources**: configured: defaults of maximum_expression_depth (10,000, D63) and
maximum_evaluation_depth (1,000,000, D75) (from `src/processor.c`).

### D89. A bound on evaluation steps (P9 accepted)

**Summary**: `maximum_evaluation_step_count` in `sxml_processor_limits` bounds
evaluation steps (0 means 10^9); the machine charges one step per task and leaf
work charges through `sxml_dynamic_context_charge_steps`.

Recorded 2026-10-16 (orchestrator accepted P9, with "0 means sxml's default").
`uint64_t maximum_evaluation_step_count` in `sxml_processor_limits`; 0 means
`SXML_EVALUATOR_DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EVALUATION_STEP_COUNT`, 10^9 steps (about a
minute of work, far beyond any QT4 test). `sxml_evaluator_configuration` has
the same field with 0 meaning no bound. The machine charges one step per task
run; `sxml_dynamic_context_charge_steps` lets leaf work charge what it reads: a
general comparison charges the product of its operand counts first (O(1) for
ranges), so `-1 = -100000000000 to -1` stops at once, even though an early
match would have ended it (the price of charging up front). The count restarts
with every evaluation; past the bound, LIMIT_EXCEEDED with the diagnostic
filled. Native bodies that loop over many items without tasks (fn:count,
fn:string-join, sorting, regex) do not charge yet; each can call the function
when needed. `xpath_evaluate_fuzz` sets 10^7 steps.

### D90. map:merge merges into its largest map (fuzzing follow-up of 1.26)

**Summary**: map:merge starts from its first largest map and puts earlier maps'
entries first through `sxml_map_put_first`, so folds that merge small maps into
an accumulator cost O(N log N), not O(N^2).

Recorded 2026-10-16. A fold that merges a small map into its accumulator was
O(n^2): map:merge inserted every entry of every map into a new map.

- map:merge starts from its first largest map L (`src/function_library_map.c`)
  instead of the empty map. With L first, it is taken as it is (no map has
  duplicate keys, so inserting it into the empty map meets none, under every
  policy). With L later, and without a duplicates function, the entries of the
  earlier maps are put first, last map and last entry first, through
  `sxml_map_put_first` (`src/xdm_map_internal.h`): an entry of an equal key is
  dropped and the earlier entry takes the front with its key and the combined
  value (use-first/any: the earlier value; use-last: the later; combine:
  earlier then later; reject: FOJS0003). These combinations are associative, so
  the result, entry order and kept key included, is the forward insertion's.
  The maps after L are inserted as before. A duplicates function keeps the
  forward order (its calls stay in F&O 4.0 order) but still takes the first map
  as is.
- Persistent maps (D61) number entries from 2^63: puts last count up from
  there, puts first down; `previous_entry_stamp` beside `next_entry_stamp`.
- Cost: O(m log n) for the m entries outside L, so `fold-left(1 to N, map{},
  fn($m, $i) { map:merge(($m, {$i: $i})) })` and its mirror `map:merge(({$i:
  $i}, $m))` (QT4 duplicates-maps-2) are O(N log N). `map_merge_scales` in
  `tests/function_library_higher_order_test.c`: folds of 10,000 steps, 3.6 s
  for the case under ASan (release: 320,000 merges in 1.8 s); the quadratic
  version took 6-18 s under ASan for 1,000. map:put in a fold was already O(log
  n) per step.

**Sources**: map_merge_scales folds of 10,000 steps under ASan, 320,000 merges
in release, and the quadratic version for 1,000 (`ctest`, from
`tests/function_library_higher_order_test.c`).

**Summary**: Packet 1.23b adds 62 library functions (math, QName and namespace,
node, string, URI, sequence, context), writes annotation types in adaptive
output, makes the static base URI lexical, and charges leaf steps.

Recorded 2026-10-17.

  namespace-uri-from-QName, expanded-QName, in-scope-prefixes,
  in-scope-namespaces, namespace-uri-for-prefix); node: doc-available (loads

- **Adaptive output** (`src/serialize.c`): the constructor-function form writes

### D92. The QT4 driver: running tests, assertions, reports (packet 1.25)

**Summary**: `sxml-qt4 run` gives each test case its own processor under a 512
MiB budget allocator, evaluates assertions as XPath over `$result`, and reports
pass, wrong-error, fail, error or not-run as text or JSON.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `sxml-qt4 run [--catalog] [--spec] [--test-set=NAME |
TEST-LIST] [--format=text|json]`; `tests/qt4/driver/test_run.c`, `assertion.c`,
`report.c`, `reason.c`, `command_run.c`.

- **Isolation**: each test case gets its own processor, made through a budget
  allocator (at most 512 MiB live; header-prefixed blocks) with
  `maximum_evaluation_step_count` 10^8; afterwards the budget must have no live
  allocation, else the outcome is error "leaked N allocations". A crash still
  ends the process: whole-suite runs use one process per test set. No
  `--output=FILE`: the CLI platform layer has no file writer (redirect standard
  output).
- **Environment**: sources parsed with document and base URI = their `uri`
  (made absolute against the test-set file) or `file:///SUITE-PATH`; "."
  context value, "$name" variables `item()*`, `uri` available documents; params
  via `select` with `as` from `sxml_xpath_parse_sequence_type`; QName param
  names through the environment's namespaces; static base URI
  `file:///SUITE-PATH` of the test-set file unless given or `#UNDEFINED`. The
  resolver serves `file:///` URIs as suite files and nothing else.
- **Assertions** are XPath over `$result` (and `$expected`, the assertion's
  value) with the environment's namespaces: assert-eq = one atomic item and
  `$result = $expected or deep-equal(...)` (untyped cast, NaN = NaN);
  permutation by per-item deep-equal counts; assert-type = `$result instance of
  TEXT`; assert-xml = result written as XML (nodes by the adaptive serializer,
  atomics as escaped text joined by spaces), both sides `parse-xml`ed in a
  wrapper element and deep-equal with comments and PIs (no full
  canonicalization; prefixes never matter); expected files lose their XML
  declaration and surrounding space. A wrong error code is the outcome
  "wrong-error" and counts as passed. Serialization assertions are
  "unsupported": the outcome is not-run, not fail (deviation from the task
  text). Verdicts combine worst-to-best fail < unsupported < wrong-error < pass
  on a fixed 32-frame stack (D71).
- **Outcomes**: pass, wrong-error, fail, error (a status without an error
  record, a limit, a leak, an environment that cannot be set up), not-run (not
  applicable or unsupported). Text lists every non-pass, non-not-run case, a
  line per test set and a final `total:` line; JSON (schema in `report.h`)
  lists every case. Exit 1 on a fail or error.
- **Slice gate**: ctest `qt4/slice` runs the slice and fails when fewer pass
  than `tests/qt4/slice-baseline.txt` (198); a higher count asks for the
  baseline to be raised. Goldens `qt4/run_*` over `input/run-catalog.xml` cover
  every assertion kind passing and failing.

### D96. Phases 2 to 4 overlap

**Summary**: Packets marked Early in the Phase 3 and 4 task files may start
once the Phase 1 gate has closed and their prerequisites are committed, while
gates stay sequential and file ownership rules hold.

Recorded 2026-10-17. To reach working XQuery and XSLT sooner (D11), packets
marked **Early** in `docs/tasks/phase-3.md` and `phase-4.md` may start once the
Phase 1 gate has closed (the substrate freeze) and the packets in their "After"
lists are committed, while earlier phases still run. All other packets of a
phase wait for the previous phase's gate.

- Ownership rules of D45 hold across phases: packets that run at the same time
  never own the same file; a file named by packets of two phases belongs to
  whichever runs first, and the other waits.
- Seams first: Phase 2 wave 0 makes library parts, evaluator parts for the
  reserved IR kinds and lowering parts register by glob (packets 2.0, 2.1), so
  XQuery and XSLT packets add files instead of editing the evaluator, the
  lowering machine or the processor's lists.
- Gates stay sequential: the Phase 3 review needs the Phase 2 gate, and a
  phase's review counts only its own targets. Early packets do not move their
  phase's gate forward.
- `CLAUDE.md` names the current phase; at each gate the review names the next
  phase file and the Early packets that may run with it.

### D97. Scope of Phases 2 to 4

**Summary**: Phases 2 to 4 support codepoint, HTML ASCII and UCA-fallback
collations, leave out HTML parsing, schema awareness, streaming, Update, Full
Text and EXPath, and scan regex, picture strings and CSV by hand.

Recorded 2026-10-17 (non-goals per PLAN.md, made concrete).

- **Collations**: the Unicode codepoint collation and the HTML ASCII
  case-insensitive collation (both required by F&O 4.0), and UCA collation URIs
  with fallback (on by default): codepoint order, with strength primary and
  secondary matching case-blind (QT4 simple-uca-fallback). Full UCA (DUCET
  tables, tailoring, numeric and case-order options; advanced-uca-fallback)
  stays out: the tables cost more `wasm` size than the 81 tests that need them
  are worth. fallback=no on a UCA URI is FOCH0002.
- **Out**: fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc (an HTML5 tree builder is its own
  project; 1,400 QT4 cases, excluded by D95), invisible XML, schema awareness
  (validate is XQST0075; XSLT validation="strict" and type attributes raise
  XTSE1660, as for a basic processor), streaming (streamable="yes" runs
  unstreamed, as a non-streaming processor may), the Update Facility (its tests
  are not run; %updating is rejected statically), Full Text, EXPath, XPath 1.0
  compatibility mode and XSLT backwards-compatible behaviour, civil-timezone
  and Olson names (no tz database), calendars other than AD and ISO and
  languages other than English in format-date and format-integer (the fallback
  markers F&O allows).
- **Later in this plan**: fn:serialize with every method (3.4),
  fn:load-xquery-module (3.11); fn:transform only if Phase 4 sweeps leave time.
- **Hand-written scanners**: regex syntax (D53), picture strings of the
  formatting functions and CSV are scanned by hand, because their lexical rules
  are run-time options (decimal formats, CSV delimiters) that a tree-sitter
  grammar cannot take. Everything else keeps D12, including XSLT value
  templates (`grammars/value_template`).

**Sources**: QT4 cases of fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc, and tests needing
advanced-uca-fallback (from `third_party/qt4tests/catalog.xml`).

### D98. Substrate review at the Phase 1 gate (packet 1.29)

**Summary**: The Phase 1 substrate review keeps all earlier records and adds a
base URI for parentless roots, stored parentless namespace nodes, and contract
comments on named item types and host re-entry.

Recorded 2026-10-17 by the Phase 1 review agent (D11). Before the freeze (D99)
every record that touched the substrate headers (D19-D43, D68, D69, D73, D77,
D89) was checked against the Phase 2-4 task files; "Proposed" was empty. All
earlier records stand. Found and changed:

- **Base URI of a parentless root** (`tree.h`): the arena tree had no way to
  give a constructed element, attribute, text, comment or PI a base URI; only
  `start_document` carried one, but XQuery 4.0 constructors (packet 3.5) need
  the static base URI and XSLT 4.0 the instruction's (section 11.1: it matters
  only for a parentless node, a child takes its parent's; XQuery copies behave
  the same, QT4 cbcl-base-uri-001 to -004). New field
  `sxml_arena_tree_configuration.base_uri`, copied by `finish`, reported as
  `sxml_tree_description.base_uri`; zero keeps the old behaviour.
- **Parentless namespace nodes** (`tree.h`, contract only): computed namespace
  constructors and xsl:namespace make namespace nodes without an element, which
  D39's (element, namespace number) cannot name. A tree may now hold one stored
  namespace node, its root (index 0, namespace number 0), built by an
  `add_namespace_binding` sent first; its name is the prefix, its content the
  URI (empty URI: XQDY0101). The arena tree and `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node`
  implement it (`src/arena_tree.c`, `src/tree.c`, test
  `parentless_namespace_nodes_are_stored`); the adaptive serializer and the
  evaluator's namespace paths still assume an element and are packets 3.3 and
  3.5's.
- **Named item types** (`types.h`, comment): `find_type` no longer claims to
  find them; XQuery `declare type` and xsl:item-type are aliases in a module's
  static context, never registered by name.
- **Host re-entry** (`xdm.h`, comment): a host function body, generator,
  resolver or builder that starts an evaluation nests it on the C stack;
  bounding that is the host's (D71 holds for sxml's own code).
- `status.h`, `string.h`: "D92" is Unicode's definition D92, not this file's.
  Deferred, each needing its own record when it comes: adopting heap buffers
  for strings (Phase 0 question 7, only if Phase 2 profiling asks), registering
  schema-derived atomic types (Phase 5), a frozen shareable tree (D35), a
  per-element base URI for XSLT literal result elements that come from
  different stylesheet modules and are copied as parentless nodes with relative
  xml:base (no QT4 or XSLT test seen needs it).

### D99. Substrate frozen

**Summary**: The substrate headers (`status.h`, `view.h`, `memory.h`,
`string.h`, `name.h`, `types.h`, `tree.h`, `xdm.h`) are frozen: any contract
change needs a decision record first, and only additions that keep old
behaviour are allowed.

Recorded 2026-10-17 at the Phase 1 gate (PLAN.md: "substrate frozen at the
Phase 1 gate"). Frozen: `include/sxml/status.h`, `view.h`, `memory.h`,
`string.h`, `name.h`, `types.h`, `tree.h`, `xdm.h` (with `export.h`), as of the
commit that records this, including D98. Not frozen: `xml.h`, `processor.h`,
`xpath.h`, `serialize.h`, `version.h` (D47: they change through their design
packets, and after packet 2.2 only with a record, until release 0.2.0 makes
them stable). Rule for a frozen header:

- Any change, a comment that changes a contract included, needs a new decision
  record first that names the header, the change and the packet that needs it;
  implementation packets still write the need under "Proposed" and stop
  (CLAUDE.md).
- Allowed with a record: new functions, new types, new enumeration constants at
  the end of an enumeration whose header says it only grows (built-in types,
  well-known namespaces, statuses), and new fields at the end of configuration
  and request structs whose zero value keeps the old behaviour. Not allowed
  without reopening this record: changing or removing a declaration, the
  meaning of an existing field or status, the 16-byte item and sequence layout
  (D34), node numbering (D39), or an operations table (interfaces are not
  extended in place: a new table type instead).
- Comments that only fix wording or a citation need no record.
- ABI: nothing is ABI-stable before release 0.2.0 (packet 2.18); the freeze is
  about the design, so fields are still added at the end only.

### D100. Phase 1 gate review (packet 1.29)

**Summary**: The Phase 1 gate review found the rubric met, followed every
indirect call for recursion, and ran all gate checks locally because GitHub
Actions is refused; the CI boxes stay open.

Recorded 2026-10-17 by the review agent (D11), who did not write Phase 1.

- **Rubric** over `include/sxml/` (all headers read), the evaluator, lowering,
  XDM, tree, XML parser and processor (sampled), the rest spot checked: names
  and glossary, at most three parameters (also every function-pointer type),
  lifecycle quintets (public and internal types complete), ownership, units,
  failure and thread safety in public headers, error codes (61 distinct, all
  well formed), spec citations. No writable file-scope data in `libsxml`, the

  are vendored, D42); no `malloc`/`free` outside `src/allocator.c`; no

- **D71 through pointers**: every indirect call in `src/` was followed. Cell

  (a flat loop frees); concatenations are flattened, so a part is never a
  concatenation; the evaluator runs IR, native-row and coerced bodies as tasks
  and calls only map, array, constructor and host bodies directly;
  `sxml_evaluator_call_function_item` refuses a running context; arena-tree and
  tree-builder operations never call back into `tree.c`; tree owners only
  destroy; generators, resolvers and output streams are the host's.
  `tools/check-call-cycles.py` now also links the QT4 driver (with the CLI
  framework) as a second program: 85 files, no cycle.
- **CI cannot run**: every GitHub Actions job since 2026-10-16 is refused
  ("recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be
  increased"); the last green run is 38931572793 (Phase 0 gate). All gate

  22): presets `debug`, `debug-gcc`, `release`, `wasm`, `fuzz`, lint, slice,
