  gate stay open until the owner restores billing and a run is green.

### D101. Part registries and the evaluator seams (packet 2.0)

**Summary**: CMake registers function library parts and evaluator parts by glob
over their source files, a part serves the languages it names, and the
evaluator machine API lets parts push tasks and catch errors.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D45 and D55 for Phases 2 to 4.

- **Library parts by glob.** `cmake/SxmlParts.cmake` reads every
  `src/function_library_*.c` and generates `function_library_parts.c` in the
  build tree from each definition `const sxml_native_function_view
  sxml_function_library_<part> =`; files without one (case tables, deep
  equality, `function_library.c`) are not parts. A part serves every language
  unless it also defines `const sxml_language_set
  sxml_function_library_<part>_languages = SXML_LANGUAGE_XSLT;` (any of
  `SXML_LANGUAGE_XPATH`, `_XQUERY`, `_XSLT` joined by `|`): CMake reads the
  names, the generated table also points at the variable, and a unit test
  checks the two agree. `src/function_library_parts_internal.h` declares
  `sxml_function_library_registered_parts()` (every part, sorted by name) and
  `sxml_function_library_parts_for_language()` (a static list per language).
  The processor and the fuzz fixture take the XPath list; XQuery and XSLT
  compilation take theirs (3.x, 4.x). A new part declares its own `extern` view
  (or none: the generated unit declares it); `function_library_internal.h`
  keeps the Phase 1 declarations.
- **Evaluator parts by glob.** The same module reads `src/evaluator_*.c` for
  `const sxml_evaluator_part sxml_evaluator_part_<part> =`: a table of IR
  expression kinds and step functions. The machine runs its built-in kinds
  itself and every other kind through the registry; a kind no part claims, or
  two parts claim, is SXML_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE (a unit test checks each
  reserved kind has exactly one). Parts `construct` (seven constructors,
  SHALLOW_COPY), `try` (TRY_CATCH), `template` (APPLY_TEMPLATES) and `global`
  (no kind; `sxml_evaluator_start_global_initializers`, called before the main
  function's body runs for globals with an initializer and no value) return
  UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE until 3.5, 3.6, 4.x and 3.10 fill them. A given value of
  a global with an initializer wins (an external variable's default). 3.10's
  reads on demand need the reading task to wait for the initializer; if the
  global part cannot do it with tasks pushed at the start (in dependency
  order), 3.10 proposes a machine change.
- **A part is live when its file is**: a committed part file joins every build,
  the processor and the fuzz fixture at once, so its rows must not repeat a
  name and arity another part serves (the library then refuses to start,
  INVALID_ARGUMENT); a packet moving rows moves them in one commit.
- **Machine API** in `src/evaluator_machine_internal.h` (defined in
  `src/evaluator.c`): the task type, top task, push an expression task in the
  top task's frame, push a part task (a step function and owned state with its
  release function), hand a value down (finish), take the value of the task
  above, read and bind atoms, raise (report into the error record), and
  catching: a task whose `catches_errors` is set receives a dynamic or type
  error raised above it. The run loop locates the error, unwinds every task
  above the innermost catching task above its base, stores the status in the
  context (`caught_status`) and steps that task again; limits, memory and
  invalid-argument statuses are never caught. No C recursion: step functions
  return to the one loop (D71).
- Rejected: a hand-kept part list (every new part edits the processor, the fuzz
  fixture and tests: D45's conflict); per-language libraries chosen at run time
  from flags in the view (needs a change of the frozen row header and filtering
  memory).

### D102. The stylesheet AST (packet 4.2)

**Summary**: One stylesheet AST holds modules, one node kind per XSLT 4.0
element, attributes read into typed forms, and a resolved static context per
element, built by the reader of packet 4.5.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `src/xslt_ast_internal.h`, internal, after D52 and the IR
unit (D55).

- **One AST per stylesheet** (a used package is another): modules, nodes,
  attributes, expressions, static contexts, a declaration list, name tokens,
  namespace bindings and URIs, text; index-addressed arrays with entry 0 "none"
  that grow through an allocator while the reader builds and are sealed before
  lowering (as `sxml_ir_unit`). Module URIs get their own allocations, so the
  per-expression `sxml_ast` borrows them as source name. The AST owns those
  ASTs and a reference to each module's document node.
- **Nodes**: one kind per XSLT 4.0 element in the 4.0 schema
  (schema-for-xslt40.xsd; xsl:transform is STYLESHEET, xsl:note never arrives),
  plus LITERAL_RESULT_ELEMENT, TEXT_NODE, EXTENSION_INSTRUCTION,
  UNKNOWN_INSTRUCTION (forwards-compatible) and DATA_ELEMENT. A node's
  attributes are consecutive; children linked as in D52.
- **Attributes**: one kind per attribute name of the schema; the value is read
  into the form the element syntax names: EXPRESSION, PATTERN, VALUE_TEMPLATE,
  SEQUENCE_TYPE, ITEM_TYPE (each its own `sxml_ast`), TEXT, BOOLEAN, NUMBER,
  KEYWORD, NAME, NAME_LIST, NAMESPACE_BINDING. QName-valued attributes are
  resolved while reading (XTSE0280); names inside expressions stay as written
  for static analysis. An AVT is always a VALUE_TEMPLATE, even without `{`: an
  XPath AST with a STRING_TEMPLATE body, lowered as string templates are.
  Standard attributes stay as TEXT; their effect is in the static context.
- **Static context per element**, resolved and shared until something changes:
  statically known namespaces (after fixed-namespaces), xpath default namespace
  (or ##any), default collation, mode and validation, expand-text, version,
  cumulative excluded and extension namespaces, static base URI. Lowering never
  walks up the tree.
- **Reader duties** (4.5): whitespace and commentary stripping, use-when,
  shadow attributes, simplified stylesheets (synthesized STYLESHEET and
  TEMPLATE match "."; expand-text from the version, 3.7), include and import
  read in place depth first (duplicate includes in a level ignored, 4.0),
  syntax of every value. Import precedence is computed by `sxml_xslt_ast_seal`
  from the module tree (post-order, includes share their includer's), since
  modules are added in pre-order.
- **Who writes what**: the builder and lifecycle functions are defined in a new
  `src/xslt_ast.c` with `tests/xslt_ast_test.c`, both written by packet 4.5
  (the AST's only producer, as 1.16 wrote `xpath_ast.c`); added to 4.5's files
  in `docs/tasks/phase-4.md`. A text form (`sxml_xslt_ast_write_text`) serves
  golden tests; the header writes out for-each-group-001, a template rule and
  an xsl:function in it.
- Rejected: one shared `sxml_ast` for all expressions (its capacity is fixed
  from one concrete syntax tree, D52); keeping attribute values as text for
  lowering to parse (every lowering part would repeat the checks, and XTSE
  errors belong to reading); a fixed-capacity AST sized from the trees (modules
  arrive one by one through the resolver).

### D103. Lowering parts and the embedding entry (packet 2.1)

**Summary**: The `sxml_xpath_lowerer` opens the lowering machine: procedures
are descriptors, lowering parts register by glob and may replace core kinds per
language, and an embedding entry lowers one XPath AST into the current
function.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D63 and D71 for Phases 3 and 4.
`src/xpath_lower_internal.h` (module `xpath_lower`) opens the lowering machine
to other files.

- **The lowerer** (`sxml_xpath_lowerer`, lifecycle quintet): one lowering into
  one unit, over a static context, for one `sxml_language` (D101), with a part
  view (empty: the registry). Building blocks are exported under
  `sxml_xpath_lowerer_*`: scratch memory, add an expression or a slot, bind in
  a block, finish a block, constants, raise, push and pop variables, read the
  focus, resolve and coerce types, signatures, enter and leave an IR function.
- **Procedures are descriptors**: a frame holds a pointer to a static
  `sxml_xpath_lowering_procedure` (name, step function, locals size); the
  core's 24 procedures are a table of them, so core and part frames run alike.
  Steps ask for parts with `sxml_xpath_lowering_call_*` and return; no step
  runs a machine (D71). `_push_procedure` pushes any procedure with initial
  locals (copied bytes; one depth level), for constructs that are not AST kinds
  (XSLT instructions over the D102 AST); `sxml_xpath_lowerer_run_procedure`
  runs one from outside.
- **Lowering parts by glob**: a file `src/<name>_lower.c` or
  `src/<name>_lower_<part>.c` defining `const sxml_xpath_lowering_part
  sxml_xpath_lowering_part_<part> =` (languages, rules of AST kind to a
  procedure or a leaf function) is registered by
  `sxml_generate_lowering_part_registry` in `cmake/SxmlParts.cmake` (generated
  `lowering_parts.c`, `sxml_xpath_lowering_registered_parts()`, sorted by
  file). `call_expression` takes the first part serving the lowerer's language
  that lists the kind, then the core; so a part may replace a core kind for its
  language (XQuery FLWOR). A unit test checks that no two registered parts list
  one kind for a common language. The CMake function and its two lines in the
  root `CMakeLists.txt` join packet 2.0's files after 2.0 is committed (2.1
  adds them then).
- **Embedding entry**: `sxml_xpath_lowering_call_embedded` (from a step) and
  `sxml_xpath_lowerer_lower_embedded` (outside) lower one XPath AST into the
  current function: variables the caller pushed are in scope as their atoms,
  the focus is the caller's choice (absent, slots, fixed) or the current one,
  the static context is the AST's (namespaces, function table with XSLT's
  in-scope functions; same heap and allocator; its variable declarations are
  the unit's globals in order). The lowerer's AST, static context and focus are
  restored afterwards. `sxml_xpath_lower` lowers its main function through it,
  so the slice dumps cover it.
- After a failure a lowerer is fit only for finalize. `sxml_xpath_lower` and
  `_compile` (`xpath_static_internal.h`) are unchanged: XPath, the registered
  parts; XQuery and XSLT compile with a lowerer of their own.
- Rejected: parts as a second enum range in the core's switch (every part would
  edit the core); running a nested machine for embedded expressions (C
  recursion through a step).

### D104. The public API for Phase 2 (packet 2.2)

**Summary**: Phase 2 adds decimal formats and collations to the static context,
default language, environment variables and a trace sink to the dynamic
context, new resource kinds, and version macros for 0.2.0.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D51's "left out until needed" for Phase 2.
`processor.h`, `xpath.h`, `version.h`; only new fields at the end of structs
and new constants at the end of enumerations, so Phase 1 code compiles
unchanged (zero keeps the old behaviour).

- **Decimal formats** (static context): `sxml_decimal_format` (name, index 0
  the unnamed format) with properties as text, `{kind, value}`, one kind per
  F&O 4.0 property (11). Text, not codepoints, because every source gives text
  (xsl:decimal-format attributes, XQuery declarations, QT4 `decimal-format`),
  and 4.0's marker-and-rendition form (`%:pc`, type `'.|.:.*'`) parses once in
  sxml. An absent kind has its default. A breach (wrong form, markers not
  distinct, zero-digit not an Nd zero, duplicate names) is INVALID_ARGUMENT for
  the XPath API; XQuery and XSLT raise their own codes (XQST0097/8, XTSE1300)
  before handing formats over.
- **Collations** (static context): `default_collation_uri` (empty is codepoint;
  XPath 4.0 puts it in the dynamic context, but every host knows it statically)
  and `collation_bindings`, host URIs that stand for a supported collation (the
  spec's "mapping from URI to collation"). `sxml_collation_is_supported(uri)`
  tells hosts and the QT4 driver which URIs sxml implements (D97); packet 2.12
  defines it in `src/xpath.c` over the collation lookup that 2.13 later
  completes. No host collation interface: D97 keeps collations inside sxml.
- **Dynamic context**: `default_language` (empty is "en"),
  `environment_variables` (name/value views; sxml never reads the platform's),
  `trace_sink` (null means the processor's).
- **Resources**: kinds TEXT, BINARY, COLLECTION, URI_COLLECTION, XQUERY_MODULE,
  XSLT_MODULE, XSLT_PACKAGE, each with the forms it allows (a wrong form is
  INVALID_ARGUMENT); new form SEQUENCE with an owned `items` sequence for
  collections; request fields `encoding_name` (fn:unparsed-text's argument;
  sxml decodes by the resource's encoding, then the request's, then BOM, then
  UTF-8), `is_default_collection`, `target_namespace_uri` (import module) and
  `package_version` (xsl:use-package; uri_reference is the package name). The
  table resolver serves bytes for every kind that takes them. `processor.c`
  gains the SEQUENCE case of fn:doc's switch (INVALID_ARGUMENT).
- **Trace sink**: one interface for fn:trace, fn:message and xsl:message (and
  failed xsl:assert): `receive(state, event)` with kind, label, value (borrowed
  sequence), `is_terminating` and `error_code` for XSLT, location and
  processor; the null sink discards; a failure stops the evaluation; a sink may
  nest an evaluation, as a host function may.
  `sxml_stream_trace_sink(&output_stream)` writes `label: value` lines
  (adaptive, item separator " "): the default implementation and test double,
  defined by 2.12 in `src/processor.c`. `processor.h` now includes
  `serialize.h` (no cycle). The two new functions are declared only until 2.12;
  nothing calls them before.
- **Version**: `SXML_VERSION_ENCODE(major, minor, patch)`,
  `SXML_VERSION_NUMBER` and `SXML_API_VERSION` = 0.2.0, the first public
  release's API; 2.18 sets the version macros themselves.
- Still left out, each a new field later: host extension functions,
  cancellation, a random seed, default calendar and place.
- From now on these headers change only through a record until 0.2.0 (D47,
  D99).

### D105. The regex engine: the whole F&O 4.0 dialect (packet 2.3)

**Summary**: The regex engine grows the seed in place to the whole F&O 4.0
dialect: category and block escapes, lookaround without recursion, case-blind
matching, named groups and generated Unicode 16.0 tables.

Recorded 2026-10-17. D9 is met by growing the D53 seed in place, behind the
same `src/regex_internal.h` (compile, match at, find, find next), not by a
rewrite: its parser, emitted program and backtracking machine already follow
Saxon HE's design.

- **Syntax** (F&O 4.0, section 6.1.3): category escapes `\p{Lu}` (no `Cs`, as
  the grammar), block escapes `\p{IsX}` by the Blocks.txt name without spaces
  plus the four renamed XSD 1.0 names (`IsGreek`, `IsCombiningMarksforSymbols`,
  `IsCyrillicSupplementary`, `IsPrivateUse`); unknown names are FORX0002
  (6.1.7). `\i \c` are XML 1.0 fifth edition NameStartChar and NameChar. XSD
  1.1 hyphens: a "-" that separates no range is a character (`[a-d-b-c]`, QT4
  re00056a). `\b \B`, `(?=) (?!) (?<=) (?<!)` and the
  `(*positive_lookahead:...)` spellings; `(?<name>...)`, `\k<name>`. Assertions
  take no quantifier.
- **Lookaround** without recursion: LOOK_START pushes an assertion entry on the
  backtrack stack; LOOK_END of a positive assertion drops the choices above it
  but keeps the slot-restoring entries (captures stay, and are undone if
  matching later backtracks past the assertion; first match wins, 6.1.8.3), of
  a negative one undoes them and fails; backtracking onto the entry fails a
  positive assertion and resumes a negative one after it. A lookbehind branch
  is fixed-length (6.1.8.5), so it starts with STEP_BACK n.
- **Case-blind** matching (6.2): variants by `fn:lower-case`/`upper-case`
  through `sxml_function_library_map_case` (the tables of
  `src/function_library_case.c`, shared), plus 94 pairs those mappings do not
  reach (KELVIN SIGN, final sigma, ...), generated with the same code as the
  case tables. A literal becomes a class of its variants at compile time; a
  range checks the input's variants at match time; back-references compare
  codepoint by codepoint.
- **Names**: the compiled regex keeps each group's name and whether it is in a
  lookahead (new `sxml_regex_group_name`, `_find_named_group`,
  `_group_is_in_lookahead`); while compiling, names live in a table that grows
  through the stack allocator like the group stack.
- **Tables** (`tools/generate-regex-tables.py`, Unicode 16.0: UnicodeData,
  SpecialCasing, Blocks): 4,099 category runs packed in `uint32_t` (\\d and \\w
  now derive from them), 342 blocks, 94 pairs; about 25 KB of read-only data.
- Not done: counted repetition is still expanded, so `a{2147483647}` is
  LIMIT_EXCEEDED (QT4 cbcl-matches-004, -038).

**Sources**: category runs, blocks, case pairs and read-only size of the
generated regex tables (`tools/generate-regex-tables.py`, from
`src/regex_unicode.c`).

### D106. The XQuery and serialization API (packet 3.0)

**Summary**: `include/sxml/xquery.h` adds `sxml_xquery_query`, and
`serialize.h` gains every Serialization 4.0 method and parameter, tri-state
flags whose zero means the default, and a reader for fn:serialize options.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `include/sxml/xquery.h` is new; `serialize.h` grows by new
constants at the end of `sxml_serialization_method` and new fields in
`sxml_serialization_parameters`, regrouped by size (enumerations, presence
flags, views) because clang-tidy's padding check rejects the interleaved order.
Callers initialize by field name, so Phase 1 and 2 code compiles unchanged
(zero is still the adaptive method with its defaults); nothing is ABI-stable
before 0.2.0 (D99).

- **Methods**: XML, XHTML, HTML, TEXT, JSON, CSV after ADAPTIVE. No constant
  for implementation-defined (namespaced) methods; the readers raise SEPM0016
  for them. A method not implemented yet returns UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE (the
  header's contract); `src/serialize.c` still returns INVALID_ARGUMENT for
  non-adaptive methods until 3.3 changes it.
- **Parameters**: one struct with every Serialization 4.0 parameter, including
  the 4.0 additions (canonical, csv-*, escape-solidus, indent-unit,
  indent-attributes, json-lines, line-ending), field names the parameter names
  with `_`. Booleans are `sxml_serialization_flag` (DEFAULT, NO, YES), because
  several defaults are "yes" (escape-solidus, escape-uri-attributes,
  include-content-type, omit-xml-declaration) and a zero struct must mean
  "defaults"; DEFAULT is fn:serialize's default (F&O 4.0 table), so
  omit-xml-declaration defaults to yes; XSLT sets NO itself. Enumerations have
  their default as constant 0 (UTF-8, standalone omit, normalization none, LF,
  json-node-output-method xml). Parameters the spec lets be absent (doctype-*,
  html-version, indent-unit, item-separator, media-type, version) are `has_` +
  text; html-version stays text (an xs:decimal lexical form) because the HTML
  method also falls back on version. csv-separator and csv-quote-character are
  codepoints, 0 the default. Element-name lists are name pool identifiers
  (`sxml_element_name_view`, in serialize.h because name.h is frozen);
  character maps are codepoint/replacement pairs. Encodings: UTF-8, UTF-16 (big
  endian), US-ASCII, ISO-8859-1 (`sxml_character_encoding`); other names
  SESU0007. Indent unit default two spaces.
- **Errors**: a value Serialization 4.0 does not permit is SEPM0016 (a dynamic
  error) when serialized, so fn:serialize sees the spec code; what XDM cannot
  even express (ill-formed UTF-8, unknown constants, name 0, a repeated
  character-map codepoint) is INVALID_ARGUMENT.
- **Parameter reader**: `sxml_serialization_parameter_reader` (lifecycle
  quintet; allocator and item heap) reads fn:serialize's `$options` (empty, a
  map, or an `output:serialization-parameters` element) into the struct and
  owns the copied text and lists until its next read. Map: XPTY0004 for wrong
  types, SEPM0016 for bad values; element: SEPM0017, SEPM0018, SEPM0019
  (Serialization 4.0, 3.1); method xml when none is given. The textual forms of
  XQuery output declarations and xsl:output (yes/no/1/0, `\t`, QName lists) are
  read by internal code of 3.10 and Phase 4, not by a public function.
- **XQuery**: `sxml_xquery_query` (quintet, like `sxml_xpath_expression`; the
  main module's text is `expression_text`, glossary) compiled with the shared
  `sxml_static_context_configuration`, evaluated with
  `sxml_xquery_evaluation_request` holding the shared dynamic context. Host
  variable declarations are in scope in the main module only (a prolog
  declaration of the same name is XQST0049); bindings also bind every module's
  external variables. Library modules come from the resolver, kind
  XQUERY_MODULE, one request per location hint (an empty uri_reference for
  none); the parameter document of output:parameter-document is an XML_DOCUMENT
  request, read at compile time (XQST0119/XQST0115). Output declaration errors
  (XQST0108-0110, SEPM0016) are compile errors.
  `sxml_xquery_query_get_serialization_parameters` returns the struct by value:
  declarations over the parameter document over XQuery defaults (method xml);
  the host overrides fields of the copy (CLI `--method`).
- Left out, each a later field: XQuery-only static context settings from the
  host (boundary-space, construction, ordering), a list of the query's external
  variables, fn:load-xquery-module options (3.11 is internal),
  implementation-defined serialization parameters.

### D107. Unicode tables and functions (packet 2.4)

**Summary**: Generated Unicode 16.0 tables in `src/unicode_tables.c` serve
normalization (UAX #15), grapheme iteration (UAX #29), fn:char with HTML names,
fn:characters and fn:normalize-unicode.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `src/unicode_internal.h` (defined in `src/unicode.c` over
the data of `src/unicode_tables.c`, generated by
`tools/generate-unicode-tables.py` from Unicode 16.0 and the WHATWG
`entities.json`), used by `src/function_library_unicode.c` (fn:char,
fn:characters, fn:graphemes, fn:normalize-unicode) and open to the serializer's
normalization-form (3.3) and to collations (2.13).

- **Separate from the regex tables** (D105): those hold general categories,
  blocks and case variants; these hold combining classes, full canonical and
  compatibility decompositions (looked up, not expanded at run time; Hangul by
  the arithmetic of Unicode 16.0, section 3.12), primary composites, the
  composing starters, the UAX #29 properties (Grapheme_Cluster_Break,
  Indic_Conjunct_Break, Extended_Pictographic packed per run) and the 2,125
  HTML names. No property is in both.
- **Normalization** (UAX #15) works on the whole string: decompose into a
  codepoint array that grows through the caller's allocator, put each run of
  non-starters in canonical order (insertion sort for short runs, a stable
  counting sort by combining class for long ones, so the cost stays linear),
  compose in place by the UAX #15 sample algorithm, encode. The result is UTF-8
  owned through that allocator. FULLY-NORMALIZED prepends a space when the
  first character is a composing character, then NFC (F&O 4.0 rules). ASCII
  input is returned as it is.
- **Graphemes**: an iterator over a string yields byte ranges; its state
  (previous break value, count of regional indicators, the emoji and conjunct
  sequences in progress) decides rules GB3 to GB999 of UAX #29 (Unicode 16.0,
  with GB9c) one codepoint at a time.
- **fn:char**: an integer must be a permitted character (FOCH0005, also beyond
  0x10FFFF); a name is looked up case-sensitively by binary search; the escapes
  are \\n \\r \\t \\b \\f.

**Sources**: HTML names in the generated Unicode tables
(`tools/generate-unicode-tables.py`, from `src/unicode_tables.c`).

### D108. The QT4 driver for Phase 2: environments, scope, areas (packet 2.16)

**Summary**: The QT4 driver applies decimal-format, collation, resource and
collection environments, satisfies more dependencies, marks whether each case
is in the pass-rate denominator, and reports in-scope counts per area.

Recorded 2026-10-17. Extends D83 and D92 in `tests/qt4/driver/`.

- **Environments now applied**: `decimal-format` (every attribute one D104
  property, value as written; the name's prefix bound by the element's in-scope
  namespaces, unprefixed names in no namespace); `collation` (any D97 URI runs:
  codepoint, HTML ASCII, UCA unless `fallback=no`; `default="true"` sets
  `default_collation_uri`; other URIs stay "environment collation"; the
  driver's own check until 2.12's `sxml_collation_is_supported` exists);
  `resource` and `collection` through a resource table (`resource_table.c`,
  glossary `qt4_resource_table`): TEXT and BINARY by the resource's absolute
  URI (relative ones against the test-set file; TEXT gets the `encoding`
  attribute as the external encoding), else `file:///SUITE-PATH`; COLLECTION
  and URI_COLLECTION as SEQUENCE (document nodes, or their document URIs as
  xs:anyURI), `uri=""` is the default collection; collection sources with a
  `uri` are also available documents; a collection's resources are served like
  the environment's and their URIs follow the documents' in fn:uri-collection.
  Still skipped: collections with a `query` (3.13). Resources are not served to
  fn:doc.
- **Dependencies** now satisfied: feature simple-uca-fallback,
  non_empty_sequence_collection, arbitraryPrecisionDecimal;
  unicode-normalization-form NFC NFD NFKC NFKD (Phase 2 makes them work; the
  D95 denominator counts their cases anyway). Not collection-stability: its two
  cases ask for it to be absent.
- **Scope**: applicability also says whether a case is in the D95 denominator
  (spec matches, no non-goal test set, no required non-goal feature; tables in
  `applicability.c`). Out-of-scope cases that apply still run, so pass counts
  stay comparable. `sxml-qt4 list` ends with "N test cases: A applicable, S
  skipped; D in scope" and marks "out of scope: ..."; `list --spec=XP40` gives
  31,543 in scope, `--spec=XQ40` 41,174 (D95: about 31,500 and 41,200).
- **JSON report** (still version 1, members only added): test sets, totals and
  a new `areas` array (D94's prefixes) carry `in_scope` and `in_scope_passed`;
  `in_scope_passed / in_scope` is the gate rate. `tools/conformance-report.py`
  (1.27) may read them; it ignores them now.
- Measured (release): XP40 passed 23,146 to 24,451, no pass lost; not run
  18,448 to 16,321. The ten new "error" outcomes are UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE in
  newly run cases, not the driver.

**Sources**: sxml-qt4 list --spec=XP40 and --spec=XQ40, cases in scope
(`sxml-qt4`); XP40 passed and not run, before and after (`sxml-qt4`, release
build); quoted from D95.

### D109. try/catch in the evaluator (packet 3.6)

**Summary**: TRY_CATCH is one catching task with start, body, handler and
finally phases; catch clauses match by name test, bind error details as a map,
and finally re-raises a pending error.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D101 for TRY_CATCH (`src/evaluator_try.c`;
XQuery 4.0, section 4.20).

- **One catching task** per TRY_CATCH, phases start, body, handler, finally.
  The try clause's value is read completely before it counts, so a lazy
  sequence's error is caught by the try that made it. Catch clauses are tried
  in order, the first whose name tests match wins (`*`, EQName,
  `p:*`/`Q{uri}*`, `*:local`); an error with no code in the record counts as
  err:FOER0000.
- **Error details** (glossary `error_details`): a clause's `error_details` slot
  is bound to `$err:map`, entries keyed by xs:string in table order: "code"
  (xs:QName, prefix kept only with a namespace), "description", "value",
  "module", "line-number", "column-number"; none for an empty value.
  `$err:stack-trace` and `$err:additional` are always `()` in sxml, so they
  have no entry. Lowering (3.7) reads each `$err:` variable as `map:get($slot,
  "local-name")` and `$err:map` is the slot. They are copied out of the record
  before anything else runs (D41).
- **Own error record**: when the caller passed none, the outermost try points
  the context's record at one in its task state while it runs and puts NULL
  back when it ends or unwinds; inner tries use it. Uncaught errors are still
  reported nowhere. Done inside the part because `src/evaluator.c` belongs to
  2.6 in this wave; the machine may later keep its own record instead, with no
  visible change.
- **finally**: an error of the try clause that no clause matches, and an error
  of the catch clause, are caught only to run the finally clause; their details
  are kept (glossary `pending_error`) and raised again through the heap when it
  succeeds (the finally clause may raise and catch errors on the same heap). An
  error of the finally clause replaces them; a non-empty value is XQTY0153
  (type error). Limits, memory and invalid arguments run no catch or finally
  clause.
- XPath 4.0 has no try/catch (checked in the 4.0 draft): nothing for 2.5.
  XSLT's xsl:try (4.x) can lower to the same kind.
- `tests/evaluator_machine_test.c` no longer expects UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE for
  TRY_CATCH (list `evaluated_kinds`, where 3.5 adds the constructors).

### D110. Node constructors in the evaluator (packet 3.5)

**Summary**: Each node constructor makes its own self-destroying arena tree and
copies nested constructed nodes into it, with the listed content convention,
name checks, fixed construction modes and base URIs.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `src/evaluator_construct.c` evaluates the seven
constructor kinds and SHALLOW_COPY (D55, D101).

- **One tree per constructed node.** Each constructor makes a new arena tree in
  the item heap's memory that destroys itself with its last reference (as
  fn:json-to-xml); a nested constructor's node is a tree of its own that the
  enclosing constructor copies with `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node`. So a
  constructor's step only waits for its content value and then does leaf work
  (no C recursion, D71); copying costs one evaluation step per copied node,
  each content item one (D89). The arena tree gets the evaluation's error
  record: it reports only while events are sent, inside the step.
- **Content convention for lowering (3.9, 4.x).** A content expression of kind
  SEQUENCE lists the enclosed expressions and literal text of a direct
  constructor, one atom each, read directly (not pushed); atomic items are
  joined by spaces only within one atom (`<c>{1}{2}</c>` is "12", XQuery 4.0,
  4.12.1.3). Any other content expression (an ATOM, a LET...) is one enclosed
  expression: a computed constructor's whose value is a SEQUENCE must be bound
  to a slot first. Arrays are flattened with an explicit stack of content
  frames; JNodes add their atomized value; function items are XQTY0105.
- **Names.** The name atom holds an xs:QName (used as it is, prefix kept) or an
  xs:string, xs:untypedAtomic or xs:anyURI: trimmed, `Q{uri}local`,
  `Q{uri}prefix:local` or a lexical QName resolved with the unit's static
  namespaces (prefix 0 = default element namespace, elements only); XQDY0074
  otherwise, XPTY0004 for another type or not exactly one item. XQDY0096 and
  XQDY0044 are checked here for every name; an attribute in a namespace without
  a prefix gets `xml` or `ns0`. PI targets XQDY0041 (any non-NCName string, as
  QT4 expects), XQDY0064, XQDY0026; comments XQDY0072; namespace prefixes
  XQDY0074, URIs XPTY0004 (not one string), XQDY0101 from the builder. Written
  namespace bindings (the `namespace_bindings` run) are sent after the start
  event: lowering should give a direct constructor's own declarations
  (enclosing ones are inherited through the copy while copy-namespaces is
  inherit).
- **Modes fixed for now**: construction strip (xs:untyped, xs:untypedAtomic),
  copy-namespaces preserve, inherit; ELEMENT and DOCUMENT follow XQuery
  (duplicate attributes XQDY0025, XQTY0024, XPTY0004 for attributes in a
  document), SHALLOW_COPY follows XSLT 4.0 5.7.1 (later duplicates replace,
  XTDE0410, XTDE0420, XTDE0450, XTTE3180 for more than one item; element
  namespaces copied). construction_flags and name_namespaces select the other
  modes (D124).
- **Base URIs**: elements get the static base URI as their tree's base URI
  (`sxml_arena_tree_configuration.base_uri`, D98), documents through their
  start event; attributes, text, comments and PIs have none (QT4 fn-base-uri-5
  to -7).
- **Deviation**: `text {""}` gives the empty sequence, not an empty text node:
  the arena tree drops empty text (D40). Inside a constructor the two are the
  same (the empty text node is deleted).

### D111. The query AST for XQuery and the parser part seam (packet 3.1)

**Summary**: The query AST gains 66 XQuery kinds and 24 fields, and
`sxml_ast_build_with_parser_part` runs the one XPath walker with a part's
grammar tables and three hooks.

Recorded 2026-10-17, extending D52 and D59. `src/xpath_ast_internal.h`.

- **Kinds**: 66 XQuery kinds appended to `sxml_ast_kind`, one per new visible
  node type of `grammars/xquery` (`SXML_AST_KIND_<NODE TYPE>`);
  `allowing_empty` is absorbed as flag ALLOWING_EMPTY. 24 fields appended (the
  grammar's, plus MODULE, which the front end gives the child of `module`, the
  one named child without a grammar field). Tokens in fields `mode`/`kind`
  become the new detail `keyword` (PRESERVE, STRIP, ORDERED, ..., LAX, STRICT);
  the decimal-format property name the detail `decimal_format_property`
  (`sxml/xpath.h`'s kind); the other XQuery tokens flags (FIXED, EXTERNAL,
  STABLE, DESCENDING, EMPTY_GREATEST, EMPTY_LEAST, ONLY, STATIC,
  PRESERVE_NAMESPACES, INHERIT_NAMESPACES). Front-end marks:
  BOUNDARY_WHITESPACE on direct element text, NAMESPACE_DECLARATION_ATTRIBUTE
  on `xmlns` attributes. Leaves: QNAME has a name payload, the direct text
  kinds, CDATA, comments, pragma contents and string constructor characters a
  decoded text, a direct PI the new payload `processing_instruction` (target,
  content). The header writes out AST and IR of five XQuery examples (group by,
  a tumbling window, a direct constructor with namespaces, try/catch/finally, a
  prolog function).
- **Parser part seam**: `sxml_ast_build_with_parser_part(request, part, &ast)`
  runs the one XPath walker (D59: iterative, A.3.2 and lookup key checks, depth
  bound) with a part's language and root node type, its sorted node type and
  field tables (consulted after XPath's), unnamed child fields, and three
  stateless hooks: `apply_token` (claims a token before the XPath rules),
  `describe_payload` (fills a payload before the XPath decoders, e.g. XQuery
  string literals with references) and `finish_node` (called once per node when
  it is complete, leaves at once; for XQST0118, XQST0040, boundary whitespace).
  Hooks reach the AST and source text through the opaque `sxml_ast_front_end`,
  add flags with `sxml_ast_add_flags`, and raise any err: code with
  `sxml_ast_front_end_raise` (the error record gets that code). Without a part
  the walk is unchanged: all 32,928 applicable XP40 queries build
  byte-identical ASTs. With a scratch part of only the tables, all 43,663 valid
  XQ40 queries and the 145 parsable library modules build.
- **Who writes what**: 3.2 defines `sxml_xquery_build_ast` (declared now) and
  its part in `src/xquery_parse.c`; it needs `sxml_grammar_xquery` added to the
  `sxml` link line of the root `CMakeLists.txt` (one word, 3.2 adds it). Parts
  are passed by each entry point, not registered by glob: the entry point
  chooses the grammar.
- `tests/xpath_parse_test.c`'s kind and field name tables grow with the
  enumerations (static asserts); 3.1 appended the XQuery names.
- Rejected: a parser registry by glob (one grammar per entry point, so nothing
  to discover); the XQuery tables in `xpath_parse.c` (the part owns its
  grammar's names, as lowering parts own their kinds); hook state pointers
  (everything a hook needs is in the AST).

**Sources**: applicable XP40 queries building byte-identical ASTs without a
part, and valid XQ40 queries and library modules with a scratch part.

### D112. The XSLT API (packet 4.0)

**Summary**: `include/sxml/xslt.h` adds `sxml_xslt_stylesheet`, compiled from
the principal module or through the resolver, with output definitions, one
transform call per invocation, result delivery kinds and a result document
handler.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `include/sxml/xslt.h` is new, header only, after
`xquery.h` (D106); 4.15 implements it in `src/xslt.c`.

- **Stylesheet**: `sxml_xslt_stylesheet` (lifecycle quintet, like
  `sxml_xquery_query`) compiled from the principal module's bytes, or fetched
  through the resolver as an XSLT_MODULE (a URI reference) or an XSLT_PACKAGE
  (name and package-version), chosen by `sxml_xslt_principal_module_source`.
  Includes, imports and used packages always come from the resolver (XTSE0165,
  XTSE3000, XTSE0180). Static parameters are `sxml_variable_binding_view`
  values given at compile time (XTDE0050 is then a compile failure with
  DYNAMIC_ERROR). Of the shared static context only static_base_uri, the
  default collation and collation bindings are read; namespaces, variable
  declarations and decimal formats must be empty, since the stylesheet declares
  its own.
- **Output definitions**: `sxml_xslt_output_definition` = the D106 parameters
  struct + `build_tree` (a serialization flag) + `has_serialization_method`
  (false: method chosen from the raw result, XSLT 4.0 26.1.2, which serialize.h
  cannot express). Read by name with
  `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_get_output_definition` (0 = unnamed); XSLT's
  omit-xml-declaration default is filled in as NO, indent stays DEFAULT and
  means yes for html/xhtml when sxml serializes.
- **Transformation**: one call, `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_transform`, primes and
  invokes (one execution scope per call; a primed object for several
  invocations is left out). The request embeds the shared dynamic context:
  context value = global context item (one item or absent), variable bindings =
  stylesheet parameters, trace sink = xsl:message (terminating events end in
  XTMM9000/XTMM9001 or the given code, D104). `sxml_xslt_invocation_kind`
  APPLY_TEMPLATES (0; initial match selection defaulting to the global context
  item, initial mode 0 = default mode, `selects_unnamed_mode` for the spec's
  note), CALL_TEMPLATE (name 0 = xsl:initial-template, focus on the global
  context item), CALL_FUNCTION (arguments by position, arity = count). Template
  and tunnel parameters are two binding views. Fields are grouped by size (no
  padding).
- **Delivery**: `sxml_xslt_result_delivery` DEFAULT (by build-tree), RAW, TREE
  (sequence normalization, base URI = result URI), SERIALIZED (to an
  `sxml_output_stream`); the principal result is the call's output sequence
  (empty when serialized) and its URI the base output URI.
- **Result documents**: `sxml_xslt_result_document_handler` with `open`
  (request: href, absolute URI against the base output URI, effective output
  definition, processor; the handler fills a target: delivery and output
  stream) and `close` (URI, value, `is_abandoned`), called once per successful
  open; XTDE1490 is checked before open, a failing open (D50 statuses) stops
  the transformation. The null handler evaluates and discards. Default
  implementation and test double: `sxml_xslt_result_document_collector`
  (quintet; keeps values or bytes by URI, `_get_result_document_count`,
  `_get_result_document`, `_clear`) for the 4.1 driver's assert-result-document
  and the WebAssembly host.
- Left out, each a later field or function: a primed transformer for several
  invocations, a context item for the initial template other than the global
  context item, initial function arguments by name, the stylesheet's parameter
  list, xsl:message output other than the trace sink, warnings, host extension
  functions and instructions, schema awareness and streaming (D97).

### D113. Lowering completions (packet 2.5)

**Summary**: Lowering completes for member, for key/value, destructuring let,
dynamic node tests, the item axis, constructor functions with keywords, method
calls, but with and more jnode() selectors, all over existing IR and library
calls.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D63's "Not lowered in Phase 1" (only the
computed node constructors are left, for Phase 3). `src/xpath_lower.c`,
`src/xpath_static.c`; IR kinds, the evaluator and public headers are unchanged:
each construct lowers to existing IR plus library calls, found by name like
fn:root (`find_builtin_function`, now with a namespace); a missing one is
UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE naming the gap.

- **for member / for key/value** (XPath 4.0, 4.13.1): the binding collection is
  a MAP over the arrays or maps calling array:split or map:entries (their
  argument coercion gives the type error and accepts JNodes), then the ordinary
  MAP with the position slot, so positions count across all arrays or maps. The
  member is `item?1`; key and value are map:keys and map:items of the
  single-entry map. XQST0089 for equal key and value names and for a position
  variable named like a range variable.
- **Destructuring let** (4.13.2): the value coerced to the declared type
  (default item()*, or one array(*) / map(\*); with a declared type also
  coerced to the single array or map), then fn:items-at(V, i),
  fn:subsequence(V, n) for the last of n, `V?i`, or `V?name`; a declared record
  type without the variable's field binds a RAISE of XPTY0004.
- **Dynamic node tests** (4.7.5.3-4): the selector is lowered with an absent
  focus (reading it raises XPDY0002) and coerced to xs:anyAtomicType\*; the
  step uses `*` of the axis's principal node kind, then a FILTER keeps a node
  when some selector item is fn:atomic-equal to one of its keys: fn:jkey of a
  JNode, fn:node-name and fn:local-name of an XNode.
- **The item axis** (4.7.4): per origin, a CONDITIONAL on count(fn:jvalue(G)):
  two or more items, the child step; none, (); one, the child step from the
  array `[jvalue(G)]` (a map or array origin is a JTree root). Deviation: that
  JNode's parent is the wrapper array's JNode, not G, and it sorts after G's
  tree, so parent/ancestor identity and mixed document order differ from the
  specification (QT4 JAxes-370..372, 384, 387, 388). The faithful form needs an
  axis value in the evaluator (Proposed).
- **Constructor functions** (4.5.1.3): `find_function` gives constructor
  entries the parameter `$value as xs:anyAtomicType? := .`, so keyword
  arguments (`xs:int(value := '1')`) name it and an arity-0 query finds the
  constructor with a parameterless signature: `xs:int()` casts the context
  value and `xs:int#0` is a closure capturing it (body CAST).
- **Method calls** (4.15.5): a link of the chain: MAP over M, the item coerced
  to map(\*), `?N` looked up and dynamically called with the map first;
  arguments lowered in the body with the outer focus (as "=!>"); a placeholder
  is XPST0003.
- **but with** (4.15.4): a chain link: A coerced to record(*), B to map(*),
  map:merge((A, B), {'duplicates': 'use-last'}). Deviation: the merged map is
  not coerced to A's record type (the IR cannot name a type known only at run
  time); a later coercion checks the fields.
- **jnode() selectors** (3.2.12): decimal and double literals, negative numbers
  ("-" and the digits, built in the type frame's scratch) and QName literals
  (the EQName; in no namespace the local name, the form the evaluator's cast
  reads).
- The free-variable analysis sees every variable of a destructuring let (the
  former four-candidate limit is gone).
- Measured (release, XP40): 23,698 to 24,206 passed, none lost; slice 198/198.

### D114. The regex library part (packet 2.3)

**Summary**: `src/function_library_regex.c` holds every regex function of F&O
4.0, section 6.3, adds fn:analyze-string, fn:matching-segments and fn:regex,
and makes named groups reach their results.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D101 made parts files of their own.

- `src/function_library_regex.c` holds every function of F&O 4.0, section 6.3:
  fn:matches, fn:replace and fn:tokenize move there from the string part
  (removal only; no wave-0 packet owned that file), plus fn:analyze-string,
  fn:matching-segments and fn:regex. Named groups reach results: `$<name>` in
  replacement strings (FORX0004 when no group has the name), name keys in the
  groups maps of fn:replace and fn:matching-segments, `name` attributes in
  fn:analyze-string.
- fn:analyze-string builds a parentless untyped element in an arena tree, as
  fn:json-to-xml does; fn:group elements nest by range and by the regex's own
  nesting of parentheses (new `sxml_regex_group_parent`, so `(b)(x?)` and
  `(b(x?))` differ, QT4 analyzeString-017/-017a); lookahead groups follow as
  fn:lookahead-group.
- fn:regex returns a map (no static context knows the named record types yet,
  so `fn:compiled-regex-record` assert-types fail) whose functions are
  anonymous function items of hidden rows capturing pattern and flags; their
  signatures reuse the resolved parameter types of fn:matches#3 and
  fn:replace#4 from the evaluation's function table. Each call compiles again
  (no cache).
- `tests/function_library_test.c` (owned by 2.17 later, by nobody now) names
  the regex part in its fixture so its regex cases keep running; new cases and
  an allocation-failure loop over the new functions.

### D115. Evaluator: JNode selectors, jkey and jvalue, fold fixpoints (packet 2.6)

**Summary**: fn:jkey and fn:jvalue get their own part, and the evaluator adds
selector interpretation on JNodes, JNode name tests and lookups, numeric
predicates, maps and arrays as typed functions, and fold fixpoints.

Recorded 2026-10-17. Sections are those of the XPath 4.0 editor's draft
vendored with QT4 (PR 2734 for selectors).

- **fn:jkey, fn:jvalue** move from 2.17 to 2.6: new part
  `src/function_library_jnode.c` (F&O 4.0, 16.1.2, 16.1.3; `$input as jnode()?
  := .`). Nearly every prod-PathExpr.J and prod-AxisStep.J case uses them; 2.17
  no longer writes them. fn:jtree stays in `src/function_library_json.c`.
- **Selector interpretation** (4.7.3, 4.7.5.4; replaces D85's "not done"): in a
  path's MAP, a JNode N with a non-navigational body (glossary `navigational`,
  decided once per MAP from the IR: ".", STEP, a path MAP, DOCUMENT_ORDER,
  fn:root/TREAT of "/", FILTER of such, union, sequence, conditional, let;
  tables of 48 entries, beyond that navigational as in Phase 1) evaluates the
  body and selects the children of N whose jkey is atomic-equal to an item of
  its atomized value; a body that reads the focus is XPDY0002 there. Task phase
  bits of the MAP keep the analysis.
- **Name tests on JNodes**: an NCName matches string/anyURI/untypedAtomic keys,
  a prefixed name or wildcard matches xs:QName keys. The IR does not tell `a`
  from `Q{}a` (both match strings; JAxes-292 waits for lowering). The attribute
  and namespace axes from a JNode raise XPTY0004 (4.7.5.1).
- **Lookups** on a JNode use the items of its jvalue (each a map or array).
- **QName key tests** (D113's proposal, accepted by the orchestrator): a
  jnode() key test of type xs:QName given as `Q{uri}local` compares the key's
  expanded name (names the pool never saw match nothing); other texts are cast
  as before. Untested end to end: lowering still refuses prefixed QName
  literals in jnode() (QT4 sequence-type-61). The other D113 proposal,
  SXML_AXIS_ITEM, needs a tree.h addition and lowering together; not taken
  here.
- **Numeric predicates** (4.4.1): a value whose first item is numeric selects
  by "= position()" (any item), an integer range by its bounds; a later
  non-number is FORG0006 (was FORG0006 for every second item).
- **Maps and arrays as typed functions** (3.2.9, 3.2.10): when the type
  annotation does not decide it, a map matches function(K) as R for K a single
  atomic type and R allowing () when every value matches R; an array
  function(I) as R for I a single integer type when every member matches R.
- **Fold fixpoints** (glossary `fixpoint`): fn:fold-left/-right and
  array:fold-left/-right stop early when the function is an inline function
  (through coerced functions whose accumulator parameter and result are
  item()\*) of body `if (C) then $acc else E` (or the mirror), C a value or
  general comparison of numeric constants, captured values and $acc, and C
  holds for the next accumulator: every later call would return it (QT4
  fold-left/right-022/023). `sxml_evaluator_test_fixpoint` is declared in
  `src/evaluator_internal.h` (one additive declaration outside the packet's
  files; 2.0 is done).
- **Not done here**: `/` and `/x` from a JNode need lowering to treat as
  `document-node()|jnode()` (4.7.1.1; 6 PathExpr.J cases; lowering);
  fn:function-lookup of focus functions (position#0, last#0) needs the focus at
  the call, which a leaf row cannot see (lowering); assert-eq on a JNode result
  needs the driver to atomize (2.16); `count(reverse(1 to 10^11))` needs a
  descending range representation (substrate, 2.17); the O(1) comparison of a
  range with an integer (RangeExpr-408h, -410h) is ready but waits for
  `tests/xpath_test.c` (see "Proposed"). fn-function-lookup stays at 85%: its
  other 85 failures are functions other packets add.

**Sources**: fn-function-lookup pass rate and failures.

### D116. Collations and comparison options (packet 2.13)

**Summary**: `src/collation.c` implements the codepoint, HTML ASCII, Unicode
case-insensitive and UCA-fallback collations with byte-comparable keys behind
one resolver, and fn:deep-equal supports every 4.0 option.

Recorded 2026-10-17. Completes D97's collations in `src/collation.c`
(`src/collation_internal.h`), used through one resolver.

- **Four collations**: codepoint, HTML ASCII case-insensitive, and also the
  Unicode case-insensitive collation (F&O 4.0, section 5.2.5, which every
  processor must recognize; D97 predates it), and UCA URIs with fallback.
  fallback=no, and a fallback value other than yes/no, is not supported
  (FOCH0002); unknown keywords and values are ignored, the last value of a
  keyword wins, `maxVariable`, `caseFirst` and `caseLevel` also in their
  `max-variable` spellings.
- **UCA fallback** (glossary `uca_fallback`): every codepoint's full
  compatibility decomposition gives collation elements: a base character
  primary = its lower-case codepoint + 1 (codepoint order without case),
  secondary common, tertiary 1/2 for lower/upper (swapped by caseFirst= upper) +
  2 for a compatibility variant; a combining mark (combining class > 0) only
  secondary = 2 + codepoint. Variable characters (whitespace, then P, Sm/Sk/So,
  Sc up to maxVariable) are shifted to a quaternary weight or blanked. Levels:
  primary, secondary (backwards reverses it), case (caseLevel), tertiary,
  quaternary (shifted only), identical (codepoints). lang, version,
  normalization, numeric and reorder are ignored. QT4 fn-collation,
  misc-UCACollation and fn-compare pass with it; the tables of
  advanced-uca-fallback stay out (D97).
- **Keys and matching**: a key lists each compared level's nonzero weights in
  three bytes, levels separated by three zero bytes, so keys compare as bytes
  (`fn:collation-key` returns them as xs:base64Binary) and strings compare by
  keys. Substring matching (contains, starts-with, ends-with,
  substring-before/-after/-before-last/-after-last) compares collation units
  and accepts matches at codepoint boundaries only; the codepoint collation
  stays a byte search. distinct-values, duplicate-values, all-equal and
  all-different hash collation keys.
- **One resolver** (`sxml_function_library_find_collation` /
  `_resolve_collation`, `src/function_library.c`): empty is the default
  collation, which is the codepoint collation until the static context's
  `default_collation_uri` and `collation_bindings` reach the evaluator
  (Proposed); a relative URI resolves against the static base URI (none:
  FOCH0002); FOCH0002 only for URIs sxml does not support. Bodies outside the
  string, sequence and deep-equal parts keep
  `sxml_function_library_check_collation`, which now also raises FOCH0002 for
  supported collations other than codepoint (Proposed:
  `sxml_function_library_compare_collated`).
- **`sxml_collation_is_supported`** (D104) is defined in `src/collation.c`, not
  `src/xpath.c`: the lookup lives there and 2.12 has not run; 2.12 must not
  define it again. The QT4 driver's collation check calls it; its dependency
  table now also lists unicode-normalization-form FULLY-NORMALIZED (accepting
  2.4's proposal).
- **fn:deep-equal 4.0** (`src/function_library_deep_equal.c`): every option. A
  resumable body (D75) for `items-equal` (asked before each item pair,
  attributes and single text nodes included; a leaf entry stays for
  array:index-of). "ordered": false and `unordered-elements` are unordered
  cursors on the explicit stack: each unit tries the unmatched candidates, a
  difference inside a trial truncates the stack to the cursor and tries the
  next (first fit). Function items: same item, or same body, arity, name and
  signature with deep-equal captured values; separately written inline
  functions are not compared for equivalence (Proposed). Without schemas
  typed-values and type-variety change nothing; debug writes nothing; options
  are coerced (a node or xs:untypedAtomic for a boolean).

### D117. The XSLT 4.0 test driver (packet 4.1)

**Summary**: `sxml-xslt-test` is a sibling of `sxml-qt4` that reads the XSLT
4.0 test catalog, decides applicability and scope, plans each case's
invocation, and runs a 154-case slice against a baseline.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `tests/xslt/driver/`, the developer tool `sxml-xslt-test`,
public API only.

- **A sibling, not a mode of sxml-qt4**: the XSLT catalog has its own
  namespace, schema and semantics (dependencies as elements in
  `<dependencies>`, stylesheets, invocations, `assert` over the result
  document), so its catalog, applicability and commands are new modules; it
  links `sxml_qt4_driver_library` for documents (a document loaded by
  `sxml_qt4_document_load` with its catalog namespace switched to
  `http://www.w3.org/2012/10/xslt-test-catalog`), the QT4 environment reader
  (sources, params, resources, collections, collations, schemas), suite paths,
  test lists, reasons and the run report (spec "XSLT40").
- **Reading**: a ref looks in the test set, then catalog.xml; every
  `<dependencies>` child is a dependency whose type is its local name. Names
  (params, initial template, mode, function) are xs:QNames: a prefix bound by
  the element, Q{uri}local as an EQName, an unprefixed name in no namespace,
  `#default`/`#unnamed` kept as keywords. initial-function gives CALL_FUNCTION,
  else initial-template CALL_TEMPLATE (one case also names a mode: ignored,
  listed), else APPLY_TEMPLATES. `<output>` of `<test>`, else of the
  environment.
- **Applicability**: spec tokens `XSLTnn` / `XSLTnn+` (case replaces set; no
  spec = every version, as D83); other dependencies match their whole value
  against a table (`xslt_applicability.c`): features higher_order_functions,
  namespace_axis, serialization, built_in_derived_types, HTML5, XPath_3.1 (XSLT
  3.0's optional 3.1 support), streaming-fallback; English numbering, AD/ISO
  calendars, every year_component_values phrase, the normalization forms,
  UTF-8, HTML 5, on-multiple-match recover, package_version_resolution
  highest_version (until 4.16 decides), enable_assertions, codepoint collation,
  any maximum_number_of_decimal_digits. Not: dynamic_evaluation,
  disabling_output_escaping, numbering combinations, the non-goals. Then the
  environment (source validation, XInclude, XML 1.1 sources, schemas, unknown
  collations) and posture-and-sweep tests. Scope (D95): spec matches, group
  (directory under tests/) not strm or sandp, no required non-goal feature.
  Measured: 13,867 cases resolve, 8,387 applicable, 8,728 in scope (D95: about
  8,700).
- **Plan** (`xslt_test_run.h`): principal module = first non-secondary module
  of `<test>`, else of the environment, else the defines-stylesheet source (16
  cases); a package is RESOLVED_PACKAGE, a stylesheet TEXT with base URI
  file:///SUITE-PATH; other modules are served by the resolver; static params
  go to the stylesheet configuration, others are stylesheet parameters; role
  "." is the global context item; delivery SERIALIZED (serialize="yes"), RAW
  (tree="no"), TREE (tree="yes"), else DEFAULT; base output URI from output
  file=, else file:///TEST-SET-DIRECTORY/output/TEST-CASE/; result documents to
  `sxml_xslt_result_document_collector`, messages to the trace sink. Assertion
  semantics for the checks are in `xslt_assertion.h` (`assert` with the result
  document as context item, $RESULT-VAR bound for raw results).
- **Run**: not applicable is not-run "skip: ..."; assert-warning or
  assert-posture-and-sweep anywhere is not-run "unsupported: KIND"; an unknown
  or malformed assertion or no principal module is an error; all else is
  not-run "XSLT not implemented" until 4.15 implements xslt.h. 4.15 (or a
  follow-up) adds the execution: a processor per case with the QT4 limits, the
  plan applied, the assertions checked.
- **Slice**: `tests/xslt/slice.txt`, 154 in-scope applicable cases spread over
  the twelve core sets of the Phase 4 gate; ctest `xslt/slice` against
  `tests/xslt/slice-baseline.txt` (0 until XSLT runs); `xslt/list_slice` keeps
  them resolving.

**Sources**: xslt40-test cases that resolve, are applicable and are in scope
(`sxml-xslt-test`, from `third_party/xslt40-test/catalog.xml`); the slice: 154
in-scope applicable cases (from `tests/xslt/slice.txt`); quoted from D95.

### D118. Patterns: front end, match expressions, priorities (packet 4.4)

**Summary**: An XSLT pattern parses to its own AST kinds and becomes an XPath
boolean match expression lowered through the embedding entry; a match function
serves template rules, and default priorities follow section 6.4.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `src/xslt_pattern.c`, `src/xslt_pattern_internal.h` (new
module header), after D29, D52, D103, D111.

- **Pattern AST**: 19 kinds appended to `sxml_ast_kind`, one per `..._pattern`
  node type of `grammars/xslt_pattern` (root PATTERN), the field PATTERN and
  the flag OPEN (map pattern `*`); everything inside predicates, node tests,
  names and constants stays the XPath kinds. Built by
  `sxml_xslt_pattern_build_ast` (declared in `xpath_ast_internal.h` beside the
  other front ends) through the D111 parser part seam. Every syntax error is
  XTSE0340 (6.3.1), as is an outermost function call not binding to fn:doc#1,
  id#1-2, element-with-id#1-2, key#2-3, root#0 (prefixed names checked when the
  match expression is built). 4.4 made these additive edits to
  `src/xpath_ast_internal.h`, `tests/xpath_parse_test.c` (names) and the `sxml`
  link line of the root `CMakeLists.txt` (`sxml_grammar_xslt_pattern`), as D111
  foresaw.
- **Match expression**: a pattern becomes an XPath AST (root XPATH) of
  xs:boolean over the item as context value, built by one loop over an explicit
  task list (D71) and lowered like any XPath expression through the embedding
  entry (D103); no new IR kind. Copied subtrees keep their source spans (the
  output AST starts with a copy of the pattern's text store). Private variables
  are in namespace `urn:x-sxml:pattern-variable`. XNode patterns are read right
  to left (6.3.2.3): a step is a self test on the item, the steps to its left a
  condition on its parent ("/") or an ancestor ("//"); a step with predicates
  is selected again from its origin so positions count as in the formal
  definition; leading steps use child-or-top, attribute-or-top,
  namespace-or-top. Patterns with intersect/except, a filter on a parenthesized
  pattern or an RHS parenthesized pattern beyond steps and unions use the
  formal definition (some ancestor-or-self candidate $x with the item in
  $x/(EE)). Simple, atomic, map, record, array and JNode patterns test the item
  directly (6.3.3-6.3.9; sequence patterns: count, then every item).
- **Errors in patterns (6.5)**: a match expression may raise; every evaluator
  of one (APPLY_TEMPLATES 4.8, xsl:number 4.11, grouping 4.9, keys 4.10) treats
  a dynamic or type error as "no match". current() in patterns is the item
  being matched; 4.10 must provide it (the match expression keeps current() as
  written).
- **Match function**: `sxml_xslt_pattern_lower_match_function` adds a top-level
  IR function (item()) as xs:boolean whose fixed focus is its parameter, for
  template rules (callers outside a lowering machine, no locals in scope);
  inline uses lower the match expression themselves.
- **Default priority**: `sxml_xslt_pattern_compute_default_priority` (6.4,
  incl. the 4.0 union minimum, element/attribute table, atomic 0.5 - 2^-N by
  derivation depth, map, record, array, JNode rules, `##any` through a flag).
- Suite: of 19,441 pattern attributes in xslt40-test, 19,288 parse; all of them
  build a match expression; 18,916 lower with only the stylesheet's namespaces,
  372 need what a stylesheet adds (XSLT functions current/key/id/accumulators,
  145; schema or user types, 227).
- Rejected: evaluating root(.)//(EE) for every pattern (quadratic per match); a
  lowering part over pattern kinds (would need the core's node test resolution,
  which is private to `xpath_lower.c`).

**Sources**: pattern attributes in xslt40-test (third_party/xslt40-test) that
parse, build a match expression and lower.

### D119. Number formatting: one picture engine, decimal formats as settings (packet 2.9)

**Summary**: One hand-scanned picture engine in `src/format.c` serves
fn:format-integer and fn:format-number, formats numbers as exact decimal text,
and applies decimal formats as checked settings.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `src/format.c`, `src/format_internal.h`,
`src/function_library_format.c` (part `format`).

- **One engine** for fn:format-integer and fn:format-number pictures, open to
  fn:format-date (2.14: `sxml_integer_picture_parse_primary_format_token` and
  `sxml_format_integer`), xsl:number and xsl:decimal-format (4.10) and XQuery's
  decimal-format declaration (`sxml_decimal_format_apply` checks a format's
  properties: MALFORMED_INPUT for a wrong form or markers that are not
  distinct; callers map it to FODF1290, INVALID_ARGUMENT, XQST0097/8 or
  XTSE1300). Pictures are scanned by hand (D97) and parse into plain values
  that borrow the picture string; the grouping positions are rescanned while
  formatting, so parsing needs no memory.
- **Numbers as decimal text**: integers and decimals exactly, doubles and
  floats by their shortest decimal form (F&O 4.0, 4.9.5) after the percent or
  per-mille multiplication in their own type (overflow gives infinity);
  rounding half to even on the digits, any size. A mantissa that rounds up to
  10^N keeps its exponent (QT4 numberformat304). QT4
  fn-format-number-limits-007 expects Java's "4.9e-324"; sxml gives the
  shortest "5.0e-324".
- **format-integer**: digit patterns in any Nd family and radix 2 to 36, a to z
  bijective (to 2^64-1), Roman 1 to 3999, English words below 10^21 (British

  out of a sequence's range, use the token "1" (D97: no other languages or
  sequences). Title case keeps "and" and the part after a hyphen lower-case
  ("Twenty-one").

  map (keys by atomic-equal string, QName keys in a namespace ignored, others
  XPTY0004; values coerced to xs:string). The static context's formats (D104)

### D120. Value templates (packet 4.3)

**Summary**: The `grammars/value_template` grammar inherits the XPath grammar,
and `sxml_xslt_build_value_template_ast` builds a value template as a string
template AST, finding XTSE0370 and XTSE0350 after a syntax error.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D97, D102 and D111.

- **Grammar** `grammars/value_template` inherits `grammars/xpath`:
  `value_template` (the XPATH root) with field body `value_template_body`
  (STRING_TEMPLATE), parts `value_template_fixed_part`
  (STRING_TEMPLATE_FIXED_PART) and the XPath `enclosed_expression`. Its own
  `src/scanner.c` wraps the shared query scanner and appends two tokens after
  the shared list (which is untouched): the fixed part (5.6: `{{`, `}}`; a
  backquote and "(:" are text) and a zero-width start token, so the body exists
  for a zero-length template.

  `src/xslt_value_template_internal.h` (the packet named no header; the

  describe_payload hook that decodes the template's own fixed parts; a fixed
  part of an XPath string template inside a variable part keeps the XPath
  decoder (told apart by the body's last child, the variable part being
  walked). The AST equals that of `` `...` `` but for spans.

  scan (fixed parts, string literals, comments, nested brackets and string
  templates; nesting up to 64 in one word) finds XTSE0370 (an unescaped `}` in

### D120b. The XML and XHTML output methods (packet 3.3)

**Summary**: The serializer splits into parts, and `src/serialize_xml.c`
implements the XML and XHTML methods: character pipeline, pull-based sequence
normalization, namespace declarations, indentation, XHTML and Canonical XML
rules.

Recorded 2026-10-17 as a second D120 (4.3 has D120); renamed at the Phase 2
gate (D151). `src/serialize_internal.h` splits the serializer into parts:
`src/serialize.c` keeps the output stream and buffer, the parameter checks, the
character pipeline, sequence normalization, the adaptive method and the
dispatch; `src/serialize_xml.c` has the XML and XHTML methods and the node
writer the adaptive method uses. Packet 3.4's HTML, text, JSON and CSV parts
build on the same internal interface.

- **Dispatch** (D106 follow-up): HTML, text, JSON and CSV return
  UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE until 3.4; parameters C can say but XDM cannot
  (enumerations out of range, ill-formed UTF-8, name 0, a character map
  codepoint twice or not an XML Char) are INVALID_ARGUMENT for every method;
  indent-unit, doctype-system, doctype-public and html-version values the spec
  forbids are SEPM0016.
- **Character pipeline** (Serialization 4.0, section 4): `sxml_serializer`
  writes markup, text, attribute values, URI attribute values and CDATA
  sections. Text and attribute values go through the character map (sorted
  once, binary search), then `sxml_unicode_normalize` (D107; the serialize.h
  form maps onto unicode_internal.h's, fully-normalized as NFC plus SERE0012
  for a construct that starts with a composing character) on each unmapped
  segment, then escaping, line endings and the encoding into a 512-byte staging
  area. References are `&#xHEX;`; C0 and C1 controls, NEL and LINE SEPARATOR
  are always references in text and attributes (also with version 1.0: XML
  1.1's repertoire, QT4 K2-Serialization-7, Serialization-xml-27 to -31); a
  character the encoding lacks is a reference there and SERE0008 in markup.
  UTF-16 is big endian; byte-order-mark writes EF BB BF or FE FF.
- **Sequence normalization** is a pull iterator (`sxml_sequence_normalizer`)
  that never builds the result tree: frames flatten arrays and JNode values,
  atomic items are cast to text joined by a space or the item separator,
  documents give their children, text is merged in a heap buffer. SEPM0004
  (doctype-system or standalone with text or several elements at the top) runs
  the iterator once more first.
- **Namespaces**: each element's declarations are computed against a stack of
  written bindings: its in-scope namespaces (minus xml) plus what its own and
  its attributes' names need, declared where the written bindings differ,
  `xmlns=""` where a default goes out of scope, and `xmlns:p=""` only with
  undeclare-prefixes and version 1.1 (SEPM0010 with 1.0). XHTML with HTML5
  applies prefix normalization (XHTML, SVG, MathML elements unprefixed; their
  prefixes dropped unless an attribute of an ancestor-or-self uses them, Issue
  2821). Canonical XML uses the same rule (it is C14N 1.1's namespace axis) and
  sorts declarations and attributes by heapsort (no recursion, O(n log n)).
- **Indentation** (5.1.4, 6.1.5): an element's content is indented only when it
  has element, comment or PI children and no text other than whitespace, its
  name is not in suppress-indentation (XHTML: also without regard to case), it
  has no xml:space="preserve", it is not a formatted or inline HTML element and
  has no inline child, and its parent is indented itself, so nothing below
  mixed or suppressed content moves. Whitespace-only text is dropped where
  whitespace is added. indent-unit defaults to two spaces; indent-attributes
  puts each further attribute on its own line. Newlines between top-level nodes
  and after the declaration only when indenting; none otherwise (QT4
  Serialization-xml-01, -xhtml-72).
- **XHTML** (section 6): html-version defaults to 5.0; minimized tags only for
  elements expected to be empty (`<br/>` with HTML5, `<br />` before),
  `<p></p>` otherwise; `<!DOCTYPE html>` before an html document element with
  HTML5 and no doctype-system; include-content-type (default yes) adds `<meta
  charset="ENC"/>` (HTML5) or the http-equiv form (media type text/html by
  default) as head's first child and drops existing charset or Content-Type
  meta children; escape-uri-attributes (default yes) applies URI escaping to
  the attributes of appendix D.
- **Canonical XML**: UTF-8, LF, no declaration, doctype, CDATA, character maps
  or indentation; start-end tag pairs; line feeds around nodes outside the
  document element; SERE0024 for top-level text, more or fewer than one
  element, or a relative namespace URI.
- **Adaptive nodes** (D82) are written by the same XML writer with the default
  parameters; a stored parentless namespace node (D98) is written from its name
  (the prefix) and content (the URI).
- Not done here: `sxml_serialization_parameter_reader` (declared by D106) has
  no definition yet; it belongs with fn:serialize (3.4). Not checked:
  SERE0005/SERE0006 (names and characters of the XML version), comments with
  "--" (SERE0003). The CLI's `--method` stays adaptive until 3.12.

### D121. The XQuery front end (packet 3.2)

**Summary**: `sxml_xquery_build_ast` is the XQuery parser part on the XPath
walker, with the XQuery tables, decoding of literals and direct constructor
text, and static checks in its finish hook.

Recorded 2026-10-17, extending D29, D59 and D111. `src/xquery_parse.c` defines
`sxml_xquery_build_ast`: the XQuery parser part on the XPath walker;
`sxml_grammar_xquery` joins the `sxml` link line.

- **Tables and tokens**: the 66 node types and 23 grammar fields XQuery adds
  (24 with MODULE, D111); the module's child takes field MODULE. `mode` and
  `kind` tokens become the keyword detail, a decimal-format property name its
  detail, the other token fields flags. The `empty` token of
  order_specification is claimed before the XPath rules, which read `empty` as
  the empty-sequence occurrence.
- **Decoding** (describe_payload): XQuery string literals and BracedURILiterals
  replace references; direct element text also "{{" and "}}"; attribute value
  text also the doubled delimiter, read from the DIRECT_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE node
  (the first node containing the text on the parent chain of the last added
  node), then attribute value normalization (literal tab, line feed, carriage
  return to a space). Every decoded text (also CDATA, comments, PI content,
  pragma contents, string constructor characters and string template fixed
  parts) gets the end-of-line handling of A.3.3.1. A reference to a character
  outside XML 1.0 Char, or above U+10FFFF, is XQST0090. "(# r #)" has an empty
  PRAGMA_CONTENTS.
- **Checks** (finish_node): XQST0118 and XQST0040/XQST0071 on names as written
  (pairwise up to 32 attributes, else a heapsort of node indices in one work
  array from the AST's allocator); namespace declaration attributes are
  flagged, XQST0022 for an enclosed expression, XQST0070 for the reserved
  bindings of 4.12.1.2, XQST0085 for a prefix bound to "" (XML Names 1.0, xgc:
  xml-version); BOUNDARY_WHITESPACE on text written as whitespace only with no
  CDATA section or text next to it; a version other than 1.0, 3.0, 3.1, 4.0 is
  XQST0031, an encoding that is no EncName XQST0087; a string field name in a
  record declaration annotated `%constructor` (unprefixed or
  Q{http://www.w3.org/2012/xquery}) is XPST0003, the third D29 false accept. A
  direct comment ending in "-" is already rejected by the scanner.
- **Left to later packets**: duplicate expanded names under different prefixes
  (XQST0040, lowering), the prolog's XQST0070 for namespace declarations,
  imports and default namespaces and its duplicate declarations (3.10), a
  prefixed `%constructor`.
- **Results** (a scratch harness over the case loader of
  `tools/qt4-parse-check.py`, which itself checks only the grammar): all 43,663
  valid XQ40 queries build, 70 of them with the static error their test expects
  (XQST0022 16, XQST0031 5, XQST0040 4, XQST0070 8, XQST0071 9, XQST0085 5,
  XQST0087 4, XQST0090 13, XQST0118 6); the 145 parsable library modules build;
  all 772 XPST0003 queries fail statically.

**Sources**: valid XQ40 queries, parsable library modules and XPST0003 queries
through the C entry, a scratch harness over the case loader
(`tools/qt4-parse-check.py`).

### D122. Date and time functions (packet 2.8)

**Summary**: `src/function_library_temporal.c` adds timezone adjustment,
parts-of-dateTime, build-dateTime, seconds, unix-dateTime, civil-timezone
without a database, and a hand-written parse-ietf-date scanner.

Recorded 2026-10-17. New part `src/function_library_temporal.c` (test
`function_library_temporal`): adjust-dateTime/date/time-to-timezone,
civil-timezone, days-in-month, parts-of-dateTime, build-dateTime, seconds,
duration-to-seconds, unix-dateTime and parse-ietf-date.
`src/operator_temporal.c` is unchanged.

- **Gregorian components** (PR 1481): the seven `*-from-dateTime` rows of
  `src/function_library_context.c` (2.12's file, edited because no other packet
  runs on it; two hunks) take the union of the eight Gregorian types and give
  the empty sequence for a component the type lacks (absent components are zero
  in the datum).
- **Shifts**: a dateTime or date moves by whole minutes through
  `sxml_operator_make_temporal_value` (D72: every int64_t year, FODT0001
  beyond); a time moves within its day. The implicit timezone and the clock
  come from the dynamic context, read once per evaluation (D88).
- **build-dateTime** declares `map(*)?`: the row text cannot spell the record's
  optional fields, so the body coerces each field by XPath 4.0, 3.4.3:
  xs:untypedAtomic cast, an integral xs:decimal relabeled to xs:integer,
  xs:double/xs:float cast to xs:decimal (seconds only), an xs:duration without
  months relabeled to xs:dayTimeDuration; other types, extra keys or two items
  are XPTY0004. Then FODT0005 (field set), FORG0001 (ranges, gMonthDay against
  1972), FODT0003 (timezone). parts-of-dateTime returns a plain map with the
  record's keys in order.
- **Seconds** keep nine fraction digits, truncated like casts (D36), so
  `seconds(3.14159265358979323846) eq
  xs:dayTimeDuration('PT3.14159265358979323846S')`; fn:seconds builds the
  duration from the decimal's digits (FODT0002 beyond int64_t seconds), not by
  duration arithmetic, which rounds.
- **unix-dateTime**: milliseconds beyond uint64_t are FODT0001.
- **civil-timezone** (D97, no database): no place gives the implicit timezone
  (the default place is taken to be one whose civil timezone it is); "UTC",
  "Etc/UTC", "GMT", "Etc/GMT" give PT0S; any other place FODT0004.
- **parse-ietf-date**: hand-written scanner of the grammar of 9.10.1 (D97),
  ASCII case-insensitive, longest names first; a tzoffset of one to four digits
  is H, HH, HMM, HHMM, with a colon minutes are 0 or 2 digits; hour 24 only as
  24:00:00 (next day); FORG0010 otherwise.
- **Open**: fn-parts-of-dateTime 8/20 (assert-type needs the named record type,
  Proposed); civil-timezone 4/9 (D97); days-in-month-006/007 need
  fn:format-integer (2.9).
