### D124. IR extensions for try/catch and constructors (packet 3.6b)

**Summary**: The IR gains adders and accessors for name tests, catch clauses
and namespace bindings, and node constructions gain `name_namespaces` and
`construction_flags`, which the evaluator, verifier and text form honour.

Recorded 2026-10-17; accepts the IR proposals of D109 and D110
(`src/ir_internal.h`, `src/ir.c`, `src/ir_verify.c`).

- **Adders**: `sxml_ir_unit_add_name_tests(unit, sxml_ir_name_test_view,
  &list)`, `sxml_ir_unit_add_catch_clauses(unit, view, &list)` and
  `sxml_ir_unit_add_namespace_bindings(unit, view, &list)` work as
  `sxml_ir_unit_add_sort_keys`, with accessors `sxml_ir_unit_get_name_tests`,
  `_get_catch_clauses`, `_get_namespace_bindings`. A LOCAL_NAME_WILDCARD test's
  local name is interned in the item heap's name pool (pool text never moves),
  so callers may free theirs; an empty one is INVALID_ARGUMENT. The static
  namespaces are one run of the same array.
- **`sxml_ir_node_construction`** gains `name_namespaces` (a binding run; empty
  means the unit's static namespaces; lowering gives the static namespaces
  extended by enclosing direct constructors, for QT4 Constr-compelem-compname)
  and `uint32_t construction_flags`
  (`SXML_IR_CONSTRUCTION_NO_PRESERVE_NAMESPACES`, `_NO_INHERIT_NAMESPACES`,
  `_PRESERVES_TYPES`, `_XSLT_RULES`; 0 = construction strip, copy-namespaces
  preserve, inherit, XQuery rules). Lowering (3.9, 3.10) sets them per
  constructor from the prolog; XSLT (4.x) sets XSLT_RULES on literal result
  elements and xsl:element/xsl:document.
- **Evaluator** (`src/evaluator_construct.c`): flags pick the copy request of
  content nodes (no-preserve, no-inherit, keep annotations), xs:anyType for
  elements under PRESERVES_TYPES, XSLT rules (REPLACE duplicates, XTDE codes)
  for ELEMENT and DOCUMENT; SHALLOW_COPY drops the element's namespaces under
  NO_PRESERVE (copy-namespaces "no") and keeps its type under PRESERVES_TYPES.
  Names given as strings resolve with `name_namespaces`. `src/evaluator_try.c`
  reads clauses through the accessors.
- **Verifier**: TRY_CATCH needs a body and clauses or a finally body; each
  clause one or more name tests of a known kind, an error details slot of the
  function (bound in its handler only) and a handler. The constructor kinds and
  SHALLOW_COPY: fields the kind does not use must be empty (kinds as in the
  header), lists in range, known flags; a NONE name or value is allowed (the
  empty sequence: `attribute {()} {}` raises at run time, `namespace {()}
  {...}` is the default namespace). Only APPLY_TEMPLATES stays reserved.
- **Text form**: constructors print name, value, then `(namespaces p="u"
  ""="d")`, `(name-namespaces ...)` and the flag words on one line, then the
  content; TRY_CATCH prints body, `(catch (TESTS) $SLOT HANDLER)` per clause
  and `(finally BODY)` (golden text in `tests/ir_test.c`). Dumps of the other
  kinds are unchanged.
- Test units of `tests/evaluator_try_test.c` and
  `tests/evaluator_construct_test.c` use the adders; all of them pass the
  verifier (checked once in a scratch build, after giving `shallow_others` one
  content expression per copy: the IR is a tree).

### D125. fn:divide-decimals and the precision it supports (packet 2.7)

**Summary**: `sxml_decimal_divide_to_precision` computes `divide-decimals`
exactly with libmpdec's truncating division, adjusting the precision to fit
`maximum_digit_count`, and returns a map with xs:decimal "quotient" and
"remainder".

Recorded 2026-10-17. `sxml_decimal_divide_to_precision` (`src/decimal.c`), part
`numeric` row `divide-decimals`.

- **Method**: the divisor's power of ten is shifted by -precision (exact, no
  digits move) and libmpdec's truncating `mpd_qdivint` and `mpd_qrem` give
  quotient \* 10^precision and the remainder value - quotient \* divisor in one
  exact step each (F&O 4.0, section 4.3.1); the quotient has the sign of value
  / divisor, the remainder that of the value.
- **Precision range** (the rules' "adjusted to the nearest value supported"): a
  positive precision is lowered until quotient and remainder both fit
  `maximum_digit_count` (bounds from the adjusted exponents and the divisor's
  digits), to 0 at least; one below every digit of the quotient is raised to
  just below it (the quotient is 0 either way). So `divide-decimals(10, 3,
  100_000)` gives 9,997 decimal places at the default limit; an integer
  quotient wider than the limit is FOAR0002; a zero divisor FOAR0001.
- **Result**: a map with keys "quotient" and "remainder" (xs:decimal), row
  result type `record(quotient as xs:decimal, remainder as xs:decimal)`. It is
  not annotated with fn:division-record: no static context knows the F&O named
  record types yet (the Proposed item of D122; QT4 divide-decimals-019 to -021
  and fn-random-number-generator-35a to -37a wait for it).

**Sources**: decimal places of divide-decimals(10, 3, 100_000) at the default
maximum_digit_count.

### D126. Lowering XQuery expressions: FLWOR, typeswitch, switch, try/catch (packet 3.7)

**Summary**: Lowering part `xquery` lowers FLWOR as clause segments joined by
tuple arrays, typeswitch and switch as CONDITIONAL chains, and try/catch as
TRY_CATCH, with no new IR kind.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D55 for these kinds. `src/xquery_lower.c` is
lowering part `xquery` (SXML_LANGUAGE_XQUERY only, D103); no IR kind added.
Contract in `src/xquery_lower_internal.h`.

- **FLWOR** replaces the core's FLWOR for XQuery. Clauses between two tuple
  stream clauses are a clause segment: for = MAP (position slot,
  ALLOWING_EMPTY), let = LET (destructuring as D113), where = CONDITIONAL, one
  frame per binding or clause. A segment ending at a tuple stream clause
  returns tuple arrays (one member per live slot variable, innermost of each
  name; constants and globals are not packed); then order by = SORT with each
  key lowered over the members unpacked from the SORT's focus, count = the
  position slot of the unpacking MAP, while = fn:take-while with a closure
  fn($tuple, $position) { boolean(C) } (no condition evaluated after the first
  false). The closure captures every visible variable the condition references
  (overcapture is harmless) and, only when lowering it read the focus, the
  FLWOR's focus parts (three slots kept after the captures, bound by LETs at
  the closure's start). A MAP over the result unpacks the members with LOOKUP
  before the next segment.
- **order by**: empty least unless written (the prolog default is 3.10's);
  collation literals resolved against the static base URI; codepoint is NONE,
  html-ascii-case-insensitive and UCA URIs are kept (the evaluator's SORT still
  raises FOCH0002 for them, D116 Proposed), anything else is XQST0076. "stable"
  changes nothing (SORT is stable).
- **trace** clause: lowered (static errors stand) as the never-taken branch of
  a CONDITIONAL; trace output is implementation-defined and its errors must not
  fail the FLWOR (4.13.10).
- **typeswitch**: operand once; CONDITIONAL chain over INSTANCE_OF (a union
  case is a CONDITIONAL of the type tests); case variables bound to the
  operand. **switch**: switch value = coerce(fn:data(comparand),
  xs:anyAtomicType?) or true(); a case operand matches when its atomized value
  is empty and the switch value is, or some item is fn:deep-equal to it; each
  case's tests sit in the previous case's else branch (2.6.5).
- **try/catch**: TRY_CATCH (D109, D124); unprefixed error names use the default
  element namespace; `$err:` variables the handler references are LOOKUPs of
  the details slot, `$err:map` the slot, stack-trace and additional `()`.
- ordered/unordered: their content. Extension expressions: pragma names must
  resolve (XPST0081); every pragma is ignored; none and no expression is
  XQST0079. validate: XQST0075 (D97). String constructors: fn:string-join of
  the parts, interpolations string-join(E, " ").
- **Entry points** `sxml_xquery_lower` / `sxml_xquery_compile` (internal, for
  tests and drivers until 3.12): a main module without prolog declarations
  (UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE otherwise, 3.10). Group by and the windows are
  UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE; 3.8 adds them as tuple stream clauses in
  `finish_segment` (the tuple layout is in the FLWOR frame's locals).
- Measured with a scratch harness (the QT4 driver with the XPath API compiling
  through `sxml_xquery_compile`), XQ40: every failure left in prod-ForClause,
  LetClause, WhereClause, OrderByClause, CountClause, WhileClause,
  TypeswitchExpr, SwitchExpr, ExtensionExpr, StringConstructor is a node
  constructor (3.9) or a prolog (3.10), but for three (fn:message missing,
  `local:` undeclared, one driver assertion).

### D127. Lowering node constructors (packet 3.9)

**Summary**: Lowering part `construct` lowers XQuery direct and computed
constructors to the IR constructor kinds, extending the static context with
namespace declaration attributes and turning prolog setters into construction
flags.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D110 and D124 for XQuery.
`src/xquery_lower_construct.c` is lowering part `construct`
(SXML_LANGUAGE_XQUERY, D103) for the DIRECT_\* and COMPUTED_\* kinds; no IR
kind or header change.

- **Direct elements**: ELEMENT_CONSTRUCTOR whose content is a SEQUENCE of one
  atom per attribute and piece of content in order (D110); literal text and
  CDATA are xs:string constants; boundary whitespace is dropped unless the
  prolog says boundary-space preserve. Names are xs:QName constants (prefix
  kept) resolved while lowering (XPST0081); two attributes with one expanded
  name are XQST0040.
- **Namespace declaration attributes** extend the static context through the
  embedding entry (D103), not new machinery: the element's attributes and
  content are lowered with a copy of the static context whose bindings are its
  declarations followed by the current ones, so the core resolves names inside
  enclosed expressions (and nested constructors) with them. An element, direct
  or computed, sends as namespace bindings the declarations of its own and
  every enclosing direct constructor (innermost per prefix, found by walking
  the frame chain), so they are in scope whatever copy-namespaces says; a
  computed name inside one gets the extended bindings as name_namespaces. A
  computed namespace constructor binds no prefix statically.
- **Attribute values**: "" for none, the constant for text alone, the enclosed
  expression's atom alone (the evaluator joins with spaces); mixed parts are
  joined with `||`, each enclosed part as a TEXT_CONSTRUCTOR of its value
  (atomized and space-joined, empty gives ""), so no library call is needed.
- **Computed** constructors: a literal name is a constant (xs:QName for element
  and attribute, xs:string for PI target and namespace prefix), a name
  expression an atom; content is the atom of the enclosed expression (value, or
  an ATOM content expression for element and document). Direct comments and PIs
  are constructors of constants.
- **Prolog setters** (boundary-space, construction, copy-namespaces) are read
  from the module's PROLOG node and become construction_flags of element and
  document constructors; they take effect once 3.10 lets prologs through
  `sxml_xquery_lower` (D126 rejects them now).
- Results (scratch harness: xpath.c compiling with sxml_xquery_compile, as
  3.7's): the 13 constructor test sets 0 to 932 of 1,165 passed, 59 not run
  (dependencies); of the 174 failures and errors, 167 are queries with a prolog
  (3.10). The 7 others are not lowering's: URI whitespace of "Q{ _ _ }x" in the
  evaluator (2), `local:` not predeclared (3.10, 3.12), `text {''}` (the D110
  deviation) and a missing function (3).

**Sources**: the 13 constructor test sets before and after, a scratch harness
compiling with sxml_xquery_compile.

### D128. The HTML, text, JSON and CSV methods; fn:serialize (packet 3.4)

**Summary**: The HTML, text, JSON and CSV serialization methods and
fn:serialize run on the one existing serializer pipeline, each method choosing
an escape style, with HTML as a mode of the XML node writer.

Recorded 2026-10-17. Every method runs on the 3.3 pipeline (D120b); no second
writer or escaper was added.

- **Escape styles**: `sxml_escape_style` grows HTML, NONE (text), JSON and CSV;
  a method picks one in `sxml_serializer_resolve_pipeline`, so character maps,
  normalization, line endings and the encoding apply to all of them in one
  place. A new character context RAW_TEXT (glossary `raw_text`) writes mapped,
  normalized, unescaped text (HTML script and style; SERE0008 for an
  unencodable character). Character maps now apply to every method but adaptive
  and the canonical forms (section 12).
- **HTML** is a mode of the XML node writer in `src/serialize_xml.c`
  (`is_html`, with `has_html_rules` for what XHTML and HTML share);
  `src/serialize_html.c` holds what HTML adds: void and HTML 4 empty elements
  (one table, also used by XHTML), boolean attributes (the HTML 4.01 and HTML5
  lists), raw text elements, processing instructions (`<?t d>` before HTML5,
  SERE0015 for ">"; `<!--?t d?-->` with HTML5). Requested version:
  html-version, else version, else 5.0. No-namespace elements are HTML elements
  (unknown names inline, as span); with HTML5 also XHTML-namespace ones
  (unprefixed, prefix normalization of D120b); others are XML islands. Doctype
  `<!DOCTYPE html ...>`. SERE0014 for controls before HTML5.
- **Text and CSV** (`src/serialize_text.c`): text writes the string value of
  the result tree with escape style NONE. CSV takes a map (rows, columns) or a
  sequence of arrays; members atomize (one-member arrays unwrapped, nodes by
  string value), else SERE0025; a field is quoted when it, or a replacement of
  one of its mapped characters, holds the separator, the quote or a line end;
  separator equal to the quote or a line end is SEPM0016.
- **JSON** (`src/serialize_json.c`): frames on a heap stack (D71); nodes by a
  sub-serialization (`sxml_serializer_write_node_as_string`, which calls only
  the XML and text methods, so no cycle); doubles by their xs:double cast text,
  NaN null, infinities 1e9999 (SERE0020 when canonical); canonical: keys sorted
  by UTF-16 units (heapsort), numbers as ECMAScript from the shortest digits;
  SERE0022 checked by sorting only when some key is not string-like;
  indentation off with json-lines.
- **SERE0006** (left by D120b): XML and XHTML with version 1.0 (the default)
  raise it for C0 controls in text and attributes; 1.1 writes references.
  **SERE0003** for comments with "--" or a final "-" and PIs with "?>" (XML,
  XHTML). A character map may map any XML 1.1 Char (U+0001 included;
  serialize.h says XML 1.0's production, D120b already writes the 1.1
  repertoire).
- **Parameter reader** (`src/serialize_parameters.c`): both forms decode each
  parameter into one value and assign it the same way. Two arenas: a read fills
  the spare one and swaps on success. Map: unknown string keys are XPTY0004
  (F&O 4.0 option conventions, QT4 serialize-xml-107-40, deviating from
  serialize.h's "ignored"), a QName key in no namespace XPTY0004, in a
  namespace ignored; nodes atomize for character map values. Document: unknown
  output:\* children, attributes other than value (character-map: character,
  map-string), non-whitespace text and children in no namespace are SEPM0017;
  two children with one name SEPM0019; element lists use the default namespace
  (the spec's example), method names do not. fn:serialize
  (`src/function_library_serialize.c`) skips the encoding phase: UTF-16 is
  written as UTF-8, ISO-8859-1 bytes decoded, no byte order mark.
- Not done: SERE0005 (names of the XML version), the text of nodes inside the
  JSON method beyond the four node methods, records omitting empty entries in
  JSON (no record marker on maps).

### D129. Date formatting: the picture engine over format-integer (packet 2.14)

**Summary**: Date and time formatting reuses the format-integer picture engine
for each variable marker, scans the picture in three passes, supports the AD
and ISO calendars and English names only.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D97, D119 and D122. `src/format_date.c` with the
module header `src/format_date_internal.h`, part
`src/function_library_format_date.c` (part `format_date`), test `format_date`.

- **One engine**: a variable marker's first presentation modifier is a primary
  format token of the D119 engine; a minimum width widens the digit pattern
  (optional signs from the right, then prepended digits of the family) and
  parses it again; non-digit tokens are padded with spaces. Fractional seconds
  parse the reversed token (so `[f#99]` is FOFD1340) and write the fraction's
  digits directly with the effect of 9.9.4.5's reversal (`[f,*-2]` of .006 is
  "0", as QT4 expects).
- **Scan**: three passes over the picture (syntax FOFD1340, then components
  FOFD1350, then writing), so a rejected picture writes nothing. Whitespace in
  a marker is dropped; the last comma starts the width; a lone "]" is FOFD1340.
- **Calendar arithmetic** on a year of the same 400-year cycle, so day of week,
  ISO week (W) and week in month (w, the month of the week's Thursday) hold for
  every int64_t year; W, w and F's numbers follow ISO 8601 in both calendars.
- **Calendars and languages** (D97): AD (default; year 0 is 1 BC, eras AD/BC)
  and ISO (absolute year, era "-"). Other designators and any name in a
  namespace format as AD after "[Calendar: AD]"; a name in no namespace that is
  no designator, or no EQName, is FOFD1340. A prefix is not resolved (no
  statically known namespaces at run time): any prefix counts as a namespace. A
  non-English $language gives "[Language: en]"; the empty sequence or "" gives
  none (the default language is not read: English whatever the host names).
  $place is ignored.
- **Names**: English months and days, conventional day abbreviations (Tues,
  Weds, Thurs/Thur) before cutting at the maximum width; am/pm; AD, BC, ISO
  always in capitals. Title-case words capitalize after a hyphen ("Twenty-One",
  QT4 format-date-en125), unlike format-integer's "Twenty-one" (D119). Timezone
  names need a database (D97): [ZN] and other tokens use 01:01; ZZ gives
  military letters, "J" without a timezone.
- Measured (debug driver, XP40): fn-format-date 20 to 124 of 124 run,
  fn-format-time 19 to 94 of 94, fn-format-dateTime 5 to 80 of 80.

### D130. Elements to maps and back (packet 2.10)

**Summary**: fn:element-to-map, fn:element-to-map-plan and fn:map-to-element
work without recursion over node indices, frame stacks and XDM maps, on untyped
input only, following QT4 where the text leaves choices open.

Recorded 2026-10-17. `src/function_library_element_map.c` (part `element_map`)
implements fn:element-to-map-plan, fn:element-to-map and fn:map-to-element (F&O
4.0, section 14.6).

- **No recursion, no new machinery** (D71). fn:element-to-map keeps one element
  slot per node of the subtree and walks the node indices twice: in document
  order it chooses layouts (a child is converted only when its parent's layout
  converts children, so a plan's `error` below an `xml` element is never
  reached), in reverse document order it builds values, whose children are then
  done. fn:element-to-map-plan walks the same ranges once. fn:map-to-element
  keeps a stack of frames and sends tree builder events to a new arena tree
  that destroys itself (D40, D110); the `xml` layout parses through the
  document loader and copies with `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node`. Grouping,
  duplicate keys and plan lookup use XDM maps (D37) as indices, nothing of its
  own.
- **Untyped input only**: sxml is not schema-aware, so the schema-based layouts
  (14.6.6) and the nilled forms on the element-to-map side never apply; xsi
  attributes are ignored, and plan analysis skips xsi:nil="true" elements as
  14.6.4 says.
- **Choices the text leaves open**, following QT4: without a plan entry,
  attributes stay xs:untypedAtomic while simple element content gets the
  inferred type (14.6.3, `<a x="1">2</a>` gives `{"a":{"@x":"1",
  "#content":2}}`); a cast failure under a prescribed type is FOJS0010 even
  with a fallback; a leading zero after an optional sign makes a string. In
  fn:map-to-element, matching a value against a layout looks one level down
  only (list members against the child name's candidates by form), so it needs
  no recursion; elements in a namespace from `Q{uri}` keys use the default
  namespace, attributes made-up prefixes `ns0`, `ns1`, ...; prefixes of
  `p:local` keys resolve against the static namespaces of the innermost unit
  (as the static base URI, D91).
- QT4: fn-element-to-map 179/181 run, fn-element-to-map-plan 20/20,
  fn-map-to-element 223/228. Open: element-to-map-101 and -507 assert `?a?…` on
  the context value, which the driver does not set (XPDY0002);
  map-to-element-014 and -021 expect XQuery's decoding of `&amp;` in string
  literals under XP40; -120 and -121 need fn:serialize.

### D131. Resources, the evaluation environment, lexical decimal formats and collations (packet 2.12)

**Summary**: The processor's document loader carries the evaluation environment
(resolver, trace sink, default language, environment variables) for resource
functions, and units carry lexical decimal formats, collation bindings and the
default collation.

Recorded 2026-10-17. Implements D104 in `src/processor.c`,
`src/processor_internal.h`, `src/xpath.c`, new part
`src/function_library_resource.c`; accepts three Proposed items (2.6's range
fast path, 2.9's decimal formats, 2.13's default collation).

- **Evaluation environment** (glossary): what library functions read from the
  host beyond fn:doc, carried by the processor's document loader of each
  evaluation: resolver (dynamic context's, else processor's), trace sink
  (same), default language ("en" when empty), environment variables. Natives
  reach it with `sxml_processor_get_evaluation_environment(dynamic_context)` /
  `sxml_processor_document_loader_from_dynamic_context`; NULL for a dynamic
  context the processor did not make (unit tests): nothing available, no
  variables, "en", trace discarded. The loader also retrieves TEXT/BINARY bytes
  (`_retrieve`/`_release`, BYTES only, else INVALID_ARGUMENT) and keeps
  collections per kind and absolute URI for the evaluation (fn:collection is
  deterministic; SEQUENCE only).
- **Text decoding** (F&O 4.0, 17.1.5, after bin:infer-encoding): candidate =
  resource's charset, else the encoding option; no candidate: BOM decides, else
  UTF-8 (bad bytes FOUT1200); a candidate skips a BOM that agrees ("UTF-16"
  without BOM is big-endian) and decodes a disagreeing one as characters (so it
  fails, FOUT1190); UTF-8, UTF-16LE/BE, ISO-8859-1, US-ASCII (the XML parser's
  names). Non-XML characters are FOUT1190; `fallback` gives U+FFFD;
  `normalize-newlines` maps CR LF and CR to LF; -lines always normalizes and
  rejects that key (XPTY0004, QT4 40-014); -available is false for
  FOUT1170/1190/1200. fn:json-doc is the text (any codepoint) handed to the
  fn:parse-json row, found by name in the XPath part list, with its options. No
  media-type handling.
- **fn:trace and fn:message** stay in the error part (the library tests list
  parts explicitly); both nondeterministic and context-dependent.
  `sxml_stream_trace_sink` writes `label: value` lines (adaptive, " ").
  `sxml_collation_is_supported` is 2.13's (D116).
- **Static context checks** (xpath.c): decimal formats (kinds once,
  `sxml_decimal_format_apply`, names distinct), collation bindings (absolute,
  not already known, target supported), default collation known; dynamic
  context: xs:language, distinct UTF-8 environment variables. Breaches are
  INVALID_ARGUMENT.
- **Lexical decimal formats and collations**: `sxml_ir_static_context` (decimal
  formats, default collation URI, bindings) is copied into the unit by
  `sxml_ir_unit_set_static_context`, set by lowering from the new
  `sxml_xpath_static_context.unit_static_context`;
  `sxml_dynamic_context_get_running_unit` gives the unit of the innermost IR
  task (as the static base URI). fn:format-number resolves names (xs:QName;
  string QName with the unit's static namespaces, EQName, NCName, spaces
  trimmed; FODF1280 otherwise), the named or unnamed format then the map's
  properties; the collation resolver tries the unit's bindings first and its
  default for "", fn:default-collation returns it.
- **Range fast path** (2.6's patch) in `src/evaluator.c`; the step-bound test
  uses a quantifier (a concatenation of a long range is not charged up front
  either: `0 = (1 to 10^11, 2)` runs unbounded; left as found).
- Measured (release, XP40): fn-unparsed-text 54 to 94/94 run, -lines 39 to
  58/58, -available 7 to 57/57, unparsed-binary 16 to 21/21, json-doc 36 to
  73/77 (4 need a fallback function), collection 18 to 24/25, uri-collection
  7/7, environment-variable 6 to 12/12, available-environment-variables 2 to
  10/10, default-language 0 to 5/5, message 3 to 14/14, trace 31/31,
  format-number 252 (2.9) to 285/286. "Before" counts are at the packet's start
  (24fc6ac).

### D132. Packets start when their dependencies are committed (amends D96)

**Summary**: A packet of a later phase may start once every packet in its
"After" list is committed, while phase gates still close each phase and
re-check early work.

Recorded 2026-10-17 by the orchestrator, toward the owner's goal of working
XQuery and XSLT. A packet of a later phase may start as soon as every packet in
its "After" list is committed, whether or not it is marked "Early". The phase
gates still close each phase: a phase is done only when its gate review passes,
and gate reviews re-check the work of later-phase packets that started early.
First applied to 3.8, 3.10 and 3.13.

### D133. The built-in record types of F&O 4.0 (packet 2.6b)

**Summary**: Each function library declares the 16 nominative record types of
F&O 4.0 once in its item heap's type registry, functions return records
annotated with them, and maps coerce to them.

Recorded 2026-10-17. Accepts the Proposed items of D122 and D125.

- **One table, declared once per registry**: `src/function_library_records.c`
  lists the 16 nominative record types of F&O 4.0, appendix C (glossary
  `builtin_record_type`), each as its fn local name and the text of a
  structural record type in the specification's field order and types (a field
  whose type allows the empty sequence is optional, D7; "xs:positive-integer"
  of fn:location-record read as xs:positiveInteger).
  `sxml_function_library_initialize` declares them in the type registry of its
  item heap before any row is resolved: all names first, so fields may name
  table types, recursion included, then each type's fields from its resolved
  text. A name the registry knows already is skipped, so libraries sharing a
  heap declare once. No globals; static analysis resolves `fn:dateTime-record`
  through the registry like any named type, and rows may name them.
- **Records are annotated**: `sxml_function_library_make_record` makes a record
  of a built-in type by name (`sxml_record_make`). fn:parts-of-dateTime,
  fn:divide-decimals, fn:random-number-generator (and ?next), fn:regex,
  fn:matching-segments and its captured groups return annotated records; their
  rows name the types. The function items of a generator and of a compiled
  regex take their signatures from the record's field types, so ?take is
  `fn(xs:nonNegativeInteger) as xs:double*` (take(-1) and take(()) are
  XPTY0004) and ?next is `fn() as fn:random-number-generator-record`; fn:regex
  no longer looks its functions up in the function table.
- **Coercion to a nominative record type** (XPath 4.0, section 3.4.2): the rule
  of a structural record type, the new record annotated with the nominative
  type (`src/evaluator_function.c`), so a map coerces to fn:division-record.
  Matching stays nominative: an unannotated map is no instance.
  fn:build-dateTime keeps `map(*)?` and its own coercion (D122).
- **idiv**: a zero divisor is FOAR0001 before NaN or an infinite dividend
  (FOAR0002), so `INF idiv 0` is FOAR0001 (F&O 4.0, op:numeric-integer-divide).
- Measured (release driver, XP40, passed of cases): fn-parts-of-dateTime 8 to
  20 of 20, fn-divide-decimals 19 to 21 of 21, fn-random-number-generator 50 to
  54 of 61, fn-regex 27 to 29 of 30, fn-matching-segments 37 to 38 of 39,
  op-numeric-integer-divide 132 to 132 of 143 (wrong errors 2 to 0).

### D134. The QT4 driver for XQ40 (packet 3.13)

**Summary**: The QT4 driver runs XQ40 through a temporary XQuery adapter over
`sxml_xquery_compile`, answers module and collection queries, checks
serialization assertions, and gains an XQuery slice and per-spec gate rates.

Recorded 2026-10-17. Extends D92, D94 and D108 in `tests/qt4/driver/`.

- **XQuery adapter (temporary)**: `--spec=XQ40` compiles the test's query as an
  XQuery main module through `xquery_adapter.c` (glossary
  `qt4_xquery_adapter`): `sxml_xquery_compile` (D126) and the evaluation of
  `src/xpath.c`, behind functions with the signatures of
  `include/sxml/xquery.h` named `sxml_qt4_xquery_*`. It is the one driver file
  with `src/` headers (a PRIVATE include line in the driver's CMakeLists).
  Packet 3.12 deletes it and drops `qt4_` from the calls. Until 3.10 a prolog
  gives UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, an "error" outcome. Params, context items and
  collection queries stay XPath expressions.
- **declared="true"** (params and `$name` sources) under XQ40: bound in the
  dynamic context, not declared by the host (a host declaration of the prolog's
  name is XQST0049, D106). Under XP40 they are declared as before.
- **Modules**: the resource table answers XQUERY_MODULE with the file of a
  `<module>` of the test case whose uri is the target namespace: the one whose
  location equals the hint (as written or absolute), else the one whose file
  name is the hint's last segment, else the first; resource URI
  `file:///SUITE-PATH`. No longer a skip reason. Unused until 3.10/3.11.
- **Collection queries**: each `<query>` is evaluated (XPath, the test's
  contexts so far) and its value follows the collection's documents in
  fn:collection; no longer a skip reason.
- **Serialization assertions**: serialization-matches serializes the value with
  the query's parameters (the adapter gives XQuery's default, method xml; XPath
  runs use the same) through `sxml_serialize_sequence` and applies fn:matches
  with the flags (letters only) to the text; output that is not UTF-8 fails.
  assert-serialization-error judges an error raised by the evaluation, else by
  serializing, like `error`. assert-serialization (only in comments of the
  suite) stays unsupported. assert-xml is unchanged (nodes through the adaptive
  method, which writes nodes as the XML method). Feature `serialization` is
  satisfied.
- **Slices**: `qt4/xquery-slice` runs `tests/qt4/xquery-slice.txt`
  (`--spec=XQ40`, 186 XQ-only cases that pass now, up to four per test set with
  five or more such passes, spread evenly) against
  `tests/qt4/xquery-slice-baseline.txt` (186, only goes up);
  `run-slice-test.cmake` takes SLICE_FILE and SPEC. Golden `qt4/run_xquery` and
  new cases in run_pass, run_fail cover each new feature.
- **Report**: `tools/conformance-report.py` writes the D95 gate rate
  (in_scope_passed / in_scope) per spec and, for XQ40 with an XP40 run in the
  same directory, the XQ-only rate (run cases whose XP40 outcome is "skip:

### D135. Prologs: the static context, declared functions and variables (packet 3.10)

**Summary**: The XQuery prolog is read into one `sxml_xpath_static_context`;
declared functions become one IR function per arity, and variables become
initializer functions computed in dependency order, only when reached.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D55 and D101 for XQuery main modules.
`src/xquery_static.c` (`src/xquery_static_internal.h`) reads the prolog into
one `sxml_xpath_static_context`; `src/xquery_prolog.c` lowers the module and
now holds `sxml_xquery_lower` / `sxml_xquery_compile` (moved from
`src/xquery_lower.c`); `src/evaluator_global.c` computes globals. No new IR
kind, no header change, no machinery beside the core's.

- **Static context**: namespace declarations and the default element namespace
  (prefix 0) first, then the host's bindings, then `local` and `output` (XQuery
  predeclares them); variables: the host's, then the prolog's (global n); a
  function table finds declared functions, then the host's table. Duplicates
  are found by sorting (XQST0033, XQST0049 also against host declarations,
  XQST0034 for overlapping arity ranges); setters and the context value
  declaration at most once (XQST0068, 0038, 0032, 0067, 0065, 0069, 0055,
  0099); XQST0070, XQST0066, XQST0039, XQST0148, XQST0045 (function names and
  annotations in reserved namespaces, the XQuery namespace for unprefixed
  annotations; so `%updating` is rejected, D97), XQST0106/XQST0116, XQST0009
  (schema import, D97), XQST0038 (unsupported default collation). External
  functions are XPST0017. Module imports and item type/record declarations are
  UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE for now.
- **Unprefixed function names** (5.14.2): the core resolves them to fn and
  looks names up without interning, so the prolog interns fn:L for every
  unprefixed call/reference name when it declares a no-namespace function or a
  default function namespace; the table then tries the declared no-namespace L
  (or L in the default function namespace, also among library functions: `pi()`
  under the math namespace) before fn:L. A written `fn:L` finds the same
  (Proposed: a default function namespace in the XPath static context).
- **Declared functions**: one IR function per arity of the arity range, added
  to the unit before any body is lowered (recursion and mutual recursion are
  STATIC_CALLs on the evaluator's stack, D75); the full arity holds the body
  with its result COERCEd; a shorter arity binds the missing defaults (coerced,
  no focus) and calls the full one; `:= .` is
  SXML_PARAMETER_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_VALUE, which the core supplies at the call.
  Bodies are level-0 functions with an absent focus.
- **Variables and the context value**: each value or default is an initializer
  IR function of arity 0, coerced to the declared type. When the prolog has
  initializers or a context value declaration, the unit gets the **context
  global** (name 0, the last global; glossary) and the query body and every
  variable initializer read the focus as the fixed focus of it (5.17); the main
  function's focus slot receives the host's context value, which the global
  part copies (coerced) into the context global unless a non-external
  declaration gives the value.
- **Computation order**: after lowering, the expression, atom and map entry
  runs each body and initializer added are scanned for globals read and
  declared functions called or referenced; an iterative walk from the query
  body orders the reached variables dependencies first; a cycle through a
  variable is XQDY0054, raised at compile time (5.16 allows static detection).
  Reached variables get, in that order, an initializer that calls their lowered
  one; the global part sorts the variables to compute by initializer index and
  runs each as a CALL on the machine (a pushed task turned into a CALL, as the
  machine's static calls are), so unreached variables are never computed
  (`declare variable $x := 1 div 0; 2` is 2); BEING_COMPUTED still gives
  XQDY0054 for dynamic cycles.
- Rejected: computing on first read (needs every atom read in the machine to
  suspend: a change across `src/evaluator.c`); relowering in dependency order
  (two lowerings; the extra initializers cost one call).
- **Later additions** (same packet): named item types are aliases in the XPath
  static context (`named_item_types`, `sxml_xpath_find_named_type`, also for
  cast targets; resolved in rounds, so forward references work) with a cast as
  constructor function for generalized atomic types; records are nominative
  registry types (reused when an earlier compilation for the item heap declared
  the name) with a constructor IR function (a map of the fields, %static
  fields' defaults, coerced to the record); the QT4 tests call constructors of
  records without `%constructor`, so every record gets one. Decimal formats
  (XQST0111, XQST0114, XQST0097 for a value's form, XQST0098 otherwise) and the
  default collation go into `unit_static_context` (D131), which the module
  entry copies into the unit. `sxml_xpath_static_context` gets a function
  namespace rule (fn; a declared default; no namespace first, which the XQuery
  table falls back from to fn), replacing the interning workaround above; an
  empty namespace declaration binds the prefix to no namespace, which the core
  reads as undeclared (the lowerer accepts it); `xq` is predeclared;
  annotations of inline functions and function types are checked (XQST0045,
  XQST0125). Output declarations are checked by name (XQST0109, XQST0110);
  their values are 3.12's to read.

### D136. Node, sequence, string and type functions (packet 2.17)

**Summary**: One options reader serves every option map, and new node,
sequence, string and type functions, fn:parse-xml-fragment and
fn:system-properties are added, with collations resolved by the ordering
functions.

Recorded 2026-10-17. F&O 4.0 sections are those of the current editor's draft.

- **One options reader** (glossary `option_definition`):
  `sxml_function_library_read_options` (`src/function_library_options.c`,
  declared in `src/function_library_core_internal.h`) reads every map that
  follows the option parameter conventions (1.7): a definition is a name and a
  sequence type; values are coerced with `sxml_evaluator_coerce`; a string key
  that names no option is XPTY0004, an xs:QName key in a namespace is ignored.
  The string and JSON parts use it (their own readers are gone); the
  element-map, resource and serialization-parameter readers of other packets
  could move to it.
- **xnode()?** for fn:name, local-name, namespace-uri, node-name, base-uri,
  document-uri, nilled (as F&O 4.0 types them): a JNode is XPTY0004 (QT4
  PathExpr-J-461, -462).
- **Node functions** (`src/function_library_node.c`): siblings (the parent's
  child step); innermost/outermost in document order (a node's subtree follows
  it, so only the next member, or the last kept one, needs an ancestor walk);
  lang (caseless by full lower-case mapping); id, element-with-id and idref
  scan the target document for the is-id / is-idrefs nodes the parser marks
  (xml:id, DTD ID/IDREF/IDREFS), FODC0001 for a root that is not a document;
  path in every 4.0 form; location from the tree's `get_location`
  (`tree_internal.h`), as an fn:location-record: the processor's loader does
  not keep locations, so documents it parses give the empty sequence, which F&O
  allows; fn:doc accepts and ignores `$options`.
- **parse-xml-fragment** (`src/function_library_json.c`): the entity, after a
  UTF-8 byte order mark and a text declaration (which must have an encoding and
  no standalone, else FODC0006), is parsed by the loader as the content of an
  element of a document made around it, whose children are copied into a new
  document node; binary input is taken as UTF-8. **strip-space="all"** (both
  parse functions) copies through a tree builder that drops whitespace-only
  text outside xml:space="preserve". **system-properties** (17.1.9) lives in
  the same part: the 14 built-in properties, sxml not schema-aware and without
  the optional features.
- **Type part** `src/function_library_type.c` (19.1): type-of; schema-type,
  atomic-type-annotation and node-type-annotation make an fn:schema-type-record
  from the type registry; base-type, primitive-type, members and matches are
  anonymous function items over native rows that capture the type identifier as
  xs:integer; constructor is the type's constructor body (as xs:T#1), absent
  for xs:anyAtomicType, xs:anySimpleType and namespace-sensitive types; variety
  "mixed" for xs:anyType and xs:untyped; xs names carry the xs prefix.
- **String part**: pad-string, index-of-substring (codepoint matching).
- **Sequence part**: starts-/ends-/contains-subsequence as one resumable body
  (D75): one call of `$compare` per step; without it fn:deep-equal's leaf
  entry, no calls.
- **Collations** (D116's proposal for these bodies, accepted): fn:min, fn:max,
  fn:highest, fn:lowest, fn:sort-by, array:sort and array:sort-by resolve
  through `sxml_function_library_find_collation` / `_resolve_collation` and
  compare with `_compare_collated`; each sort key definition carries its
  collation (the default when a sort key record names none).
  `sxml_higher_order_check_collation` is gone;
  `sxml_function_library_check_collation` has no caller left (its definition in
  `src/function_library.c` may go). Order-by keys in the evaluator's SORT still
  accept only the codepoint collation.
- **Not done**: a descending range for `count(reverse(1 to 10^11))` (one QT4
  case, RangeExpr-408g; needs a frozen-header addition, see "Proposed"); the

  fn/map/array/math name of the XP40 sets, function-lookup at arities 0 to 6):
