### D137. Group by and window clauses (packet 3.8)

**Summary**: XQuery group by stays a tuple stream clause and windows are
segment clauses like for, both lowered to calls of two internal native rows,
sharing one condition closure procedure with while.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D55 and D126 for these clauses. No IR kind
added; contract in `src/xquery_flwor_internal.h`: lowering in
`src/xquery_lower_window.c`, two internal native rows in `src/xquery_flwor.c`
in no function table (a STATIC_CALL targets the row: `Q{}group-by#3`,
`Q{}window#4`).

- **group by** stays a tuple stream clause. Its grouping specifications are
  bindings of the segment before it (a value is a let, 4.13.8's rewrite); after
  the last, each grouping variable is rebound to its grouping key: coerced to
  `xs:anyAtomicType?` (atomized, XPTY0004 for two items), and to a declared
  type again (so `as attribute(*)` is XPTY0004); XQST0094 when no variable of
  the FLWOR has the name. Tuple arrays before a group by pack every variable,
  constants too. The row takes the tuple arrays, the key member numbers and one
  collation URI per key ("" = default collation; XQST0076 for one
  `sxml_collation_find` does not know, relative URIs against the static base
  URI) and returns one tuple array per group, same layout, groups in the order
  of their first tuples: the first tuple's keys, every other member the
  concatenation of its values. Keys are equal when both empty or atomic-equal,
  strings under a non-codepoint collation by collation key, dates and times
  without timezone given the implicit one (fn:deep-equal); hashed as
  fn:distinct-values does.
- **Window clauses** are not tuple stream clauses (glossary): a clause of a
  segment like for (4.13.4.3), a MAP over the window arrays (glossary
  `window_array`) the window row returns; the body binds the declared variables
  by LOOKUP ($w with its type) and lowers the rest of the segment. XQST0103 for
  two variables of one name. The row's kind bits: sliding, has end, only end.
  Without end clause a tumbling window ends before the next start; tumbling
  `only end` without an end item stops.
- **Condition closures** (glossary): one lowering procedure for window start
  and end conditions (4 and 8 parameters named by the window variables; the row
  takes the effective boolean value) and the while clause (D126: tuple unpacked
  from parameter 1; its body is now `conditional(C, true(), false())`, not
  `fn:boolean(C)`), so capture analysis and focus capture exist once;
  `sxml_xquery_unpack_tuple` is shared.
- Measured (3.13's `--spec=XQ40`, release): prod-GroupByClause 35/40 (not run
  2; group-020 is a prolog, group-025 a UCA tailoring, use-case-groupby-Q4 an
  evaluator SORT over an empty input: `sxml_sort_finish` allocates 0 bytes,
  INVALID_ARGUMENT); prod-WindowClause 125/158 (19 not run, the 14 errors are
  prologs). The FLWOR sets are as D126 measured.

### D138. The JavaScript package and release 0.2.0 (packet 2.18)

**Summary**: The JavaScript package is hand-written TypeScript over a C shim
linked into `sxml.wasm`, supplying its own WASI imports, with disposable
handles, a 2,000,000-byte size budget and release 0.2.0.

Recorded 2026-10-17, completing D10 and D47. Node 22.22, WASI SDK 34.

- **Layout** (`bindings/javascript/`, glossary `javascript_package`,
  `javascript_shim`): the shim `sxml_javascript.c` (with its interface
  `sxml_javascript.h`, not a public header) uses only the public API, as the
  CLI does. It builds as a library in every preset, so `-Werror`, clang-tidy
  and ast-grep see it (`cmake/SxmlLint.cmake` globs `bindings/`); under WASI it
  links into `sxml.wasm`, a reactor module (`-mexec-model=reactor`,
  `export_name`, `--strip-all`). The package is hand-written TypeScript
  (`src/index.ts`, `src/wasi.ts`), erasable syntax only, so Node.js (22.18 and
  later) runs it and its tests directly; `tsc` 5.9.3, a devDependency,
  type-checks (ctest `javascript/typecheck` after `npm ci` there) and builds
  `dist/`. No runtime dependencies.
- **WASI**: the module imports only `clock_time_get`, `fd_write`, `fd_close`
  and `fd_seek` (sxml does no I/O; resources come through the resolver). The
  package supplies these itself in Node.js and browsers alike (real clocks;
  EBADF; ENOSYS for any other import), instead of `node:wasi` and a browser
  polyfill: one code path. So D65's fast-call workaround does not concern the
  package; `tools/run-wasi.mjs` is unchanged. Checked in headless Chromium
  (fetch, resolver, clock).
- **API**: `load()` gives an `Sxml`; `createProcessor({resolver})`;
  `Processor.parse`, `compile` (an `XPathExpression` with named external
  variables, `item()*`, NCName or `Q{uri}local`), `evaluate`, `value`,
  `serialize`, `dispose`; `Value.serialize`, `toString` (adaptive), `dispose`;
  failures throw `SxmlError` (status, code `prefix:local`, description, line,
  column). JavaScript data becomes XDM as fn:parse-json reads its JSON (a
  string is an xs:string), one general rule instead of per-type conversions;
  serialization options are fn:serialize's options map, read by
  `sxml_serialization_parameter_reader` (camelCase keys accepted). The resolver
  is a synchronous callback (`sxml_host.resolve` import) returning a string,
  bytes or nothing; an exception it throws is rethrown; it must not use its
  processor. XQuery arrives additively once `xquery.h` is implemented: a
  `Processor.compileQuery()` giving an expression object with the same
  `evaluate` and the query's serialization parameters as the default of
  `serialize`; resource kinds already include `xquery-module`.
- **Memory**: every package object owning C memory is a handle (glossary);
  `dispose()` releases it, a `FinalizationRegistry` releases what is never
  disposed. A processor's destruction releases its live values and expressions
  first, since they cannot outlive it in C. Each processor has a counting
  allocator: tests check that destruction leaves 0 allocations and run the
  allocation-failure loop (D23) from JavaScript.
- **Size budget** (D93, glossary `size_budget`): at this commit the `sxml` CLI
  module is 1,820,106 bytes stripped, 629,585 gzipped (zlib -9); `sxml.wasm`
  1,788,836 and 617,898. Phase 2 grew both past D93's 1.5 MB and 450 KB (from
  1,213,261 and 358,020); `-flto -Oz` saves 2%, so the growth is code and
  tables, not flags. The budget becomes 2,000,000 bytes stripped and 700,000
  gzipped for both modules, checked by ctest `javascript/size_budget` (wasm
  preset), which prints the sizes. The owner may instead want optional parts as
  separate modules (PLAN.md, risks): see "Proposed".
- **npm name**: `sxml` is taken on npm (another project, 1.0.4); the package is
  `sxml-js` until the owner chooses.
- **Release 0.2.0**: `SXML_VERSION_*` 0.2.0, equal to `SXML_API_VERSION`; CMake
  project version 0.2.0; `CHANGELOG.md`; `docs/RELEASE.md` says how to cut a
  release. From 0.2.0 the public headers are stable (D47): a release adds
  declarations (minor before 1.0.0) and never changes one without a major
  (before 1.0.0, minor) version and a record. Tagging and publishing to npm are
  the owner's.

**Sources**: sxml CLI module and sxml.wasm, stripped and gzipped (zlib -9), and
the saving of -flto -Oz (`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`, `ctest`,
wasm build); configured: the size budget, 2,000,000 bytes stripped and 700,000
gzipped (from `bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt`); quoted from D93.

### D139. The stylesheet reader and static expressions (packet 4.5)

**Summary**: `sxml_xslt_read_stylesheet` reads every module with one explicit
stack, checks elements against tables generated from the XSLT 4.0 schema, and
evaluates static expressions through the ordinary front end with a static
scope.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D81, D102, D118, D120. `src/xslt_ast.c` (the builder
of D102), `src/xslt_read.c` with `src/xslt_read_internal.h`
(`sxml_xslt_read_stylesheet`), `src/xslt_static.c` with
`src/xslt_static_internal.h` (the static scope); the packet named no headers,
so each module has its own.

- **Walk**: each module is parsed by the XML parser into an arena tree with
  locations; one explicit stack of open elements (D71) holds the elements of
  every module being read, so an include or import pushes the new module's
  document frame and is read in place (D102's pre-order). Text runs are
  collected between elements (comments, PIs, xsl:note dropped, 3.11.1) and
  stripped by 3.11.1's rules.
- **Tables**: one row per XSLT element, generated from the 4.0 schema
  (attributes and their types, D102) and the element syntax summaries of the
  spec (required attributes, category, content model); one row per attribute
  (value syntax, keyword mask). Where the two disagree the schema wins
  (record-type has no constructor, field has default).
- **Static expressions** (9.7) run through the one front end, lowering and
  evaluator (sxml_xpath_lower, sxml_evaluator_evaluate) with a static scope:
  the static variables so far (later hides earlier) and a function table that
  puts system-property, available-system-properties, function-available,
  element-available and type-available (native rows of a small function
  library) in front of the processor's. 4.10 may move these rows to a library
  part for non-static XSLT expressions. Shadow attributes are value templates
  evaluated to a string (the AST is that of a string template, D120); the
  shadow's static context is the element's native or fixed namespaces with the
  parent's default element namespace and base URI. Values of static variables
  are coerced by binding them to a declared variable (XTTE0570, XTTE0590 for
  supplied parameters); a required static parameter without value is XTDE0050.
- **Modules** (3.10): hrefs are resolved against the element's static base URI
  and asked from the resolver as XSLT_MODULE; unavailable or not well-formed is
  XTSE0165. A reference to a module whose URI is on the path being read is
  ignored when every step of that path and the reference is an include (an
  include cycle, 4.0), else XTSE0210; an include of a URI already in the
  stylesheet level is ignored (included_module 0).
- **Node contents** (TEXT_NODE value templates, xsl:select) name their
  expression before it exists: the AST numbers expressions in order, so the
  reader gives the next index and hands the AST over after the node.
  `sxml_xslt_ast_add_node` marks a module simplified when its first node is a
  synthesized STYLESHEET (the header has no other writer for the flag).
- **Checks while reading**: XTSE0010 (placement, order, required attributes and
  children), XTSE0090, XTSE0805, XTSE0020 (values), XTSE0110, XTSE0120,
  XTSE0125, XTSE0130, XTSE0260, XTSE0280, XTSE0340/0350/0370 and XPST0003 from
  the front ends, XTSE0500, XTSE0530, XTSE0740, XTSE0808, XTSE0812, XTSE1430,
  XTSE0122 (fixed-namespaces by URI is not read), XTSE1660 (import-schema,
  strict/lax validation, schema types; D97). Errors keep their code and point
  at the attribute or element (module URI, line, column; an expression's own
  offset added on its first line).
- Left to lowering: duplicate declarations, XTSE3450 between static variables,
  the arity and ordering rules beyond leading children, the values static
  variables give non-static expressions (the AST does not keep them: lowering
  re-evaluates their select with the same scope).

### D140. URIs, QNames and hashes (packet 2.11)

**Summary**: fn:hash computes MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, BLAKE3 and CRC-32 without
allocation, and fn:parse-uri, fn:build-uri, fn:decode-from-uri, fn:parse-QName
and fn:resolve-QName share one percent-decoding octet reader.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D88, D91, D101. New part
`src/function_library_hash.c` (fn:hash) over `src/hash.c` /
`src/hash_internal.h`; rows added to the uri part (decode-from-uri, parse-uri,
build-uri) and the qname part (parse-QName, resolve-QName).

- **Hashes**: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, BLAKE3 (the draft keeps it) and CRC-32 as
  one call `sxml_hash_compute` (algorithm, message view) into a fixed 32-octet
  `sxml_digest`: no allocation, no state; BLAKE3 merges chunk chaining values
  with a 54-entry stack (no recursion). The effective name is
  fn:upper-case(fn:normalize-space()) with Unicode case mapping, matched byte
  for byte; anything else is FOHA0001. No options are defined, so any
  unqualified key is XPTY0004. One step per 64 octets.
- **fn:parse-uri** follows F&O 4.0, 7.6.2 step by step; each regular expression
  is matched by hand over the octets (no regex per call). The parts are views
  into one working copy (backslashes made slashes) and one rewritten copy for a
  drive letter. Implementation-defined: known hierarchical schemes are file,
  ftp, http, https; a port that is not 1 to 18 digits is left out (the field is
  xs:integer?); a zero-length authority (`////host`) is the empty sequence, as
  QT4 fn-parse-uri-048b/049b expect. query-parameters keeps keys in
  first-appearance order with all values; repeated keys are chained through an
  index map (O(n log n), not quadratic). The result is an annotated
  fn:uri-structure-record (D133).
- **Percent decoding** (glossary): one octet reader for decode-from-uri,
  parse-uri (URI decoding) and query parameters (form decoding, `+` as space);
  broken escapes take `%` and up to two octets (QT4 `%üü` is U+FFFD then `ü`);
  UTF-8 breaks off at the first octet outside Unicode's well-formed ranges;
  U+0000, U+FFFE, U+FFFF become U+FFFD.
- **fn:build-uri** reuses the escaping table of encode-for-uri (three new
  kinds: path segment, query parameter, fragment). Deviation: a URI without a
  scheme gets `//` before an authority (the spec text adds nothing, which would
  make `{'host': 'x', 'path': '/p'}` read back as a path); an empty query (from
  an empty map) adds no `?`.
- **fn:parse-QName** is marked USES_DYNAMIC_CONTEXT so no pass folds it:
  prefix:local is the xs:QName cast with the static namespaces of
  `sxml_dynamic_context_get_running_unit` (D131; FONS0004 from the cast,
  predeclared prefixes included); NCName and Q{uri}local are made directly;
  FOCA0002 for the rest. **fn:resolve-QName** looks the prefix up in the
  element's in-scope namespaces only (no predeclared fallback: `xs:x` on `<a/>`
  is FONS0004).
- Measured (release driver, XP40, passed of cases): fn-parse-uri 0 to 74/74,
  fn-build-uri 0 to 48/48, fn-decode-from-uri 0 to 29/29, fn-parse-QName 6 (all
  wrong errors) to 19/19, fn-resolve-QName 4 to 8/8 run (23 XQuery-only),
  fn-hash 1 to 54/54.

### D141. CSV parsing: fn:parse-csv, fn:csv-to-xml, fn:csv-doc (packet 2.15)

**Summary**: A hand-written CSV scanner yields one token per call without
allocation; fn:parse-csv parses once, fn:csv-to-xml walks its result and
fn:csv-doc reads through fn:unparsed-text.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D97, D128, D131, D133. New module `src/csv.c` /
`src/csv_internal.h` and part `src/function_library_csv.c`.

- **Scanner** (D97, by hand): `sxml_csv_read_token` gives one `csv_token`
  (field, row end, input end; glossary) per call and keeps its place in a
  `csv_cursor`, a plain value: no object, no allocation. A field is a view into
  the text; only a quoted field with a doubled quote or a CR needs
  `sxml_csv_decode_field`, into caller memory no longer than the field. Special
  characters are matched as whole UTF-8 sequences byte by byte.
- **Rules where F&O 4.0 is loose**: CR is a newline, so it cannot be a
  separator, quote or comment marker (FOCV0002, like LF); trimming removes
  U+0020 and U+0009 from unquoted fields and all four XML whitespace characters
  from header names; with trim-rows, a blank row is padded to the first row's
  width like any short row; select-columns beyond a header's end name the
  zero-length string; a selected position past int64_t selects nothing.
- **fn:csv-to-arrays** is not implemented: F&O 4.0 dropped it (issue 2961,
  absorbed into fn:parse-csv) and QT4 has no test set for it.
- **One parse, three functions**: fn:parse-csv builds columns, column index and
  rows once; the record's get is a function item over a static row (after
  fn:regex, D133) capturing rows and column index, signature from the record's
  field type. fn:csv-to-xml walks that result, as the specification defines it
  over fn:parse-csv. fn:csv-doc calls the fn:unparsed-text row (found by name,
  as fn:json-doc finds parse-json), so text decoding (D131) is written once.
- Measured (release driver, XP40, passed of cases; before at 3a3a3cb, all wrong
  errors): fn-parse-csv 35 to 107/124, fn-csv-to-xml 9 to 68/68 run, fn-csv-doc
  4 to 20/20. The 17 parse-csv failures are assertions such as `?get(1, 1) =
  "one"` that read the result as the context value, which the driver does not
  bind (Proposed below); with it, 124/124.

### D142. Sequence constructors and node construction (packet 4.6)

**Summary**: XSLT instructions are lowering procedures on the XPath lowerer: a
sequence constructor is one atom per child, and literal result elements, value
templates and xsl: constructors lower to the existing IR constructor kinds.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D102, D103, D110, D120, D124, D127, D139.
`src/xslt_lower.c`, `src/xslt_lower_construct.c`, `src/xslt_simple_content.c`
with `src/xslt_lower_internal.h`; no IR kind, no evaluator change, no public
header.

- **One machine**: XSLT instructions are lowering procedures pushed with
  `sxml_xpath_lowering_push_procedure` (D103) on a lowerer of language XSLT;
  every expression and value template goes through the embedding entry with an
  XPath static context made once per AST static context (namespaces,
  xpath-default-namespace as prefix 0, base URI, the processor's function
  table). The files define no lowering part (no XPath AST kind is XSLT's yet);
  instructions are found through `sxml_xslt_instruction_rule` views, one per
  file, listed in `src/xslt_lower.c` (4.7 to 4.14 add a view and one line).
- **Sequence constructor** = one atom per child, bound in the caller's block;
  its value is the SEQUENCE of them, given to constructors as one ATOM content
  (D110: one enclosed expression, so 5.7.1 joins adjacent atomic values across
  instructions). Variables a child pushes stay in scope until the constructor
  ends (4.7's xsl:variable). A constructor call may install a focus (FIXED for
  xsl:copy select, SLOTS for the for-each of xsl:array).
- **Literal result elements**: ELEMENT_CONSTRUCTOR with XSLT_RULES, an xs:QName
  constant, namespace bindings from the stylesheet tree's in-scope namespaces
  minus xml, the excluded namespaces (unless an alias outputs them) and alias
  literal URIs (11.1.3, 11.1.4; aliases resolved by import precedence,
  XTSE0810); xsl:inherit-namespaces="no" is NO_INHERIT. Attributes are
  ATTRIBUTE_CONSTRUCTORs of their AVT.
- **Value templates and simple content** (5.6, 5.7.2): string templates lowered
  here; each enclosed value goes through the internal native row
  `merge-text-nodes` (adjacent text nodes to one xs:untypedAtomic, else the
  value as it is) and fn:string-join. Fixes D120's deviation: `{//item/text()}`
  is "onetwo". The same path gives xsl:attribute, xsl:value-of, xsl:text,
  xsl:comment (hyphens fixed with fn:replace, 11.8), xsl:processing-instruction
  (leading space, "?>", 11.6) and xsl:namespace (XTDE0930) their strings.
- **Names**: a name (and namespace) without enclosed expressions is resolved
  while lowering to an xs:QName constant; an invalid one becomes a RAISE of
  XTDE0820/0830/0850/0855/0860 when evaluated. A computed name is a string
  resolved by the evaluator with the instruction's in-scope namespaces as
  name_namespaces (without the default one for attributes), or
  fn:QName(namespace, name) (prefix dropped for "").
- **XSLT error codes** where the evaluator raises XQuery's: a TRY_CATCH around
  the constructor alone whose clauses RAISE the XSLT code
  (`sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_mapped_expression`): XQDY0137 to XTDE3365, XPTY0004
  to XTTE3375 (maps), XQDY0074/0044/FOCA0002 to XTDE08x0 (names), XQDY0041/0064
  to XTDE0890, XQDY0074/0101 to XTDE0920/0925.
- **Others**: xsl:copy is SHALLOW_COPY with the content as its own body;
  xsl:copy-of a MAP that SHALLOW_COPYs elements and documents with `(@*,
  node())` as content and other nodes whole; xsl:map/xsl:record a
  MAP_CONSTRUCTOR (fields, then the content's maps as a merged entry), with
  [xsl:]duplicates map:merge; xsl:array array:of-members over JNodes (fn:jtree
  for non-JNodes), xsl:array-member fn:jtree; xsl:select its content
  expression; extension and unknown instructions their xsl:fallback children or
  XTDE1450.
- **Stylesheet AST** (accepts D139's Proposed item): appended
  SXML_XSLT_AST_KIND_RECORD and attribute kinds CONSTRUCTOR (record-type,
  BOOLEAN) and RECORD_FIELD (EXPRESSION); xsl:record reads attributes in no
  namespace as fields (no shadow or standard attributes), xsl:-prefixed ones as
  standard attributes and xsl:duplicates.
- **Entry** (until 4.8 and 4.15): `sxml_xslt_lower_initial_template` lowers one
  template's sequence constructor as the main function (focus = global context
  item), optionally inside a DOCUMENT constructor (the principal result tree),
  then runs the standard passes and seals.
- Deviations: xpath-default-namespace="##any" reads as none; attribute sets
  (4.12), xsl:type/validation ignored (D97); a zero-length text node is no node
  (D110).

### D143. Conformance sweep 1: computed constructors in XPath, the JSON fallback, descending ranges, function equivalence (packet 2.19)

**Summary**: Computed constructors are available in XPath, the JSON functions
call their fallback, sequences gain a descending integer range, and deep-equal
treats function items with the same static form as equal.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D95, D110, D127, D133, D136, D141. Accepts the
Proposed items "QT4 assertions see the result as the context value", "Decimal
zero against doubles", "A descending integer range" and "Equivalence of
function items" (orchestrator, packet 2.19).

- **Computed constructors are XPath 4.0** (section 4.13): the lowering part
  `construct` (D127) serves every language; direct constructors only parse in
  XQuery. 136 "error" outcomes of XP40 (prod-Comp\*Constructor) become passes.
- **The fallback option** of fn:parse-json, fn:json-to-xml and fn:json-doc (F&O
  4.0, 17.4.4 to 17.4.6): the three rows are resumable bodies (D75) of the json
  part; before the parse, the fallback is called once per codepoint that has an
  `unpermitted_escape` (`sxml_json_find_unpermitted_escape`, a lexical scan
  that pairs surrogates as parsing does), with the escape as written; its
  result is coerced to xs:anyAtomicType and its string value becomes the
  `json_replacement` the parse inserts for every escape of that codepoint
  (`sxml_json_parse_options.replacements`, U+FFFD without one). A fallback
  whose arity is not 1 is XPTY0004 when the options are read. fn:json-doc's row
  moves to the json part; the resource part keeps reading its text
  (`sxml_function_library_read_json_document`).
- **fn:generate-id of a JNode**: "j" tree, then "c" child index for the node
  and each ancestor below the root, read upwards: unique per JNode (JTree and
  path), the same for two cells of one JNode.
- **Decimal zero**: `sxml_double_write_exact_text` writes a zero of either sign
  as "0", so 0.0 eq 0e0 and the hash of 0.0 match.
- **A descending integer range** (additive, D99):
  `SXML_SEQUENCE_REPRESENTATION_DESCENDING_INTEGER_RANGE` and
  `sxml_sequence_make_descending_integer_range` in `include/sxml/xdm.h`; the
  range cell with a second cell class. fn:reverse of a range in either order is
  O(1); count, get_item and iteration are O(1) per item; the general comparison
  of a range with one integer and the temporal check read either order. Fast
  paths that only know ascending ranges iterate a descending one.
- **Equivalent function items** (F&O 4.0, 1.9.5): deep-equal treats two IR
  functions of one unit as the same body when they have the same `static_form`
  (`sxml_ir_function_has_same_static_form`): the IR text form of each (D51
  printer, explicit stack) without names, annotations and the atoms of the
  function's own captures, with every nested FUNCTION_DEFINITION printed as the
  function it defines; the captured values are compared by deep-equal as
  before. Slots are numbered by position, so renaming a variable does not
  change the form.
- **QT4 driver**: assertions see the result as the context value; a source that
  only has a uri and is not well-formed stays unavailable, so fn:doc raises
  FODC0002 instead of an "error" outcome.
- math:sin, math:cos and math:tan name their parameter $radians.
- **fn:last#0 and other focus-dependent named references** keep their name on
  the closure (XPath 4.0, 4.5.4), so function-name(fn:last#0) is fn:last and
  fn:last#0 differs from fn:position#0 under deep-equal.
- Measured (release, XP40, before at 62947af with the 3.10 prolog commit after
  it): passed 30,389 to 30,628 (+239, none lost), errors 187 to 2, in scope
  96.3 % to 97.0 %; prod 96.6 to 98.1 %, fn 98.3 to 98.9 %, op 99.7 to 99.8 %,
  misc 97.8 to 98.2 %; slice 198/198.
- Not done (open, for later sweeps): fn:function-lookup of a focus-dependent
  function (45 cases need the dynamic focus at the call), casts to array, map
  and record types (prod-Cast\*Expr.composite, 82 cases), counted regex
  repetition without expansion (cbcl-matches-004, -038: the last two "error"
  outcomes, LIMIT_EXCEEDED), partial application of a dynamic call with the
  wrong arity (xqhof8, xqhof9).

**Sources**: XP40 passes, errors, in-scope rate and area rates, before at
62947af and after, and the slice (release build).

### D144. Templates and modes (packet 4.8)

**Summary**: Each xsl:template becomes an IR function of five parameters, modes
sort their rules by precedence and priority, and APPLY_TEMPLATES runs as a part
task calling match and template functions on the machine.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D55, D101, D118, D124, D139, D142.
`src/xslt_lower_template.c`, `src/evaluator_template.c`,
`tests/evaluator_template_test.c`; APPLY_TEMPLATES, the one reserved IR
extension point of XSLT, is accepted by the verifier. No other IR kind, no
public header.

- **IR** (`src/ir_internal.h`, the reserved part, completed):
  `sxml_ir_apply_templates` = select (NONE: the function's focus, for
  next-match and apply-imports), mode (0: the current mode), rule search
  (FROM_START, AFTER_CURRENT_RULE, IMPORTED_ONLY), and three atoms:
  `parameters` and `tunnel_parameters`, two maps from xs:QName to values, and
  `separator` (6.7). The by-name parameter binding list is gone (maps replace
  it). A template rule gains `lowest_imported_precedence` (the import subtree
  of its stylesheet level, for apply-imports, 6.11); a mode gains
  `built_in_template` and `fails_on_multiple_match`. Adders
  `sxml_ir_unit_add_template_rules`, `_add_modes`; accessors `_get_mode`,
  `_get_template_rules`; the text form prints search and maps. Verifier: modes
  in range, match functions of arity 1, template functions of arity 5.
- **Template function**: one IR function per xsl:template with five parameters:
  item()?, position, size (its focus slots) and the two parameter maps. Its
  body binds each xsl:param from map:contains/map:get (coerced, XTTE0590) or
  its default (select, content as a temporary tree without as, "" or ()
  implicitly, XTDE0700 when mandatory), checks xsl:context-item (XTTE3090,
  XTTE0590), and coerces the result to `as` (TRY_CATCH mapping XPTY0004 to
  XTTE0505). A named template has a second function lowered with an absent
  focus, called where the caller's focus is absent (xsl:function, the initial
  template without a global context item: the main function tests the focus
  with a TRY_CATCH of XPDY0002), so reading `.` there raises XPDY0002 (10.1.2).
- **Instructions**: xsl:call-template is a STATIC_CALL (XTSE0650, XTSE0680
  unless version < 2.0, XTSE0690); xsl:apply-templates, next-match,
  apply-imports are APPLY_TEMPLATES. Tunnel parameters (10.1.6): inside a
  template's function its received tunnel map (slot 5) with the tunnel
  xsl:with-param values put in (map:put), else the empty map. next-match and
  apply-imports pass the received non-tunnel map too when their effective
  version is 4.0 or more (6.11). Lexically outside a template body (another
  focus or function): XTDE0560 when evaluated. apply-templates without select:
  XNode child::node(), JNode child::*, map/array jtree(.)/child::*, else
  XTTE0510.
- **Modes** (6.9): the unnamed mode is mode 1; then every mode xsl:mode
  declares (XTSE0545 over all its attributes, XTSE0020 for a non-private
  unnamed mode, XTSE4005, XTSE4010 for enclosing modes) and every mode a
  template, apply-templates or default-mode names (XTSE3085 under
  declared-modes). Rules per mode (#all: every mode but enclosing ones) sorted
  by precedence, priority (explicit or D118's default) and declaration order
  (6.8), heapsort. XTSE0660, XTSE0080.
- **Built-in templates** (6.10) are template functions lowered from short XPath
  snippets and the existing kinds (APPLY_TEMPLATES in the current mode with the
  received maps, TEXT_CONSTRUCTOR, SHALLOW_COPY with copy-namespaces, RAISE
  XTDE0555), one per on-no-match used; shallow-copy-all reads as shallow-copy.
- **Evaluator** (`src/evaluator_template.c`): a part task per APPLY_TEMPLATES;
  each match function and template function is a CALL on the machine (no C
  recursion, D71: 100,000 levels tested); the task catches errors while a match
  function runs (6.5: no match); the dynamic context's current_mode and
  current_template_rule_index are set around each template call and restored on
  return and on unwinding; on-multiple-match="fail" checks the tied rules
  (XTDE0540).
- **Entry**: `sxml_xslt_lower_initial_template` lowers templates and modes,
  then the invocation (`sxml_xslt_invocation`): a call of the initial template
  (xsl:initial-template or a named one) with the global context item, or
  apply-templates to it in the initial mode (default mode of the principal
  module; XTDE0045 for an unknown one; XTDE0040 for an unknown initial
  template). A simplified module is applied in the unnamed mode.
- Left out: xsl:sort in apply-templates (4.9), current() and fn:apply-templates
  (4.10), mode `as`/`typed`, warnings, packages (xsl:override, visibility
  beyond XTSE0020), the 4.0 JNode shallow copy.
- Measured with a scratch harness (lower, evaluate, serialize; assertions
  through the XPath API) over the applicable in-scope cases of the sets of the
  packet: 316 of 615 pass (match 93/193, mode 70/162, tunnel 53/58,
  declared-modes 14/14, apply-templates 27/39, next-match 28/51, call-template
  21/42, built-in-templates 4/5, template 5/6, apply-imports 1/5, priority
  0/40). Of the rest, 99 need global variables (4.7), 73 other instructions, 59
  stylesheet parameters (4.7, 4.15), 21 packages, 18 XSLT functions (current,
  document, xsl:function: 4.10, 4.12), 11 `~T` patterns (D139). Patterns with
  predicates select the step again from its parent (D118), so many sibling
  rules cost quadratic time (match-242: 60 s in a debug build).

**Sources**: 100,000 levels of template calls (`ctest`, from
`tests/evaluator_template_test.c`); applicable in-scope cases of the packet
sets, a scratch harness (lower, evaluate, serialize), and match-242 in a debug
build.

### D145. Control flow and variables (packet 4.7)

**Summary**: XSLT control flow lowers to existing IR kinds: xsl:if, choose and
switch as CONDITIONAL chains, for-each as MAP, try as TRY_CATCH, iterate as
fn:scan, with one procedure for all variable bindings.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D71, D103, D109, D124, D126, D135, D142.
`src/xslt_lower_control.c` (rule view `sxml_xslt_instruction_rules_control`,
one line in `src/xslt_lower.c`'s list), `tests/xslt_lower_control_test.c`; no
IR kind, no evaluator change, no public header.

- **Reused kinds** (D126): xsl:if (with 4.0 then/else), choose and switch are
  CONDITIONAL chains, each later test lowered in the previous else branch;
  switch coerces the select value to one xs:anyAtomicType and compares each
  test value by "=" (8.3); xsl:for-each is a MAP whose body is the sequence
  constructor with a SLOTS focus, separator a text node guarded by position()
  lt last() (7.1.1); xsl:try is TRY_CATCH, errors tokens as name tests, the
  nine $err: variables pushed as LOOKUPs of the details slot (stack-trace and
  additional are ()), the try body the children before xsl:catch (xsl:catch
  gives () where it stands).
- **Variable bindings** (9.3, 9.4): one procedure for xsl:variable, iterate
  xsl:param and xsl:with-param, and global initializers: select, else content
  (a document node unless "as" or a disqualifying child), else "" (or () with
  "as"); "as" coerces with XTTE0570 (a TRY_CATCH mapping XPTY0004) for
  variables and the TEMPLATE_PARAMETER role (XTTE0590) for parameters. A local
  xsl:variable is a LET in the sequence constructor's block and a scope entry
  until it ends (D142).
- **xsl:iterate** (7.2) is fn:scan(input, state, closure): no recursion (D71),
  100,000 items in a unit test. The state is an array [control, output,
  parameters...]; the closure (every visible variable captured, D126; the size
  captured only when the body reads last()) unpacks the parameters, runs the
  body with focus (item, position, size), and reads the last item of its value:
  an iteration marker {Q{XSLT}iterate: [0, (), values...]} from
  xsl:next-iteration or {..: [1, value]} from xsl:break gives the next state,
  anything else keeps the parameters. After a break the remaining items return
  the state without output. The result is the states' outputs, then
  xsl:on-completion (focus absent, final parameters) unless a break happened.
  XTSE3120 (tail position, checked on the AST), XTSE3130, XTSE0670, XTSE0580,
  XTSE3125.
- **8.5**: two internal native rows (as merge-text-nodes): `vacuous` and
  `remove-deemed-empty` (arrays flattened on an explicit stack).
  where-populated filters its content; a sequence constructor with
  on-empty/on-non-empty children (skipped by `lower_child`, a hook in
  `src/xslt_lower.c` pushes `sxml_xslt_lowering_call_conditional_content` at
  its end) is `if (vacuous(R)) then on-empty-or-R else (children with each
  on-non-empty's value in place)`, each lowered in its branch with the
  variables before it in scope; XTSE0010 for an on-empty not last.
- **xsl:message, xsl:assert** (23): the body is a document node of the select
  value and the content (TRY_CATCH: a body that cannot be built is an empty
  document, the transformation does not fail); the internal row `xslt-message`
  hands it to the trace sink as an XSLT_MESSAGE event with is_terminating and
  the code; terminate (an AVT, fixed or compared when evaluated) then raises
  fn:error(code, string(body), body). error-code: EQName or lexical QName,
  resolved while lowering, or by the row `error-code` with the instruction's
  namespaces as a map constant; an invalid one is the default (XTMM9000,
  XTMM9001). Assertions are always enabled.
- **Globals** (9.5, 9.11): `sxml_xslt_lowering_declare_global_variables` before
  the main function (one per name by import precedence, XTSE0630; declared in
  every static context) and `_add_global_variables` after: initializers of
  arity 0 with the context global (D135) as fixed focus, wrappers in dependency
  order (references in the declaration's expressions, explicit-stack DFS:
  XTDE0640 for a cycle, XPST0008 for a self-reference), a required xsl:param
  raises XTDE0050. The main function reserves its context slot when there are
  globals; callers pass absent global slots (as the XQuery tests). Static
  parameters are recomputed from their select (the AST keeps no static value).
- **Others**: xsl:fork is its content; xsl:evaluate its xsl:fallback children
  or XTDE3175 (sxml claims no dynamic evaluation, D117; a real one needs a
  nested evaluation, not done). xsl:for-each with xsl:sort is
  UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE until 4.9 (which can sort the input atom before the MAP).
  Deviations: D110's missing zero-length text nodes change on-empty-113/114 and
  message-0304; dependencies through functions and templates are not seen.
- Measured with a scratch harness (each case's initial template, or its
  `match="/"` template, through `sxml_xslt_lower_initial_template`; xml, error
  and string assertions): of 181 runnable cases of choose, for-each, iterate,
  try, switch, where-populated, on-empty, on-non-empty, message, evaluate,
  assert and decl-variable, 105 pass (before: none of these instructions
  lowered); most of the rest need apply-templates or template parameters
  (D144's driver path, 4.15), stylesheet functions (4.10, 4.12) or current-date
  in the harness, 52 have XPath assertions.

**Sources**: xsl:iterate over 100,000 items (`ctest`, from
`tests/xslt_lower_control_test.c`); 181 runnable cases of the control flow and
variable sets, a scratch harness through sxml_xslt_lower_initial_template.

### D146. The XQuery API and the sxml xquery command (packet 3.12)

**Summary**: `include/sxml/xquery.h` is implemented over the XPath API's one
evaluation path, output declarations are read as serialization parameter texts,
and the CLI gains `sxml xquery` and `sxml serialize`.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D106, D134, D135. `include/sxml/xquery.h` is
implemented in `src/xquery.c`; no header changed.

- **One evaluation path**: `src/xpath.c` exports its context checks and the
  evaluation of a sealed unit through `src/xpath_api_internal.h`
  (`sxml_static_context_configuration_is_valid`,
  `sxml_processor_static_context`,
  `sxml_dynamic_context_configuration_is_valid`, `sxml_evaluate_unit`, glossary
  `unit_evaluation`); the XQuery API compiles with the same static context and
  evaluates through the same function. Globals are bound by name except the
  context global (name 0), which no binding reaches. The unit's static base URI
  (the host's or a base-uri declaration's) is the one evaluation uses.
- **Compiling**: `src/xquery.c` parses with `sxml_xquery_build_ast` (a library
  module is XPST0003, as the header says), compiles with the new
  `sxml_xquery_compile_module` (`src/xquery_lower_internal.h`: lower, passes,
  seal over a caller's AST; `sxml_xquery_compile` is now parse + that) and
  reads the output declarations from the AST it kept. Module import stays
  UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE until 3.11 (the resolver hook is the header's).
- **Output declarations**: option names resolve against the unit's static
  namespaces (`sxml_xpath_resolve_name`); declarations in the serialization
  namespace become `sxml_serialization_parameter_text`s (glossary) read by
  `sxml_serialization_parameter_reader_read_texts`
  (`src/serialize_internal.h`), one reader per query owning the views: the
  parameter document first, then the declarations over it, method xml when
  nothing names one. The textual decoding is the parameter document's
  (`src/serialize_parameters.c` now decodes a value attribute and a declaration
  with one function; QNames resolve with a binding view, first binding of a
  prefix wins), so xsl:output can use it in Phase 4. Errors are static at the
  declaration: a value a parameter does not permit SEPM0016 (SESU0007/SESU0011
  for encodings and normalization forms), XQST0119 when the document cannot be
  loaded (processor's resolver, kind XML_DOCUMENT, resolved against the static
  base URI), XQST0115 when it is not a valid parameter document. XQST0108 waits
  for library modules (3.11).
- **QT4 driver**: the adapter (D134) is deleted; the driver calls
  `include/sxml/xquery.h` and has no `src/` include any more.
- **CLI**: `sxml xquery (QUERY-FILE | --expression=TEXT)`, `sxml serialize
  [--method] [--indent] FILE`, and `sxml xpath --method` with adaptive, xml,
  xhtml, html, text, json. `--param` declares and binds for XPath, only binds
  for XQuery (the query declares it external; a host declaration would make the
  prolog's XQST0049). The three commands share `apps/sxml/query_command.{c,h}`
  (glossary `query_run`). `--output`/`--force` stay planned: the CLI framework
  has no file writer.
- **WebAssembly**: the CLI module grows from 1.83 MB to 3.45 MB stripped (767
  KB gzipped) with the XQuery grammar; `javascript/size_budget` allows
  3,700,000 / 820,000 for the CLI (Proposed below). `sxml.wasm` (1.83 MB) is
  unchanged; `compileQuery()` in the JavaScript package is left out because it
  would link the same grammar into it.

**Sources**: the CLI module (1.83 MB to 3.45 MB stripped, 767 KB gzipped) and
sxml.wasm (1.83 MB), before and after the XQuery grammar
(`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`, wasm build); configured:
javascript/size_budget for the CLI, 3,700,000 / 820,000 bytes (from
`bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt`).

### D147. Counted repetition with counters (packet 2.19b)

**Summary**: A regular expression quantifier whose copies would exceed 256
instructions compiles to a counted loop whose counter and progress are register
slots, so large counts compile and nothing recurses.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D53, D71, D105. Closes D105's "Not done". (Completed
by the Phase 3 review, D161, from the text 2.19b left uncommitted.)

- **When**: a quantifier whose copies would add more than
  `SXML_REGEX_LARGEST_EXPANSION` (256) instructions, each copy counted as at
  least one, compiles to a counted loop (glossary): the atom once, between
  `COUNTED_LOOP_START` (counter := 0), `COUNTED_LOOP_CHOOSE`, a jump out,
  `COUNTED_LOOP_BODY` (progress := position) and `COUNTED_LOOP_END` (counter +
  1, back to CHOOSE). Smaller counts keep D53's copies, which are faster (a
  loop pays four instructions and three backtrack entries per iteration); x\*,
  x+ and x? are unchanged. `a{2147483647}` is six instructions;
  `(?:a{1000}){1000}` and `(?:(?:){1000}){1000}` now compile (they were
  LIMIT_EXCEEDED).
- **Matching**: CHOOSE iterates below the minimum, offers an iteration as a
  choice below the maximum (greedy first, reluctant second, section 6.1.4) and
  leaves at it. Counter and progress are register slots (as progress registers
  are), set with RESTORE_SLOT entries like SAVE, so backtracking into an
  earlier iteration finds its counter, lookaround keeps working (a positive
  assertion keeps restoring entries), and nothing recurses (D71). The
  parameters (minimum, maximum, unbounded, reluctant, the two slots) are in a
  `counted_loops` table of the compiled regex, shared like classes by the
  copies of an enclosing atom: copies run one after the other and every slot
  change is undone in order, so they can share slots.
- **Empty iterations**: above the minimum an iteration that consumed nothing
  fails, as CHECK_PROGRESS in D53's unbounded loops; below it, it stands for
  all the iterations still needed (the counter jumps to the minimum), since
  each would again match nothing at the same place. This keeps
  `(a?){2147483647}b` fast and finds the same matching segments; which
  substring a group inside captures then is implementation-dependent (F&O 4.0,
  section 6.1.5).
- **Quantities** above 4294967295 still saturate to it (cbcl-matches-004:
  `a{99999999999999999999999999}` is false, which the test allows).

### D148. Library modules and module import (packet 3.11)

**Summary**: XQuery library modules are loaded into a module set through the
resolver, one per module URI, each with its own static context, and the whole
set lowers into the main module's unit.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D106, D134, D135, D146. No header changed; no IR
kind added.

- **Module set** (`src/xquery_module.c`, `src/xquery_module_internal.h`;
  glossary `module_set`): a work list over the set from the main module. Each
  module import asks the processor's resolver (kind XQUERY_MODULE) once per
  location hint, the hint resolved against the importing module's static base
  URI (its base URI declaration over the host's base or its module URI), or
  once with an empty uri_reference when it has none and no module of the
  namespace is loaded. A module is identified by its module URI (glossary): the
  resource URI, else the absolute hint, else the hint, else the namespace; one
  met again is the module loaded before, which ends cycles and loads a module
  once per compilation. The module URI is interned in the name pool, so error
  records may name it as their source after compilation. Errors: XQST0088,
  XQST0047 (one namespace imported twice by a prolog), XQST0070 (prefix
  xml/xmlns, before loading), XQST0059 (no module for a hint or a hintless
  import, a main module, another namespace); a library module's XPST0003 is
  located in it.
- **Imports name namespaces** (5.12.2): a module imports every module of the
  set whose target namespace it imports, itself excepted, and sees their public
  declarations only (not what they import, not %private).
- **Static contexts**: one per module, read in the reading order (a depth-first
  walk, imported modules first; a cycle is broken where the walk meets it), so
  every declared function is an IR function from 2 on and every module's prolog
  variables are globals numbered after the host's in that order.
  `sxml_xpath_static_context.global_numbers` (internal, NULL = position + 1)
  maps a module's variables in scope (its own, then the imported public ones)
  to those globals. A library module starts from XQuery's default static
  context (no host namespaces or variables, its module URI as static base URI,
  the host's functions and collations); its module declaration and imports bind
  prefixes (XQST0033); public functions, variables, item types and records
  outside its target namespace are XQST0048; output declarations XQST0108; a
  context value with a value XQST0113. Imported public item types are aliases
  of the importer (read before it). Linking adds the imported public variables
  and makes the function table find imported public functions and constructors
  (after the module's own, before the host's); XQST0049 and XQST0034 are
  checked against them. Duplicate named types are now XQST0146 (5.19), as QT4
  expects.
- **Lowering**: the whole set lowers into the main module's unit; each library
  module's functions and initializers with a lowerer of its own (its static
  context and AST). The dependency graph of D135 spans every module, so one
  walk orders all variables and finds XQDY0054 through imports; unreached
  library variables are never computed.
- **CLI**: `sxml xquery` imports modules from the local files the hints name
  (its resolver already served them); a static error in a library module names
  that module's file.
- **Not done** (each in Proposed below or a later packet):
  fn:load-xquery-module (needs the evaluator); the static base URI and source
  name of a library module at run time (cbcl-module-002, base-URI-modules-001,
  xqhof16, xqhof18, try-catch-map3: the unit has one of each); named item types
  across an import cycle (modules-43); every module of a namespace for a
  hintless import (modules-collide-var-001, -fn-001: one request gets one
  module, as the QT4 driver serves the first); a library module's context value
  type (contextDecl-050, -051, -054: not checked).
- Measured (release, all 737 XQ40 test sets): 39,541 to 39,698 passed, no case
  lost; prod-ModuleImport 23 to 112 of 141 (94 errors to 1; the rest XQ10-only,
  schema import or above), prod-AxisStep.J +24, prod-ItemTypeDecl +9,
  prod-CompNamespaceConstructor +6, fn-id +5, prod-NamedRecordTypeDecl +5,
  prod-ContextItemDecl +5. misc-HtmlTestSuite (1,379) now gets past its import
  and stops at fn:parse-html; fn-load-xquery-module (141) and misc-Subtyping
  (159) stay "not run".

**Sources**: XQ40 passes, all 737 test sets, before and after, and the test
sets that changed (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build).

### D149. Keys and XSLT functions (packet 4.10)

**Summary**: An XSLT function table puts stylesheet functions and the XSLT-only
library part before the processor's; xsl:key indexes are built lazily with
map:build once per evaluation and tree through an evaluation memo.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D101, D103, D118, D139, D142, D144. `src/xslt_key.c`
with `src/xslt_key_internal.h`, `src/function_library_xslt.c`,
`tests/xslt_key_test.c`; no IR kind, no public header.

- **XSLT function table** (glossary): `sxml_xslt_declare_functions` puts one
  table in front of every static context of the stylesheet (before 4.12's
  components table): stylesheet functions lowered into the unit, then the rows
  of the XSLT-only library parts (D101: parts whose language set has XSLT and
  not XPath), then the processor's table. A stylesheet function becomes an IR
  function when an expression first names it; `sxml_xslt_lower_functions`
  lowers the bodies asked for (twice: before the templates are released, again
  after the global variables).
- **Library part `xslt`** (`sxml_function_library_xslt_languages =
  SXML_LANGUAGE_XSLT`): system-property, available-system-properties,
  function-available, element-available, type-available (moved from
  `src/xslt_static.c`, which now serves its expressions the first five rows,
  `sxml_xslt_static_functions`), current, document (4.0 options map or base
  node), unparsed-entity-uri and -public-id (the zero-length value: trees keep
  no unparsed entities). Names given as strings resolve against the running
  unit's static namespaces (D84): a static expression's own, a stylesheet's
  those of the invocation's template (D142), not each expression's (Proposed
  below).
- **fn:current**: a parameter default `SXML_PARAMETER_DEFAULT_CURRENT_ITEM`
  (`function_library_internal.h`); lowering reads focus part `CURRENT_ITEM`,
  the focus the innermost embedding started with
  (`sxml_xpath_lowerer.embedding_focus`, set in the embedding frame), so in a
  pattern it is the item matched (D118). Inside an inline function it is
  UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE (it would need a capture).
- **Entries taking the caller's context value themselves**: an entry whose
  `parameter_types` already cover the parameters the caller supplies is called
  as it is instead of the entry of the longer arity (`src/xpath_lower.c`,
  static calls and references). fn:key#2 is an IR function (key-name,
  key-value, context) distinct from fn:key#3.
- **Keys** (20.2): the declarations of one name are one key (XTSE1222 when
  collation or composite differ; XTSE1205 for use and content, or neither). Its
  build function is `map:build` over the tree's nodes and attributes with the
  use values of each matching declaration (match-N: the D118 match function in
  a TRY_CATCH giving false, 6.5; use-N: the attribute or sequence constructor
  with the node as fixed focus) as keys; fn:key dispatches on the resolved name
  and looks values up in the index that the internal row key-index returns. Key
  values: string-like as xs:string, or their collation key under a
  non-codepoint collation; numbers as xs:double (eq promotes, so 3.7 matches
  number('3.7')); a composite key is one string of tagged canonical texts.
  Result: `/.` (document order, no duplicates); fn:key#3 keeps
  descendants-or-self of $top; fn:key#2 raises XTDE1270 when the root is not a
  document node.
- **Evaluation memo** (glossary; `src/evaluator.c`, additive to
  `evaluator_internal.h`): entries (computation address and number, subject
  node by identity) to a value, released when the evaluation ends. key-index
  calls the build function on a miss (a resumable body, D75) and stores the
  map: each index is built once per evaluation and tree, lazily. 4.12
  (xsl:function cache) and 4.14 (accumulators) can use the same memo.
- **fn:copy-of** is xsl:copy-of's copy (`sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_copy_of`,
  exported from `src/xslt_lower_construct.c`); **fn:snapshot** an XPath text
  over fn:copy-of, fold-right and computed constructors (ancestors with their
  attributes and namespaces).
- **Patterns** (D118 amended): a step whose predicates are all non-positional
  (each a comparison, logical, instance-of, castable or quantified expression,
  a string or boolean literal, nodes, or a call of a listed boolean or string
  function, and none names position or last) is tested on the item with a
  singleton focus instead of being selected again from its origin (6.3.2.3
  gives the same result). attr/match runs in 12 s in a debug build (match-242
  was 60 s alone).
- Left to other packets: current-group, current-grouping-key, current-merge-\*
  (4.9), regex-group (4.11), accumulator-before/-after (4.14),
  current-output-uri (4.13), xsl:evaluate (4.7: XTDE3175, D145),
  fn:apply-templates (needs the mode at run time; 5 cases), fn:transform (out
  of scope), function-available at run time (the dynamic context's table is the
  host's: Proposed).

### D150. Functions and declarations (packet 4.12)

**Summary**: Stylesheet functions, attribute sets, decimal formats, the global
context item, whitespace stripping and host parameters are lowered, with
globals ordered by a component dependency graph.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D101, D135, D139, D142, D144, D145.
`src/xslt_lower_declaration.c`, `src/xslt_whitespace.c` with
`src/xslt_whitespace_internal.h`, `tests/xslt_declaration_test.c`; hooks in
`src/xslt_lower.c`, `src/xslt_lower_construct.c`, `src/xslt_lower_template.c`,
`src/xslt_lower_control.c`, `src/processor.c`. No IR kind, no evaluator change,
no public header.

- **Stylesheet functions** (10.3), as XQuery's declared functions (D135):
  `sxml_xslt_declare_components` (before templates) adds one IR function per
  arity of each component's arity range and puts a function table in front of
  every static context's (so patterns, AVTs, globals and 4.10's table see
  them); bodies are lowered after the templates (they may call them) with an
  absent focus, parameters as slots 1.., the result coerced to `as` (TRY_CATCH
  mapping XPTY0004 to XTTE0780). A shorter arity binds the defaults of the
  left-out optional parameters (`required="no"`; select, content as a temporary
  tree without `as`, else ()) and calls the full arity; a default "." is
  SXML_PARAMETER_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_VALUE (the caller's focus, supplied by the
  core); other defaults see no focus. Eclipsed functions (higher precedence,
  containing arity range) and those given up under
  override-extension-function="no" have no IR function. A function in no
  namespace switches the static contexts to NO_NAMESPACE_FIRST, the table falls
  back to fn, and unprefixed call names are interned first (as XQuery).
  XTSE0080, 0580, 0740, 0760, 0761, 0769, 0770, XTSE0020 (override vs
  override-extension-function). cache, new-each-time, streamability and
  visibility are ignored.
- **Attribute sets** (10.2): all declarations of one name (by precedence, then
  order) are one IR function of the focus (item()?, position, size, as a
  template function) plus an absent-focus variant; each body is the invocations
  of every declaration's use-attribute-sets, then its xsl:attribute children.
  `sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_attribute_sets` calls them with the current focus;
  literal result elements, xsl:element and xsl:copy (with the selected item's
  focus) put the result before their own attributes. XTSE0710, XTSE0720
  (explicit-stack DFS).
- **xsl:decimal-format**: merged per name by import precedence (XTSE1290 only
  for a conflict at the winning precedence, XTSE1300 from
  sxml_decimal_format_apply) into the unit's static context (D131), which XSLT
  sets here, once; a packet adding collations to the unit's static context must
  merge with it.
- **xsl:global-context-item** (3.4.9): checked in the main function before the
  invocation: XTDE3086 (required, none), XTTE0590 (as), XTSE3088 (a supplied
  item when use="absent"); XTSE3087, XTSE3089 statically. 4.8's
  `bind_has_focus` is now `sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_has_focus`. Item types of
  `as` (ITEM_TYPE values) are resolved as sequence types (their AST root is
  SEQUENCE_TYPE): this also fixes xsl:context-item's `as` (context-item 12 to
  29 passed).
- **Whitespace stripping** (4.2.2): a copy through a filtering tree builder
  (the specification's "copy of the source tree"), so parsed trees never change
  and nothing recurses; best match by precedence, default priority, declaration
  order; xml:space; XTSE0270. The host strips the global context item
  (`sxml_xslt_strip_document`); fn:doc and document() get stripped documents
  through a new **document preparation** of the processor's document loader
  (`sxml_processor_document_loader_configuration.document_preparation`, applied
  to documents from the resolver, not to available documents), which
  `sxml_xslt_whitespace_stripping_as_document_preparation` makes. 4.15 must
  install both.
- **Globals (extends D145)**: initializers are lowered before the templates are
  released (a global's content may call a template: it crashed before); the
  computation order also follows the components an initializer reaches: a graph
  over declarations (globals read, functions named, templates called, every
  template rule for apply-templates, attribute sets used), whose strongly
  connected components (Tarjan, on an explicit stack) give the order. Cycles
  through components are left to the evaluator; D145's direct cycles stay
  static errors.
- **Host parameters** (D112): a supplied stylesheet parameter is a BOUND global
  slot of the unit, found by name (the evaluator coerces it, and its
  initializer does not run); static parameters also go to the reader. Nothing
  else was needed for the harness; 4.15 maps `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_transform`'s
  parameters the same way.
- Not done: xsl:character-map (4.13 owns serialization), memoization (`cache`,
  `new-each-time="no"`: function-1025/1026/1031), a parameter left out before a
  keyword argument gets () not its default (the core's rule for library
  functions), function-lookup of stylesheet functions at run time (the dynamic
  context's table is the host's).
- Measured with a scratch harness (lower, evaluate, serialize; XPath
  assertions; host parameters): function 13 to 98 of 124, attribute-set 1 to
  47/49, strip-space 8 to 25/26, global-context-item 0 to 10/12, context-item
  11 to 29/32, param 14 to 31/31, variable 16 to 90/108, whitespace 20 to 24/27
  (before: HEAD of 4.8, without 4.7), format-number 66/70; 4.8's eleven sets
  474 of 614 (D144: 316 of 615).

### D152. Sorting and grouping (packet 4.9)

**Summary**: The evaluator's SORT gains per-key collations, an order atom and
composite keys; xsl:sort becomes SORT keys, and xsl:for-each-group and
xsl:merge reuse SORT and the XQuery group-by row through one grouping row.

Recorded 2026-10-17, after D79, D116, D118, D136, D137, D142, D144, D145.
`src/xslt_lower_group.c`, `src/xslt_group.c` (`src/xslt_group_internal.h`),
`tests/xslt_group_test.c`; hooks in `src/xslt_lower.c`,
`src/xslt_lower_control.c` (xsl:for-each), `src/xslt_lower_template.c`
(xsl:apply-templates), `src/xpath_lower.c` (context functions),
`src/evaluator.c` (SORT). No IR kind, no public header.

- **Evaluator SORT** (fixes 3.10's Proposed (a) and D116/D136's last
  codepoint-only body): a descending key reverses the whole order, empty keys
  included (XQuery 4.0, 4.13.9: "empty greatest descending" puts () first);
  each key's collation is resolved once per SORT through the one resolver
  (`sxml_function_library_find_collation`, FOCH0002 otherwise, also for an
  empty input) and strings compare with
  `sxml_function_library_compare_collated` (glossary `sort_key_rule`).
  `sxml_ir_sort_key` gains `order` (an xs:string atom, "ascending" or
  "descending", read when evaluated: an xsl:sort order AVT) and `is_composite`
  (XSLT 4.0, 13.1.2: a key is a sequence compared item by item, the shorter
  first; otherwise more than one item is XPTY0004 as before). The text form
  prints them; the verifier checks the atom.
- **xsl:sort** is one SORT key per xsl:sort, under for-each, apply-templates
  (the select value is sorted before the MAP or APPLY_TEMPLATES), perform-sort
  and for-each-group (`sxml_xslt_lowering_call_sort`). AVTs use the
  instruction's focus; data-type number/text convert the key (`data(K) !
  number(.)`), a QName converts nothing; lang/case-order without collation give
  `UCA?fallback=yes;lang=L;caseFirst=C` (D116's fallback, lang ignored), none
  the codepoint collation. Fixed invalid values are XTSE0020, computed ones
  XTDE0030 when evaluated; XTSE1015, XTSE1017, XTSE1040; a TRY_CATCH maps
  XPTY0004 to XTDE1030 and FOCH0002 to XTDE1035. Stable is always.
- **xsl:for-each-group**: a MAP over the population makes one grouping pair per
  item ([item, keys] atomized, untyped as string, distinct for group-by; [item,
  matches] for patterns: the match expression lowered in place with the item as
  fixed focus, errors are no match, 6.5); the row `for-each-group($pairs,
  $method, $collation)` of `src/xslt_group.c` returns group arrays [current
  group, current grouping key]; group-by calls the XQuery group-by row (D137)
  over [item, key] tuples (composite keys one member per item, padded with
  empty members), so keys compare exactly as XQuery's; adjacent runs and
  pattern boundaries are the row's. xsl:sort sorts the group arrays with the
  initial item as context item, the group's position and count, and the current
  group bound. The body is a MAP over the groups whose focus is the initial
  item with the MAP's position and size slots. XTSE1080, XTSE1090, XTTE1100,
  XTDE1110.
- **xsl:merge** is the same parts: per merge source (for-each-item,
  for-each-source as `doc(resolve-uri(., base))`, or none) tuples [source
  number, item, keys...] (keys with a singleton focus), all tuples sorted
  stably by the first source's merge keys (SORT keys are tuple members,
  `tuple_key_offset`), runs of equal keys by the row (composite, the first
  key's collation), and the merge-action as the group body. XTSE2200, XTSE3190,
  XTSE3195, XTSE3200.
- **Context functions** (glossary): in XSLT, fn:current-group(),
  current-grouping-key(), current-merge-group(), current-merge-key(),
  current-merge-key-array() read the variable Q{XSLT}local-name the instruction
  put in scope (XTSE0080 keeps the namespace out of stylesheet variables); a
  variable bound to NONE (pattern grouping) or none in the current function
  raises XTDE1061/1071/3480/3510 when evaluated. `name#0` makes a closure over
  the value (4.0: it retains it). current-merge-group($source) is map:get of
  Q{XSLT} current-merge-sources. Lowering-wide XPath ASTs (short texts, match
  expressions) are kept until the lowering ends (`sxml_xslt_lowering_keep_ast`
  in `src/xslt_lower.c`, glossary `kept_ast`; 4.14 uses them too).
- Deviations: the current group is lexical, so a template called from the body
  sees none (XTDE1061; the spec makes it dynamic there); split-when and
  merge-when are UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE; sort keys of groups are evaluated with
  the group's position; merge inputs are always sorted (no XTDE2220, XTDE2210),
  equality under the first key's collation, a composite merge key is the keys'
  concatenation; current-merge-group with an unknown name gives () (not
  XTDE3490), with () an error.
- Measured with a scratch harness (each case's initial template or match="/",
  xml/error/string/file assertions; release of HEAD 2f0c640 plus the packet):
  insn/sort 74 of 82 runnable cases (before: 0, xsl:sort was UNSUPPORTED),
  insn/for-each-group 79 of 86 (before: 0), insn/merge 61 of 88 (before: 0);
  the rest need xsl:function, schemas, collections, xsl:number or accumulators,
  or are the deviations above (split-when, XTDE2210, XTDE2220, XTDE3490). QT4
  XQ40: prod-EmptyOrderDecl 28 to 32, prod-OrderByClause 139,
  prod-GroupByClause 37, unchanged; ctest (debug, debug-gcc, wasm) and lint
  pass.

### D153. Numbering and analyze-string (packet 4.11)

**Summary**: xsl:number is lowered as the specification's formal definition in
XPath texts with one format-place-marker row over the format-integer engine,
and xsl:analyze-string as fn:matching-segments with captured groups in a
context variable.

Recorded 2026-10-18, after D105, D114, D118, D119, D142, D145, D149, D152.
`src/xslt_lower_number.c` (rule view `sxml_xslt_instruction_rules_number`, one
line in `src/xslt_lower.c`), `tests/xslt_number_test.c`; additive edits to
`src/format.c`, `src/function_library_format.c`, `src/function_library_xslt.c`,
`src/xpath_lower.c` and `src/function_library_internal.h`; no IR kind, no
evaluator change, no public header.

- **xsl:number** (12) is 12.3's formal definition as XPath texts with their
  inputs as variables (D152's way): the selected node (XTTE0990, also for an
  absent focus, XTTE1000), the nodes count is tried on (the ancestors-or-self
  and their preceding siblings; for level="any" the preceding nodes and the
  ancestors-or-self), a FILTER of them by the count pattern's match expression
  (D118, inline, the item as fixed focus, an error is no match, 6.5; without
  count, a text for the selected node's kind and name), the same for from (on
  the ancestors-or-self, or the any-level candidates), then one text per level:
  matches-from's root case is `(from | root($s))[last()]`, a counted node's
  preceding siblings are the counted candidates with its parent before it.
  value (12.2) is `xs:integer(round(number(.)))`, exact for xs:decimal,
  XTDE0980; start-at (12.1) re-bases in a text (XTDE0030); XTSE0975 statically.
- **Formatting** is one internal row, format-place-marker
  (`src/xslt_number_internal.h`, defined beside fn:format-integer), over D119's
  engine: `src/format.c` splits the format into prefix, format tokens with
  their separators (". " before a number formatted by the first token) and
  suffix, and `sxml_integer_formatting` gained grouping-separator/grouping-size
  (a string every N digits of a decimal representation). An unparsable token is
  "1" (12.4). Ordinal: any value but "", no, 0, false. lang (xs:language or "")
  and letter-value (alphabetic, traditional) are checked (XTDE0030) and
  otherwise ignored: English only (D97). An empty place marker gives prefix and
  suffix (Saxon's behaviour; QT4 number-0806, -3205 expect it). Title-case
  words are "Twenty Two" here (Saxon's; number-0105, -2506), "Twenty-two" in
  fn:format-integer.
- **xsl:analyze-string** (17.1) is fn:matching-segments (one regex engine,
  D105, D114) of the select value coerced to `xs:string?`, the non-matching
  segments put between the matches by an XPath text (strings; matches stay
  fn:matching-segment-records), inside a TRY_CATCH mapping FORX0002/0001 to
  XTDE1140/1145; then a MAP over the segments whose body is a CONDITIONAL of
  the two children (select or sequence constructor) with the segment's string
  as context item in a slot of its own and the MAP's position and size.
  XTSE1130, XTSE1132, XTSE3185. compiled-regex is UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.
- **Captured groups, a context variable** (glossary): a new parameter default
  `SXML_PARAMETER_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_VARIABLE` makes the caller pass the variable
  Q{XSLT}N (N the parameter's name) lexically in scope, or () (captured from an
  inline function only when captured; a function item of the shorter arity
  captures it, so regex-group#1 keeps the groups, 17.2.2).
  xsl:matching-substring has Q{XSLT}regex-groups = the segment's groups map
  with entry 0 (value, position, nr 0) first; xsl:non-matching-substring has
  (). fn:regex-groups and fn:regex-group (rows of the `xslt` part) read it;
  regex-group(N) also finds a named group by its nr (analyze-string-406, as
  XSLT 3.0 had it). 4.9's context functions (current-group and the others,
  D152) can use the same default instead of a second mechanism.
- Measured with a scratch harness (lower, evaluate, serialize; XPath assertions
  through `sxml xpath`) over the in-scope cases (D95; the
  combinations_for_numbering ones are not): insn-number 152/161,
  insn-analyze-string 56/62, misc-regex 64/65, fn-format-number 67/70 (with
  4.12's decimal formats); before the packet none of the instructions lowered.
  Of the rest: German words (6), Unicode digit sequences, the four
  dynamic-scope cases below, xsl:sort under xsl:number's callers, an
  attribute-set case.
- Deviations: the captured groups are lexical, so a template called from
  xsl:matching-substring sees none (17.2 says they pass through apply-templates
  and call-template; QT4 analyze-string-078 to -081): an implicit tunnel
  parameter would carry them (src/xslt_lower_template.c). A start-at known
  statically is checked when evaluated (XTDE0030, not XTSE0020, number-0109).
  German and other languages, the Unicode numbering sequences (circled digits,
  number-0819..0821, out of scope by combinations_for_numbering otherwise) and
