### D154. XQuery conformance sweep 1 (packet 3.14)

**Summary**: The dynamic context keeps one global table per unit, a native step
kind evaluates another sealed unit on the machine, and fn:load-xquery-module is
built on it as XQuery's own function table.

Recorded 2026-10-18, after D71, D75, D95, D135, D148. No public header changed;
no IR kind added.

- **Global tables** (glossary `global_table`): the dynamic context keeps one
  table of global slots per unit (the evaluation's own first), and a task reads
  the table of its function's unit. The evaluator's restriction "only the
  evaluation's own unit reads globals" is gone; a unit with no table (a
  function item called after its evaluation ended) still reads none, so
  closures keep capturing globals (D55).
- **Unit evaluation** (glossary `unit_evaluation`): a resumable native step
  kind, `SXML_NATIVE_STEP_KIND_EVALUATE_UNIT`
  (`src/function_library_internal.h`), asks the machine to evaluate another
  sealed unit on its own task stack: a global table from the step's global
  values (coerced, XPTY0004), its initializers
  (`sxml_evaluator_start_global_initializers` now takes the table), its main
  function, and the next step gets the value, as after a CALL. The tables live
  until the evaluation (or `call_function_item`) ends. No C nesting (D71).
- **fn:load-xquery-module** (F&O 4.0, 18.2; `src/xquery_load_module.c`):
  XQuery's own function table, put after the host's by
  `sxml_xquery_compile_module` for one compilation, so only programs that
  compile XQuery link it (the JavaScript package's `sxml.wasm` does not, D146);
  fn:function-lookup does not see it (18.2 says the context is not changed; QT4
  does not ask). Its first step writes the module record (glossary
  `module_record`) as a main module, `import module namespace sxml-loaded =
  "NS" at hints; map { "variables": map {QName(NS, v): $sxml-loaded:v, ...},
  "functions": map {QName(NS, f): map {N: sxml-loaded:f#N, ...}} }`, as 18.1
  words it ("as if by evaluating a named function reference Q#N"): the public
  names are read from the ASTs of a first pass that loads the import alone; the
  content option is served by a resolver in front of the evaluation's, as the
  module of the namespace asked for without hint, with the caller's static base
  URI as module URI. The second step returns the record the unit evaluation
  made. Variables' values bind globals by name (any module of the set) after an
  exact type match (FOQM0005, no conversion); context-value and context-item
  (both: FOQM0005). Errors: FOQM0001, FOQM0002 (the import's XQST0059),
  FOQM0003 (any other static error), FOQM0006 (xquery-version above 4.0, no
  evaluation environment); dynamic errors of globals as they are. The QT4
  driver claims feature fn-load-xquery-module for XQ40 runs only. Not done:
  trusted=false (FODC0016, 11 cases), a library module's context value type
  (D148).
- **QT4 driver**: an out-of-scope case (D95) that ends in XPST0017 or
  `SXML_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE` is "not run: needs the non-goal ...", so
  misc-HtmlTestSuite (1,379, fn:parse-html) and fn-parse-html are no longer
  failures; leaks, wrong results and other errors of such cases still count. A
  param's QName prefix is resolved on its element.
- **Arena trees**: blocks of 4 KiB instead of 64 KiB; each element constructor
  makes a tree, and 10,000 of them took 655 MB (fold-left-021 and slice-185
  ended in the driver's memory limit).
- **Measured** (release, all 737 sets of each spec, code of 00ac981): XQ40
  39,698 to 39,924 passed, in scope 96.4 % to 96.9 %, XQ-only 85.3 % to 97.9 %
  (9,321 of 9,523; the non-goal cases no longer run), "error" outcomes 5 to 1
  (modules-40, below), none lost but
  fn-system-properties-supports-dynamic-xquery-false (now not run, as the
  feature is claimed); fn-load-xquery-module 0 to 103 of 117 run,
  misc-Subtyping 0 to 109 of 110; method-\* 97.5 %. XP40 unchanged: 30,630
  passed, in scope 97.0 %, 0 errors (32 out-of-scope failures now not run).
  Slice 198/198.
- **Not done** (Proposed below): closures reading globals at call time (D135
  (c)); defaults that read the focus (D135 (b)); keyword arguments after an
  omitted parameter of a declared function (modules-40, the last "error"); a
  library module's static base URI and source name at run time; hintless split
  namespaces; ##any; function-lookup of declared functions. Each needs
  `src/xpath_lower.c`, `src/ir_internal.h` or `include/sxml/xquery.h`, which
  other packets were editing.

**Sources**: XQ40 and XP40 passes, all 737 sets of each spec, before and after,
and the slice (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, `tools/conformance-report.py`, release
build, at 00ac981); memory of 10,000 element constructors with 64 KiB arena
blocks (655 MB).

### D155. Accumulators (packet 4.14)

**Summary**: Each XSLT accumulator lowers to match and rule functions and a
fold-left traversal without recursion, its values built lazily once per
evaluation and tree in the evaluation memo, with copies linked to originals.

Recorded 2026-10-18, after D118, D144, D149, D150. `src/xslt_accumulator.c`
with `src/xslt_accumulator_internal.h`, five internal rows in
`src/function_library_xslt.c`, `tests/xslt_accumulator_test.c`; hooks in
`src/xslt_lower.c` (declare, lower, scope of the main function, release, the
rule view; field `accumulators` of `sxml_xslt_lowering`),
`src/xslt_lower_construct.c` (xsl:copy-of) and `src/xslt_key.c` (fn:copy-of,
fn:snapshot). No IR kind, no evaluator change, no public header.

- **Lowering** (as templates, D144): each xsl:accumulator-rule is a match
  function (its pattern, D118, in a TRY_CATCH making every error false, 6.5)
  and a rule function of ($node, $value) with the node as fixed focus and
  `$value` (no namespace) bound, its select or sequence constructor coerced to
  `as` (XPTY0004); initial-value the same over the root. One declaration per
  name, the highest import precedence (XTSE3350 at a tie); XTSE3355, XTSE3185,
  XTSE3300 (use-accumulators of xsl:mode and xsl:source-document: names of
  accumulators, none twice, #all alone). streamable is read and ignored.
- **Traversal** (19.4, no recursion, D71): per accumulator an IR function
  lowered from an XPath text (as src/xslt_key.c's, D149): a fold-left over
  `$root/descendant-or-self::node()` (attributes and namespaces are not
  visited) whose state map holds the value, an explicit stack of nodes whose
  end event is pending, and two maps from generate-id to the pre- and
  post-descent values; each node first closes the stack entries that are not
  its ancestors (end events, innermost first), then has its start event; the
  last rule in document order of the phase whose pattern matches gives the
  value. Depth is found in one step for a first child or a sibling, else by the
  ancestor axis.
- **Values** (19.3, lazily per tree): fn:accumulator-before/-after are IR
  functions of a function table put in front of every static context (after the
  XSLT function table, before 4.12's). Row accumulator-values builds once per
  evaluation, accumulator and root, through the evaluation memo (D149, reused:
  no new store); while building, the entry is the empty sequence, so a rule
  asking for its own accumulator raises XTDE3400; a failed build leaves a retry
  mark, so every later call raises the error again (19.5). XTDE3340
  (accumulator-name: an xs:QName, or an EQName resolved as fn:key's names),
  XTTE3360.
- **Applicability** (19.2): row accumulator-scope records the applicable
  accumulators of a tree in the memo: the main function for the initial match
  selection (use-accumulators of the initial mode's xsl:mode; none without
  one), xsl:source-document for its document (with streamable="yes" only
  accumulators declared streamable); every other tree has all of them;
  accumulator-values raises XTDE3362 for one left out.
- **Copies** (19.10): fn:copy-of, fn:snapshot and xsl:copy-of with
  copy-accumulators="yes" link each copy to its original in the memo (row
  accumulator-link, only when the stylesheet declares an accumulator); the
  accumulator functions map a node under a linked copy to the node at its place
  in the original and read that tree's values.
- **xsl:source-document** (18.1, no streaming): fn:doc of href, the scope, the
  content with the document node as singleton focus (no packet owned it).
- Not done: streaming; XTDE3350 (an absent focus raises XPDY0002);
  xsl:merge-source use-accumulators (4.9's xsl:merge); a copy of a copy; 19.5's
  functional dependency (one failing rule fails every call on that tree).
  Costs: a node deeper than a first child or a sibling pays its depth; a call
  on a linked copy pays the copy's size; memo entries are a list (many linked
  copies make lookups linear).

### D156. Output and result documents (packet 4.13)

**Summary**: Stylesheet outputs compile output definitions, character maps and
result document instructions from the sealed AST, and xsl:result-document is
two internal rows that a result writer delivers to the handler.

Recorded 2026-10-18, after D106, D112, D120b, D128, D144, D145, D146, D150.
`src/xslt_output.c` with `src/xslt_output_internal.h`, the library part
`src/function_library_output.c` (XSLT only), `tests/xslt_output_test.c`; hooks:
one rule view in `src/xslt_lower.c`, declarations in
`src/xslt_lower_internal.h`, the tunnel mark in `src/xslt_lower_template.c`,
`result_writer` in the evaluation environment (`src/processor_internal.h`). No
IR kind, no evaluator change, no public header.

- **Stylesheet outputs** (glossary), compiled from the sealed AST and keeping
  nothing of it (4.15 makes them next to the unit): output definitions, named
  character maps, result document instructions. An xsl:output's attributes
  become serialization parameter texts (D146; booleans yes/no, names as
  EQNames, html-version as a decimal) merged over the definition's declarations
  (highest precedence wins, XTSE1560 for two at that precedence unless a higher
  one follows; the name lists of cdata-section-elements and
  suppress-indentation are the union) and read by
  `sxml_serialization_parameter_reader_read_texts` over the parameter document
  (read at compile time through the resolver; a document that cannot be found
  is ignored, 26.1.5; its parameters win over the attributes, so texts it gives
  are dropped). build-tree is read here; omit-xml-declaration defaults to no;
  has_serialization_method when a text or the document gives method. Reader
  errors (SEPM0016, SESU0007, ...) become static errors at the declaration.
  `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_outputs_get_definition` is what
  `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_get_output_definition` returns.
- **Character maps** (26.1.6): the declaration of highest precedence per name
  (XTSE1580 for a tie there), expanded once each in post-order on an explicit
  stack (XTSE1590, XTSE1600), concatenations merged "later wins" by a heapsort
  into one sorted map; use-character-maps of an output definition concatenates
  in increasing precedence, then the parameter document's maps; of
  xsl:result-document over the definition's (26.2.4). `fn:character-map`
  (26.1.7) returns one as a map.
- **xsl:result-document** (26.2) is two internal rows around its content (`let
  $o := result-document-open(N, (values), temporary) let $raw := ... return
  result-document-close($o, $raw)`), N the AST node index naming its result
  document instruction, values its value templates in a fixed order. Open
  checks XTDE1480, resolves format (XTDE1460) and href against the base output
  URI, checks XTDE1490, merges the effective definition (the definition's texts
  with the instruction's over them, "" absent for doctype-\*, "#absent" for
  item-separator, the instruction's parameter document over all, output-version
  as version) and makes the URI the current output URI. Close calls the
  handler's open, delivers (DEFAULT by build-tree, RAW, TREE, SERIALIZED) and
  close: the handler sees each result document when its raw result is complete,
  so open and close alternate as D112 says and a nested result document comes
  first. A document whose content failed is dropped (the handler never saw it).
- **Temporary output state** (26.2.6): lexically inside xsl:variable, param,
  with-param, function, key, sort, accumulator-rule, merge-key a RAISE of
  XTDE1480; dynamically, an xsl:apply-templates or call-template there puts
  Q{urn:x-sxml:output}temporary-output-state into the tunnel parameters it
  passes, and open tests the received map; a function call invocation sets the
  writer's flag.
- **Delivery** (shared by both results): `sxml_xslt_serialize_result` (the
  method given or chosen from the raw result, 26.1.2; indent DEFAULT is yes for
  html and xhtml), `sxml_xslt_build_result_tree` (the serializer's sequence
  normalizer into an arena tree, base URI the result's URI),
  `sxml_xslt_result_builds_tree`. The **result writer** (glossary) delivers the
  principal result after the evaluation
  (`sxml_xslt_result_writer_deliver_principal_result`: XTDE1490, an empty
  principal result with a result document of its URI discarded).
- **fn:current-output-uri**: the writer's current output URI (the innermost
  open result document, else the base output URI); absent in temporary output
  state (function call invocation) or without a base output URI. Not cleared in
  functions, global variables and patterns (26.3.1): a context variable (D153)
  bound by those lowerings would do it (current-output-uri-001, -005, -401).
- **Collector**: the public `sxml_xslt_result_document_collector_*` of xslt.h
  is implemented here (values or bytes by URI, the byte bound), so 4.15 does
  not need to.
- Not done: XTDE1500 (reading a written URI), disable-output-escaping (ignored,
  as Serialization 4.0 allows), both parameter documents of xsl:output and
  xsl:result-document at once (the instruction's replaces the definition's),
  validation and type of xsl:result-document.
- Measured with a scratch harness (lower, evaluate with a result writer and a
  test handler, deliver; serialization assertions on the principal result
  serialized by its definition, assert-result-document by URI, a result
  document with the base output URI standing for an empty principal result):
  decl/output 235/244, decl/character-map 32/33, insn/result-document 129/149
  (17 need accumulators or xsl:merge), insn/xsl-document 23/25,
  fn/current-output-uri 6/16 (the clearing above, initial functions, the
  harness's base output URI). Before: no xsl:result-document was lowered and
  xsl:output was not read.

### D157. The XSLT API, the XSLT driver's runs and sxml transform (packet 4.15)

**Summary**: `src/xslt.c` implements `include/sxml/xslt.h`, passing invocation
values as invocation globals bound by name; the XSLT driver runs the suite and
the CLI gains `sxml transform`.

Recorded 2026-10-18, after D112, D117, D139, D144, D145, D149, D150, D156.
`src/xslt.c` implements `include/sxml/xslt.h` (unchanged), imitating
`src/xquery.c`; no IR kind, no evaluator change, no public header.

- **Compile**: the principal module is the text or one resolver request
  (XSLT_MODULE: the reference resolved against the static base URI;
  XSLT_PACKAGE: name and package-version, "\*" for none; XTSE0165 and XTSE3000
  when not delivered, XTSE3000 for a principal package that is no xsl:package),
  read with the static parameters and the default collation (D139), lowered
  once as apply-templates in the default mode (every static error of the
  lowering is found here), its outputs compiled (D156), a function library over
  the XSLT parts made, the static parameters retained. The AST is kept: any
  other invocation (call-template, an initial mode, an initial match selection,
  a function call) lowers its own unit when a transformation asks (the main
  function is the invocation, D144). On failure an error location names the
  caller's name for the principal module (the AST that its module URIs borrowed
  from is gone); collation bindings of the host are not passed (the reader
  takes only a default collation).
- **Shared evaluation** (accepts 4.10's Proposed item, D149):
  `sxml_unit_evaluation` gains `extension` (`src/xpath_api_internal.h`): a
  function table for the dynamic context (the XSLT library parts, so
  function-available and fn:function-lookup see the XSLT functions), the
  document preparation (strip-space for fn:doc and document(), D150) and the
  result writer; XPath and XQuery pass NULL. Names given as strings still
  resolve against the unit's static namespaces (per-expression namespaces are
  left open).
- **Invocation globals** (glossary): the run-time values of an invocation are
  globals of the unit after the stylesheet's globals and the context global,
  named `Q{urn:x-sxml:invocation}template-parameters`, `tunnel-parameters`
  (maps from xs:QName, default the empty map; only when the lowering request
  sets `reads_invocation_parameters`, which src/xslt.c always does),
  `initial-match-selection` and `function-arguments` (an array; members coerced
  to the parameter types). src/xslt.c binds them by name like stylesheet
  parameters, so one mechanism carries everything the host supplies.
  Apply-templates without a selection or focus is XTDE0044; an initial function
  that is not visibility="public"/"final" (2.4.5: xsl:stylesheet functions are
  private) or has no IR function of that arity is XTDE0041.
- **Prime and run**: the global context item is stripped
  (`sxml_xslt_strip_document`); static parameters, then the request's
  stylesheet parameters, then the invocation values are bound by name (XTDE0050
  is the initializer's, computed eagerly); a result writer per transformation
  (temporary output state for a function call) delivers the raw result. Changed
  in D156: a result document whose absolute URI is the base output URI (no
  href) is the principal result, delivered as the request asks (CLI stdout),
  not to the handler; XTDE1490 when the raw principal result is not empty.
- **Driver** (`tests/xslt/driver/xslt_execution.c`, D117's plan): a budgeted
  processor per case; the resolver is the QT4 resource table over a
  never-loaded QT4 "file catalog" with XSLT_MODULE served as XML_DOCUMENT and
  XSLT_PACKAGE as the matching <package>; params by XPath; no source, initial
  template or mode means call-template (xsl:initial-template); a serialization
  assertion without <output> serializes (the bytes parsed back for the other
  assertions); result documents to the collector, messages to a trace sink.
  Assertions (`sxml_xslt_test_check_assertions`): all-of/any-of/not on an
  explicit stack, assert-message (best over messages) and
  assert-result-document call the new `sxml_qt4_check_assertion_element` (the
  QT4 checks of one element), serialization-matches and assert-serialization on
  the serialized bytes as an xs:string (assert-serialization: equal after
  normalize-space, or deep-equal once parsed). Embedded stylesheets are not
  run. `tools/run-xslt.sh` (one process per test set, XT40/) and
  `tools/conformance-report.py` (XT40: areas by suite group, the twelve core
  sets, the XSLT slice; the QT4 report's JSON names its program, accepts 4.1's
  Proposed item).
- **CLI**: `sxml transform [--param]... [--initial-template] [--initial-mode]
  [--method] STYLESHEET [INPUT]` (docs/CLI.md); the stylesheet's base URI is
  `file:PATH` (the local resolver reads `file:` relative paths), so includes
  and fn:doc resolve against the stylesheet; --param values are passed as
  static parameters too; result documents with an href are not written;
  messages to stderr. The WebAssembly CLI's size budget is raised to 5,000,000
  / 1,100,000 bytes (Proposed).
- Fixed on the way: allocation-failure paths in `src/xslt_lower_control.c` (a
  double release of the global arrays, arithmetic on NULL) and
  `src/xslt_lower_template.c` (`allocate_zeroed` leaves NULL on failure); the
  reader passes the XML parser's diagnostic of a module that is not
  well-formed.
- Measured (release, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, whole suite): in scope 7,585 of 8,728
  passed (86.9 %; D95 gate 70 %), 785 failed, 7 errors (memory and step limits:
  array-022, error-0640a/g, function-1031, json-to-xml-013,
  result-document-1501/1502), all 274 test sets finished. Core sets:
  apply-templates 97.4, mode 87.3, match 92.8, for-each-group 90.7, sort 100,
  key 97.1, number 57.5 (114 in-scope cases need combinations_for_numbering,
  such as circled digits, which format-integer lacks), choose 95.4, copy 88.4,
  value-of 53.3, result-document 94.0, function 89.5 %. Top causes: wrong
  results 460 (assert-xml 148, assert 78), XPST0017 70 (packages, fn:transform,
  fn:apply-templates, map:for-key, stream-available), XTSE0340 49 (priority
  patterns), XPST0008/XTSE0650/XTSE0710 around packages (4.16), XPST0051 26
  (record and type aliases), XTDE1450 25 (call-template-ext). Not done:
  function-available and fn:function-lookup of key, accumulator-before/ after
  and stylesheet functions at run time (they are unit functions of the
  lowering, not library rows), per-expression namespaces for names given as
  strings, collation bindings of the host, an implicit package (an
  xsl:stylesheet) as RESOLVED_PACKAGE (Proposed).

**Sources**: XSLT passes in scope, whole suite, with the core sets and the top
causes (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, `tools/conformance-report.py`, release build);
configured: the WebAssembly CLI size budget, 5,000,000 / 1,100,000 bytes (from
`bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt`).

### D158. XQuery conformance sweep 2 (packet 3.14)

**Summary**: XQuery parameter defaults become default functions called with the
caller's focus, XQuery closures read globals at call time, units keep IR
modules, and fn:load-xquery-module honours `trusted`.

Recorded 2026-10-18, after D135, D148, D154. Closes D135 (b) to (g) and D154's
"Not done" but where said. No public header changed; no IR kind.

- **Default functions** (glossary `default_function`, D135 (b), (g)): a
  declared function's optional parameter whose default is not `:= .` is
  `SXML_PARAMETER_DEFAULT_EXPRESSION` with a `default_function_number`
  (`sxml_function_parameter`): an IR function of three parameters, the caller's
  context value, position and size, whose body is the default coerced to the
  parameter's type, lowered with those slots as its focus; its IR function's
  `focus` names the parts it reads (the lowering focus records `parts_read`).
  Static calls go to the full arity and call the default functions of the
  omitted parameters with their own focus
  (`sxml_xpath_lowerer_call_default_function`), so keyword arguments after
  omitted parameters work (modules-40) and `$x := string()` sees the caller's
  context value (5.18.3). A reference F#N whose omitted defaults read the focus
  is a closure that captures those parts and calls the defaults when called (so
  `$x := (., local:f#0)` ends); a reference made without a focus is the shorter
  arity's IR function, which calls the defaults with its absent focus. Defaults
  are lowered first in every module; one that calls a default not lowered yet
  passes all parts without reading them, and a fixpoint over the default
  functions' calls adds the parts they pass on.
- **Closures of XQuery globals** (D135 (c)): `find_free_variables` captures no
  global in XQuery (the unit's global table is read at call time, D154); the
  dependency walk ignores a variable's edge to itself (a read while it is
  computed is BEING_COMPUTED, XQDY0054). XPath and XSLT still capture (function
  items outlive their evaluation there).
- **fn:function-lookup** (D135 (d)): `sxml_evaluator_find_unit_function` finds
  a top-level named IR function of the calling task's unit (XQuery declared
  functions, XSLT stylesheet functions) before the host's table.
- **"##any"** (D135 (e)): `has_any_default_element_namespace` in the XPath
  static context; prefix 0 is bound to no namespace (constructed elements); an
  unprefixed name test or element test is `*:local`, an unprefixed type name is
  in xs (`sxml_xpath_resolved_name`'s `is_any_namespace`).
- **QT4 driver** (D135 (f)): assert-eq atomizes a single node.
- **IR modules** (glossary `ir_module`; D148's Proposed): a unit keeps one
  (source name, static base URI) per library module
  (`sxml_ir_unit_add_module`); every IR function a library module's lowering
  makes carries its `module_number`; the evaluator's static base URI and error
  locations read the function's module.
- **Trust** (F&O 4.0, 18.2): `trusted` (default false) marks the loaded unit
  untrusted (`sxml_ir_unit_set_untrusted`), as is every unit an untrusted call
  loads; fn:doc, unparsed-text(-lines), unparsed-binary, collection and
  uri-collection raise FODC0016 when the running unit is untrusted
  (`sxml_dynamic_context_check_trust`).
- **A library module's context value type** (D148): without a main module
  declaration, the first library module's type is the context global's
  (fn:load-xquery-module checks it, FOQM0005).
- **Function annotations**: IR functions carry their %annotations, copied into
  the unit (`sxml_ir_unit_add_function_annotations`,
  `sxml_xpath_lowerer_read_annotations`) for inline and declared functions;
  partial applications keep them (static and fn:partial-apply).
- Also: keyword placeholders take their written order (FunctionCall-416); an
  xs:untypedAtomic array lookup key is cast to xs:integer (4.7.3).
- **Not done**: hintless imports of a namespace split over modules (needs a
  resolver contract in `include/sxml/xquery.h`, kept as D148 says); a fixed
  default's one value for every call (function-decl-40-060); the focus of
  fn:function-lookup (XP and XQ, 47 cases); static-base-uri#0 made in a library
  module and called elsewhere (xqhof16, 18); "fixed" default element
  namespaces; both main and library context value types at once
  (contextDecl-050, -051).
- **Measured** (release, all 737 sets of each spec; before at 01cf728, after at
  5611dd2): XQ40 39,928 to 40,025 passed, in scope 96.9 % to 97.2 %, XQ-only
  9,325 to 9,404 of 9,523 (97.9 % to 98.8 %), failed 518 to 422, "error"
  outcomes 1 to 0 (the Phase 3 gate's last open count); none lost;
  prod-FunctionDecl 211 to 227, fn-function-annotations 14 to 23,
  fn-load-xquery-module 103 to 111, prod-DefaultNamespaceDecl 71 to 78,
  app-Demos 4 to 11; method-\* 97.5 %. XP40 30,630 to 30,646, in scope 97.0 %
  to 97.1 %, 0 errors, none lost. Slice 198/198.

**Sources**: XQ40 and XP40 passes, all 737 sets of each spec, before
(`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build, at 01cf728); XQ40 and XP40 passes, all 737
sets of each spec, after, and the slice (`tools/run-qt4.sh`,
`tools/conformance-report.py`, release build, at 5611dd2).

### D159. XSLT conformance sweep 1 (packet 4.17)

**Summary**: The shared picture engine gains alphabets and symbol sequences
such as circled digits, key and accumulator builds share one kept-build step,
guarded matches are one helper, and focus-independent filters evaluate their
predicate once.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D119, D149, D153, D155, D157.

- **Numbering sequences** in the shared picture engine (`src/format.c`, so
  fn:format-integer and xsl:number both have them): a token of one codepoint
  names an alphabet (glossary: a, A, Greek alpha with final sigma, Alpha
  without U+03A2), counted as before by bijective numeration, or a symbol
  sequence (glossary): one symbol per number over runs of codepoints, decimal
  outside them: circled digits 0 to 50, parenthesized and full-stop digits to
  20 (DIGIT ZERO FULL STOP for 0), digit-comma 0 to 9, dingbat and double
  circled digits, circled and parenthesized ideographs, Aegean, Coptic epact,
  Rumi, Brahmi, Sinhala archaic, counting rod and Mende Kikakui numbers. The
  kinds LOWER_/UPPER_ALPHABETIC became ALPHABETIC and SYMBOLS with a
  `sequence_index`. The XSLT driver declares the 19 combinations.
- **Kept builds** (`src/function_library_xslt.c`): key-index and
  accumulator-values share one step (`step_kept_build`): the memo entry is the
  empty sequence while the build runs, so a key whose pattern or use calls
  fn:key for itself raises XTDE0640 (it ran out of memory), as accumulators
  raise XTDE3400.
- **Guarded matches**: the four copies of "an error while matching is no match"
  (keys, accumulators, group-starting-with/ending-with, xsl:number count/from)
  are `sxml_xslt_lowering_make_guarded_match`, whose clauses raise XTDE0640 and
  XTDE3400 again (6.5: circularity overrides).
- **Filters** (`src/evaluator.c`): a FILTER whose focus slots are all unused
  (the predicate does not depend on the focus) computes the predicate once and,
  for a single item or (), applies it as a constant predicate: `$s[$k]` takes
  one item instead of testing every position (it was quadratic: 20,000 accesses
  took 26 s, now 0.02 s).
- **xsl:analyze-string** takes its segments from the internal row
  analyze-segments (`src/xslt_number_internal.h`, defined in
  `src/function_library_regex.c`: fn:matching-segments with the gaps as
  strings) instead of fn:substring per gap, which is linear per call on
  non-ASCII text (result-document-1501/1502 ran out of steps).
- **fn:map-for-key** (20.2.3) as two stylesheet functions over the key index
  (XTDE1262 for composite or collated keys, XTDE1270); function-available sees
  the running unit's named functions and the fn functions lowering implements
  (key, map-for-key, copy-of, snapshot, accumulator-before/-after).
- The snippet-text helpers of `src/xslt_key.c` and `src/xslt_accumulator.c` are
  one module, `src/xslt_snippet_text.c`.
- **Measured** (release, whole XT40): in scope 7,585 (b67c93f) to 7,737 of
  8,728 with this packet alone (86.9 % to 88.6 %), and 7,879 (90.3 %) at
  4cb75fd with packet 4.16's packages; errors 7 to 3; number 57.5 to 97.4 %,
  result-document 94.0 to 95.3 %, map-for-key 0 to 6 of 8, error 447 to 449.
  XP40 30,646 and XQ40 40,025 passed, unchanged; slice 198.
- **Not done** (causes found): value-of (53.3 %) needs zero-length text nodes
  (Proposed) and the cdata attribute; the "~T" type patterns of priority and
  type-alias (XTSE0340) are not in the 13 October 2026 draft, which has
  atomic(), so they were left; the remaining errors are memory
  (json-to-xml-013, array-022: about 9 KB per small tree, each element
  constructor builds a tree of its own, and about 1.5 KB per JSON object) and
  xsl:function cache="yes" (function-1031); static-base-uri, base URIs of
  constructed nodes and names given as strings still read the unit's static
  context, not the expression's (Proposed); call-template-ext (extension
  instructions as template calls, 10.1.3) needs the reader to keep extension
  attributes as expressions; host collation bindings.

### D160. Packages (packet 4.16)

**Summary**: XSLT packages are read into one AST, one copy per xsl:use-package,
and a package table of component instances with visibilities binds each
reference through overrides before one lowering into one unit.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D112, D117, D139, D148, D157. `src/xslt_package.c`
with `src/xslt_package_internal.h` (the package table, glossary); no IR kind,
no evaluator change; `include/sxml/xslt.h` changes one comment (provisional,
D151).

- **D148's design for XSLT**: a package is a set of modules whose components
  have a visibility. One AST holds every package: the reader asks the resolver
  for each xsl:use-package (kind XSLT_PACKAGE, the name as uri_reference and
  absolute_uri, the package-version or "\*") and reads the package's principal
  module in place as a module of relation USED_PACKAGE, the top of a package
  (XTSE3000 when nothing is delivered, XTSE3005 for a package that uses itself,
  XTSE3008 for a use in an imported module). It is read again for every use, so
  each use has components of its own (3.4.5: a package used twice may be
  overridden twice), and parsed once per compilation (same name and range: the
  document is reused). The children of xsl:override are declarations, each with
  a static context of its own (where xsl:original is looked up). For precedence
  a USED_PACKAGE module counts as imported, so an override's template rules
  come before the used package's (3.4.6). One lowering lowers every package's
  declarations into one unit.
- **The table** is made first in the lowering: the package of each module and
  static context; per package, from the last to the first, one component
  instance per own winning declaration (visibility from xsl:expose and the
  visibility attribute, 3.4.5.1; an xsl:stylesheet's named templates and modes
  are public), per overriding declaration (its visibility, else private) and
  per accepted component (xsl:accept, else public/final become private; hidden
  ones are left out), each instance of the used package pointing at its
  successor in the user. **Binding** (3.4.5.5): the referring package's
  instance, then the successors; the last one's declaration is called.
  xsl:original binds to the overridden instance's declaration (3.4.5.4).
  Stylesheet parameters are public, as in XSLT 3.0 and the suite (4.0's 3.4.5.1
  says private; the 3.4.5.2 rule for using packages says public).
- **Lowering**: functions (each static context's function table binds through
  its package; xsl:original in an overriding function), attribute sets (one per
  name and package; xsl:original in use-attribute-sets), global variables (one
  per name and package; each package's static contexts get a view of the names
  it binds with D148's `global_numbers`, plus $xsl:original in an overriding
  variable; a global no view binds, an overridden or hidden abstract one, gets
  no initializer), named templates (call-template, xsl:original), modes (a mode
  is a package and a name: each package has its own unnamed mode, a named mode
  binds like a component, #all is the template's package's modes, XTSE3085 per
  package), and the invocation: the top-level package's public or final initial
  template and function, an initial mode it declares public or final or does
  not declare. Abstract components' bodies raise XTDE3052. The existing checks
  between declarations (XTSE0630, XTSE0660, XTSE0770, XTSE0545, attribute set
  merging) apply within a package.
- **Static errors**: XTSE0020 (package-version of xsl:package or
  xsl:use-package), XTSE3003 (another name, a version out of range), XTSE3010,
  XTSE3020, XTSE3022, XTSE3025 (xsl:expose), XTSE3030, XTSE3032, XTSE3040,
  XTSE3051 (xsl:accept), XTSE3050, XTSE3055, XTSE3058, XTSE3060, XTSE3070
  (arity ranges, parameter, result, variable and context item types identical
  by subtyping both ways, tunnel and required flags), XTSE3080.
- **Versions** (3.4.1): `sxml_xslt_package_version_matches` (versions, "*",
  lists, V.*, V+, to V, V to W). The resolver chooses the version; the driver
  (`tests/xslt/driver/xslt_package_version.c`) serves the highest one the range
  matches, settling D117's package_version_resolution as highest_version, and
  reads the name and version of a catalog <package> without uri= from its file.
- **D157's Proposed item accepted**: a RESOLVED_PACKAGE principal module may be
  an xsl:stylesheet or xsl:transform (3.4: an implicit package); a simplified
  module stays XTSE3000 (`src/xslt.c`, the xslt.h comment).
- **Not done**: keys, accumulators, decimal formats, namespace aliases,
  strip-space, outputs and named types are still stylesheet-wide, not per
  package (use-package-101, -104, override-misc-006); xsl:with-param of
  xsl:use-package and a used package's own static parameters;
  xsl:package-location (the resolver decides); XTSE3075; an abstract variable a
  view binds is computed eagerly, so XTDE3052 also when it is never read
  (accept-042, -043a: XSLT globals are all computed first).
- Also: a library package's global variables have no global context item
  (2.3.2, XPDY0002); the reader's `decide_role` no longer dereferences a
  missing rule (a lint finding).
- Measured (release, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, in-scope passed before -> after):
  decl/package 53 -> 68 of 72, override 30 -> 91 of 102, accept 33 -> 48 of 50,
  expose 12 -> 42 of 42, attr/package-version 25 -> 33 of 34, use-package 13 ->
  34 of 53 (34 of the 45 run: the 8 others need package_version_resolution
  lowest_version or unspecified, and one streaming); the six sets +150. Whole
  suite 7,585 -> 7,864 in scope (4.17's numbering included). No other test set
  lost a case.

**Sources**: XT40 in-scope passes, before and after, of the six package sets
and the whole suite (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build).

### D162. D97's exclusions are delays, not non-goals (owner)

**Summary**: The features D97 leaves out are delayed, not dropped: schema
awareness stays Phase 5, the rest becomes Phase 7, and until then each is
rejected or ignored in one place with the specification's error.

Recorded 2026-10-18 on the owner's word: "D97 is accepted only as a delay --
these features need to be supported ultimately." Amends D97 and the "Not in
year one" list of PLAN.md.

- D97 still fixes what Phases 2 to 4 deliver and what their gates count (D95);
  nothing in those phases changes.
- Everything D97 leaves out is owed later, not dropped: full UCA (DUCET,
  tailoring, numeric and case-order options; advanced-uca-fallback),
  fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc (an HTML5 tree builder), invisible XML, schema
  awareness (validate, XSLT validation and type attributes), streaming, the
  XQuery Update Facility, Full Text, EXPath, XPath 1.0 compatibility mode and
  XSLT backwards-compatible behaviour, civil-timezone and Olson names (a
  timezone database), calendars other than AD and ISO and languages other than
  English in the formatting functions, and fn:transform.
- Schema awareness stays Phase 5. The rest becomes Phase 7 ("Deferred features"
  in PLAN.md), planned in `docs/tasks/phase-7.md` after the Phase 4 gate, one
  packet per feature, each with its QT4 or xslt40-test sets counted once it
  lands.
- Until then, code that rejects or ignores one of these features does it in one
  place each, with the error the specification gives a processor without the
  feature, so that adding it later replaces that place instead of unpicking
  special cases (the design principle in CLAUDE.md). Size-driven choices (UCA
  tables, a timezone database, HTML5) are revisited against the wasm budget
  then; a feature may be a build option.

### D163. XSLT conformance sweep 2 (packet 4.17)

**Summary**: Parentless text nodes may be empty, text events carry CDATA
requests, arena trees start small, IR modules carry each expression's static
context at run time, and named declarations are local to their package.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D99, D148, D159, D160, D161, D162.

- **Zero-length text nodes** (D159's Proposed item, accepted; additive to the
  frozen `include/sxml/tree.h`, D99): XDM 4.0, 7.5.7.1 lets a text node without
  a parent be empty ("text nodes are allowed to be empty only if they have no
  parents"). The builder contract: a parentless text whose events are all empty
  is a zero-length text node; inside a parent empty text still makes none, so
  the node disappears when it is added to content. TEXT_CONSTRUCTOR (XQuery
  `text {""}`, xsl:value-of, xsl:text) makes it; simple content drops
  zero-length text nodes first (XSLT 4.0, 5.7.2 step 1). D110's deviation is
  gone.
- **CDATA requests** (additive to tree.h): `sxml_text_event. is_cdata_section`
  and `sxml_node_description.is_cdata_section` (glossary `cdata_section`) carry
  XSLT 4.0, 11.4.3's cdata attribute of xsl:value-of and xsl:text (construction
  flag CDATA_SECTION; a computed value is one CONDITIONAL). A text node built
  from several events keeps the request when one has it
  (implementation-defined; value-of-012 expects mixed nodes and fails). Copies
  keep it; the serializer writes such a text node as CDATA sections with the
  XML and XHTML methods.
- **Sized arena trees**: the first node segment holds 2 nodes, a growable tree
  without initial memory takes 768 bytes with its own allocation as the arena's
  first memory, location segments are made only when kept, the base URI is an
  exact allocation, the text store starts at 64 bytes. A constructed tree of a
  few nodes is about 1.3 KB (was 5 to 9 KB). JSON parsing reuses the key items
  of a parse (a cache of 32 keys). array-022 (209,579 small element trees) runs
  within the driver's 512 MB.
- **The evaluation memo** is an open-addressing hash; subjects are the same
  when they are one node, atomic items of one type that are atomic-equal, or
  arrays whose members are, item by item. **xsl:function cache="yes"** (10.3.7;
  not for new-each-time="yes"): the full arity calls the internal row
  cached-call(number, [$p1, ...], body#n), body the sequence constructor's IR
  function; equal arguments give the first call's value (function-1031).
- **The static context of a call at run time** (D159's Proposed item, accepted,
  D149's names-as-strings item with it): one mechanism, the unit's modules
  (glossary `ir_module`, widened from D148): a module may carry its own decimal
  formats and collations and its own static namespaces besides its static base
  URI; STATIC_CALL and the node constructors gained `module_number`. XSLT
  lowering makes one module per AST static context (xml:base, namespaces,
  [xsl:]default-collation, the package's decimal formats, 3.4.8) and the XPath
  lowerer stamps the function calls of an expression with its context's module
  (`sxml_xpath_static_context.ir_module_number`); XSLT stamps the elements,
  documents and temporary trees it constructs. The evaluator's lexical getters
  (`sxml_dynamic_context_get_static_base_uri`, new `_get_static_context`,
  `_get_static_namespaces`) read the innermost IR task's expression module,
  then its function's, then the unit's. So fn:static-base-uri, resolve-uri#1,
  doc, base URIs of constructed nodes, default collations, names given as
  strings (fn:key, system-property, function-available, format-number) and
  decimal formats per package follow the expression. Not covered:
  fn:function-lookup of fn:key and the accumulator functions (lowered snippets,
  not natives), and XSLT's own library calls (they read the unit's).
- **Declarations local to a package** (D160's Proposed item, accepted; 3.4.8):
  one rule, each named-declaration table is keyed by name and the package of
  the declaration, and a reference looks up its own package's (as attribute
  sets and modes already were): keys (the XSLT function table has one state per
  package, so fn:key and fn:map-for-key of package P see P's keys; the
  accumulator table keeps each static context's inner table instead of the
  first context's), namespace aliases (collected after the package table),
  decimal formats (through the modules above), character maps and output
  definitions (each package has its unnamed definition; xsl:result-document
  reads its package's). The output compilation, which runs without the package
  table, names a package by its top module (`sxml_xslt_package_top_module`, the
  same rule the table uses). Accumulators themselves are still stylesheet-wide.
- **D162 one-place rules** (from D161): XTDE0160 for an instruction whose
  effective version is below 2.0 (3.8, 27.4: XSLT 2.0 and 3.0 modes run as 4.0)
  in `lower_child`; XTSE1650 (xsl:import-schema) and XTSE1660 ([xsl:]type,
  validation="strict", typed modes) in the reader's `reject_schema_awareness`;
  lax and preserve are taken as strip (27.2). One system property table
  (`src/system_property.c`, glossary `system_property`) serves
  fn:system-properties and the XSLT fn:system-property.
- **Merges**: `sxml_ir_slot_atom` (10 copies), `sxml_xml_text_trim_whitespace`
  (16), `sxml_xslt_lowering_resolve_declared_type` and `_expression_context` (3
  and 2), the two remaining heapsorts onto `sxml_sort_in_place`, one
  boolean-attribute helper (yes, true, 1).
- Lint at HEAD fixed: invocation global names are byte views (`src/xslt.c`),
  the driver's serialization comparison returns its verdict, `decide_role`
  reads a RULE frame's rule once.
- **Measured** (release, whole suites, before at 9e7f5fc, after at the last
  commit of this packet): XT40 in scope 7,879 to 7,986 of 8,728 (90.3 % to 91.5
  %), errors 3 to 1; value-of 8 to 14 of 15 (53.3 % to 93.3 %, every core set
  now 80 % or more), seqtor 61 to 85 of 92, text 9 to 15, base-uri 32 to 49 of
  52, collations 23 to 34, resolve-uri 15 to 21, use-package 34 to 41 of 53,
  error 465 to 470, function 111 to 113; no test set lost a case. XP40 30,646
  to 30,647 and XQ40 40,030 to 40,034 passed, 0 errors; slices 198 and 186.
- **Not done**: json-to-xml-013 still runs out of the driver's 512 MB: it turns
  a 19 MB file into 209,579 documents that an xsl:for-each returns as one
  sequence before the enclosing element copies them, and then a tree of 2.7
  million nodes (2 GB without a budget); it needs content that streams into the
  constructor (Proposed). XTDE3052 for an abstract variable is still raised
  when the globals are computed, read or not (accept-042, -043a: XSLT globals
  are all computed first, so a lazy error needs lazy globals). Accumulators are
  stylesheet-wide; fn:function-lookup does not find fn:key or the accumulator
  functions (they are lowered stylesheet functions, not rows).

**Sources**: XT40, XP40 and XQ40 passes, whole suites, before, and the slices
(`tools/run-xslt.sh`, `tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build, at 9e7f5fc); XT40,
XP40 and XQ40 passes, whole suites, after at the last commit of this packet, by
test set, and the slices (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, `tools/run-qt4.sh`,
`tools/conformance-report.py`, release build); size of a constructed tree of a

19 MB file, a tree of 2.7 million nodes, 2 GB without a budget.

  `tools/update-test-suites.sh`, excluded from private snapshots and linked
  (`tools/private-build.sh`, `tools/check-main.sh`). Dropped, as no test reads
  them: the reports' HTML, CSS and images (`nistMeta/*.html`, 25 MB) and CVS
  backup copies (`.#FILE.REVISION`). In scope: the tests of `suite.xml`
  applicable to an XSD 1.1 processor (version tokens 1.1, XML-1.0, XML-1.0-5e,
  Unicode_6.0.0, CTR-all-compile, full-xpath-in-CTA,
  comments-and-PIs-excluded), not queried or disputed, expecting valid or
  invalid: 41,538 (15,330 schema tests, 26,208 instance tests; NIST 23,170,
  Microsoft 14,363, Sun 1,606, Saxonica 1,376, IBM 919, others 104). The other
  token choices move the count by at most 47. (D168, the driver, measures
  41,518: it applies the version tokens per element where this count or-ed
  them.)
- **schema.h** (new, after `xslt.h`'s pattern): `sxml_schema` (quintet)
  compiled from `sxml_schema_document`s given as TEXT, NODE (a parsed document
  or an inline xs:schema element) or RESOLVED through the resolver;
  `sxml_schema_find_type`, `_find_element_declaration`,
  `_find_attribute_declaration`; `sxml_schema_validator` (quintet) with
  `_as_tree_builder` and `_get_outcome`; `sxml_schema_validate_node`;
  `sxml_schema_report_sink`. XSD 1.1 only (1.0 documents are read as 1.1);
  schema location hints in instances are not followed (Part 1, 4.3.2 allows
  it); an import that cannot be read is not an error by itself (4.2.6.2).
- **Validation is a tree builder filter**, not a tree walker: the validator
  receives builder events (from the XML parser while parsing, from
  `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node`, from construction) and sends them, annotated,
  to a result builder; the null builder makes it a pure check (`sxml validate`
  builds nothing). One mechanism serves the CLI, XQuery validate, XSLT
  validation, fn:doc validation and fn:xsd-validator, and the validated tree is
  an ordinary arena tree, since the events already carry type annotation,
  is-id, is-idrefs and nilled (`tree.h`, D39). Defaults and schema normalized
  attribute values are events too. A failed validation delivers no tree (its
  events are discarded).
- **Errors**: codes are XSD constraint names in no namespace
  (`cvc-complex-type.2.4`, `src-resolve`; Part 1, appendix C), static errors
  for compilation and dynamic errors for validation; XQuery and XSLT wrap them
  in their own codes, as XSLT rewrites XQDY0102 to XTDE0430. A report sink
  receives every error (the CLI shows all of them); the null sink stops at the
  first.
- **types.h** (frozen; additive, D99): `sxml_content_type_variety` and
  `sxml_complex_type` as the new union member `complex_type` of
  `sxml_type_description` (xs:anyType and xs:untyped MIXED;
  `src/types_builtin.c` now says so), `sxml_facet_kind`, `sxml_facet`,
  `sxml_facet_view` and the new last field `facets` of the description (empty
  for built-in and item types; `src/types.c` clears it when it normalizes an
  item type). Reason: "everything the registry knows about one type" must
  include what typed values (content variety, simple content type) and casting
  (facets) need. Facet values are text (the registry holds no items, as for
  JNode key constants), canonical in the base type, QNames as EQNames so no
  namespace context is needed. Assertion facets are not registry facets: they
  are XPath, kept by the schema, evaluated by validation and, in schema-aware
  expressions, after the cast, so `src/cast.c` never starts an evaluation
  (D71). Comments: the top of the header and `sxml_type_registry_find_type`.
- **Registration is internal**: `sxml_type_registry_register_schema_type` in
  `src/types_internal.h` (declared now, defined by 5.5), called only by schema
  compilation, which checks XSD's constraints first; a public function would
  let hosts register definitions that bypass them, and the registry would need
  a second copy of those checks. Schema types are never interned and are
  registered without entering the name index: names belong to a schema
  (`sxml_schema_find_type`), as D98 made named item types aliases of a module,
  so two schemas of one processor may define one name. Registered types outlive
  their schema (trees keep their annotations).
- **tree.h, xdm.h** (frozen; contract comments): a tree without
  `get_typed_value` gets typed values derived from string value and type
  annotation (simple types by casting with the element's namespaces, complex
  types by content type variety, nilled: none) in `sxml_node_make_typed_value`.
  The old text said such a tree holds only untyped nodes; for those nothing
  changes, so no tree that kept the contract changes behaviour. Reason: one
  derivation for every tree (arena and host trees alike) and nothing stored per
  node; the arena tree stays as it is.
- **processor.h** (with a record, D47): `SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_SCHEMA_DOCUMENT` at
  the end of the kinds (forms BYTES, DOCUMENT_NODE), using
  `target_namespace_uri` for the namespace; the QT4 driver's resolver lists it
  (`tests/qt4/driver/resource_table.c`).
- **Reuse, not parallel machinery**: schema documents through the XML parser
  and an arena tree (D12); facets and lexical spaces through `src/cast.c`
  alone; patterns through the regex engine with an XSD dialect flag (D53);
  assertions, type alternatives and identity constraints compiled with
  `xpath.h` and evaluated by the one evaluator on subtrees the validator
  records; schema-element(N) and schema-attribute(N) resolved statically to
  choices of the existing element(M, T) and attribute(N, T) tests over the
  substitution group, so matching and subtyping need no schema in the type
  registry (static analysis then no longer sets the `is_schema_declaration`
  flag of `sxml_node_test`, D58).
- **Integration** (5.11, 5.12), each replacing one rejection place (D161,
  D162): `sxml_static_context_configuration.in_scope_schemas` (a view of
  compiled schemas, last field, empty = not schema-aware) with a record by
  5.11; XQuery import schema (XQST0009, `src/xquery_static.c`) and validate
  (XQST0075, `src/xquery_lower.c`); XPST0008 of schema-element in
  `src/xpath_static.c`; FODC0009 of the xsd-validation option
  (`src/function_library_json.c`); fn:xsd-validator (absent, XPST0017);
  xsl:import-schema (XTSE1650) and validation and type attributes (XTSE1660,
  `src/xslt_read.c`); the QT4 and XSLT drivers' feature lists.
- **Gate (proposed, for the owner)**: in-scope XSD 1.1 tests ≥ 90%, the
  datatype groups (NIST, MS-DataTypes, MS-Regex: 30,598) ≥ 95%, the structure
  groups (8,645) ≥ 80%, the XSD 1.1 groups (Saxonica, IBM: 2,295) ≥ 70%;
  schema-aware QT4 XQ40 cases (about 1,100) ≥ 70%; schema-aware XSLT cases
  (about 690) ≥ 60%; the Phase 2 to 4 gates still held and no count dropped; no
  crash, leak or error outcome.
- **`sxml validate`** is designed in `phase-5.md` (synopsis, options, JSON
  shape, exit codes) and enters `docs/CLI.md` with packet 5.10 (D44: only once
  it works).

**Sources**: files and size of the vendored xsdtests in third_party/xsdtests;
in-scope XSD 1.1 tests of suite.xml, schema and instance tests, by contributor,
gate groups, and the other token choices (from
`third_party/xsdtests/suite.xml`); schema-aware QT4 XQ40 cases (about 1,100)
and XSLT cases (about 690); quoted from D168.

### D166. Content that streams into a constructor; XSLT sweep 3 (packet 4.17)

**Summary**: Element and document constructors become receiving tasks into
which delivering content tasks stream their values, so constructed content
builds directly in the receiver's tree instead of as separate trees.

Recorded 2026-10-18, after D71, D101, D110, D163. Accepts D163's Proposed item
"content that streams into a constructor", as one mechanism of the shared
evaluator and IR, used by XSLT and XQuery alike.

- **Receiving and delivering tasks** (glossary `receiving_task`,
  `delivering_task`; `src/evaluator_machine_internal.h`, "Delivering"): a
  document or element constructor (and SHALLOW_COPY of an element or document)
  whose content expression is not a D110 enclosed list opens its node, sets its
  part task's `receive` function and pushes the content as a delivering task
  (`sxml_evaluator_task.delivers_content`). When a delivering task finishes,
  the machine hands its value to the nearest receiving task below and the task
  below gets (). Delivering passes on only where a value reaches the receiver
  unchanged: LET bodies and conditional branches (they replace their task), a
  content LET's bound expression, each body of a MAP (not a path's MAP, whose
  body may select JNodes), the body of a function a delivering call enters (not
  through a coerced function item: its COERCE_RESULT task delivers), and the
  template calls of a delivering APPLY_TEMPLATES (which delivers its separators
  itself). A try/catch body never delivers, so no caught error leaves part of a
  content behind. The order and the rules of XSLT 4.0, 5.7.1 and XQuery 4.0,
  4.12.1.3 are those of the content sequence: the receiver adds each value as
  before (arrays flattened, atomic items joined within one enclosed expression,
  nodes copied, documents unwrapped, XTDE0410 and XQTY0024 from the same
  state).
- **Building into the receiver**: a constructor in a delivering task builds its
  node in the receiver's tree when that is what copying a tree of its own would
  give (`sxml_construction_open`): the same rules and construction flags and
  copy-namespaces preserve; no-inherit becomes the element start's
  `ignores_parent_namespaces`; a document's children become the content. Text,
  attribute, comment and processing-instruction constructors add their node
  directly (a namespace node keeps its own tree, whose builder checks
  XQDY0101); xsl:copy of another node delivers the node, which the receiver
  copies.
- **Content LETs** (glossary `content_let`, `sxml_ir_let.is_content`, printed
  `(let $n content ...)`): a LET whose variable only the result of its block
  reads, first and in order; in a delivering task its bound expression delivers
  too. Lowering marks them with `sxml_xpath_lowerer_mark_content_let` (the
  block's open LET made for the item, else marking stops unless the item is
  ()). The machine also evaluates `let $v := E return $v` as E in place.
- **Lowerings**: an XSLT literal result element, xsl:element, xsl:document and
  a temporary tree (9.4) compute their content in a block inside the
  constructor; a sequence constructor marks its children's LETs when it is a
  body or content (not with xsl:on-empty or xsl:on-non-empty, which read the
  atoms). XQuery computed element and document constructors do the same; a
  direct element constructor too, literal text as text constructors, unless two
  enclosed expressions are adjacent (`<c>{1}{2}</c>` stays a D110 enclosed
  list). Other temporary trees (with-param, message bodies) still take their
  content as a value.
- **Arena nodes**: content and in-scope namespaces share a union (a node has
  one or the other by kind), 72 to 56 bytes.
- **XSLT driver**: result documents are collected only for
  assert-result-document (else the null handler, which still checks them); the
  evaluation step budget is 4 x the QT4 driver's (D89), as json-to-xml-013
  takes about 190 million steps.
- **Measured** (release, whole suites, before at 53bd400): json-to-xml-013
  peaks at about 410 MB (2.1 GB before) and passes; XT40 in scope 7,986 to
  7,987 of 8,728 (91.5 %), errors 1 to 0, no test set lost a case; XP40 30,647
  and XQ40 40,034 passed, 0 errors; slices 198 (qt4/slice) and 147 (xslt/slice,
  of 154). The driver change was committed with 457f530 (packet 5.3), which
  took the working tree's file.
- **Not done**: XTDE3052 when an abstract variable is read (accept-042, -043a):
  v1-proxy is a global that reads the abstract v1, and globals are computed
  before the evaluation (XQuery's too, D148: only unreferenced ones are
  skipped), so a lazy error needs globals computed on first read, which a step
  function's synchronous atom reads cannot do today (Proposed). A RAISE read in
  place of the abstract variable alone was tried and dropped: v1-proxy still
  raises when it is computed.

**Sources**: json-to-xml-013 memory; XT40, XP40 and XQ40 passes, whole suites,
and the slices, before (at 53bd400) and after the change (`tools/run-xslt.sh`,
`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build).

### D167. Schema components and compile stages (packet 5.2)

**Summary**: Schema components live in one index-addressed store, one table per
XSD 1.1 component kind with fixed built-in entries, compiled in six ordered
stages from READ to ASSERTIONS, with content models as deterministic automata.

Recorded 2026-10-18. The internal design of Phase 5 (D165), in
`src/schema_internal.h`; golden `src/xslt_ast_internal.h`.

- **One store, index-addressed** (D24, D52): `sxml_schema_components` holds one
  table per component kind of XSD 1.1 Part 1, 2.2 (type definitions simple and
  complex together, element and attribute declarations, attribute uses,
  attribute groups, model group definitions, model groups, particles, schema
  wildcards, identity constraints, type alternatives, assertions, notations,
  facets) and per linking record (XPath records, namespace contexts, schema
  references, documents, list entries, namespace bindings, text bytes), entry 0
  "none" in each. One generic append (`sxml_schema_components_add_entries`, by
  table) and edit, typed read accessors. Property records (content type, scope,
  value constraint, open content, type table) are fields. Built-in components
  first, with fixed indexes: type definitions 1 to 54 are the registry's
  built-ins by `sxml_builtin_type` (so a registered built-in and its component
  share a number), 55 the list type of xsi:schemaLocation, particles 1-2, model
  group 1, wildcards 1-2 for xs:anyType, attributes 1-4 the xsi: ones.
  xs:untyped, xs:untypedAtomic and xs:numeric have components but no XSD name.
- **Fields are "as read" or "property"**: the reader writes what the XML says,
  QName attributes as schema references (a table of symbol space, name,
  position); RESOLVE turns them into index fields beside them, and no later
  stage reads a reference. Children known when read are linked by index
  directly. Stages write the properties their comments name.
- **Six stages, one file each**, run in order by `sxml_schema_initialize`
  (5.4), each reading only what earlier ones wrote: READ (schema_read.c,
  schema_assemble.c), RESOLVE (schema_resolve.c), SIMPLE_TYPES (5.5),
  COMPLEX_TYPES (5.6, with schema_content_model.c), IDENTITY_CONSTRAINTS (5.8),
  ASSERTIONS (5.9); errors go through one function,
  `sxml_schema_compilation_report` (record gets the static description and the
  configured URI, the sink a detailed one); a stage that reported stops the
  pipeline after it. Stubs of compile stages check nothing and return OK (so
  5.4 can measure schema tests alone); validation-time seams of unfinished
  features return UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE where used (D162), and the stubs handle
  the trivial case (no type table, no assertions, no identity constraints) so
  ordinary validation is not blocked by them.
- **`struct sxml_schema` is in the internal header** (processor, creating
  allocator, embedded components), so every `src/schema*.c` reaches the
  components; its functions stay 5.4's.
- **Content models** (5.6's plan): an opaque compiled model per complex type,
  in a block of the components (blocks never move, freed with the components,
  so no destroy hook): a deterministic Glushkov automaton, small maxOccurs
  expanded, large ones counted (as D147), UPA as a determinism check with
  element-over-wildcard, all groups as counted tables, open content as a
  matcher fallback, substitution groups as head transitions giving the member.
  The validator steps a cursor (`state` + caller-owned counter values) with
  start, step, can_end and list_expected.
- **Validator seams**, plain calls (D71): type alternatives and assertions
  (5.9), identity constraints (5.8) over a recorded subtree (an arena copy of
  the outermost element that needs one, with each element's governing
  declaration by node index), the ID table and the validator's report function
  (5.7), the derivation check (5.6) for xsi:type, substitution and type tables.
- **Sharing the header**: after 5.2, `src/schema_internal.h` is shared like a
  ledger: a packet adds what its files need as one small insertion in its own
  section, committed alone; it does not change other packets' fields. The text
  form writer is 5.4's (`src/schema_text.c`).

### D168. The XSD 1.1 test driver (packet 5.3)

**Summary**: The XSD 1.1 test driver `sxml-xsd-test` shares the budget,
selection, slice and report mechanisms with the QT4 driver, names test sets by
directory and file, and applies version tokens per level.

Recorded 2026-10-18. `tests/xsd/driver/`, the developer tool `sxml-xsd-test`
(list, run), public API only, a sibling of sxml-qt4 and sxml-xslt-test that
links `sxml_qt4_driver_library`.

- **Shared, not copied** (the drivers' common mechanisms moved into the QT4
  driver's library): the test budget (`budget.h`, from the copies in
  `test_run.c` and `xslt_execution.c`), the test selection over a test catalog
  interface (`selection.h`, from `xslt_selection.c`; the XSLT and XSD catalogs
  each adapt to it in a dozen lines), one slice-test script
  (`run-slice-test.cmake`, SPEC optional), documents in another suite's
  namespace and attributes in a namespace (`document.h`), report areas
  configurable (`report.h`, empty = D94's). The QT4 commands keep their own
  walking for now (a later cleanup can move them onto `selection.h`).
- **Names**: suite.xml names test sets only by href and testSet/@name repeats
  (Assert, CTA, TargetNS, VC, Zone), so a test set is named
  DIRECTORY-without-Meta "-" FILE-without-extension (`saxon-Assert`,
  `ms-DataTypes_w3c`, `nist-NISTXMLSchemaDatatypes`); the prefix is the
  contributor area of the report and the dashboard. A test is `GROUP/TEST`
  (unique per test set, xsts.xsd). `tools/run-xsd.sh` derives the same names
  from suite.xml with sed.
- **Scope, per element** (refines D165's count): xsts.xsd says the version
  tokens of testSet, testGroup and test each mean "run if any of them is
  supported", so each level must apply on its own; D165 or-ed the three levels
  together. Supported tokens and their classes as D165 lists them; an unknown
  token is an unsupported class. Measured: 41,518 in scope (15,329 schema
  tests, 26,189 instance tests; NIST 23,170, Microsoft 14,363, Sun 1,606,
  Saxonica 1,375, IBM 919, W3C WG 41, Oracle 26, Boeing 18), 20 fewer than
  D165's 41,538: 19 XSD 1.0 instance tests of
  `wgMeta/substitution-groups.testSet`, five of which name files that do not
  exist, and the 1.0 group of a Saxonica set. Gate groups: datatypes 30,598,
  structures 8,626, XSD 1.1 2,294. The introspection set is listed and not run;
  expected `indeterminate` or none applying, status queried or disputed: not
  run, out of scope.
- **Run**: each applicable test in a processor of its own (QT4 limits) through
  the test budget, its documents read (a missing one is an error); then not
  run, "XSD not implemented", until 5.4 and 5.7 fill the one marked place in
  `xsd_test_run.c` (plan in `xsd_test_run.h`: schema documents as TEXT with
  file:///SUITE-PATH, strict validation with a counting report sink, a group
  without a schema test validated against the built-in components alone, a
  group whose schema fails makes its instance tests fail). Report spec XSD11,
  program sxml-xsd-test.
- **Slice**: `tests/xsd/slice.txt`, 147 in-scope tests, one per test set plus
  the rest in proportion; baseline 0. A full release run takes 45 s (one
  process per test set; NIST, 23,170 tests in one file, is the longest).

**Sources**: in-scope tests, schema and instance tests, by contributor and gate
group, applying version tokens per element (`sxml-xsd-test`,
`tools/run-xsd.sh`, from `third_party/xsdtests/suite.xml`); slice: 147 in-scope
tests (from `tests/xsd/slice.txt`); a full release run (45 s)
(`tools/run-xsd.sh`, release build); quoted from D165.

### D169. Phase 4 gate review (packet 4.18)

**Summary**: The Phase 4 gate review passes with XT40 at 91.5 % in scope and
XP40 and XQ40 unregressed, adds `xslt_fuzz`, fixes XSLT error locations, and
declares `xslt.h` stable.

Recorded 2026-10-19 by the review agent (D11), after D95, D123, D151, D161,
D166. Checked locally (D123): `tools/check-main.sh` on clean HEAD (77bc5d5
before and 8d2aa06 after this review's changes) builds `release`, `debug`
(ASan, UBSan), `debug-gcc` and `wasm`, and every test passes; the full lint at
8d2aa06 is clean (no call cycle). The dashboard is regenerated at 8d2aa06.

- **Numbers** (release, tools/run-xslt.sh, run-qt4.sh XP40 and XQ40,
  run-xsd.sh, every test set finished, 0 crashes, no leak reported by the
  drivers' budgets, 0 "error" outcomes): at 77bc5d5 XT40 7,987 of 8,728 in
  scope, **91.5 %** (gate 70 %); XP40 30,647 passed, in scope 30,629 of 31,543,
  **97.1 %** (gate 90 %); XQ40 40,034 passed, in scope 40,016 of 41,174, **97.2
  %** (gate 85 %); no regression from 30,647 / 40,034. Core sets (gate 80 %
  each): apply-templates 97.4 %, mode 88.5 %, match 93.8 %, for-each-group 90.7
  %, sort 100 %, key 97.1 %, number 97.4 %, choose 95.4 %, copy 89.0 %,
  value-of 93.3 %, result-document 95.3 %, function 91.1 %. Slices: qt4/slice
  198, qt4/xquery-slice 186, xslt/slice 147 (ctest, every preset). After this
  review's changes, case by case: XT40 gains try-002, -022 and -045 (7,990,
  91.5 %), XP40 and XQ40 identical, nothing lost. The 24 sandp test sets the
  XSLT runner starts end at once with "unknown test set" (out of scope, D95).
- **Fuzzing**, 300 s per target, seven at once on a loaded machine (fork mode
  for the evaluating targets): cast_fuzz 1,068,415 runs, regex_fuzz 461,213,
  xml_parse_fuzz 62,095, xpath_compile_fuzz 10,066, xpath_evaluate_fuzz about
  10,000, xquery_fuzz about 9,600 and the new xslt_fuzz about 8,300; no crash,
  leak or sanitizer report. Timeouts for triage only (P9): one xquery_fuzz
  input and four xslt_fuzz inputs, all suite stylesheets slow by nature under
  ASan (a loop of 1,000,000, primes to 1,000, match="$nodes" over 2,000 nodes),
  each finishing in 5 to 12 s alone. **xslt_fuzz** (`tests/fuzz/xslt_fuzz.c`,
  new): compiles the input through `xslt.h` and transforms it twice (templates
  applied to a small document, serialized, result documents collected as trees;
  xsl:initial-template called, raw result), small limits, a resolver table with
  one module and one document; seeds are the suite's `.xsl` files.
- **The XSLT driver's step budget** (D166, 4 x QT4, 400 million): a fair test
  limit, not a mask. json-to-xml-013 costs time linear in its input (13,000 to
  209,579 cities: 1.5 s to 25 s, release), about 900 steps a city, 65 a node; a
  profile is flat (JSON parsing 23 %, coercion 10 %, construction 6 %, template
  dispatch 4 %), no pattern matching hot spot. What the fuzzing found instead:
  a pattern rooted at a variable (match="$a-nodes", 6.3.1) tests membership by
  a scan of the variable's value, so N nodes matched against M is N x M (1,000
  nodes 0.6 s, 4,000 9.4 s); within the budget for the suite's case, a design
  for a later sweep (a node set index by document order per global value),
  Proposed.
- **D71**: no call cycle (tools/check-call-cycles.py, 163 files); through
  function pointers: the evaluator's guard (`is_running`, D151) refuses a
  nested run on one dynamic context and the lowering machine's (D161) a nested
  lowering; resumable natives (fn:key's index, cached calls, accumulators)
  return CALL steps to the machine; D166's receive function only adds items to
  a construction and calls no machine; the result document handler, the trace
  sink and the resolver are host code, and a transformation one of them starts
  runs on a dynamic context of its own, as xslt.h allows; whitespace stripping
  is a tree builder filter.
- **Fixed**:

  - Error locations of XSLT: expressions are parsed from attribute text, and
    their AST spans stayed relative to that text, so a dynamic error or a
    static error found by lowering (XPST0008, XPST0017) said 1:5 for an
    expression on line 4. The reader now places each AST in its module
    (`sxml_ast_move_source_spans`, with the rule its own relocate_error used,
    now shared). An error located in a unit lowered for one invocation
    (call-template, call-function, another mode) named its module with memory
    freed when the transformation ended (found by ASan in a new CLI test): the
    name now points to the stylesheet's module URI (status.h, D21).
  - err:XTMM9000 and err:XTMM9001, the default codes of xsl:message and
    xsl:assert, had no prefix and were shown Q{...}XTMM9000.
  - `sxml transform` with a relative STYLESHEET resolved "../" in an href to
    the file system's root (file:sub/x.xsl with ../b.xml is file:/b.xml by RFC
    3986): the base URI now has the working directory
    (`sxml_platform_read_working_directory`, the invocation's
    `working_directory`; file:///C:/ for Windows). Error reports name the
    module file of a static error's location.
  - Merged: `sxml_xml_byte_is_whitespace` replaces thirteen private copies
    (casting, function library, XPath and XQuery static analysis, XQuery and
    XSLT lowering, constructors); one `sxml_xslt_lowering_add_expression` for
    seven copies.
  - `tests/xslt_test.c` covers the collector's caller-memory lifecycle, the
    last functions of xslt.h without a test.
- **Larger duplicates, listed** (one shared mechanism each, later): typed array
  allocation (count x size checked, then allocate) is a private helper in 19
  files; group-adjacent and group-starting-with compare keys in
  `src/xslt_group.c` with their own equality, next to the FLWOR's
  `keys_are_equal` (group-by itself is shared); the window clause and
  group-starting-with/ending-with are two run detectors over one sequence.
  D161's follow-ups are done (sweep 2, D163: slot atoms, trim, declared types,
  heapsorts).
- **Delayed features (D162)**, one place each with the specification's error:
  xsl:import-schema XTSE1650 and validation or type attributes XTSE1660

  (`src/xslt_lower_control.c`; dynamic evaluation is optional), extension

- **`sxml transform` matches docs/CLI.md**: every example of the page gives its
  output and exit code; the options, the usage errors, exit 3 for a missing
  file and 1 for a stylesheet or input that is not well-formed behave as

- **xslt.h is stable** (D161's rule): consistent with `xpath.h` and `xquery.h`,
