### D170. The schema document reader and assembly (packet 5.4)

**Summary**: One table of schema element roles drives a loop reading schema
documents into components, assembly reads each document once with redefine and
override applied last, and RESOLVE turns references into indexes.

Recorded 2026-10-18. READ and RESOLVE (D167) and `sxml_schema`'s quintet;
golden `src/xslt_read.c`, `src/xquery_module.c`.

- **One table of schema element roles** (`src/schema_read.c`): a role is what
  an element is where it appears (global or local element, group definition or
  reference, a facet, ...); its rule lists the unqualified attributes and
  required ones the schema for schema documents allows, the child slots its
  children fill in order (a slot: roles, required, repeated, ending the
  content), and its reader. Attributes of other namespaces than XSD's are
  allowed (openAttrs), `vc:` attributes decide conditional inclusion (4.2.2,
  src-cip). What breaks the schema for schema documents is reported with the
  role's representation constraint (src-element, src-ct, src-simple-type, ...),
  or the component's properties constraint where there is none
  (mg-props-correct, an-props-correct, n-props-correct, as-props-correct,
  sch-props-correct); equal `id` values are cvc-id.2.
- **The walk** is a loop over node indexes from the element read to its last
  descendant; an element's children get their roles when it is read, so an
  element without one (ignored, misplaced, in an annotation) is skipped with
  its subtree. Components are added in document order, linked to the parent's
  component at once; lists (particles, attribute uses, facets, ...) are written
  in a second pass, once, whole.
- **As read, for the later stages**: a simple type restriction has variety
  ATOMIC until RESOLVE gives it its base's; the xs:assertion facets of a
  simpleContent restriction join the type's assertions with its xs:assert
  children, in document order; defaultOpenContent is applied to complex content
  when appliesToEmpty or the type has a particle or complexContent (clause 6's
  emptiness needs COMPLEX_TYPES); an attribute use with ref and
  inheritable="false" takes the declaration's.
- **Assembly** (`src/schema_assemble.c`): a work list; a document is read once
  by absolute URI and the namespace its components get (a chameleon document
  included into two namespaces is read twice from one tree); the children of
  xs:redefine and xs:override are read after every document, replacing the name
  index entry of what they name (4.2.4, 4.2.5); an override child with nothing
  to replace is not read; a component replaced twice is src-redefine or
  src-override; a redefined document that reaches the redefining one is
  src-redefine; a redefinition's base or self-reference names the original
  (src-redefine.5, 6.1, 7.1; the original must be the redefined document's).
  Redefines and overrides are read innermost first (a chain replaces the inner
  redefinition) and a component replaced twice in one document is the error. A
  document the resolver does not deliver is no error (4.2.3 clause 2.4,
  4.2.6.2; schema.h says otherwise, Proposed); an unlocated import of the xml:
  namespace reads its known document (xml.xsd); an import without a location of
  a namespace already read reads nothing; an xs:schema element that conditional
  inclusion ignores is empty.
- **Not done**: src-redefine 6.2.2 and 7.2.2 (a group or attribute group
  redefined without a self-reference must restrict the original); the original
  of an override or redefinition stays a component (unnamed) and is compiled.
- **RESOLVE** (`src/schema_resolve.c`): references through the name index
  (src-resolve; src-resolve.4.2 for namespaces not imported, at READ), base,
  item and member types, restriction varieties, substitution group
  affiliations, element types through heads, members transitively, ref identity
  constraints; cycles of groups (mg-props-correct.2), derivations
  (ct-props-correct.3, st-props-correct.2) and substitution groups
  (e-props-correct.6), each a walk with an explicit stack. Attribute groups may
  refer to each other in a cycle (XSD 1.1, bug 15795).
- **Text form** (`src/schema_text.c`): D167's lines for every table, the
  xs:schema element's namespace context always first, content models (5.6's
  writer) after the components.
- **Driver**: sxml-xsd-test compiles every schema test and every instance
  test's schema (resolver over the suite files); instance tests are not run
  until 5.7 ("XSD validation not implemented").
- **Measured** at 21c9531 with 5.5 and 5.6: schema tests 15,163 of 15,329 in
  scope pass (98.9 %, gate of the packet 85 %); every schema document reads
  without a crash, leak or limit (10 particle tests reach the content model
  state limit in COMPLEX_TYPES); no reader error on a valid schema; the XSD
  slice 110 of 147.

**Sources**: XSD schema tests in scope with 5.5 and 5.6, and the XSD slice
(`tools/run-xsd.sh`, at 21c9531).

### D171. Simple types and facets (packet 5.5)

**Summary**: Casting to a registered schema simple type applies its whiteSpace
facet, its built-in ancestor's lexical mapping and every facet of its chain,
and SIMPLE_TYPES makes facet values canonical before registering types.

Recorded 2026-10-18. Fills SIMPLE_TYPES (D167) and registration (D165).

- **One lexical engine.** Casting to a registered type is its whiteSpace facet
  (the nearest on its chain of registered bases, else the built-in one), the
  lexical mapping of its built-in ancestor (src/cast_lexical.c), then every
  facet of it and its registered bases (new src/cast_facet.c, part of the cast
  engine): steps by conjunction, the patterns of a step by disjunction. A
  failure is FORG0001 whose description starts with the constraint name
  (cvc-minInclusive-valid, ...), so validation (5.7) can report it with XSD's
  code. Facet values are read with the lexical mapping of the value's built-in
  type, never cast back through src/cast.c (D71). Equality is atomic-equal in
  that type (QNames by EQName); order is XSD's (`sxml_cast_order_values`: NaN
  incomparable, a date without a timezone compared at -14:00 and +14:00,
  durations at the four reference dateTimes of Part 2, E.3.3). Lists made by
  xs:list may be empty; a union's facets apply to the value its first accepting
  member gives, and no other member is tried after them.
- **Patterns**: `sxml_regex_flags.is_xsd_pattern` (D53's flag), the regex
  anchored to the whole value, ^ and $ ordinary, back-references, reluctant
  quantifiers, (? and (\* groups and \\b \\B FORX0002. A pattern is compiled
  per check, in heap memory (open: a cache).
- **Registration** (`sxml_type_registry_register_schema_type`, src/types.c): no
  interning, no name index; facets copied, in the component's facet order, so a
  stage can pair registered (canonical) values with the components' fixed
  flags.
- **SIMPLE_TYPES** reads "simple" as "variety not COMPLEX" and replaces the
  variety of a restriction with its base's, so READ may write any simple
  variety for xs:restriction (comment at the stage's declaration). Order: an
  explicit stack over the type table; a type met again on it is
  st-props-correct.2. Facet values are made canonical (counts, keywords,
  enumeration values cast to the base, bounds read in the built-in type and
  compared with the base's bounds as Part 2, 4.3.7.4 to 4.3.10.4 say:
  incomparable values break no rule); the base's effective facets include the
  implicit ones of built-in types (whiteSpace, fractionDigits 0 of xs:integer,
  minLength 1 of the built-in lists, explicitTimezone of xs:dateTimeStamp). A
  failed type is not registered and the types made from it are skipped without
  a second report. Then value constraints of attribute declarations and uses
  are cast to their types (a-props-correct.2, au-props-correct.2). NOTATION
  enumeration values are read as QNames and must name notation declarations;
  xs:NOTATION itself (a declaration's type, a list item, a union member, a
  restriction without enumeration) is enumeration-required-notation. In the XSD
  dialect an unknown block name is all characters (Part 2, G.4.2.4) and an
  unescaped "-" never starts a range.
- **Measured** (release, schema tests only: instance tests wait for 5.7): NIST
  3,953 of 3,953, MS-Regex 2,590 of 2,590, MS-DataTypes 2,240 of 2,247,
  MS-SimpleType 322 of 334, Saxon Simple 65 of 65; the rest are the reader's
  (duplicate ids, include and redefine order, stZ033's chain of redefinitions)
  and complex types'. All XSD: 15,073 passed, 335 failed of the 15,408 run.
  XP40 30,647 and XQ40 40,034 unchanged, slice 198.

**Sources**: XSD schema tests by test set, run, passed and failed
(`tools/run-xsd.sh`, release build); XP40 and XQ40 passes, unchanged, and the
slice (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build).

### D172. Complex types and content models (packet 5.6)

**Summary**: Content models compile to one automaton format with counters,
expanding small repetitions; UPA is a determinism check, and restriction of
content is a walk over pairs of configurations of both models.

Recorded 2026-10-18. Fills COMPLEX_TYPES and the content model plan of D167
(`src/schema_complex_type.c`, `src/schema_content_model.c`).

- **One automaton format.** A content model is states whose transitions are
  labelled by an element declaration (with the declarations substitutable for
  it, 3.3.6.3) or a schema wildcard and carry counter tests (a counter in a
  range) and counter operations (set to one, add one); final states may need
  tests. Sequences and choices compile through Glushkov's position automaton
  and a subset construction; an all group compiles to two states (before and
  after the first member) whose transitions count each member. The matcher,
  list_expected and the restriction walk step this one format.
- **Expansion, counters, determinism.** A particle with maxOccurs (or,
  unbounded, minOccurs) up to 16 is expanded into copies, a larger one keeps
  one copy under a counter; a compilation past the state limit is tried again
  counting every repetition above one. When the counters cannot choose between
  two transitions of one particle ((a{1,20}){1,20}, (a+){1,100}: weakly but not
  strongly deterministic) the counted particles involved are expanded and the
  model compiled again, so the matcher never backtracks and needs one state and
  one value per counter. When that expansion passes the limit too (MS
  particlesZ035, Z036, maxOccurs in the thousands nested), the counters are
  kept and the transitions ordered (fewer operations first, so an inner
  repetition before an outer one); the matcher takes the first whose tests
  hold, exact unless an outer minimum needs the inner repetitions spread.
  Bounds: the configured states (and positions), 4 nodes, 32 edges or
  transitions and 64 list entries per state.
- **UPA as determinism** (cos-nonambig): two transitions of a state for
  different element particles sharing a name (also through substitution
  groups), or for different wildcard particles whose namespaces overlap, whose
  tests can hold together. An element particle beats a wildcard particle
  (3.8.6.4). Exclusive counter tests do not compete: (a{2}, a) is valid.
- **Substitution groups**: a head's transition lists the head and each member
  substitutable for it (blocking by the head's disallowed substitutions, its
  type's and the intermediate types' prohibited substitutions). Abstract
  declarations are listed too (D167 said not): the validator raises cvc-elt.2
  for them, as for an abstract head.
- **Open content** is the matcher's fallback; suffix mode appends a suffix
  state that only its wildcard enters and keeps.
- **Restriction of content** (cos-content-act-restrict, 3.4.6.4) is a walk over
  pairs of configurations (state and counter values) of the two models: each
  move of the restriction, element by element (and each name a restriction's
  wildcard shares with the base's element transitions), must be a move of the
  base whose default binding subsumes the restriction's; names the restriction
  takes by an element are not its wildcard's. A base wildcard with no global
  declaration of the name takes the restriction's local element whatever its
  process contents (XSD 1.0's NSCompat; read literally 3.4.6.4 refuses it,
  against the suite: MS particlesJ*, ctG*). Past 65,536 configurations the
  derivation is accepted provisionally, as 3.4.6.3 allows.
- **The stage**: particles (p-props-correct), attribute groups (closures over
  cyclic references, 3.6.2.1, then written), complex types base first with an
  explicit stack (content type of 3.4.2.2 and 3.4.2.3.3 with the synthesized
  particles, simple content types through `sxml_schema_compile_simple_type`,
  attribute uses and wildcards with wildcard union and intersection,
  assertions; cos-ct-extends, derivation-ok-restriction, ct-props-correct; the
  content model; registration), xs:anyType's and xs:untyped's content models,
  then element declarations (e-props-correct 2, 4, 6, 7; value constraints cast
  to the simple type). Attribute restriction is checked with XSD 1.0's clauses
  (uses allowed, types derived, fixed values, required kept, wildcard subset,
  not weaker), not against xs:anyType.
- **Registration**: a complex type with a simple base is registered with base
  xs:anyType, since `sxml_type_registry_register_schema_type` takes only
  complex bases for complex types (Proposed).
- **Text form**: `sxml_schema_content_model_write_text` prints a model in
  D167's form, for 5.4's `sxml_schema_components_write_text`.
- **Not done**: type table equivalence (cos-element-consistent clause 4 and the
  wildcard clause), the disallowed-names clauses of Wildcard Subset,
  cos-ct-extends 1.5 and 1.6 and derivation-ok-restriction.4 (locally declared
  types), xs:assertion facets of simpleContent restrictions.
- **Measured** (schema tests only, with 5.4's uncommitted reader; the instance
  tests wait for 5.7): MS-Particles 851 of 853 run, ModelGroups 377 of 391,
  Group 215 of 218, ComplexType 546 of 550, Wildcards 313 of 315, Sun MGroup 40
  of 40, CType 31 of 31, Saxon All 62 of 62, Open 49 of 51, IBM allGroup 9 of
  9, openContent 24 of 24. The rest are the reader's (duplicate ids, an all
  group with maxOccurs 0 accepted by XSD 1.1, openContent mode="none" with a
  wildcard, xs:redefine of a group) or disputed by the versions
  (particlesK006).

**Sources**: XSD schema tests by test set, with 5.4's uncommitted reader
(`tools/run-xsd.sh`).

### D173. Validation and the typed tree (packet 5.7)

**Summary**: The schema validator is a filtering tree builder that holds each
element start until its governing type is chosen, steps content model cursors,
sends schema normalized values, and records subtrees for deferred checks.

Recorded 2026-10-18. The schema validator of D165 and the seams of D167
(`src/schema_validate.c`, `src/schema_validate_value.c`,
`src/schema_validate_record.c`, `src/schema_validate_internal.h`); golden
`src/xslt_whitespace.c`, `src/arena_tree.c`.

- **A filtering tree builder.** An element's start is held back with its
  bindings and attributes (glossary pending_element) until its first content
  event or its end; then its governing type is chosen (its declaration's, after
  the type table seam; the configured governing type for the root; xsi:type
  when validly derived, cvc-elt.4; abstract declarations cvc-elt.2 and types
  cvc-type.2), xsi:nil applied (cvc-elt.3), and its start, bindings and
  assessed attributes go on. One validation frame per open element (glossary
  validation_frame) on a scratch array (D71). Each element is assessed
  strictly, laxly or skipped (glossary assessment); lax and skipped elements
  are xs:anyType, their unassessed attributes xs:untypedAtomic (XDM 4.0,
  3.3.1.1).
- **Content**: children step the parent type's content model cursor (5.6;
  wildcards by process contents, open content by the matcher); an error in
  content is reported once and the rest of the element is assessed laxly.
  Simple content is collected and assessed at the end, then sent as one text
  event of its schema normalized value, or of the declaration's default or
  fixed value when the element is empty (cvc-elt.5); whitespace text in content
  that is not mixed is dropped (XDM 4.0, 7.5.7.4), and empty content allows no
  character children at all (3.4.4.2 clause 1.1). Element Declarations
  Consistent at validation (XSD 1.1, 3.4.4.2): an element a strict or lax
  wildcard matched must have a type derived from that of a like-named
  declaration (or substitution group member) of the content model or its base
  types; a skipped one is not checked.
- **Attributes**: an attribute use of the name (also of an xsi: name: a
  required xsi:type), else the four xsi: declarations, else the attribute
  wildcard by process contents (strict needs a global declaration,
  cvc-assess-attr); missing required uses cvc-complex-type.4; uses with a
  default or fixed value not present are added. Values are sent as their schema
  normalized values.
- **Simple values** go through the cast engine (D171): an invalid value is
  reported with the facet's cvc-\*-valid name the cast puts first in its
  description, else cvc-datatype-valid.1.2.1; xs:anySimpleType and
  xs:anyAtomicType values are xs:untypedAtomic (also for value constraints in
  SIMPLE_TYPES and COMPLEX_TYPES, which reported au-props-correct.2,
  a-props-correct.2 and e-props-correct.2 for them); fixed values compare item
  by item (atomic-equal), mixed ones as strings; ENTITY values must name an
  unparsed entity of the document.
- **IDs** (cvc-id, XSD 1.1, 3.17.5.2): an ID identifies its attribute's
  element, or the parent of an element whose content is the ID (the validation
  root's content identifies nothing); one value may identify one element more
  than once; IDREFs are checked when the validation root ends.
  `sxml_schema_id_request` gained `element_number`.
- **The recorded subtree** (glossary recorded_subtree): while an element whose
  declaration has identity constraints or whose type has assertions is open,
  the annotated events also go to an arena tree through a counting builder, so
  each element's declaration is known by node index; the checks are deferred
  and run, in end order, through the seams of 5.8 and 5.9 when the outermost
  recorded element ends. Type alternatives get a parentless copy of the element
  with its attributes as they appear and its in-scope namespaces; the
  attributes it inherits are 5.9's.
- **Typed values** are derived in `sxml_node_make_typed_value` (D165): a nilled
  element none, empty content the empty sequence, element-only content
  FOTY0012, mixed content and xs:anySimpleType xs:untypedAtomic, otherwise the
  string value cast with the element's (an attribute's parent's) in-scope
  namespaces.
- **`sxml_schema_validate_node`** copies the node through a validator into a
  new arena tree (`sxml_tree_builder_copy_node`, annotations dropped); a copy
  of a node that is no document keeps its base URI.
- **Driver** (`tests/xsd/driver/xsd_test_run.c`): instance tests validate while
  parsing; the instance's xsi:schemaLocation and xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation
  hints are followed by the driver, not the library (schema.h: hints are not
  followed; 4.3.2 allows either): the hinted documents are added as RESOLVED
  documents relative to the instance, and a hint that breaks the schema is not
  followed. The suite expects hints for 55 instance tests of groups without a
  schema test and for some with one.
- **schema.h** (provisional, comment only): a document the resolver does not
  deliver is no error for include, redefine and override either (XSD 1.1, 4.2.3
  clause 2.4), resolving 5.4's Proposed item.
- **Quick fix for 5.6**: ##definedSibling excludes the substitution group
  members of the content model's declarations (3.10.4.2).
- **Not done**: the attributes an element inherits (for type alternatives,
  5.9); the XML 1.1 instances of saxon-XmlVersions (the parser reads XML 1.0);
  identity constraints and assertions stay UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE where used
  (D167, D162).
- **Measured** (release, at the packet's last commit): XSD in scope 40,755 of
  41,518 (98.2 %): instance tests 25,533 of 26,189 (97.5 %; NIST 100 %,
  Microsoft 95.0 %, Sun 93.9 %, IBM 65.3 %, Saxonica 74.5 %; 632 meet identity
  constraints, assertions or type alternatives and are not run), schema tests
  15,222 of 15,329; gate groups: datatypes 100 %, structures 95.6 %, XSD 1.1
  83.3 %; the XSD slice 147 of 147. XP40 30,647, XQ40 40,034 and XT40 7,990
  unchanged.

**Sources**: XSD in scope, instance and schema tests by contributor, gate
groups and the slice, at the packet's last commit (`tools/run-xsd.sh`,
`tools/conformance-report.py`, release build); XP40, XQ40 and XT40 passes,

### D174. Schema-aware XPath and XQuery (packet 5.11)

**Summary**: XPath and XQuery become schema-aware through `in_scope_schemas` in
the static context, one schema scope module for lookups and errors, import
schema, validate as an internal row, and fn:xsd-validator.

Recorded 2026-10-18. Replaces the rejection places of D97 and D162 for XPath
and XQuery (XPST0008 of schema-element, XQST0009, XQST0075, FODC0009 of
fn:parse-xml, the driver's non-goal features); golden `src/xquery_flwor.c` (an
internal native row), `src/function_library_csv.c`.

- **xpath.h** (stable API, additive): `sxml_schema_view` and the last field
  `sxml_static_context_configuration.in_scope_schemas`, the in-scope schema
  definitions; empty is not schema-aware. Schemas must be the processor's and
  outlive what is compiled with them (validation reads them at run time). The
  view goes into `sxml_ir_static_context` (copied into the unit like the
  decimal formats, D131), so static analysis and run time read one field;
  `sxml_xpath_static_context.processor` gives the resolver for schema imports.
- **One module, `src/schema_scope.c`** (glossary schema_scope): lookups of
  types and global declarations across the in-scope schemas (built-in types
  first, then the first schema that has the name), substitution group members,
  constructor functions of schema simple types (used by static calls in
  `src/xpath_lower.c` and by fn:function-lookup), and
  `sxml_schema_scope_raise`, the one way a schema error becomes a language
  error: the language's code, "constraint: description".
- **schema-element(N), schema-attribute(N)** resolve statically to the choice
  of element(M, T) tests over N and the non-abstract, not blocked members of
  its substitution group (T the declared type, "?" when nillable), and to
  attribute(N, T); `is_schema_declaration` is no longer set. A union with a
  list member is not an item type (XPST0051).
- **import schema** (XQuery 4.0, 5.11): prefixes bind like namespace
  declarations ("default element namespace" counts for XQST0066); XQST0057,
  XQST0058; a namespace a host schema defines (or xs) is taken from there; the
  others compile into one schema of RESOLVED documents (hints, or the namespace
  alone; target namespace checked) kept by the processor until it is finalized
  (`sxml_processor_keep_schema`), as it keeps registered types: a unit owning
  schemas would make finalization a cycle (D71), since a schema's assertions
  and identity constraints are XPath units. When a document is not delivered,
  compilation is tried once more without the hints the resolver does not
  deliver (hints may be ignored). Errors: src-import and schema_reference
  XQST0059, sch-props-correct.2 XQST0035, others XQST0012. A main module
  without schemas gets the processor's one schema of the built-in components
  (`sxml_processor_get_builtin_schema`), so lax validation, xsi:type and
  validation by a built-in type always have one. A long-lived processor that
  compiles many importing queries keeps their schemas; caching them by
  documents is a later step.
- **validate** lowers to the internal row `validate($node, $mode, $type)`
  (`src/function_library_schema.c`): XQTY0030, XQDY0061, XQDY0084 (strict, no
  declaration), XQDY0027 (invalid, constraint named), XQST0104 statically;
  "type xs:untyped" copies without annotations. The schema is the in-scope one
  that declares the root's name or defines the type.
- **System properties**: fn:system-properties gives schema-aware and
  accepts-typed-data true; XSLT's is-schema-aware stays false (5.12).
- **fn:xsd-validator** (F&O 4.0, 17.2.5), a new library part: options
  validation-mode, type, return-typed-node, return-error-details (message and
  rule maps from a report sink); V validates with the in-scope schemas of its
  caller's static context (a function item holds no schema). The options
  schema, schema-location, target-namespace and use-xsi-schema-location are
  FODC0009 (one place): compiling a schema while a query runs needs the
  processor, which run time does not reach. The option limit of
  `function_library_core_internal.h` is 12.
- **xsd-validation of fn:parse-xml** validates the parsed document (FODC0008,
  FODC0014); fn:doc and fn:parse-xml-fragment keep FODC0009 (the loader keeps
  one tree per URI; a fragment has no validation root).
- **QT4 driver**: schemaImport, schemaValidation and typedData are supported

  into one schema that is the in-scope schema of XPath and XQuery and validates
  `validation="strict|lax"` sources; the resolver serves SCHEMA_DOCUMENT by

  schema_aware_test) is counted in the report members `schema_aware`,

- **Budget**: a schema-aware test case whose query runs out of the test budget

- **Measured** (release, commit f43f747): schema-aware XQ40 1,231 of 1,516
  (81.2 %; the proposed gate is 70 %), XP40 279 of 315 (88.6 %); XP40 30,924

### D175. Assertions and type alternatives (packet 5.9)

**Summary**: XSD 1.1 assertions and type alternatives compile with `xpath.h` in
XPath Valid's static context and run on the one evaluator over assertion copies
and parentless element copies with inherited attributes.

Recorded 2026-10-18. Fills ASSERTIONS and the seams of D167 for XSD 1.1
assertions and conditional type assignment (`src/schema_assertion.c`); golden
`src/schema_simple_type.c`.

- **One engine.** Tests are compiled with `xpath.h` (the XPath 4.0 front end
  reads XSD 1.1's XPath 2.0, a superset 3.13.6.2 allows) in the static context
  of XPath Valid: the record's namespace bindings (prefix 0 and xml left out),
  its {default namespace} (xpathDefaultNamespace) as the default element
  namespace, its base URI when absolute, the codepoint collation; assertions
  declare `$value` as xs:anyAtomicType\*, type alternatives nothing. A static
  or type error is as-props-correct.2 or ta-props-correct.2. Evaluation gives
  no available documents and collections and the empty default collection (a
  resolver of the file, 3.13.4.2); a dynamic or type error makes a test false;
  the result is taken as fn:boolean takes it
  (`sxml_evaluator_compute_effective_boolean_value`).
- **Assertions of complex types** run when the outermost recorded element ends,
  on an assertion copy (glossary assertion_copy): the element's recorded
  subtree copied into a tree of its own whose root is xs:anyType (3.13.4.1
  clauses 1.2 and 1.3: partially validated, nothing outside it); `$value` is
  the typed value of simple content, else empty. The recorder drops comments
  and processing instructions (clause 1.2, the suite's
  comments-and-PIs-excluded). Each false one is cvc-assertion.
- **Assertion facets** (Part 2, 4.3.13.3) run with `$value` and no context
  item, for the type's {assertions}, a list's items against their item type,
  and a union value against its active basic member (glossary basic_member):
  the member the cast engine chose, which knows no assertions, and when its
  assertions fail each later basic member whose cast of the text succeeds
  (union items of a list: the chosen member only). One report,
  cvc-assertions-valid, and the value is invalid. The xs:assertion facets of a
  simpleContent restriction are now the synthesized simple content type's
  (`facet_assertions`, as read; 5.6 gave them to the complex type).
- **Type alternatives** (3.12.4) are tested on the parentless element copy of
  D173 with the element's inherited attributes added (glossary
  inherited_attribute, 3.3.5.6): the validator keeps the inheritable attributes
  of the open elements (a use's {inheritable}, else the declaration's), with
  their values as they appeared, and the copy gets the innermost of each name
  the element does not have. The copies have the document's base URI. The first
  test that holds selects, else the default alternative, else the declared
  type.
- **Type tables compared** (3.8.6.3 equivalence, the minimum it requires: same
  expression, namespace bindings, default namespace, base URI and type, same
  default type), for cos-element-consistent and clause 4.6 of 3.4.6.4
  (`sxml_schema_type_tables_are_equivalent`).
- **Fixes in earlier stages**: an attribute reference without inheritable=
  takes its declaration's {inheritable} (`has_inheritable`, as read; RESOLVE
  took the declaration's when the reference said false); a restricted attribute
  use keeps its {inheritable} (3.4.6.4 clause 5.4);
  xpathDefaultNamespace="##defaultNamespace" on xs:schema is resolved on each
  host element (3.13.2).
- **Not done**: namespace fixup of an inherited attribute whose prefix an inner
  element rebinds; xml:base of ancestors in the copies' base URI; value
  constraints and enumerations checked against assertions at compile time;
  casting to a type with assertions in schema-aware expressions (5.11).
- **Measured** (release): Saxon Assert 101 of 101, CTA 113 of 113, IBM assert
  79 of 79, assertion 101 of 101, typeAlternatives 39 of 39,
  typeAlternativesMixed 15 of 15 (before: 188 of 448). XSD in scope 41,037 of
  41,518 (98.8 %, from 40,755); gate groups datatypes 100 %, structures 95.6 %,
  XSD 1.1 95.6 % (from 83.3 %); slice 147 of 147. No test set lost a test
  (ibm-vc, ibm-idIDREF, saxon-VC, saxon-Override and saxon-Wild gained some).
  Only schema code changed: XP40, XQ40 and XT40 are not affected.

**Sources**: XSD assertion and type alternative test sets, before and after,
XSD in scope, gate groups and the slice (`tools/run-xsd.sh`,
`tools/conformance-report.py`, release build).

### D176. sxml validate (packet 5.10)

**Summary**: `sxml validate` validates each FILE in one pass through a
validator over the null builder, uses only the schemas named by required
`--schema` options, never following location hints, and reports in text or
JSON.

Recorded 2026-10-18. The command of the 5.10 design (`docs/tasks/phase-5.md`),
in `apps/sxml/command_validate.c`; golden `apps/sxml/command_check.c`. Public
API only (`schema.h`, `xml.h`).

- **One pass per FILE**: the XML parser feeds a validator whose result builder
  is the null builder; the processor and its local-file resolver are
  `query_command.h`'s (`SXML_PARAMETER_BINDING_NONE`). SCHEMA documents are
  TEXT documents with file URIs, so includes and imports resolve relative to
  the referring document; report locations are named back by
  `sxml_query_file_of_uri`, moved with `sxml_query_make_file_uri` from
  `command_transform.c` to `query_command.c` (one helper for both commands).
- **Schema location hints are not followed, and there is no flag for them.**
  The schema is what the command line names (D44: the command line fully
  determines behaviour; XSD 1.1 Part 1, 4.3.2 leaves hints to the processor;
  `schema.h` does not follow them either). A hinted document is named with
  another `--schema`. An explicit flag can be added later if the owner wants
  one; it would be a second, visible way to name schema documents, never a
  default.
- **Required options in the CLI framework**: `SXML_CLI_OPTION_AT_LEAST_ONCE`
  (`cli_command.h`) is a repeatable option the parser requires
  (`SXML_CLI_USAGE_ERROR_MISSING_OPTION`, "missing option '--schema'"); help
  shows `--schema=SCHEMA [--schema=SCHEMA]...` and "(required; repeatable)", so
  the usage line and docs/CLI.md agree.
- **Reports**: text errors go to standard error as they arrive; JSON keeps a
  file's errors in an arena until its object is written, so `status` comes
  before `errors`. A description that starts with its constraint name (the
  facet errors of D173) is shown without it. In text, a file whose validity is
  not known gets one line on standard error. A FILE the parser rejects is
  reported as `sxml check` does; a failure of the validator (a limit,
  UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE of the 5.8 and 5.9 seams) is `failed`, exit 4.
- **Deviation from the design**: a document an include names that cannot be
  read is reported as src-resolve where its components are used, not
  src-include (D173, XSD 1.1 4.2.3 clause 2.4); docs/CLI.md says so.
- **WebAssembly**: the CLI module grows to 4,877,565 bytes stripped (1,126,567
  gzipped); its ctest budget is raised to 5,500,000 / 1,250,000 and the growth
  reported under "Proposed".
- **Measured**: the instance tests of `msData/particles` (ms-Particles_w3c, 514
  run by both) give the same validity through `sxml validate` as through
  sxml-xsd-test, the 16 that need location hints with the hinted documents
  passed as `--schema`.

**Sources**: the CLI module, stripped and gzipped (4,877,565 / 1,126,567 bytes)
(`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`, wasm build); configured: the CLI
ctest budget, 5,500,000 / 1,250,000 (from
`bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt`); validity of the instance tests of
msData/particles (ms-Particles_w3c, 514), through sxml validate and through
sxml-xsd-test (`sxml`, `sxml-xsd-test`).

### D177. Identity constraints (packet 5.8)

**Summary**: Identity constraint selectors and fields are checked against XSD's
XPath subsets on the AST, compiled with `xpath.h`, and evaluated on the
recorded subtree, with XSD equality and hash-indexed node tables.

Recorded 2026-10-18. IDENTITY_CONSTRAINTS and the identity seam of D167
(`src/schema_identity.c`, `tests/schema_identity_test.c`); golden
`src/schema_resolve.c`, `src/schema_validate_record.c`.

- **The subsets are checked on the AST, then compiled as XPath; no second path
  engine.** Each selector and field is parsed by the XPath 4.0 front end
  (`sxml_xpath_build_ast`) and its AST checked against 3.11.6.2 and 3.11.6.3: a
  union of paths of `.` and child NameTest steps (`child::` written or not),
  `.//` only first, `@` or `attribute::` only as the last step of a field, no
  predicates, NameTests QName, `*` and `p:*` (not `*:n` or `Q{}n`); otherwise
  c-selector-xpath or c-fields-xpath. Then it is compiled with `xpath.h` (XPath
  Valid, 3.13.6.2): the record's in-scope namespaces without the default
  namespace and xml, xpathDefaultNamespace as the default element namespace.
  c-props-correct.1 (a keyref refers to a key or unique) and .2 (as many
  fields).
- **Evaluation on the recorded subtree** (D173), by the one evaluator: the
  selector with the declaring element as context node; elements without a
  governing declaration (skipped, or lax without one) are not targets and are
  ignored as field nodes, as are attributes nothing governed
  (xs:untypedAtomic); a field gives at most one node of a simple type or simple
  content (cvc-identity-constraint.3); a nilled element has no value; key
  sequences are the fields' typed values, derived from the annotations (D165).
  key 4.2.1 (a field without a value), 4.2.2 and 4.2.3 (a nillable field
  element); unique 4.1; keyref 4.3.
- **XSD's equality** (Part 2, 2.2.3) is fn:atomic-equal of values of one
  primitive type, xs:untypedAtomic counted as xs:string: NaN equals itself
  (identity), 1 and 1.0 are one xs:decimal, xs:float 1 is not xs:decimal 1,
  xs:string is not xs:anyURI; field values compare item by item, so a value
  equals a list of one. A hash index over `sxml_atomic_item_hash` finds the
  candidates.
- **Node tables without state between calls**: the seam stays one plain call
  per element. A keyref evaluates its referenced key at its element and at each
  descendant whose declaration has it (3.11.5); a key sequence met with one
  node is in the table; one met with several nodes is resolved level by level
  up to the keyref's element with an explicit work list (D71): an element's own
  entry wins, children's entries that conflict are dropped. Keys of descendants
  are evaluated again for each keyref (no cache; measured fast enough on the
  suite).
- **Not done**: compiling an XPath record in its namespace context is written
  here and in `src/schema_assertion.c` (5.9, developed at the same time); one
  shared function is for a sweep.
- **Measured** (release): MS-IdentityConstraint 1,058 of 1,058 run (was 788;
  the 48 invalid schemas now rejected), Sun IdConstrDefs 48 of 48, IBM
  identityConstraint 18 of 18, xpathDefaultNSonKeyKeyRefUnique 26 of 26 (packet
  gate 80 %); 415 more XSD tests pass, none fewer; XSD in scope 41,170 of
  41,518 before 5.9 landed, 41,452 (99.8 %) with it; gate groups 100 %, 99.5 %,
  98.9 %; slice 147 of 147. No shared code changed: XP40, XQ40 and XT40 hold.

**Sources**: XSD identity constraint test sets, XSD in scope before and with
5.9, gate groups and the slice (`tools/run-xsd.sh`,
`tools/conformance-report.py`, release build).

### D178. XSD and schema-aware conformance sweep 1 (packet 5.13)

**Summary**: The QT4 driver stops reclassifying schema-aware outcomes, fixing
the two cases at their causes; validation descriptions use message templates,
and one XPath record compiler serves assertions, alternatives and identity
constraints.

Recorded 2026-10-18. Amends D174 (its QT4 outcome rules); resolves three
Proposed items (validation descriptions, locations of configured schema
documents, a simple base for a complex type).

- **Honest outcomes (amends D174).** The QT4 driver no longer counts a
  schema-aware test case that ends at the step or memory limit as "fail", nor
  one that stops at SXML_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE as "not run": D95's zero
  errors must not be met by reclassification. Identity constraints (D177) and
  assertions (D175) run. The two cases D174 moved are fixed at their causes:

  - app-CatalogCheck Catalog009 (536 MB): a group by packed every variable of
    the FLWOR into its tuples and concatenated each per group (XQuery 4.0,
    4.13.8), here `$testsets`, 737 documents, once per dependency (18,564
    tuples). A variable that no variable reference or grouping specification
    from the group by clause on names (the later clauses and the return clause;
    any reference of the name counts) is left out of the tuples: its grouped
    value is never read (`src/xquery_lower.c`). 147 MB; passes.
  - app-Demos itunes (10^8 steps): the query compares the keys of 6,597 tracks
    of a 10 MB library once per artist, 367 million steps by D89's accounting.
    A FILTER whose predicate is a leaf (BINARY, UNARY, CAST, CASTABLE,
    INSTANCE_OF over atoms) that reads the focus computes it in the filter's
    own task, one step per item instead of two (`src/evaluator.c`), and the
    typed value of an xs:string node is its string value without a cast
    (`src/xdm_node.c`): 287 million steps. The QT4 driver's budget per
    evaluation is four times SXML_QT4_TEST_MAXIMUM_STEP_COUNT, as the XSLT
    driver's (D166, for a whole large input); itunes passes in 85 s (release).
- **Validation descriptions name what failed.** A description is a message
  template (glossary message_template, `src/schema_validate_value.c`): static
  text with placeholders for the element or attribute as written, a value
  (quoted, shortened past 60 bytes, one line), a type ("type 'xs:decimal'", or
  "an anonymous type derived from ..."), the expected terms of the content
  model cursor (list_expected), and the facet the cast names with its value
  from the type or its nearest registered base. Every cvc-\* report uses one:
  "element 'price' is not allowed here; expected 'title'", "element 'p:price'
  lacks the required attribute 'currency'", "element 'price' has the value
  '-1.005', which is not valid for type 'price': the value is below the
  minInclusive facet (...); the minInclusive facet is '0'", identity
  constraints with their element and constraint, assertions with their test. A
  template per site keeps the WebAssembly module in its budget (pieces built at
  run time did not: sxml.wasm 1,997,902 of 2,000,000 bytes). The description is
  made per report, so the first one goes to the error record through the item
  heap (sxml_item_heap_raise_error, D41).
- **Configured schema documents are located by the library**: one that is not
  well-formed is reported at the parser's line and column, one that is not a
  schema document at its document element, both with its URI as source name
  (`sxml_schema_report_request.document_uri`); `sxml validate` maps URIs to
  names only (standard input stays "-").
- **One XPath record compiler**: `sxml_schema_compile_xpath_record`
  (`src/schema_assertion.c`, XPath Valid, 3.13.6.2) for assertions, type
  alternatives, selectors and fields (D177's open item); selectors and fields
  now get the record's base URI too.
- **XSD**: src-redefine 6.2.2 and 7.2.2: a group or attribute group redefined
  without a self-reference gets two unnamed complex types, one of the
  original's content or attributes and a restriction of it of the
  redefinition's, so COMPLEX_TYPES checks the restriction with its own rules
  (cos-content-act-restrict; derivation-ok-restriction 2 to 4, as 7.2.2 says)
  at the redefinition; a default open content with appliesToEmpty false is
  dropped when the explicit content type is empty (3.4.2.3.3 clause 6.1,
  `open_content_skips_empty`); the children of xs:override are read with the
  overridden document's defaults (4.2.5: they stand in D2'); a complex type
  with simple content is registered with its simple base (types.c accepts it,
  3.4.1); "-0000" is year zero (Part 2, D.3.1; also QT4
  cbcl-cast-gYearMonth-004a).
- **Not done**: is-id of union and list elements (the start event is sent
  before the value is known; it needs the start held back to the end of simple
  content); src-include for an include that cannot be read (XSD 1.1, 4.2.3
  makes it no error; D176's deviation stays); the assertion leftovers of D175
  (no test of the suite needs them); the pattern facet on canonical forms was
  already done (`sxml_cast_check_item_facets`). Remaining XSD failures: XSD 1.0

  annotations), xs:NOTATION as a union member (D171), XML 1.1 instances,
  Element Declarations Consistent with wildcards and type tables (saxon
  wild078, 079, 081).
- **Also**: src-ct for mixed attributes of xs:complexType and xs:complexContent
  that disagree and for xs:openContent in a restriction without a particle (the
  schema for schema documents, XSD 1.1 bug 16786); Wildcard Subset with its
  disallowed-names clauses (3.10.6.2 clauses 2 to 4) in one function,
  `sxml_schema_wildcard_is_subset`, for content and attribute wildcards (two

- **Measured** (release, every suite run with this code): XSD in scope 41,483

### D179. Schema-aware XSLT (packet 5.12)

**Summary**: XSLT becomes schema-aware: xsl:import-schema compiles one schema
beside the host's in-scope schemas, validation attributes wrap constructed
nodes in XQuery's validate row with XSLT's rules, and typed modes are checked.

Recorded 2026-10-18. Replaces D162's two XSLT rejection places
(`reject_schema_awareness`'s XTSE1660 and XTSE1650 in `src/xslt_read.c`, D163,
D169) with D174's mechanisms; golden `src/xquery_static.c` (import schema),
`tests/xquery_schema_test.c`.

- **xsl:import-schema** (3.13) is a new module, `src/xslt_schema.c` (glossary
  schema_import), run after reading: the declarations of the sealed AST become
  the documents of one `sxml_schema_create` (the synthetic schema document): an
  inline xs:schema as a NODE document of the module's tree (base URI the
  declaration's), a schema-location as a RESOLVED document resolved against the
  declaration's static base URI with its namespace checked, a namespace alone
  as a RESOLVED document by namespace. Of one namespace only the declarations
  of the highest import precedence count; a namespace a host schema defines (or
  XSD's) is taken from there; a location or namespace the resolver does not
  deliver is dropped (3.13: not an error by itself), probed with
  `sxml_schema_scope_probe_document`, now shared with XQuery's import schema
  (one probe, `src/schema_scope.c`). The processor keeps the schema
  (`sxml_processor_keep_schema`, D174). XTSE0215 (inline schema with a
  schema-location or another namespace), XTSE0220 (any schema error, its
  constraint and description in the message). Schema roles (4.0) are not read:
  one unnamed role.
- **In-scope schemas**: the host's (`static_context.in_scope_schemas` of the
  stylesheet configuration, now read, `xslt.h` comment, additive), then the
  imported schema; neither gives the processor's built-in schema. They live in
  the AST (`sxml_xslt_ast_set_in_scope_schemas`), the lowering's base static
  context carries them into every module's XPath static context and IR module
  and the unit (D174's one field), so `as` types, schema-element(), casts,
  constructor functions and type-available see them. The host's schemas are
  what makes a source the host validated and the stylesheet's types the same
  types (schema types are never interned).
- **Validation is D174's validate row with XSLT's rules**: mode
  `SXML_SCHEMA_VALIDATE_MODE_XSLT_RULES` (+4) and the descriptor
  `validate-items` (item()\*): every item validated (documents, elements,
  attributes) or kept; XTTE1550, XTTE1512, XTTE1510, XTTE1515, XTTE1540,
  XTTE1555 (a document's cvc-id), XTTE1535. One lowering helper
  (`sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_validation`, `src/xslt_lower_construct.c`) reads
  [xsl:]validation, [xsl:]type or the default-validation in force and wraps the
  constructed nodes of xsl:element, xsl:attribute, xsl:copy, xsl:copy-of,
  xsl:document, xsl:result-document (the result tree's document node),
  xsl:source-document and literal result elements; preserve is the
  PRESERVES_TYPES construction flag (XQuery's construction mode), strip the
  default; XTSE1505 in the reader, XTSE1520 and XTSE1530 at lowering; an
  unprefixed [xsl:]type is in the default namespace for elements and types.
  Temporary trees (9.4) are built as preserve (25.2). The evaluator delivers a
  constructed node into a receiver that preserves types also when the node
  itself strips (the same tree either way), so variables keep the D166
  streaming.
- **input-type-annotations="strip"** (4.1) is the document preparation of
  whitespace stripping (`src/xslt_whitespace.c`): the same copy, without
  annotations, for the global context item and documents fn:doc and document()
  load.
- **Typed modes** (6.9.4): a mode with typed="yes", "strict" or "lax" (or "no")
  tries one rule before all its template rules, of the highest precedence and
  priority, made from two XPath snippets: it matches an item that is not an
  XNode or an untyped (typed) element or attribute, and its template raises
  XTTE3100. Name tests are not read as schema-element() (strict, lax; XTSE3105
  not raised).
- **fn:document**'s xsd-validation option (4.0) validates each document with
  fn:parse-xml's `sxml_schema_scope_validate_document` (D174).
- **is-schema-aware** is true; default-validation strict or lax is XTSE0020
  (only preserve and strip are allowed). A schema error whose description
  already starts with its constraint name is raised without naming it twice
  (`sxml_schema_scope_raise`).
- **XSLT driver**: schema_aware is supported but stays a non-goal for scope
  (outside the D95 denominator, as QT4's schema features, D174); a test case
  requiring it, or whose environment has a schema or a validated source, is
  counted in the area "schema-aware". The environment's schemas compile into
  one schema that validates sources (strict, lax) and is the stylesheet's host

  for it; validation 1601, accumulator-073); xs:untypedAtomic as [xsl:]type;
  declarations of xml:lang and xml:space (no xml.xsd built in); xsl:copy of an
  element under preserve keeps its annotation instead of xs:anyType; the fn
  namespace schema (json-to-xml typed, D174); XTSE0265; schema roles.

### D180. Conformance sweep 2 (packet 5.13)

**Summary**: A schema document's global type named like a built-in type is that
built-in component, a source that does not validate is judged by the
assertions, and validate-items becomes a row of its own.

Recorded 2026-10-18. Clears D179's six XT40 errors at their causes; resolves
the Proposed item "xslt.h reads the host's in-scope schemas".

- **The schema for schema documents compiles beside the built-ins**
  (catalog-005b, catalog-009). XSD 1.1 Part 1 puts the built-in components in
  every schema (4.2.1, schema(D)), has every processor know them without
  reading (C.2.1, hard-coded schemas) and counts two top-level type definitions
  of one name as one component (3.4.6.5, the note on component identity);
  XMLSchema.xsd calls its xs:anyType "not the real urType, but as close an
  approximation as we can get". So a global type definition whose name a
  built-in type already has is that built-in component: the document's own
  definition is left unnamed, and sch-props-correct.2 does not hold against it.
  One place: `enter_global` (`src/schema_read.c`); other duplicates in the XSD
  namespace still conflict, and an xs:import of it was already ignored. With
  it, the built-in xml.xsd that stands in for an import of the xml: namespace
  the resolver does not deliver is used only when no document of that namespace
  is there (4.2.6.2: a processor may keep the first import of a namespace;
  `src/schema_assemble.c`): XMLSchema.xsd imports it from www.w3.org beside the
  environment's xml.xsd. catalog-009 passes; catalog-005b fails on its own data
  (29 of the suite's stylesheets use XSLT 4.0 instructions and attributes,
  xsl:item-type, method="csv", line-ending, that the catalog's
  schema-for-xslt40.xsd does not have yet).
- **A source that does not validate is sxml's answer, not an error of the
  environment** (as-3301, as-3401, match-208, match-209). Their sources give
  xs:ENTITY attributes the names of parsed entities (`<!ENTITY eac "&#xE9;">`).
  XSD 1.1 Part 1, 3.16.4 String Valid clause 2 requires a declared entity name,
  an unparsed entity of the document (Part 2, 3.4.11; Saxon's own XSD test
  saxonData/Id id017.n01 expects invalid without one). sxml's parser reads the
  internal subset and passes unparsed entities on (`src/xml.c`), so nothing of
  the DTD is missing: the right outcome needs no DTD support, and the test
  cases declare no dtd dependency, so "not run" has no ground in the catalog.
  The expected results are Saxon's, which does not make the check
  (report/results_XSLT3.0: pass; no other submission is schema-aware).
  Validation is part of the processor under test (the validator of
  xsl:import-schema and the validation attributes), so the XSLT driver judges
  an invalid source like any dynamic error of the transformation: the
  assertions decide (an expected error could pass), here "fail"
  (`sxml_xslt_test_judge_invalid_source`, `tests/xslt/driver/
  xslt_execution.c`). An environment schema that does not compile stays an
  error. The QT4 driver has no such case.
- **validate-items is a row of its own** (`call_validate_items`,
  `src/function_library_schema.c`): XSLT's rules are no longer a branch of
  XQuery's validate, so what links only XQuery's (the JavaScript module) does
  not carry them. sxml.wasm was 2,001,084 bytes stripped after 5.12, over its
  2,000,000 budget; now 1,998,723 (696,023 gzipped of 700,000).
- **xslt.h's in_scope_schemas comment is accepted** (D179's Proposed item): it
  documents what the stylesheet does with an existing field of xpath.h's static
  context (D174), is additive (a host that passed schemas before had them
  ignored), matches `src/xslt.c` and the lowering, and XSLT 4.0 allows it (F.2:
  an implementation may make schema components available beyond
  xsl:import-schema). It is what lets a host-validated source and the
  stylesheet share one schema's types.
- **Not done**: is-id of union and list elements (D178) is not cheap: the
  element's start event goes to the builders, with its attributes and namespace
  bindings, before its content; holding it to the end of simple content means
  holding those and any comments and processing instructions too, and tree.h is
  frozen (D99), so no later mark is possible. Left for a sweep that needs it
  (no test of the suites does).
- **Measured** (release, all four suites with this code at ae616ca): XT40 8,650
  passed (was 8,649), 558 failed, 0 errors (was 6), gate rate 8,029 of 8,728;
  schema-aware XT40 627 of 971; only the test sets as, catalog and match
  changed, none lost a test; XP40 30,931 and XQ40 41,273, 0 errors; XSD in
  scope 41,483 of 41,518; slices 198, 147 (XSLT, of 154) and 147 (XSD).

**Sources**: XT40 (and schema-aware), XP40, XQ40 and XSD passes, all four
suites, and the slices (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, `tools/run-qt4.sh`,
`tools/run-xsd.sh`, `tools/conformance-report.py`, release build, at ae616ca);
sxml.wasm stripped and gzipped, after 5.12 and after the validate-items row
(`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`, wasm build).

### D183. Phase 7 plan: one packet per deferred feature, optional features for size (packet 7.1)

**Summary**: Phase 7 is planned as one packet per deferred feature, from
optional features and the size budget through streaming, Update, HTML5, Full
Text and UCA to a review, each reusing existing mechanisms with its own gate.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D95, D97, D154, D157, D162, D165, D166, D181. Plans
Phase 7 (D162) in `docs/tasks/phase-7.md`, as D165 planned Phase 5.

- **Packets** (numbers in wave order; "a, b" are packet groups):

  - 7.2: optional features and the size budget;
  - 7.3: xsl:evaluate;
  - 7.4: XSLT backwards-compatible behaviour and XPath 1.0 compatibility mode;
  - 7.5: disable-output-escaping;
  - 7.6a, b: streaming (streamability analysis, then streamed evaluation);
  - 7.7a, b, c: the Update Facility;
  - 7.8: EXPath Binary;
  - 7.9: EXPath File;
  - 7.10a, b: HTML5;
  - 7.11: fn:transform;
  - 7.12a, b, c: Full Text;
  - 7.13: XML 1.1 input;
  - 7.14a, b: DTD processing;
  - 7.15a, b: UCA;
  - 7.16: timezone database;
  - 7.17: calendars and languages;
  - 7.18: Invisible XML;
  - 7.19: review.

  7.3, 7.5, 7.13 and 7.14 are proposed for the owner (below). The order weighs
  the cases unlocked, user demand and risk:

  - 7.4 comes early because every `version="1.0"` stylesheet now raises
    XTDE0160 when evaluated;
  - Full Text is late because it is the riskiest;
  - UCA, timezones, languages and iXML come last: they are few cases and much
    data.
- **Counts** (not run at 3b0812a; first unmet dependency where the dashboard
  has it, else from the catalogs):

  - XT40: streaming 2,932, backwards compatibility 124, xsl:evaluate 83, dtd
    78, XML 1.1 65, disable-output-escaping 32, numbering languages 14;
  - XQ40: HTML 1,401, Update 825, Full Text 685, Binary 673, XML 1.1 313, File
    271, fn:transform 133, UCA 49 (+13), infoset-dtd 32, languages 24, Olson 8,
    iXML 10, XPath 1.0 mode 5;
  - xmlconf: 275 XML 1.1 cases and 265 with external entities.

  About 4,400 of XQ40's 5,505 not-run cases and 3,330 of XT40's 4,659.
  staticTyping, the xsl-stylesheet PI, HTML4 output, XInclude and remote_http
  stay unplanned (listed in the plan).
- **Mechanisms, no parallel machinery**:

  - xsl:evaluate and fn:transform compile at run time and run a unit evaluation
    (D154, D157); fn:transform is supplied by the XSLT layer, as
    fn:load-xquery-module is supplied by XQuery.
  - HTML5, iXML, XML 1.1 and DTD entities send tree builder events; HTML tree
    construction works on a working node table first, because the adoption
    agency moves built nodes.
  - DTD validation is schema validation against components built from the DTD.
  - Updates are applied by rebuilding trees through the tree builder, so
    `tree.h` stays frozen (node identity across an update is not observable
    within a snapshot).
  - Streaming is first a static streamability pass with unstreamed evaluation,
    which yields every result and static error; then a receiving task (D166)
    fed by the parser. The feature is claimed only then.
  - Full Text selections compile into a match program as regexes do (D53); Full
    Text goes in the XQuery grammar only.
  - The XPath 1.0 mode is a static-context flag that the lowering reads.
  - disable-output-escaping uses the JAXP processing-instruction pair, because
    text nodes cannot carry a mark.
- **Header changes** (additive, each with its record): `processor.h` (optional
  features, a file-system interface, resource kinds for Full Text, entities and
  optionally collation and timezone data), `xpath.h` (the 1.0 compatibility
  flag), `xquery.h` (updating queries), `xml.h` (DTD options). No substrate
  header changes.
- **Gates** (proposed): each feature has its own gate in its packet, from 75 %
  (Full Text, languages) to 95 % (Binary, HTML5, the xmlconf cases). The Phase
  7 gate is every accepted feature's gate, the earlier gates still held with no
  passed count dropped, no error outcome, the owner's size budgets, and fuzz
  targets for every new parser.
- **PLAN.md**: the Phase 7 row names the optional features and the four
  proposed additions.

**Sources**: not-run cases per optional feature in XT40, XQ40 and xmlconf, from
the dashboard where it has the first unmet dependency, else from the catalogs
(`tools/conformance-report.py`, at 3b0812a).

### D185. XSLT conformance sweep after the Phase 4 gate (packet 4.19)

**Summary**: The XSLT sweep after the Phase 4 gate leaves "~T" type patterns
unimplemented, makes extension instructions call named templates, adds
xsl:item-type and xsl:record-type, and strips available documents as sources.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D29, D98, D152, D160, D169, D181. Verified as D181
asks: the debug preset, the unit and CLI tests touched, clang-tidy and the
call-cycle check on the files changed, and the whole XT40 suite with the
release driver after each change, compared case by case (it runs in about a
minute here). **XT40 8,650 to 8,759 passed, 0 errors, no case lost.**

- **Type patterns "~T" (priority, 34 failing): not implemented, by D29.** The
  project's draft (13 October 2026) has no type patterns: PR 2911 (14 September 2026)
  replaced them with atomic(), record(), map and array patterns, which sxml
  has; "~T" survives only in a few examples and in the typed attribute of
  xsl:mode. The suite's priority cases are written against the older draft, and
  its other expectations there (priority 1.0 for ".[p]", 0.25 for "{42}" and
  "array({'x'})") contradict 6.4 of the project's draft too. Nothing in
  priority changes.
- **Extension instructions call named templates** (10.1.3; call-template -ext 7
  to 32 of 32): an extension instruction named after a template it binds to is
  xsl:call-template of it; each attribute is parsed while lowering, as a kept
  AST (D152, `sxml_xslt_lowering_parse_attribute`), as a value template for an
  xs:boolean or atomic parameter (boolean words; xs:untypedAtomic) or as an
  expression otherwise.
- **xsl:item-type and xsl:record-type** (5.4, D98; record 22 to 39, type-alias
  13 to 25): `src/xslt_named_type.c` does what XQuery's declare type and
  declare record do: the static context's named item types (resolved in rounds;
  XPST0051, XTSE4035, XTSE4030) and nominative records in the type registry
  (XTSE4050). Both are components of a new package component kind, item type,
  so packages bind them by 3.4.5.5. xsl:field takes the draft's static and
  select. Delayed (D162): the record constructor function (5.4.2.2).
- **Available documents are source documents** (4.2.2; snapshot 16 to 34, and
  merge, document): a transformation strips each available document once and
  hands the copies to fn:doc; a global context item that is one becomes its
  copy. fn:snapshot of a namespace node.
- **merge** (67 to 79; 29 more need streaming): the XSLT driver serves
  collections (also collection 0 to 5); XTSE1060, XTSE1070, XTSE3470, XTSE3500
  for the current-group functions in patterns; XTDE2210 for fixed merge-key
  attributes that differ (raised when evaluated); XTTE2230 for incomparable
  merge keys. Left: XTDE3490 (map:get of an unknown source name, in
  `src/xpath_lower.c`), XTDE2220, computed XTDE2210, validation codes.
- **Errors in included modules** (D169's accepted design, done): each static
  context's IR module has its stylesheet module's URI as source name, and
  templates, stylesheet functions, attribute sets and global initializers take
  their element's IR module. Inline functions and xsl:iterate bodies keep
  module 0.
- **Duplicates** (D169's list): `sxml_allocator_allocate_array`
  (`src/memory_internal.h`) is the one array allocation helper; the XSLT copies
  use it, the others move when their files are next touched. The key equality
  of group-adjacent and group-starting-with stays: the FLWOR's keys_are_equal
  is in `src/xquery_flwor.c`, another packet's file at the time.
- **match="$var" membership: not done** (D169's accepted design stays open).
  The parts exist: the evaluation memo (D149) that keeps key indexes and cached
  calls, and a map from generate-id() to the node, built once by the
  cached-call row for a pattern rooted at a global variable, makes each test
  one lookup. The match expression is an XPath AST, so it needs a private
  function name it can call, or the match lowering must bind the index as a
  pattern variable; the rows live in `src/function_library_xslt.c`, another
  packet's file at the time.

**Sources**: XT40 passes, whole suite, after each change, case by case, and the
test sets priority, call-template, record, type-alias, snapshot and merge
(`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); the unit and CLI tests touched (`ctest`,
debug build).

### D187. The XQuery Update Facility 3.0 (packet 7.7a)

**Summary**: XQuery Update Facility 3.0 is parsed, checked statically and
applied: a `pending_update_list` is a sequence of function items, each changed
tree is rebuilt in one pass and handed to the host's `update_sink`.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D99, D137, D162, D183, D184. The owner chose XQUF
3.0 first (D184): packet 7.7a designs it and does the 3.0 expressions and their
application (the task file's 7.7a and 7.7b); 7.7b is now the 4.0 draft's
additions and 7.7c fn:put and revalidation.

- **Grammar** (`grammars/xquery`, D12): XQUF 3.0, Appendix A: the revalidation
  declaration, "declare updating" (the compatibility annotation, accepted
  before the other annotations), insert, delete, replace (value of), rename,
  copy-modify, transform-with (at the arrow level, under XQuery 4.0's pipeline)
  and "invoke updating". The 17 new keywords stay names. Every query and module
  of the upd-\* sets parses; the rest of XQ40 parses as before.
- **AST**: ten kinds, the fields modify and source, the keywords FIRST, LAST,
  INTO, AFTER, BEFORE, SKIP, the flag VALUE_OF.
- **Static rules** (XQUF 3.0, 2.2, 5.1 to 5.4) in `src/xquery_update.c`: one
  post-order walk over a module's AST by its links (no stack, D71) gives each
  expression a category, simple, updating or vacuous, and checks XUST0001,
  XUST0002 and XUST0028. %updating and %simple are accepted on functions and
  function items, XUST0032 on variables and XUST0033 twice: this replaces
  D162's place, the XQST0045 of `check_annotations` in `src/xquery_static.c`.
- **A pending update list is a sequence.** Each update primitive is a function
  item named upd:insertInto ... upd:rename whose body raises XUDY0038 when
  called; its captured values are the target, the parameter and the kind. So no
  item kind is added (xdm.h is frozen, D99), the evaluator keeps no update
  state, and merging the lists of the comma, FLWOR, conditional and function
  call expressions is concatenation (upd:mergeUpdates is a union); a try clause
  that fails loses its updates with its value. The static rules keep primitives
  where no XDM value is read.
- **Lowering** (the part `update`, `src/xquery_lower_update.c`): every update
  expression is a STATIC_CALL of an internal native row in no function table,
  as group by is (D137), which checks the operands (XUTY0004 to XUTY0013,
  XUDY0009, XUDY0023, XUDY0027, XUDY0029, XUDY0030, XUTY0022) and returns the
  primitives. replace value of takes its value through a TEXT_CONSTRUCTOR
  (5.4.3.2: "as in a text node constructor"). copy-modify is copy(E) per
  variable, the modify clause, then modify-copies, which applies the clause's
  list to the copies (XUDY0014) and rebinds the variables for the return
  clause.
- **Application** (`src/xquery_update_apply.c`, upd:applyUpdates): the
  compatibility checks (XUDY0015, XUDY0016, XUDY0017, XUDY0024), then each
  target tree is rebuilt through the tree builder in one pass over the old tree
  with every primitive of a node applied in the order of 3.2.2; tree.h does not
  change (D183). Changed elements and their ancestors become untyped; a
  duplicate attribute is XUDY0021.
- **The host** (`include/sxml/xquery.h`, additive): an updating query is a unit
  whose main function carries %updating; sxml_xquery_query_is_updating says so,
  and the evaluation request's update sink receives each changed tree (its old
  and new roots) after the snapshot. How a change is made persistent is the
  host's (upd:applyUpdates: implementation-defined).
- **QT4 driver**: XQUpdate is supported; the tests of a test case run in order,
  each updating one's changed trees replace the sources they came from, and the
  last test's result is checked.
- **Done in 7.7a** (amended at the end of the packet): besides the above,
  transform-with (a MAP whose body copies the item and lowers the modify clause
  with the copy as fixed focus), the prolog's construction and copy-namespaces
  modes for copies and for the nodes insert and replace copy in, upd:removeType
  (only the primitives that change a type touch their node and its ancestors,
  which become xs:anyType when typed), upd:propagateNamespace under no-inherit,
  XUDY0021 also inside removed subtrees, and `sxml xquery` writing the context
  document as an updating query left it (no flag; the file is not changed).
- **upd-\* (XQ40, release driver)**: before 0 of 825 run; after 733 passed (10
  of them with another error code), 24 failed, 0 errors, 68 not run: 27
  staticTyping, 40 revalidation lax and strict (XUST0026 until 7.7c), 1 that
  needs skip unsupported.
- **Left for 7.7b (the 4.0 draft)**: the updating return clause of copy-modify
  (id-transform-expr-014), XUDY0038 on a dynamic call of an updating function
  item (no test), the 4.0 draft's other additions. **For 7.7c**: fn:put (13
  cases) and revalidation lax and strict (40, with
  revalidate-valtrans-ins-003). **Not ours**: copies made with construction
  strip keep is-id and is-idrefs (sxml_tree_builder_copy_node, src/tree.c: "the
  ID properties stay"), so 11 cases that ask for schema IDs to go fail
  (setToUntyped, transform-expr-045 to -048); 6 propagateNamespace cases differ
  only in whitespace that assert-xml compares; valskip-repnode-006 revalidates
  a source with an IDREF.

### D188. disable-output-escaping: a text node mark (packet 7.5)

**Summary**: disable-output-escaping is a mark on text nodes
(`disables_output_escaping` in `tree.h`), set by xsl:value-of and xsl:text
outside temporary output state and honoured by the XML, XHTML and HTML output
methods.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D99, D163, D183, D184. The owner's prompt for 7.5
asked for a mark on text nodes as D163 added the CDATA request, in place of
D183's processing-instruction pair (glossary `disable_output_escaping` replaces
`output_escaping_marker`).

- **Substrate, additive** (`include/sxml/tree.h`, frozen by D99):
  `sxml_text_event.disables_output_escaping` and
  `sxml_node_description.disables_output_escaping`, false by default
  (designated initializers keep every caller as it was). Arena trees keep it in
  a node flag (the flags field is 16 bits, the node stays 56 bytes); copies
  (`sxml_tree_builder_copy_node`) keep it.
- **Per character** (XSLT 4.0, 26.1.8: "an additional boolean property
  disable-escaping associated with every character in a text node"): inside a
  parent, text events that differ in the mark make separate text nodes, so
  `<out>` with "<" then an unescaped "&lt;" serializes as `&lt;&lt;` (doe-0182
  to doe-0186). Such a final result tree has adjacent text nodes, a deviation
  from XDM 4.0, 6.7.1 limited to trees that use the deprecated feature;
  parentless text keeps one node.
- **Where it is set**: XSLT lowering of xsl:value-of and xsl:text with
  disable-output-escaping="yes" (construction flag DISABLES_OUTPUT_ESCAPING on
  TEXT_CONSTRUCTOR). The request is ignored in temporary output state (26.1.8),
  with 26.2.6's tracking of xsl:result-document: lexically inside xsl:variable
  and the other temporary containers the flag is not set; in a template that
  received the temporary-output-state tunnel parameter it is chosen at run time
  (`sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_received_output_state`, shared with
  xsl:result-document). Not covered: templates reached only through an initial
  function call (the writer's state), as for XTDE1480.
- **Where it is honoured**: the XML, XHTML and HTML methods write such text in
  the character context UNESCAPED_TEXT: mapped and normalized, not escaped,
  never in CDATA sections (26.1.8: CDATA "is treated as an alternative escaping
  mechanism"), a character the encoding cannot represent as a character
  reference. Canonical output escapes it; the text method has no escaping.
  Sequence normalization gives such a text node as a node, not merged, so it
  keeps the mark at the top level and in xsl:result-document's tree.
  Attributes, comments, processing instructions and namespaces atomize it and
  lose it.
- **Driver**: feature disabling_output_escaping is supported; the cases that
  need it unsatisfied are not run any more.

### D189. Optional features and the size budgets (packet 7.2)

**Summary**: An `optional_feature` is linked only into programs that name it in
`sxml_processor_configuration`, with large `feature_data` read through the
resolver; the JavaScript core and full modules get their size budgets.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D71, D138, D162, D183, D184. Carries out the owner's
size choice (D184): link-time optional features through one additive
`processor.h` view, one build, no `#if`, large data from the host through the
resolver.

- **Public** (`include/sxml/processor.h`, additive): `sxml_optional_feature` (a
  handle to a static const definition, opaque to hosts),
  `sxml_optional_feature_view` as the last field of
  `sxml_processor_configuration` (zero means none, so every existing
  configuration is unchanged; copied at initialize; a NULL definition is
  INVALID_ARGUMENT), `sxml_test_optional_feature()` (named "test", adds
  nothing), `sxml_all_optional_features()` (every feature, for hosts that want
  them all), `sxml_optional_feature_get_name()` and
  `sxml_processor_has_optional_feature()`.
- **Internal** (`src/optional_feature_internal.h`, `src/optional_feature.c`):

  - one `sxml_optional_feature_kind` per feature; a definition holds its kind,
    name, a `static const` operations table (`const void *`, cast by kind) and
    an optional `finalize_state`;
  - the processor keeps one slot per kind (definition, state):
    `sxml_processor_find_optional_feature(processor, kind)` gives the table or
    NULL. NULL is the D162 place's answer: the specification's behaviour
    without the feature stays where it is. No global state; a feature never
    calls another feature or back through its caller (D71);
  - `sxml_processor_set_optional_feature_state` keeps per-processor state
    (tables built from feature data), finalized with the processor.
- **Feature data** (glossary `feature_data`, D184's option 4):
  `sxml_optional_feature_read_data` asks the processor's resolver for an
  absolute URI as a resource kind whose form is BYTES, lends the bytes to a
  reader, and gives them back. It goes through the compile document loader
  (`sxml_processor_compile_document_loader_initialize`), so URI resolution and
  form checks are the existing ones. The packets with data add their resource
  kinds to `processor.h` (DUCET `allkeys.txt`, CLDR rule text, TZif), each with
  its record. The test feature reads `urn:sxml:test-feature-data` (TEXT) once
  and keeps its byte count.
- **Hosts**: the sxml command and the QT4, XSLT and XSD drivers name
  `sxml_all_optional_features()` (one line each). JavaScript: `sxml.wasm`
  (core) and `sxml-full.wasm` (every feature) are two links of the same shim,
  which differ only in `sxml_javascript_core_features.c` and
  `sxml_javascript_full_features.c`. `Sxml.features` lists the module's
  features; `createProcessor({ features })` picks some (default all; an unknown
  name throws). Up to 32 features (one mask word).
- **Budgets** (`bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt`): core 2,100,000 stripped /
  735,000 gzipped, full 3,000,000 / 1,050,000 (the owner's stripped budgets;
  the gzipped ones keep D138's 7:20 ratio). CLI unchanged (5,500,000 /
  1,250,000). `javascript/package_full` runs the package tests on the full
  module.
- **Sizes** at 2459034, before and after (stripped / gzipped): `sxml.wasm`
  2,003,575 / 697,928 to 2,004,485 / 698,244 (+910 bytes: the shim's feature
  exports 430, the slots and checks 350, export names); `sxml-full.wasm`
  2,005,513 / 698,677; the CLI 4,966,649 / 1,160,916 to 4,967,809 / 1,161,287.
  HEAD was already 3,575 bytes over the old 2,000,000 budget. The 910 bytes are
  the mechanism's fixed cost; no feature links into the core.
- **Existing parts not moved** (measured in `sxml.wasm` from the linker map,
  code and data): schema validation for fn:xsd-validator and friends 70,958;

- **Later packets** (7.8 to 7.18) each: add a kind before
  `SXML_OPTIONAL_FEATURE_KIND_COUNT`; define the definition, operations table

  `sxml_processor_find_optional_feature`; add a resource kind for any data and

**Sources**: sxml.wasm, sxml-full.wasm and the CLI, stripped and gzipped,
