### D190. XPath and XQuery conformance sweep (packet 2.21)

**Summary**: The sweep adds composite casts to arrays, maps and records, the
`caller_focus` for fn:function-lookup, paths over JNodes and implicit-timezone
equality in fn:distinct-values, with no public header changed.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D143, D158, D174, D113. Takes the "XPath and XQuery"
leftovers of `docs/agents/QUEUE.md`. No public header changed; no IR expression
kind added.

- **Composite casts** (glossary `composite_cast`; XPath 4.0, 4.19.2.4 to
  4.19.2.7): `cast as` and `castable as` an array, map or record type run the
  coercion frames with the cast rules
  (`sxml_coercion_request.applies_cast_rules`): an item that matches its item
  type stays; a generalized atomic, list or union type casts the atomized item
  with the static namespaces; arrays, maps and records rebuild their parts; a
  record cast makes a record with every field and drops other entries;
  duplicate keys are XQDY0137; anything else is XPTY0004. castable answers
  false for dynamic and type errors of the cast and of atomizing the operand
  (4.19.3). Lowering: XPST0080 for a choice that is not generalized atomic and
  for function or node types, XQST0052 in XQuery for a non-simple named type.
- **The caller's focus** (glossary `caller_focus`): a native row marked
  `SXML_NATIVE_FUNCTION_TAKES_CALLER_FOCUS` (only fn:function-lookup) gets the
  static call's context value, position and size as three extra arguments,
  dropped at run time when the context value is absent; its arities do not
  count them. fn:function-lookup binds a row that needs the focus:
  fn:position#0 and fn:last#0 return the captured part, a context-value default
  is the next arity partially applied (name kept). A dynamic call of
  fn:function-lookup passes no focus.
- **Paths over JNodes**: `SXML_IR_MAP_IS_AXIS_STEP` marks the item axis's MAP
  as navigational for the selector analysis (4.7.3); "/" is `fn:root(.) treat
  as (document-node() | jnode())` (4.7.1.1); XPTY0019 and XPTY0020 are XPTY0004
  (PR 2627); preceding:: of a JTree root is empty.
- **Contextual equality** of dates and times without timezone uses the implicit
  timezone in fn:distinct-values and fn:duplicate-values
  (`sxml_function_library_adjust_to_implicit_timezone`, shared with group by).
- **fn:doc's xsd-validation** validates the loaded document as fn:parse-xml
  does (D174); FODC0009 stays for fn:parse-xml-fragment.
- **QT4 driver**: assert-xml trims whitespace around inline expected XML that
  starts and ends with markup, as it did for files.
- **Measured** (release, full XP40 and XQ40 runs; before at 7d70d01): XP40
  30,931 to 31,098 passed, wrong error 85 to 44; XQ40 41,273 to 41,456, wrong
  error 123 to 70; none lost, 0 errors. XT40 at the same HEADs no set lost.
  sxml.wasm grew about 5.8 KB (inside D189's core budget).
- **Not done** (for later sweeps): (d) fn:serialize's canonical JSON cases call
  EXPath Binary's bin:unpack-double (27 cases, 7.8's module),
  serialize-xml-canonical-5 needs an external entity (7.14); (e) the built-in
  schema of the fn namespace (F&O 4.0, appendix D): an import of the namespace
  the resolver does not deliver could fall back to it as xml.xsd does in
  `src/schema_assemble.c`, but json-to-xml's validate, typed analyze-string
  results and their schema-element() tests also need it compiled once per
  processor and a validation against a given schema (about 25 cases); (f) the
  record model of the current draft (records annotated, record(\*) only for
  records, a record matching only with all its fields, lookups of other keys
  XPTY0004: cast-record-901, recordTypeDecl-019..021, -072, -089);
  NamedRecordTypeDecl's module cases name `recordTypeDecl/` where the suite has
  `RecordTypeDecl/` (a case-sensitive file system finds none); the item axis's
  JNode for a singleton is a child of a new array (D113); NCName and Q{}N name
  tests are one in sxml_name_test (frozen); a declared function's "$a := ."
  found by fn:function-lookup; lax validation without any in-scope schema
  raises FODC0014 (`src/function_library_schema.c`); use-xsi-schema-location.

**Sources**: XP40 and XQ40 passes and wrong errors, full runs, before at
7d70d01 and after (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build); XT40 at the same HEADs,
by test set (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); XT40 at the same HEADs, by
test set (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); growth of sxml.wasm (about 5.8
KB) (`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`, wasm build).

### D191. Optional features add library functions (packet 7.10a)

**Summary**: An optional feature's definition can carry `library_functions`,
which the processor's function library serves after the registered parts, so
the functions are absent (XPST0017) from programs that do not name the feature.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D45, D101, D162, D189. A feature whose D162 place is
"the functions are absent" (XPST0017: fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc, the EXPath
Binary and File functions) must not link its rows into a program that does not
name it, so its rows cannot be a library part of `src/function_library_*.c`
(the registry links every part).

- `sxml_optional_feature_definition` (src/optional_feature_internal.h) gains
  `library_functions`: a `const sxml_native_function_view *` of static const
  rows in the feature's own files, or NULL.
- The processor's function library serves every registered XPath part, then the
  `library_functions` of each configured feature in kind order
  (`sxml_processor_make_library_part_list` in src/processor.c). The list lives
  in allocator memory only while the library is initialized (the library does
  not keep it). XQuery and XSLT chain their own tables in front of the
  processor's, so they see the feature's functions too.
- Without the feature the functions are absent, as before: XPST0017 at compile
  time, false from fn:function-available, nothing from fn:function-lookup. A
  feature's file that holds rows names its view differently from
  `sxml_function_library_<part>`, so the CMake registry (cmake/SxmlParts.cmake)
  does not take it as a part.

### D195. XML 1.1 input (packet 7.13)

**Summary**: A document whose XML declaration says version 1.1 is parsed by XML
1.1's rules: a pre-pass refuses restricted characters and translates NEL and
LINE SEPARATOR line ends, while query texts stay XML 1.0.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D12, D81, D183, D184. Supersedes D81's "version 1.1
documents are parsed by the 1.0 rules".

- **Version**: read from the XML declaration of the decoded text before parsing
  (`sxml_xml_read_declared_version`, the pseudo-attribute reader that already
  finds the encoding name); `1.1` is XML 1.1, every other version, `1.x`
  included, and no declaration are XML 1.0 (XML 1.1, 4.3.4; XML 1.0, 2.8).
- **A pre-pass, not scanner state** (deviation from 7.13's mechanism): for a
  1.1 document the parser refuses a [2a] RestrictedChar written literally (XML
  1.1, [1] document) and translates NEL, CR NEL and LINE SEPARATOR after the
  declaration into LF in its copy of the text (2.11; CR LINE SEPARATOR stays
  two line ends). Translation must come before tokenizing, because NEL is
  whitespace in 1.1 markup (a NEL between attributes), which the grammar would
  otherwise have to know per version in every whitespace and text token. The
  grammar stays the 1.0 grammar for 7.14; NEL and LINE SEPARATOR in the
  declaration stay and are an ERROR, as 2.11 requires. Cost: a copy only for
  1.1 documents with such line ends; diagnostic positions after them are
  positions in the translated text (the byte offset can be off by one or two
  per translated character in UTF-8 input).
- **Characters and names**: character references may denote the C0 controls in
  1.1 (4.1, `sxml_xml_codepoint_is_version_1_1_char`); U+0000 never. Names need
  nothing: XML 1.0 Fifth Edition has 1.1's name characters. `xmlns:p=""`
  undeclares p in 1.1 (D81, unchanged).
- **Serialization**: version 1.1 already wrote the C0 and C1 controls as
  references and undeclare-prefixes (packets 3.3, 3.4); unchanged.
- **Drivers**: QT4 claims `xml-version 1.1` (sxml reads both versions); XT40
  supports `XML_1.1` and xml-version="1.1" sources, and keeps it among D95's
  non-goals so the gate rates keep their meaning; assert-xml with
  xml-version="1.1" writes the result with version 1.1 and parses both texts as
  1.1 documents (`tests/qt4/driver/assertion.c`, shared). XSD: the suite names
  no XML-1.1 test; the XmlVersions set's 1.1 documents now parse.
- **Query texts stay XML 1.0** (not this packet; Proposed below): XQuery's xgc:
  xml-version leaves the version of query lexing implementation-defined; sxml's
  is 1.0 (XQST0090 for `&#1;`, XQST0085 for `xmlns:p=""` in a direct
  constructor, no NEL line ends, version 1.0 as the default serialization
  version). QT4's 1.1 cases that need 1.1 query lexing fail honestly; the 1.0
  cases that need 1.0 lexing keep passing (the two sets conflict case by case).
- **Measured** (release drivers, before at 2459034 / after):

  - xmlconf XML 1.1 (`tests/xml_conformance_test.c` now selects the ibm and
    eduni xml-1.1 catalogs, eduni's NS 1.1 tests and the 1.1 erratum test,
    Fifth Edition rules for EDITION; 271 cases): 202 to 242 passed (valid
    84/84, invalid 13/13, not-wf 140/169, error 5). All 29 failures are not-wf
    cases whose fault lies in an external entity or DTD, which sxml does not

    selection is unchanged (601/175/948).
  - QT4 (the 15 test sets with xml-version dependencies): XQ40 2,497 to 2,798
    passed, XP40 1,944 to 2,235; fn-graphemes 918 to 1,189 in both. Of XQ40's
    313 1.1 cases 300 pass (95.8 %); the 13 that fail need 1.1 query lexing

  - XT40: xml-version 0 to 40 of 42, namespace 206 to 221, catalog 5 to 7,

    `src/xslt*`).
  - XSD saxon-XmlVersions 48 to 51 of 51.

### D196. xsl:evaluate (packet 7.3)

**Summary**: xsl:evaluate is a static call whose resumable body compiles the
target with `sxml_xpath_compile` and runs it as a `unit_evaluation` on the same
machine, with stylesheet functions passed as function items.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D71, D154, D162, D163, D183, D184. Replaces D162's
one place for dynamic evaluation (the XTDE3175 raise in
`src/xslt_lower_control.c`): xsl:evaluate is available, so XTDE3175 is never
raised and the xsl:fallback children are not evaluated.

- **One mechanism** (D183): the instruction is a STATIC_CALL of an internal row
  (`src/xslt_evaluate.c`) whose resumable body compiles the target expression
  with `sxml_xpath_compile` and asks the machine for a unit evaluation
  (EVALUATE_UNIT, D154), as fn:load-xquery-module does; the second step gives
  its value. A nested xsl:evaluate (in a stylesheet function the target calls)
  is one more unit evaluation on the same machine: no C recursion (D71).
- **Static context** (10.5.1), read lexically from the call's module (the
  xsl:evaluate element's, D163): its static namespaces (prefix 0 is its
  xpath-default-namespace), or the in-scope namespaces of the namespace-context
  node (XTTE3170 unless one node; xml and undeclarations dropped); base-uri
  resolved against the instruction's base URI; its collations, default
  collation and decimal formats; its in-scope schemas only with
  schema-aware="yes"; the parameters as external variables of type item()\*,
  xsl:with-param (lowered as for xsl:call-template) under with-params (XTTE3165
  unless one map with xs:QName keys). trusted="no", the default, makes the unit
  untrusted (`sxml_ir_unit_set_untrusted`, FODC0016 for resources).
  schema-aware and trusted: XTSE0020 for a fixed non-boolean word, XTDE0030 for
  a computed one.
- **Functions** (10.5.1): the F&O library, then the stylesheet functions whose
  visibility is public or final, then fn:current (XSLT 4.0 allows it: the
  current item is the target's context item); no other XSLT-defined function.
  The stylesheet functions belong to the stylesheet's unit, so the lowering
  passes them as function items (a map from name to the references of its
  arities, bound through the instruction's function table), and the target's
  function table binds them with a new function entry kind, FUNCTION_ITEM
  (`src/function_library_internal.h`): a call lowers to a DYNAMIC_CALL of the
  item as a constant, a named reference to the item. Keyword arguments to them
  are not supported (the entry has no parameter names).
- **Dynamic context** (10.5.2): the context-item value is the context item; an
  empty one, or none, is no context (XPDY0002, as evaluate-025 expects); more
  than one item is XTTE3210, XSLT 3.0's rule, which evaluate-026 and
  error-3210a expect (a deviation from the 4.0 draft, which makes the value the
  context value). Dynamic errors keep their codes; a static error of the target
  is XTDE3160 with the static error's description.
- **Counts** (release driver, whole XT40 against 9856281, case by case): 8,899
  to 8,973 passed, 0 errors, no case lost; evaluate 73 of 83 (9 of them with
  another error code), 91 % of the 80 run, 88 % of the 83; error-3175a and
  system-property-014b need the feature absent and are not run any more. The 90
  % gate of 7.3 is not met yet: 3 cases wait for html-doc and parse-html
  (7.10), 2 for trust checks in json-doc and unparsed-text-available, 1 needs a
  UCA collation strength (7.15), 1 (evaluate-008a) expects XPST0017 for a call
  use-when removes.
- **Not done**: keyword arguments to stylesheet functions; json-doc and
  unparsed-text-available do not check trust yet (evaluate-454/455,
  `src/function_library_resource.c` was another packet's file); html-doc and
  parse-html wait for 7.10.

**Sources**: XT40 passes, whole suite, case by case, against 9856281; the
evaluate cases (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build).

### D197. XSLT backwards compatible behaviour and XPath 1.0 compatibility mode (packet 7.4)

**Summary**: `xpath_1_compatibility_mode` is one static context flag that makes
the lowering insert XPath 1.0 conversions, set for XSLT elements whose
effective version is below 2.0, with no second evaluator.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D97, D162, D183, D184. Replaces D162's place for
XSLT 1.0 behaviour (`asks_xslt_1_behaviour` and its XTDE0160 in
`src/xslt_lower.c`).

- **One flag, no second evaluator**: XPath 1.0 compatibility mode is
  `has_xpath_1_compatibility_mode` of the XPath static context
  (`src/xpath_static_internal.h`) and, additively, the last field of
  `sxml_static_context_configuration` (`xpath.h`; XPath hosts only, XQuery has
  no such mode and ignores it). The lowering reads it and inserts the 1.0
  conversions as STATIC_CALLs of internal native rows in no function table
  (`src/xpath_compatibility.c`, golden file `src/xslt_simple_content.c`); the
  evaluator does not know the mode.

  - Arguments of static calls to built-in functions (XPath 4.0, 3.4.1): the
    first item; then fn:string for xs:string and xs:string?, fn:number for
    xs:double and xs:double? (the optional forms keep ()); fn:concat takes
    xs:string($v[1]) per argument (F&O 4.0). Not for partial applications,
    dynamic calls, stylesheet functions (XSLT 4.0, 10.3.2) or the lowering's
    own calls.
  - Arithmetic and unary operands (4.9): atomized, the first item, () as NaN,
    xs:boolean, xs:string, xs:decimal, xs:float and xs:untypedAtomic by
    fn:number. The operands of "to" keep their first items (4.8.2 coerces
    them).
  - General comparisons (4.11.2): one row does the mode's rules: the xs:boolean
    rule (EBV of the other operand), fn:number of every item for <, <=, >, >=;
    for = and != a pair with a numeric item compares as doubles, other pairs by
    the mode-false rules. It calls the existing
    `sxml_operator_make_general_comparison` on the converted parts.
- **XSLT**: the static context of every element whose effective version is
  below 2.0 has the mode (5.3.1, 3.8.1; 2.0 and 3.0 behaviour is 4.0's). The
  1.0 rules of the instructions, each where the instruction is lowered, through
  `sxml_xslt_lowering_has_xslt_1_behaviour` and
  `sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_first_atom` (fn:head(fn:data(.))): xsl:value-of with
  select and no separator (11.4.2), attribute value templates (5.6.1; not text
  value templates), xsl:number value (12.2: first item, () as NaN, an
  unconvertible value formatted as "NaN" between the format's prefix and
  suffix), xsl:sort keys (13.1.2, first item after data-type), keys in
  backwards compatible mode (20.2.2: use values and fn:key's argument cast to
  xs:string), and an unknown extension function bound to a fallback error
  function, XTDE1425 when called (3.8.1, 24.1.2; function-available stays
  false). supports-backwards-compatibility is yes.
- **xs:numeric is not xs:double** (XPath 4.0, 3.4.1 names xs:double only; F&O
  4.0's changes list says strings are no longer accepted where the type became
  xs:numeric): fn:format-number, fn:round, fn:floor and fn:abs do not convert
  strings or () by fn:number in the mode. The suites expect the older
  conversion: XT40 format-number 014, 035, 038-041, backwards-022, version-021,
  xpath-compat-0302 and 0401, and QT4 numberformat15, 38, 41, 42 fail. Not
  reclassified (D178).
- **Not done**: the expressions of a text value template in a 1.0 element are
  still lowered with the mode (3.8.1 asks for it off; only expand-text="yes" on
  a 1.0 element meets it); the default output method xml for a 1.0 stylesheet
  is also used for an explicit xsl:result-document (backwards-019b);
  exsl:node-set, which DocBook's 1.0 stylesheets call (docbook-001 raises
  XTDE1425; it needs a function namespace sxml_well_known_namespace lacks);
  docbook-002 meets an XPST0003 in an included module.
- **Drivers**: XT40 supports backwards_compatibility and keeps it among D95's
  non-goals, as XML_1.1 (D195); QT4 supports xpath-1.0-compatibility for XPath
  only and sets the mode for the test cases that ask for it (assertions stay
  mode false), also kept out of the denominator. The three XT40 cases that
  expect XTDE0160 (and three more asking for the feature unsatisfied) are not
  run now.
- **Numbers** (release, XT40 whole, case by case): 8,687 to 8,787 passed at
  3dc364a; 111 of the 124 cases (89.5 %, gate 80 %); QT4
  xpath-1.0-compatibility 1 of 5 (generate-id-018; the other four are the
  xs:numeric cases above). Unit test `tests/xslt_compatibility_test.c`.

**Sources**: XT40 passes, whole suite, case by case, and the
backwards-compatibility cases (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build, at 3dc364a);
QT4 xpath-1.0-compatibility cases (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build).

### D198. EXPath Binary (packet 7.8)

**Summary**: The EXPath Binary Module 4.0 is the optional feature
"expath-binary": 33 functions as its `library_functions`, a new well-known bin
namespace, and fn:unparsed-text's decoder moved to `src/text_decoding.c`.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D51, D99, D162, D163, D189, D191. The EXPath Binary
Module 4.0 is the optional feature `sxml_expath_binary_feature()`
("expath-binary").

- **Public, additive**: `include/sxml/processor.h` declares the feature
  function. `include/sxml/name.h` (frozen by D99) gains the well-known
  namespace `SXML_NAMESPACE_EXPATH_BINARY` = 13 (http://expath.org/ns/binary),
  so rows name their namespace as the fn, map and math rows do.
  `SXML_NAMESPACE_WELL_KNOWN_COUNT` is now 14: interned URIs start one later,
  which no caller sees.
- **Rows**: 33 functions in `src/function_library_binary.c`, whose view is not
  named as a part, so they are the definition's `library_functions` (D191). The
  kind's operations table is that same view. Every binary parameter is
  `(xs:hexBinary | xs:base64Binary)`; results are xs:base64Binary (1.2). The
  4.0 types are kept: `xs:unsignedByte` for octets and the `enum(...)` octet
  order, so bad values are XPTY0004 as 4.0 says (appendix F), where the QT4
  cases still expect bin:octet-out-of-range and bin:unknown-significance-order
  (26 wrong error codes, which count as passes).
- **Errors** are in the bin namespace, prefix bin, filled into the error record
  directly (static text, D21).
- **Text**: the decoder of fn:unparsed-text moves to `src/text_decoding.c`
  (`sxml_text_decoding_choose`, `sxml_text_decode`). Its encoding choice was
  already written after bin:infer-encoding, so bin:infer-encoding and
  bin:decode-string use it unchanged. bin:encode-string encodes UTF-8, UTF-16
  (big-endian, no mark), UTF-16BE/LE, ISO-8859-1 and US-ASCII. Encoding names
  are classified by `sxml_xml_classify_encoding_name`.
- **Integers** beyond int64_t are packed and unpacked through their decimal
  text on base 10^9 limbs. bin:integer-too-large is raised past 4,096 octets
  (9,865 digits, inside the heap's decimal limit).
- **System property**: the value kind DYNAMIC_XQUERY becomes KNOWN_FUNCTION,
  with a function name and arity in the row. supports-dynamic-xquery asks for
  fn:load-xquery-module#1 and supports-binary-library for bin:hex#1, so the
  property follows the configuration.
- **Hosts**: the feature is in `sxml_all_optional_features()`, so the sxml
  command, the drivers and `sxml-full.wasm` have it, and `sxml.wasm` does not.
  The QT4 driver supports the dependency feature binary, and bin-\* is no
  longer a non-goal set.
- **Counts** (release driver, XP40 and XQ40 alike): bin-\* 0 to 646 of 646, of
  which 26 have the wrong error code; fn-serialize 200 to 224 (XP40) and 258 to
  282 (XQ40), the canonical-JSON cases that call bin:unpack-double;
  fn-system-properties 23 to 23 (the -false case is now not run, the true case
  passes).

**Sources**: XP40 and XQ40 bin-\*, fn-serialize and fn-system-properties
passes, before and after (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build); configured: the
most octets of an unpacked integer, 4,096 (from
`src/function_library_binary.c`).

### D199. DTD processing: external subset, external entities, validation (packets 7.14a, 7.14b)

**Summary**: The XML parser reads the external subset, external parameter
entities and external parsed entities through a per-parse entity resolver in
`xml.h`, expanding parameter-entity references in a loop with explicit stacks.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D12, D28, D44, D71, D81, D165, D183, D184, D195.
Replaces D81's "the external subset is not read" and "external parsed entities
are skipped in content".

- **Header, additive** (`include/sxml/xml.h`): an entity resolver
  (`sxml_xml_entity_resolver`: resolve and release over
  `sxml_xml_external_entity_request` → `sxml_xml_external_entity`), named per
  parse in `sxml_xml_parse_request.entity_resolver`. The null resolver (a
  zeroed request) reads nothing outside the input, as before. The request
  carries the purpose (external subset, parameter entity, general entity),
  name, system and public identifiers and the system identifier resolved
  against the base URI of the entity holding the declaration (4.2.2). `xml.h`
  cannot name `processor.h`'s resource resolver (processor.h includes xml.h),
  so the parser has its own small interface and the processor adapts its
  resolver to it.
- **Grammar** (D12, `grammars/xml`): the start rule also reads the external
  subset and external parsed entities, each after a marker the builder writes
  (U+0001 and a letter: no [2] Char, so a document never takes these
  alternatives, and the builder refuses one without a root). New:
  `external_subset` ([30], [31]), `external_parsed_entity` ([78]),
  `text_declaration` ([77]), `include_section` ([62]), `conditional_section`
  ([63], or a parameter-entity keyword), `ignored_section_contents` ([64],
  [65], scanner token `ignored_text`), entity values with parameter-entity
  references in external DTD text. The internal subset stays strict (WFC: PEs
  in Internal Subset in the grammar).
- **What the grammar cannot express is a loop with explicit stacks** (D71), as
  the task allowed: a declaration with a parameter-entity reference outside its
  literals matches its production only after expansion, so the scanner returns
  it as one `unexpanded_declaration` token; the builder replaces the references
  (4.4.8, one space on each side, the replacement texts' own references too,
  with quote state and an explicit stack of open entities in the parser's
  expansion array) and parses the result again as the external subset in a
  frame of its own. The same loop includes a reference in an entity value in
  the literal (4.4.5: character and parameter-entity references recognized
  again, general ones kept). A conditional section whose keyword is a reference
  is read as ignored text by the grammar; the builder reads keyword, '[' and
  contents from the replacement text and the rest of the section (the '[' may
  come from the entity, a validity matter only) and parses an included section
  again. A missing '>' that comes from an entity (Proper Declaration/PE
  Nesting) ends the token at the next markup.
- **Reading**: the external subset after the internal subset (2.8), through a
  parameter entity named "[dtd]" (no Name, so unreachable); external parameter
  entities where referenced; external parsed entities in content (parsed after
  the entity marker, the tree cached per parse as an internal entity's is,
  frames of a new kind whose walk root is the entity). Each external entity is
  asked once per parse, decoded as a document is (Appendix F; its text
  declaration must agree with the bytes), its byte order mark dropped, U+0000
  refused, line ends normalized in the copy (2.11); a 1.1 document's entities
  follow 1.1 (restricted characters, NEL), and an entity of a 1.0 document must
  not declare 1.1 (XML 1.1, 4.3.4). An entity the resolver does not deliver is
  not read (4.4.3, 5.1: later entity and attribute-list declarations are
  skipped as for an unread parameter entity). Every external text counts
  against `maximum_entity_expansion_byte_count` at each inclusion.
- **WFC: Entity Declared** where it applies (no DTD, internal subset without
  references, standalone="yes") also refuses an entity declared in the external
  subset or in a parameter entity (4.1).
- **Measured** (`tests/xml_conformance_test.c`, now parsing every case with a
  file resolver; the 1.0 selection with ENTITIES other than "none" is a third
  group): standalone 1.0 unchanged 601/175/948; external 1.0 0 run before, now
  valid 127/127, invalid 54/54 (well-formed), not-wf 66/66, error 18; XML 1.1
  not-wf 140/169 to 169/169 (D195's 29). The remaining parts (the processor's
  resource kind, trust-external, the drivers, the CLI, DTD validation) follow
  in this record.
- **Validation (7.14b) is schema validation** (no second content-model engine):
  `src/dtd.c` writes the DTD as XSD documents, one per namespace (names resolve
  through the root element's xmlns attributes and the DTD's xmlns defaults;
  content models become model groups, attribute types simple types: ID,
  IDREF(S), ENTITY(IES), NMTOKEN(S), NOTATION, enumerations; an element
  referred to but not declared gets a type that refuses it).
  `src/schema_from_dtd.c` compiles them and runs a schema validator without a
  result tree; the parser sends its events to it as well (a tee). The
  constraints about declarations themselves (Root Element Type, Standalone
  Document Declaration, the PE nesting ones, Unique Element Type Declaration,
  Unique Notation Name, One ID per Element Type, ID Attribute Default, Notation
  Declared, No Duplicate Types and Tokens, Entity Declared, Fixed Attribute
  Default) the parser checks and reports through the hook, code xml-validity.
  **Public, additive**: `xml.h`'s `sxml_xml_validator` hook
  (`sxml_xml_parse_request.validator`); `schema.h`'s `sxml_dtd_validator`
  (memory_requirements, initialize, finalize, create, destroy,
  as_xml_validator, get_outcome); `processor.h`'s resource kind
  `SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_EXTERNAL_ENTITY` (form BYTES) and
  `sxml_processor_entity_resolver`, which adapts the processor's resource
  resolver for a parse.
- **Tree**: element content whitespace (a declared element-only content model)
  makes no text node (XDM 4.0, 7.5.7.3); unparsed entities keep absolute system
  identifiers, so fn:unparsed-entity-uri and fn:unparsed-entity-public-id work
  (replaces D81's "unparsed entities are not reported").
- **fn:doc and fn:parse-xml** (F&O 4.0, 17.1.1 and 17.2.1): the loader parses
  with an entity resolver over the evaluation's resource resolver.
  trust-external defaults to false, so a document that refers to an external
  DTD or entity raises FODC0016 (the 4.0 incompatibility the specification
  names); dtd-validation=true validates and raises FODC0007 (also for a
  document without a DTD, 2.8). FODC0013 stays for XInclude. XSLT's fn:document
  and stylesheet modules read external entities through the resolver. The CLI
  parses its input files with the null resolver, so it never reads an external
  entity (D44); a query reads one only through trust-external=true.
- **Measured**: DTD validation of xmlconf: standalone valid 594 of 594 valid,
  invalid 173 of 173 invalid; external valid 127 of 127, invalid 54 of 54. XT40
  8,861 to 8,931 passed (release, whole suite, none lost); dtd cases 68 of 79
  (86 %, under the 90 % gate): base-uri-051/051a/051b need an element base URI
  from the entity (tree.h; Proposed), unparsed-entity-05 to 08 need unparsed
  entities kept by xsl:copy-of (Proposed), error-1370a, 1380a and 1380b raise
  the wrong code without a focus, id-043 needs a parse-xml source in the
  driver. QT4 (release): fn-doc XQ40 69 to 73, XP40 63 to 67; fn-parse-xml XQ40
  46 to 53, XP40 35 to 42; none lost. Left for the QT4 driver (its files were
  others' work in progress): claiming infoset-dtd and dtd-validation-option,
  environment sources read with the entity resolver, and
  supports-dtd-validation true in `src/system_property.c` with the feature
  claim. Fuzzing: `tests/fuzz/dtd_fuzz.c`, 20 minutes, clean after one fix.

**Sources**: xmlconf standalone, external and XML 1.1 cases, with a file
resolver (`ctest`, from `tests/xml_conformance_test.c`); DTD validation of
xmlconf, standalone and external valid and invalid cases; XT40 passes, whole
suite, before and after; the dtd cases (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build);
QT4 fn-doc and fn-parse-xml, XQ40 and XP40, before and after
(`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build); DTD fuzzing, 20 minutes
(`tests/fuzz/dtd_fuzz.c`).

### D200. EXPath File (packet 7.9)

**Summary**: The EXPath File Module 4.0 is the optional feature "expath-file"
over a host `sxml_file_system` interface, opted into twice: hosts name the
feature and give a file system, and `sxml_all_optional_features()` leaves it
out.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D71, D99, D162, D184, D189, D191, D198. The EXPath
File Module 4.0 is the optional feature `sxml_expath_file_feature()`
("expath-file") over a host interface, the file system.

- **Public, additive**: `include/sxml/processor.h` gains the file system
  (`sxml_file_system`: an operations table with the directory, path and line
  separators and ten operations, describe, read, write, list, create_directory,
  remove, move, create_temporary, get_directory and canonicalize, each over
  request structs) and the configuration field `file_system`, next to the
  resolver and the clock. `name.h` (frozen by D99) gains
  `SXML_NAMESPACE_EXPATH_FILE` = 14 (http://expath.org/ns/file);
  `SXML_NAMESPACE_WELL_KNOWN_COUNT` is 15.
- **Opt-in twice** (D184): the host names the feature and gives a file system.
  `sxml_all_optional_features()` leaves the feature out, so naming every
  feature never grants file access. Without the feature the functions are
  absent (XPST0017); with it and the null file system, every function that
  needs files raises file:io-error.
- **Rows**: 37 functions in `src/function_library_file.c`, the definition's
  `library_functions` (D191). Paths are made absolute against CURRENT and
  normalized lexically in the library, so the host sees only absolute paths;
  directory paths end with the separator. Text goes through
  `src/text_decoding.c` (decoding moved there by D198; the encoder of
  bin:encode-string moves there too). Errors are in the file namespace, filled
  into the error record (static text). file:move onto an existing directory
  moves into it, overwriting a file of the same name, as file:copy does.
- **No recursion** (D71): copy, delete, size and list of a directory walk it
  with a work list; file:descendants is a resumable body that asks the
  evaluator to call its filter and recurse predicates.
- **System property**: supports-file-library is a KNOWN_FUNCTION row (D198) for
  file:exists#1.
- **CLI**: `apps/sxml/platform_file_system.c` implements the interface over
  POSIX (realpath is a copy under WASI). `sxml xpath` and `sxml xquery` name
  the feature and pass the file system only with `--allow-file-access`; they
  bind the prefixes bin and file always. Windows is not implemented:
  initialization reports SXML_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, and the CLI runs
  without files.
- **QT4 driver**: names the feature for a test case with a sandpit or the
  dependency feature expath-file. A sandpit is copied through the host file
  system to a fresh temporary root (root/sandpit is CURRENT, root/temp is
  TEMPORARY), served by a wrapping file system, and deleted after the case.
  expath-file is no longer a non-goal feature, nor expath-\* a non-goal set,
  and sandpits are no longer unsupported.

### D201. HTML5 parsing: a hand-written tokenizer, tree construction on a working tree (packet 7.10a)

**Summary**: fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc are the optional feature "html": a
hand-written HTML tokenizer and tree construction on an `html_working_tree`,
not tree-sitter, then mapped to XDM.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D12, D53, D71, D162, D183, D184, D189, D191.
fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc (F&O 4.0, 17.3) as the optional feature
`sxml_html_parser_feature()` (name "html"), after the HTML Living Standard of
16 October 2026, 13.2.

- **Not tree-sitter** (an exception to D12, for the reasons of D53): (1) the
  tokenizer is a state machine that tree construction switches (RCDATA,
  RAWTEXT, script data and PLAINTEXT after a start tag, CDATA sections only
  when the adjusted current node is foreign), so lexing depends on parse state
  a context-free grammar does not see; (2) HTML has no syntax errors: every
  input parses, by error recovery the standard defines exactly, whereas D12
  makes any `ERROR` node a static error and tree-sitter's own recovery is not
  the standard's; (3) tree construction moves nodes already built (adoption
  agency, foster parenting), so a walk over a concrete syntax tree would be a
  second tree builder, not a replacement for one; (4) the input is run-time
  data (`parse-html($computed)`), and tree-sitter allocates with `malloc`
  outside every allocator and limit, which D12 accepts only for source text.
- **Files**: `src/html_tokenizer.c` (the 84 states of 13.2.5 as one loop over a
  state variable; tree construction pulls tokens, characters come in runs);
  `src/html_tree_construction.c` (the 21 insertion modes and the rules for
  foreign content as a dispatch loop of steps, so "process the token using the
  rules for" is no call cycle, D71); `src/html.c` (the walk that sends the
  working tree to an arena tree, the XDM mapping, the feature);
  `src/html_encoding.c` and the generated `src/html_encoding_tables.c`
  (`tools/generate-html-encodings.py`); `src/function_library_html.c` (the two
  rows, D191's library functions, not a registered part);
  `src/html_internal.h`.
- **Working tree** (glossary `html_working_tree`): node, attribute and
  text-segment tables in allocator memory; a text node is a chain of segments
  so that later characters join it; the walk to the tree builder follows parent
  links (no stack needed). The named character references are fn:char's table
  (`src/unicode_tables.c`) plus the 106 names that also match without ";": no
  second entity table.
- **The standard as of now**: processing instructions (13.2.5.72 to .76:
  `<?target data?>` is a PI, `<?xml ...?>` a comment), no "in select" insertion
  modes, `search` special, `select` a scope boundary. F&O 4.0's note that the
  HTML parser makes no PIs predates that change.
- **Not done, by the standard's own switches**: scripting is Disabled
  (`noscript` content is parsed; 13.2.4.5), no fragment case, no declarative
  shadow roots, no sanitizer, no content patching (template `for`);
  `selectedcontent` is filled by DOM steps of the select element, not by the
  parser, so it stays empty.
- **XDM mapping** (F&O 4.0, 17.3.1; HTML, 13.2.9): XHTML, SVG and MathML
  namespaces; SVG and MathML names in their case; xlink: and xml: attributes in
  their namespaces; xmlns attributes dropped; names XML does not allow escaped
  as "U" and six hex digits; comments get a space inside "--" and after a final
  "-"; U+000C becomes a space and other characters XML does not allow U+FFFD;
  an `id` that is an NCName is an ID; a template's contents are its children.
  Base URI: the static base URI (fn:parse-html), the resource's URI
  (fn:html-doc, also its document URI).
- **Input** (13.2.3): a string is UTF-8 with a known encoding, a leading U+FEFF
  stripped (F&O 4.0); octets: byte order mark, then the encoding option (every
  label of the Encoding Standard; its 28 single-byte encodings, UTF-8, UTF-16
  and x-user-defined decode, a multi-byte or unknown label is FODC0011), then
  step 9's autodetection: well-formed UTF-8, else windows-1252 (step 10). No
  `<meta>` prescan yet (7.10b).
- **fail-on-error**: parsing stops at the first parse error (13.2.2 allows it),
  a decoding error included: FODC0011. Unknown options and html-version, method
  or include-template-content are XPTY0004.
- **Counts** (release driver): fn-parse-html 0 to 22 of 22 (XQ40 and XP40),
  fn-html-doc 0 to 9 of 10 (html-doc-010 expects FODC0011 for `<a:tag>`, which
  no rule of 13.2 makes a parse error), misc-HtmlTestSuite 0 to 1,378 of 1,379
  (XQ40; html-test-1281 expects jsoup's comment for `<?processing data?>`),
  misc-BuiltInKeywords +2 (the result type `document-node(*:html)?`). The sets
  are no non-goals of the QT4 driver any more. Outside the suite, the html5lib
  tests of web-platform-tests run in a scratch harness: tree construction 1,747
  of 1,753 (`#script-on` and fragment cases left out; the others are
  `selectedcontent` and harness limits), tokenizer 7,022 of 7,049 (the rest
  harness limits and F&O's U+FEFF rule).
- **Sizes** (stripped / gzipped): `sxml.wasm` 2,078,210 / 722,803 before and
  after (no HTML code links into the core); `sxml-full.wasm` 2,103,528 /
  733,247 to 2,182,635 / 762,413 (+79,107; budget 3,000,000); the `sxml` CLI
  module 5,848,173 / 1,239,159 to 5,927,297 / 1,267,818. The CLI module was
  over its 5,500,000-byte budget already (Proposed below).
- **Tested**: `tests/html_test.c` (tokens, trees, the input stream, both
  functions with and without the feature, allocation-failure loops),
  `tests/fuzz/html_parse_fuzz.c` (11,000 runs seeded from the suite, no
  finding), two `sxml xpath` end-to-end tests.
- **Left for 7.10b**: the `<meta>` prescan of 13.2.3.2 (step 5) and 13.2.3.4
  (changing the encoding while parsing) for octets; vendoring the html5lib .dat
  and tokenizer tests (web-platform-tests `html/syntax/parsing/resources`,
  html5lib-tests `tokenizer`) as a unit test with the scratch harness's format;
  the multi-byte decoders (Shift_JIS, EUC-JP, ISO-2022-JP, GBK, gb18030, Big5,
  EUC-KR) or a decision that they stay FODC0011; source locations for
  dm:location; XHTML (the XML syntax) recognition, which F&O 4.0 asks for with
  "should"; the CLI's relative URIs in `sxml xpath` and `sxml xquery` (no
  static base URI, so fn:html-doc and fn:unparsed-text of a relative name fail
  there); html-doc-010 and html-test-1281 stay failing unless the suite
  changes.

**Sources**: QT4 fn-parse-html, fn-html-doc, misc-HtmlTestSuite and
misc-BuiltInKeywords, before and after (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build);
html5lib tree construction and tokenizer tests of web-platform-tests, in a
scratch harness; sxml.wasm, sxml-full.wasm and the sxml CLI module, stripped
and gzipped, before and after (`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`);
configured: sxml-full.wasm budget 3,000,000 and the CLI module budget 5,500,000

### D203. fn:transform (packet 7.11)

**Summary**: fn:transform is the optional feature "xslt-transform", whose
resumable body compiles the stylesheet, primes the transformation and asks the
machine for a `unit_evaluation`, with no evaluator nested in C.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D71, D154, D157, D183, D189, D191, D196, D207.
Replaces D162's place for fn:transform (the function was absent, XPST0017;
supports-dynamic-xslt false).

- **Optional feature**: `sxml_xslt_transform_feature()` ("xslt-transform",
  declared in `include/sxml/xslt.h` as the packet's option 2), whose
  library_functions hold the one row (D191); in `sxml_all_optional_features()`.
  A host that names no XSLT and not the feature links no XSLT; `sxml-full.wasm`
  links it (D207).
- **One mechanism** (D183): the row's resumable body
  (`src/xslt_transform_function.c`, golden file `src/xquery_load_module.c`)
  reads the 33 options of F&O 4.0, 18.3 (the option limit of the option
  conventions is 40 now), compiles the stylesheet with `xslt.h`'s compiler,
  primes the transformation and asks the machine for EVALUATE_UNIT; the next
  step delivers the principal result and collects the result documents (the
  built-in collector) into the result map; one step per result runs
  post-process. `src/xslt.c` splits `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_transform` into
  prime, describe, run and deliver, so a machine transformation
  (`src/xslt_transform_internal.h`) is the same priming with the evaluation
  left to the machine. No evaluator runs nested in C (D71); compiling evaluates
  static expressions on an evaluator of their own, where fn:transform has no
  evaluation environment and raises FOXT0004, so the compiler is not
  re-entered.
- **Extension per unit evaluation**: `sxml_evaluation_request.extension` is
  kept in the unit's global table (a unit evaluation that gives none, such as
  xsl:evaluate's, inherits the asking code's);
  `sxml_dynamic_context_get_unit_extension` gives the running code's. The
  result writer is found there first, so xsl:result-document and
  current-output-uri of the inner transformation reach its own writer;
  xsl:message honours enable-messages false. The body drops the extension
  before it releases the transformation, so function items that outlive it
  (transform-003) see none.
- **Options**: exactly one of stylesheet-location/-node/-text,
  package-location/-node/-text and package-name (FOXT0002); a node is
  serialized and compiled as text with its base URI (or stylesheet-base-uri); a
  location is read as fn:doc reads it (the caller's trust and documents;
  FOXT0002 when it cannot be read); a package name is a RESOLVED_PACKAGE. The
  invocation is the first of initial-function (with function-params),
  initial-template, a source (source-node, source-location,
  initial-match-selection; at most one), else xsl:initial-template;
  initial-mode with a call is FOXT0002, xsl:unnamed selects the unnamed mode.
  The global context item is global-context-item, else the root of source-node,
  else the source-location document. Parameter maps need xs:QName keys
  (XPTY0004). delivery-format document is TREE, absent is DEFAULT (build-tree),
  raw, serialized (UTF-8, no byte order mark, as fn:serialize), file FOXT0004,
  others FOXT0002. serialization-params override the unnamed xsl:output, the
  list parameters joined. xslt-version above 4.0 and requested-properties that
  the XSLT system property table does not give (xsl:version ignored) are
  FOXT0001. trusted false (the default) makes the unit untrusted. A stylesheet
  that is not well-formed is FOXT0003; static and type errors keep their codes
  as dynamic errors.
- **Result map**: "output" or the base output URI, resolved, for the principal
  result (left out when it is empty beside result documents, unless a result
  document became it, 26.2.2); each result document by its absolute URI.
- **Drivers**: QT4 supports fn-transform-XSLT and fn-transform-XSLT30 (a 4.0
  processor serves 3.0) and serves XSLT_MODULE as suite files; fn-transform is
  no non-goal set any more.
- **Counts** (release drivers): QT4 fn-transform XQ40 0 to 129 of the 133 run
  (137, 4 not run), XP40 126 of 130; gate 80 % met. XT40 8,861 to 8,870 passed,
  none lost, 0 errors; transform 0 to 9 of 12 (transform-009 now reaches an
  assertion the driver does not check).
- **Size**: `sxml.wasm` 2,119,912 to 2,120,239 (+327, the extension lookups);
  `sxml-full.wasm` 2,224,369 to 3,554,353 (+1,329,984, XSLT).
- **Not done**: fn:transform in a static expression (transform-004: static
  evaluation has no evaluation environment); enable-assertions false
  (assertions stay enabled, fn-transform-91); a separate execution scope (cache
  false still shares current-dateTime, fn-transform-27); the inner
  transformation shares the caller's document loader (fn:doc is not stripped as
  its xsl:strip-space asks), available documents and trace sink, and
  fn:function-lookup sees the caller's table; xslt-version 2.0 behaviour (82e);
  the QT4 driver gives a query file no base URI of its own (fn-transform-94);
  ~record patterns (transform-401, XSLT).

**Sources**: QT4 fn-transform, XQ40 and XP40, before and after
(`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build); XT40 passes, whole suite, before and
after; the transform cases (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); sxml.wasm and
sxml-full.wasm stripped, before and after
(`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`).

### D205. fn:put, revalidation, untyped copies and the 4.0 return clause (packets 7.7b, 7.7c)

**Summary**: The XQuery Update Facility is completed with fn:put through the
host's update sink, lax and strict revalidation, untyped copies that drop is-id
and is-idrefs, and the 4.0 draft's updating return clause.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D99, D165, D173, D184, D187. The rest of the XQuery
Update Facility after 7.7a: fn:put and revalidation (7.7c), the 4.0 draft's
updating return clause (7.7b), and copies that drop schema identity.

- **fn:put** (XQUF 3.0, 6.1; `src/xquery_update.c`): a row of XQuery's function
  table (`src/xquery_load_module.c`, beside fn:load-xquery-module),
  `fn:put($node, $uri, $params := ())`, whose call the static rules treat as
  updating (XUST0001 as for any update). Its value is one update primitive
  `upd:put`, the node as target and the URI as parameter: FOUP0001 for a node
  that is not a document or element (6.1 leaves other kinds
  implementation-defined), FOUP0002 for a $uri with a character no URI or IRI
  reference has or that does not resolve against the static base URI to an
  absolute URI. Application checks XUDY0031 (two puts, one URI) and XUDY0037 (a
  put in a copy-modify's modify clause) and changes no tree.
- **The host** (`include/sxml/xquery.h`, additive): the update sink gets
  `receive_put_document`, called after every changed tree (3.2.2: upd:put last)
  with `sxml_xquery_put_document` (the absolute URI, the node as the other
  updates left it, the $params). The library never writes it (D184); NULL makes
  a query that calls fn:put fail with FOUP0002 before any tree is handed over.
  The node of a put on the root of a changed tree is the new root; a put on a
  node inside a changed tree gets the node as it was (node identity across a
  rebuild is not kept, D187).
- **Revalidation** (3.1, 3.2.4 upd:revalidate): XUST0026 is gone; lax and
  strict are supported. Each rebuilt tree that a type-changing primitive marked
  (upd:removeType reaches its root) is validated as "validate lax|strict { $top
  }" does, with sxml_schema_validate_node (D173) and the in-scope schemas (the
  schema declaring the root element; for lax the first without one; XQDY0061,
  XQDY0084, XQDY0027), and its validated copy is the updated tree. The mode is
  the main module's for the query and the module's for copy-modify
  (modify-copies takes it as a third argument). sxml's initial revalidation
  mode stays skip: the static context table of 3.1 lets an implementation
  overwrite lax.
- **Copies** (5.6 step 1.2; XQuery 3.1, 3.9.1.3): a copy-modify copy is untyped
  whatever the construction mode, and copies made untyped drop is-id and
  is-idrefs except for xml:id attributes. `tree.h` (frozen, D99) gets one
  additive field, `sxml_copy_request.strips_identity`; false, the old
  behaviour, is what XSLT needs (validation="strip" and
  input-type-annotations="strip" keep is-id, copy-5034 and
  strip-type-annotations-021). The update application sets it for its copies.
  XQuery's own node constructors under construction strip still keep is-id
  (`src/evaluator_construct.c` has no language flag): left.
- **The updating return clause** (XQUF 4.0 draft, copy modify): a copy-modify
  whose return clause is updating is updating, its pending update list the
  return clause's; 3.0's XUST0001 there is gone.
- **QT4 driver**: revalidation lax and strict are supported; what fn:put stores
  is serialized, parsed again and added to the test case's available documents
  at its URI (no file is written), and assertions see the available documents.
- **Left**: XUDY0038 for a simple dynamic call of an updating function item (no
  QT4 test; the one place is the evaluator's dynamic call); two cases where
  validating an element root checks IDREFs against its IDs (cvc-id.1) and the
  tests expect no such check (removeType-valskip-repnode-006,
  revalidate-valtrans-ins-002); six propagateNamespace cases whose expected XML
  has other whitespace than their queries make under boundary-space preserve
  (the suite's error: assert-xml compares canonical forms, kept strict); 27
  staticTyping.

### D206. XSLT 1.0 follow-ups: EXSLT common, text value templates, result documents (packet 7.4b)

**Summary**: XSLT 1.0 follow-ups add exsl:node-set and exsl:object-type, read
exsl:document as xsl:result-document, and lower text value templates in 1.0
elements without XPath 1.0 compatibility mode.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D197 and D99. Follows up D197's "Not done".

- **name.h (frozen, additive, D99)**: `SXML_NAMESPACE_EXSLT_COMMON = 15` for
  http://exslt.org/common, `SXML_NAMESPACE_WELL_KNOWN_COUNT` 16. Needed because
  a function row names its namespace by a well-known constant
  (`sxml_native_function.function_namespace`); the list only grows and no value
  changes.
- **EXSLT common**: `src/function_library_exslt.c`, an XSLT-only library part
  (as `output`, D149) with exsl:node-set (returns its argument: a temporary
  tree is already a document node in XSLT 2.0 and later) and exsl:object-type
  ("string", "number", "boolean", "node-set" for nodes and the empty sequence,
  "external" otherwise). function-available reports them. No other EXSLT
  module: DocBook tests the others (dyn:evaluate, set:leading, date:date-time,
  str:\*) with function-available first, and no XT40 case needs them.
- **exsl:document** in an extension namespace (24.2) is read as
  xsl:result-document (`src/xslt_read.c`): its attributes are a subset of
  xsl:result-document's (26.2), all attribute value templates; an unprefixed
  version attribute reads as the standard attribute, as on any XSLT element.
  element-available('exsl:document') is true. DocBook's chunker writes its
  secondary files through it (docbook-001 raised XTMM9000 "Can't make chunks"
  without it). Outside an extension namespace it stays a literal result
  element.
- **docbook-002's XPST0003** was fo/autoidx.xsl's xsl:key: its use attribute
  names entities of the external parameter entity common/entities.ent, which
  the module reader did not retrieve, so the expression lost its first
  argument. 7.14 (D199, 7a0c96a) now reads a module's external entities through
  the resolver; nothing else was needed.
- **Text value templates** in an element with XSLT 1.0 behaviour are lowered
  without XPath 1.0 compatibility mode (XSLT 4.0, 3.8.1): the value template
  frame lowers its expressions in a copy of the element's static context with
  the mode off.
- **xsl:result-document** whose result is the principal result (no href)
  chooses its default method as an explicit result document: xhtml for an XHTML
  html element, also in a 1.0 stylesheet (XSLT 4.0, 26.1).
- **Numbers** (release, XT40 whole suite, case by case, against 46cc929): 8,940
  to 8,943 passed: docbook-001, docbook-002, backwards-019b; no other case
  changed. Unit tests in `tests/xslt_compatibility_test.c`.
- **Size** (wasm preset, MinSizeRel objects): `src/xpath_compatibility.c` is
  6,024 bytes of code and 1,133 of data before linking, all in `sxml.wasm`,
  because the XPath lowering calls it; the EXSLT part is 961 bytes of code and
  285 of data, also linked into the core through the part registry. At 01a3993
  `sxml.wasm` is 2,294,051 bytes stripped (801,300 gzipped), over its 2,200,000
  / 770,000 budget; these two files are about 8.4 KB of that.

**Sources**: XT40 passes, whole suite, case by case, against 46cc929
(`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); code and data of
src/xpath_compatibility.c and the EXSLT part, MinSizeRel objects before linking
(wasm build); sxml.wasm stripped and gzipped
(`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`, at 01a3993); configured: the
sxml.wasm budget, 2,200,000 / 770,000 (from
`bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt`).

### D209. The timezone database (packet 7.16)

**Summary**: The optional feature "timezone-database" reads one TZif file per
zone from the host's resolver at first use, serving fn:civil-timezone and the
formatting functions' $place, with tzdata vendored for tests.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D97, D162, D183, D184, D189, D191, D208. Replaces
D97's "no tz database" and the FODT0004 place of D162 in fn:civil-timezone.

- **Data from the host, TZif**: the optional feature
  `sxml_timezone_database_feature()` ("timezone-database", `src/timezone.c`,
  `src/timezone_internal.h`) reads zones as the host has them: one TZif file
  per zone (RFC 8536, versions 1 to 4), asked of the resolver as the new
  `SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_TIMEZONE_DATA` (additive in `processor.h`) under
  `urn:sxml:timezone-data:` + a zoneinfo path (a zone name, or `zone1970.tab`,
  else `zone.tab`, for country codes). No compact form and no generator: TZif
  is the standard format, every Unix host has it in `/usr/share/zoneinfo`, and
  one reader serves both hosts and the vendored data. sxml checks a name before
  it asks (ASCII letters, digits, `_ - +`, parts between single `/`), so a
  resolver can map the path onto a directory. A zone is read at its first use
  and kept in the processor's feature state; a zone that is not delivered is
  asked again next time (no negative cache, so a query cannot grow the state
  with names that do not exist).
- **Vendored**: tzdata 2026e under `third_party/tzdata` (D13): the sources, and
  `zoneinfo/` compiled by `zic -b slim` with the zone tables, 599 files, 237
  KB; `tools/update-tzdata.sh` moves it. The QT4 driver serves it
  (`../tzdata/zoneinfo/` from the catalog), the unit tests read it from the
  source tree; the sxml command serves the host's `/usr/share/zoneinfo`;
  JavaScript hosts answer the kind `'timezone-data'`. Nothing is compiled into
  sxml.
- **Lookup** (RFC 8536, 3.2): type 0 before the first transition, the last
  transition's type, the footer's TZ string (POSIX XBD 8.3 with RFC 8536's
  167-hour and negative times) from the last transition on. Leap second records
  are skipped (xs:dateTime has no leap seconds). Years beyond ±10^9 get no
  answer.
- **fn:civil-timezone** (F&O 4.0, 9.7.4): no place is the implicit timezone,
  the UTC names stay PT0S without the database; any other place is a zone name,
  looked up at $value's instant ($value without a timezone takes the implicit
  timezone); FODT0004 without the feature, for an unknown zone, or a year out
  of range. A country code is not a zone here (the rules say "IANA timezone
  name").
- **$place of the formatting functions** (9.9.4.8): a zone name adjusts a value
  with a timezone to the zone's offset at its instant and gives [ZN] its
  abbreviation; a time alone takes the zone's standard time ("only possible
  where the value includes a date"). A country code (two ASCII letters, any
  case) does not adjust; [ZN] names the first zone of the country, in
  zone1970.tab's order, with the value's offset at that instant (2018-07-01 at
  -05:00 in "us" is America/Chicago's CDT). An abbreviation that does not start
  with a letter ("-03") is no name, and an offset with seconds (local mean
  time) is no xs:dateTime timezone: the fallback format 01:01 is kept, as for
  an unknown place and no place (format-time-030).
- **Numbers** (release drivers, against 97aedba): fn-civil-timezone 4 to 9 of 9
  (XP40 and XQ40); with the dependency olson-timezone turned on,
  fn-format-dateTime XQ40 83 to 93 of 94 run (not run 9 to 1), XP40 80 to 88
  (not run 14 to 6): all 8 olson-timezone cases and 025c/025e; fn-format-time
  XQ40 96 to 97 (025c); app-spec-examples XQ40 1,479 to 1,480 and XP40 1,346 to
  1,347 (fo-test-fn-civil-timezone-003); fn-format-date and
  misc-BuiltInKeywords unchanged; XT40 format-date and format-date-en
  unchanged. The packet's gate (all 14 cases) is met.
- **Size** (wasm preset): `sxml-full.wasm` 3,564,851 to 3,575,555 bytes
  (+10,704; gzipped 1,085,933 to 1,090,270), within its 4,000,000 budget;
  `sxml.wasm` 2,294,067 to 2,295,933 (+1,866: the two D162 places and the value
  adjustment, which ask for the feature), already over its 2,200,000 budget
  before (D206); the CLI module 6,510,188 to 6,521,732. No budget changes.
- **Not done**: the dynamic context has no default place (a host setting would
  be an additive header change); without one, no place keeps the implicit
  timezone and [ZN] the fallback format.

**Sources**: QT4 fn-civil-timezone, fn-format-dateTime, fn-format-time,
app-spec-examples and the unchanged sets, XQ40 and XP40, and XT40 format-date,
against 97aedba (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build);
sxml-full.wasm, sxml.wasm and the CLI module, before and after
(`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`, wasm build); vendored tzdata 2026e
zoneinfo: file count and size (from `third_party/tzdata/zoneinfo`).

### D210. DTD follow-ups: unparsed entities on copies, entity base URIs, sxml check with the DTD, the drivers (packet 7.14c)

**Summary**: Copies keep a document's unparsed entities, elements from external
parsed entities carry an `entity_base_uri` for dm:base-uri, and `sxml check`
gains `--external-entities` and `--validate-dtd`.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D44, D99, D178, D199. Resolves the three Proposed
items of 7.14: the base URI of an element from an external entity, unparsed
entities kept by copies, and `sxml check` with the DTD.

- **Substrate, additive** (`include/sxml/tree.h`, frozen by D99; every zero
  value keeps the behaviour before):

  - `sxml_tree_operations.get_unparsed_entity(state, entity_number, entity)`,
    optional: the unparsed entities in the order of their declarations,
    SXML_STATUS_INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE past the last;
  - `sxml_tree_builder_copy_unparsed_entities(builder, tree)`: sends them right
    after start_document. `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node` calls it for a document
    node, and so does SHALLOW_COPY of a document node that is not copied into
    enclosing content (`src/evaluator_construct.c`): XSLT 4.0, 11.9.1
    (xsl:copy) and 11.9.2 (xsl:copy-of) copy the unparsed-entities property,
    and fn:copy-of and fn:snapshot copy as xsl:copy-of does. Temporary trees,
    xsl:document and the XQuery document constructor still have none (XSLT 4.0
    sets the property to empty);
  - `sxml_element_start_event.entity_base_uri` and the optional
    `sxml_tree_operations.get_entity_base_uri(state, element, base_uri)`: the
    entity base URI (glossary `entity_base_uri`) of an element at the top of an
    external parsed entity. The XML parser sets it from the entity's frame (an
    element one deeper than the document's element depth when the frame was
    pushed); the arena tree keeps it in a short list; dm:base-uri stops its
    walk of xml:base attributes at the first element that has one and resolves
    against it instead of the tree's base URI (XML 1.0, 4.2.2; XML Base, 4.2;
    XDM 4.0, dm:base-uri).
- **Copies do not carry entity base URIs**: XSLT 4.0, 11.9.2 gives a copied
  descendant its new parent's base URI ("these differences are lost when the
  subtree is copied"). Copies that stand for the same document
  (xsl:strip-space, validating a parsed document) lose them too; left as it is.
- **XTDE1370 and XTDE1380**: each function now raises its own code (XSLT 4.0,
  20.5.2, 20.5.3; error-1380b). Without a focus both raise XPDY0002, as the two
  sections say for an omitted $doc; error-1370a and 1380a expect the XSLT 2.0
  codes and stay wrong-error passes (D178).
- **`sxml check --external-entities` and `--validate-dtd`** (D44: one intent
  per flag, nothing fetched that was not asked for). The first reads the
  external subset and external entities as local files, through the query
  commands' local-file resolver and `sxml_processor_entity_resolver`, relative
  to the file that declares them. The second validates with
  `sxml_dtd_validator` and reads nothing by itself. Its null report sink stops
  at the first error of each file, reported as `FILE:LINE:COLUMN: CODE:
  message`; the JSON statuses are `valid` and `invalid`, the latter with
  `code`. Golden file `apps/sxml/command_validate.c`; CLI tests
  `check_external_*` and `check_validate_dtd*` over `tests/cli/input/dtd/`.
- **Drivers**: XT40 serves a source given only by a select expression,
  evaluated without a focus (id-043). QT4 claims infoset-dtd and
  dtd-validation-option and parses environment sources with the entity resolver
  (external DTDs are suite files). supports-dtd-validation and
  supports-dtd-attribute-typing are true (F&O 4.0, 17.1.9: fn:doc and
  fn:parse-xml raise an error for an invalid document, and the tree has is-id
  and is-idrefs from the DTD).
- **Measured** (release drivers): XT40 8,944 to 8,952 passed, none lost (163
  wrong-error, 0 errors); dtd cases 68 to 76 of 79 (96 %, gate 90 % met). The 3
  left: base-uri-051a (fn:doc without trust-external raises FODC0016, as F&O
  4.0 asks), error-1370a and 1380a (wrong error, above). QT4 XQ40 fn-id 47 to
  61 of 61, fn-idref 34 to 51 of 54 (the 3 need schema-typed IDREFs),
  fn-system-properties 22 to 23, app-FunctxFunctx 626 to 627; XP40 fn-id 17 to
  30, fn-idref 10 to 24, fn-system-properties 22 to 23; fn-doc and fn-parse-xml
  unchanged (XQ40 73 and 53, XP40 67 and 42). XQ40 whole suite 44,835 to 45,000
  passed (with 7.11's driver claims, c857ce3), failures 336 to 336.
  supports-dtd-validation and supports-dtd-attribute-typing are true regardless
  of the optional feature dtd-validation (D211); they should follow it, which
  needs the feature in reach of fn:system-properties. xmlconf unchanged (D199's
  counts).
- **clang-tidy**: `src/processor.c`'s multi-level pointer conversion is an
  explicit cast now.

**Sources**: XT40 passes, whole suite, and the dtd cases, before and after
(`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); QT4 fn-id, fn-idref,
fn-system-properties, app-FunctxFunctx, fn-doc and fn-parse-xml, XQ40 and XP40,
before and after (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build); XQ40 whole suite passes
and failures, before and after, with 7.11 driver claims (c857ce3)
(`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build).

dtd-validation option raises FODC0013.

### D212. XSLT streamability analysis (packet 7.6a)

**Summary**: `src/xslt_streamability.c` runs XSLT 4.0 chapter 19's
streamability analysis over the stylesheet AST after lowering, raising XTSE3430
only for constructs proven not guaranteed-streamable, while evaluation stays
unstreamed.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D97, D162, D166, D183, D184. Replaces D97's
"streamable="yes" runs unstreamed" by the analysis of XSLT 4.0, chapter 19
(whose rules are XSLT 3.0's chapter 19); evaluation stays unstreamed until
7.6b.

- **Where**: `src/xslt_streamability.c`, called once from sxml_xslt_compile
  after lowering, over the sealed stylesheet AST and the XPath ASTs of its
  expressions, patterns and value templates (the same trees lowering reads; no
  tree of its own). Not over the IR: chapter 19 classifies by syntax
  production, and lowering rewrites paths, `//` and value templates. A frame
  machine with explicit stacks in allocator memory, no recursion (D71); a
  construct needing more than 100,000 frames is uncertain.
- **What**: each construct's posture, sweep and U-type (glossary `posture`,
  `sweep`, `u_type`): the general rules (19.8.1) with operand usages, choice
  operand groups and higher-order operands; every instruction of 19.8.4;
  stylesheet functions by category with streaming parameters (19.8.5);
  attribute sets (19.8.6); value templates (19.8.7); the XPath expressions of
  19.8.8 (paths with scanning expressions, axis steps with rule 4, filters,
  unions, for and quantified expressions, maps, lookups, dynamic calls, inline
  functions and named references); the table of 19.8.9 and its special
  functions (accumulator-after and -before, current, current-group, last, root,
  outermost, the higher-order functions refined by an inline function's
  signature); motionless patterns (19.8.10). Verdicts: template rules of
  streamable modes, by import precedence of xsl:mode (6.6.4);
  xsl:source-document (18.1); functions with a category; attribute sets
  (10.2.3); accumulators, their values type-adjusted by the declared type and
  capturing rules (4.0, 19.9) grounded (18.2.9); merge sources (15.4). The
  first not guaranteed-streamable is XTSE3430 at the construct (19.10).
- **Uncertain**: where sxml has no rule (an extension function, a function the
  19.8.9 table does not list, keyword arguments, a dynamic call without a
  visible signature, a binding sxml cannot trace, XPath 4.0 constructs chapter
  19 does not know), the assessment is uncertain unless the operand is
  grounded, and an uncertain verdict is never an error: sxml rejects nothing on
  a guess (19.10 lets a processor stream more than the rules guarantee).
- **Beyond the letter of chapter 19, as the XT40 cases expect**: E//T is
  E/descendant::T when T's predicates are plainly non-positional; "." is a
  pattern step (./descendant::a/b scans); xsl:copy select is assessed as
  xsl:for-each over the selection (19.8.4.12 would make the content
  higher-order); xsl:fork with at most one consuming prong takes the general
  rules (one prong may return streamed nodes); current-group() of a grounded
  population is grounded and motionless anywhere, and of a group around a
  streamed xsl:source-document grounded inside it; intersect and except with a
  motionless right operand keep the left operand's posture; one for or some
  binding over streamed nodes is S ! R with the variable as "."; a reference to
  the streaming parameter inside a higher-order operand is free-ranging
  (19.8.4.30, note); an instruction with XSLT 1.0 behaviour is roaming; xsl:map
  with duplicates (4.0) takes the general rules; group-starting-with and
  group-ending-with must be motionless patterns.
- **Driver**: the XSLT driver claims the feature streaming and no longer
  streaming-fallback, which needs an option sxml does not have (Proposed); the
  feature and the strm group stay outside the D95 denominator.
  system-property-013 (streaming satisfied="false") is therefore not
  applicable.
- **Measured** (release driver, whole XT40, ed905be and 8a8fd58): passed 8,952
  to 11,792. The 2,936 cases that need the feature streaming, not run before,
  2,841 passed (2,681 with the feature claimed and no analysis, at f12ac89);
  154 of the 156 that expect XTSE3430 pass; the strm group 2,503 of 2,564 (97.6
  %). Every other case as before (system-property-013 now not applicable: 8,952
  to 8,951).
- **Not done, left to 7.6b**: streamed evaluation itself (the receiving task
  fed by the parser, D166); the two XTSE3430 cases the analysis misses
  (sf-filter-001, marked _WRONG in the suite; si-fork-953, sorted groups in
  xsl:fork, which 19.8.4.19 allows); supports-streaming; the fallback option.
  7.6b can read the verdicts: a guaranteed-streamable mode or source document
  is what it may stream, and the postures name what each construct selects.

**Sources**: XT40 passes, whole suite, before at ed905be and after at 8a8fd58;
the streaming and strm cases (`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); XT40
streaming cases with the feature claimed and no analysis (`tools/run-xslt.sh`,
release build, at f12ac89); configured: the frame limit of the analysis,
100,000 (from `src/xslt_streamability.c`).

### D213. Full UCA collations over the host's DUCET (packet 7.15a)

**Summary**: The optional feature "uca-collation" reads the host's DUCET
`allkeys.txt` once per processor for full UCA collations, and comparisons and
sort keys without a collation now use the default collation.

Recorded 2026-10-19, after D97, D116, D162, D183, D184, D189, D191, D208.
Replaces D97's UCA fallback as the behaviour of a UCA collation URI when the
host serves the DUCET; the fallback stays for hosts that do not.

- **Public** (`include/sxml/processor.h`, additive): the optional feature
  `sxml_uca_collation_feature()` ("uca-collation", in
  `sxml_all_optional_features`) and the resource kind
  `SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_COLLATION_DATA` (form BYTES): the feature asks for
  "http://www.unicode.org/Public/UCA/16.0.0/allkeys.txt" once per processor, at
  the first UCA collation, and keeps the table (also "no data") in its slot.
  Nothing is compiled into the core (D184, D189): `sxml.wasm` gains only the
  resolution path (below).
- **Internal**: `src/collation_uca.c` reads allkeys.txt (UTS #10, 9.1) in two
  passes into sorted arrays (elements, single-codepoint entries, contractions)
  and computes implicit weights (10.1, with the file's @implicitweights and
  Unicode 16.0's Unified_Ideograph). The elements of a string: NFD with
  canonical ordering, the longest contiguous match, discontiguous contractions
  (S2.1.1 to S2.1.3), variable weighting (shifted, blanked; maxVariable groups
  from the general categories of the characters a primary starts), caseFirst
  and caseLevel from the tertiary weights of UTS #10's tertiary table (upper:
  08 to 0C, 0E, 11, 12, 1D), numeric=yes (UTS #35, 3.7: a digit run weighs as
  its count of significant digits, then its digits, in the 255 weights after
  digit zero's primary, primaries being shifted left 8 bits), the identical
  level over NFD (7.4). normalization=yes|no both normalize (the same result
  for every FCD string). `src/collation.c` keeps one element array for every
  collation (keys, comparison and matching are shared);
  `sxml_collation_resolve` is the one place a UCA URI becomes the feature's
  collation (D162's place: without the feature or data, the fallback, and
  fallback=no is not supported).
- **fallback=no**: supported only with the table and when every parameter is
  honoured: lang empty, root, und, en or en-XX (CLDR has no tailoring for
  these; others are 7.15b), no reorder (7.15b), version equal to the table's
  @version, known keywords and values. Otherwise FOCH0002 dynamically and
  XQST0038 for `declare default collation` (now checked with the processor).
  `sxml_collation_is_supported` (xpath.h) has no processor and still says false
  for fallback=no.
- **Default collation in comparisons**: value and general comparisons of
  strings and the sort keys of order by and xsl:sort without a collation now
  use the static context's default collation (XPath 4.0, 4.11.1 and 4.11.2;
  XQuery 4.0, order by), through the one resolver; before, they used the
  codepoint collation whatever the default was, which the 4 XQST0038 "wrong
  error" passes had hidden.
- **Hosts**: the QT4 driver serves the vendored copy
  (`third_party/unicode-collation/`, D13, D208) and claims
  advanced-uca-fallback and non_unicode_codepoint_collation (no longer
  non-goals); the sxml command embeds allkeys.txt without comments (generated
  at build time by `apps/sxml/embed-collation-data.cmake`) and serves it; the
  JavaScript package forwards 'collation-data' to the host's resolver and
  otherwise serves `LoadOptions.collationData`, default the allkeys.txt it
  ships next to the modules (false: none). The XSLT driver names the feature
  but serves no data yet (fallback).
- **Tests**: `tests/collation_uca_test.c` sorts a sample of Unicode's
  CollationTest (every 20th line of the _SHORT files, NON_IGNORABLE 10,314
  lines and SHIFTED 11,391, both in order; the full _SHORT files, 206,286 and
  227,801 lines, also pass, not vendored), the parameters, matching, malformed
  data and an allocation-failure loop.
- **Measured** (release drivers, the sets that use collations): QT4
  advanced-uca-fallback 49 of 49 pass (XQ40 and XP40), not run before;
  non_unicode_codepoint_collation 13 of 13 (XQ40), 5 of 5 applicable (XP40).
  XQ40 passes 3,896 to 3,961 over fn-compare, fn-contains, fn-starts-with,
  fn-ends-with, the four fn-substring sets, fn-collation-key, fn-deep-equal,
  prod-GroupByClause, prod-DefaultCollationDecl (12 of 12, no longer 4 of them
  by a wrong error), app-spec-examples and the other collation sets; XP40 3,301
  to 3,358; no case that passed fails. XT40 collations 35 to 39 of 43 (the
  default collation in comparisons and sorts), sort, merge, for-each-group,

- **Sizes** (stripped / gzipped, at 8a8fd58 and with the feature): `sxml.wasm`
