budgets as necessary), because halfway solutions already exist."

  libraries and the JavaScript package contain every language (XPath, XQuery,
  XSLT, XSD) and every optional feature. There is one WebAssembly module for

    full module's budget 8,000,000 / 2,800,000, not raised; the D225 baseline

### D273. XSLT conformance sweep: streamed availability, fn:document's options, the driver's tree delivery (packet 4.26)

**Summary**: fn:stream-available reads only a document head, fn:document takes
fn:doc's options map, globals may refer to themselves, and the XSLT driver
delivers the principal result as a tree.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D234, D245, D252, D260, D262. Verified as D181 asks:
the debug preset (the xslt*, xslt_driver, function_library*, json, xpath,
evaluator_stream and cli tests), clang-tidy on the changed files, the
call-cycle check, the book examples (D257), QT4 XP40/XQ40 sets of the changed
functions, and the whole XT40 suite with the release driver after each change,
case by case. **XT40 12,191 to 12,209 passed (118 wrong error), 327 to 309
failed, 0 errors**, run at 5a855ca plus 2.24's commits (D262's 12,187 was
before them). Commits 4e0ffdb, 3d97421, 564d293, e1188ef, 9024849, 2ff5431,
67f7ad2.

- **fn:stream-available** (18.2) opens the document as xsl:source-document
  streamable="yes" does and reads only its head
  (`sxml_evaluator_stream_check_available`, src/evaluator_stream.c, the

### D274. XSLT conformance sweep: CDATA requests, key details, strip-space "none", XTTE0950 (packet 4.27)

**Summary**: Text that asks for CDATA sections becomes its own text node in
final result trees, and the sweep adds static XTSE0020 checks, keys over
namespace nodes, strip-space "none" and XTTE0950.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D188, D245, D260, D262, D273. Verified as D181 asks:
the debug preset (arena_tree, serialize*, xslt*, xslt_key, xslt_number,
xslt_output, xslt_read, xslt_schema, xslt_value_template, evaluator_construct,
function_library*, processor, json, xquery, cli tests), clang-tidy on the
changed files, the call-cycle check, the book examples (D257), the QT4 sets of
the changed functions and serializer (XP40/XQ40: fn-serialize,
method-xml/-xhtml/-html, fn-transform, fn-doc, fn-doc-available, fn-parse-xml,
fn-collection, the construction sets), and the whole XT40 suite with the
release driver after each change, case by case. \**XT40 12,210 to 12,226 passed
(115 to 107 wrong error), 308 to 292 failed, 0 errors, no case lost\*\* (D273's
12,209 became 12,210 with 2.24's commits); at 92a8a8c, with 2.25's commits
9973519 and 5f79679, 12,239 passed and 279 failed. Commits 1018850, 2f14d94,
e0dadcc, a7086d6, c427878, 150a638, 0c0f1e9, c1436f8, 92a8a8c.

- **CDATA requests** (11.4.3, implementation-defined; D188's approach): inside
  a parent, text that differs in asking for CDATA sections is a text node of
  its own (src/arena_tree.c; the streamed serializer flushes alike unless the
  parent is in cdata-section-elements); the serializer leaves a CDATA section
  open so adjacent text nodes' sections join, and any other output or the final
  flush closes it (a "]]>" across them is still split). The XSLT lowering asks
  for CDATA only in final output state, as for disable-output-escaping (one
  mark_choice_of for both), so temporary trees keep XDM's single text node: the
  deviation from XDM 4.0, 6.7.1 stays limited to final result trees, as D188's
  is. text-012, -019, -020, value-of-012.
- **Static XTSE0020** (5.6.1: only a value written with curly brackets escapes
  the static check): a fixed start-at that is no list of integers (12.1;
  number-0109, error-1001a); static="yes" below the top level (9.2, 9.6;
  static-025); an ItemType attribute with an occurrence indicator
  (context-item-901). One sxml_xslt_lowering_read_fixed_text replaces three
  private copies.
- **Other codes**: XTSE1220 for keys of one name with different collations,
  XTSE1222 only for composite (collations-0125, error-1210b, -1220a); XTSE0620
  for a static variable with select and content (use-when-0431); XTSE3022
  before XTSE3010 (expose-914).
- **Keys over namespace nodes** (6.3, 20.2.1; key-087, -090): a key whose
  pattern has a namespace-node() test or a namespace-axis step also visits
  $root/descendant-or-self::*/namespace::*; other keys are unchanged.
- **strip-space "none"** (F&O 4.0, 17.1.1; XSLT 4.0, 20.1; document-4031,
  -4031-doc): the document request's skips_preparation
  (src/evaluator_internal.h) makes the loader read the document without the
  stylesheet's xsl:strip-space and not keep it (a new tree per call, as "all"
  makes a new stripped copy). Without a preparation (XPath, XQuery) nothing
  changes. **Left**: an available document is given as configured, which in
  XSLT is its stripped copy.
- **XTTE0950** (11.9.1.1, 11.9.2; error-0950a, -0950b, copy-of-009): XQuery's
  XQTY0086 check (sxml_construction_check_copy) applies to XSLT's copies with
  validation="preserve" too, with XSLT's code; an element SHALLOW_COPY copies
  with new content is recorded so its own attributes are copied with their
  parent. fn:copy-of now preserves type annotations, as its definition
  (validation="preserve", 20.6.1) says (validation-1203 passes too).
- **Smaller**: value template fixed parts accept XML 1.1 Char, which the XML
  parser has already checked (xml-version-007); name attributes read XPath
  4.0's Q{uri}prefix:local (PR 2272; variable-0124, function-0123).
- **The draft decides, left** (D245): key-070 (4.0 compares keys by deep-equal,
  NaN matches NaN; the suite has 3.0's eq); error-0150b, -0150c, -0150e (4.0
  simplified stylesheets need no xsl:version, so XTSE0150 is gone; an included
  catalog's text value templates give XPST0003); iterate-006 (XTSE3120 covers
  xsl:next-iteration outside xsl:iterate); maps-910 and iterate-024 hold a
  second error the reader meets first (XTSE0010, XTSE0090).
- **Left, with causes**: xsl:next-match in an attribute set (next-match- 012,
  attribute-set-0108: attribute sets are lowered outside a template body, and
  the evaluator's current rule is not cleared where the lowering clears it
  lexically); per-package xsl:strip-space for fn:document (document-2401);
  fragment identifiers in xsl:source-document (docbook-003, -004); the suite's

- The XT40 section of `docs/CONFORMANCE.md` was not regenerated (a later packet

**Sources**: XT40 passes, whole suite, case by case, after each change

changed functions and serializer (`tools/run-qt4.sh`).

### D275. XPath and XQuery conformance sweep: "//" paths, place static contexts, XML 1.1 query text (packet 2.25)

**Summary**: Absolute "//" paths map only their first step over the
descendants, comparisons use the default collation of their module, library
modules keep their static context, and `reads_query_text_as_xml_1_1` adds XML
1.1 query text.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D163, D195, D237, D259, D263, D272. One public
header changed additively (processor.h, below); one IR field
(sxml_ir_binary.module_number) and one IR global flag
(sxml_ir_global_variable.is_external).

- **Start** (release drivers, whole runs at 87686bc): XP40 32,793 passed (30
  wrong-error), 40 failed; XQ40 46,070 (49), 138 failed; XT40 12,207, 311
  failed. Most XQ40 failures are D263's kept groups (whitespace-only
  assert-xml, among them fn-analyze-string's and the six upd-propagateNamespace
  cases; recordTypeDecl/ paths; EXPath Binary's types; staticTyping).
- **"//E1/E2"** (XPath 4.0, 4.6.3; the orchestrator's priority, found by 4.26):
  an absolute "//" path lowered its whole relative path as one MAP body per
  descendant, so later steps ran once per descendant and atomic results
  repeated (//PRICE/../../name()). The first step of the relative path is now
  mapped over the descendants and each later "/" or "//" is a chain link
  (chain_locals.start_operand), as in a relative path; D259's descendant pass
  still applies.
- **XSLT globals in inline functions** (XSLT 4.0, 9.7, a variable in scope in
  its own declaration): read from the unit's global table at call time, as
  XQuery's (D154); XPath's host-bound globals stay captured (D55). A function
  item called after its evaluation ended still reads no global table (D154's
  limit, now XSLT's too).
- **The default collation of a place** (XSLT 4.0, 3.7.1): comparisons carry the
  module of their static context (sxml_ir_binary. module_number, as static
  calls do, D163) and compare strings under its default collation; the
  filter-index pass leaves such comparisons alone. D263's open item
  (choose-0107, collations-0121 to -0124).
- **A library module's static context** (XQuery 4.0, 5.2): its IR module
  records its decimal formats, default collation, in-scope schemas and
  statically known namespaces; its functions read them when they run
  (format-number with the library's decimal format; validate in a loaded
  module's function).
- **fn:load-xquery-module** (F&O 4.0, 18.2): the variables option binds
  external variables only; vendor-options is map(xs:QName, item()\*)
  (XPTY0004); content loaded without trust gets no module or schema imports
  (FOQM0003). The QT4 driver serves an undeclared module from the suite file
  its location hint names.
- **Context-dependent references** (XPath 4.0, 4.5.4; F&O 4.0, 1.7): a named
  reference to a native row with USES_DYNAMIC_CONTEXT is a closure of its
  module, so it keeps its static context and trust when another module calls
  it. fn:function-lookup's run-time results are not covered (xqhof18, xqhof19).
- **xml:id under lax validation** (xml:id 1.0, 4): without a declaration in
  scope, xml:id is assessed as xs:ID (is-id, the ID table, IDREFs to it).
  D263's open item. IDREF checks at an element validation root stay as XSD's
  cvc-id has them (no text of XQuery 4.0, 4.25, which defines validate by
  fn:xsd-validator, lifts them); the two upd- cases expecting otherwise stay
  failing.
- **XML 1.1 query text** (D195; D237's design taken by D208):
  `sxml_processor_configuration.reads_query_text_as_xml_1_1`
  (include/sxml/processor.h, additive; glossary query_text_xml_version), false
  by default: NEL and LINE SEPARATOR are line ends (a pre-pass translates them
  in a copy; error offsets after one are in the copy), character references may
  denote C0 controls, xmlns:p="" undeclares p in a direct constructor, and an
  undeclared output:version is 1.1. The QT4 driver sets it for a test that
  depends on xml-version 1.1 alone; the CLI does not.
- **omit-xml-declaration** (deviation from D237's design): D237 made the
  library's XQuery default no while the CLI writes none, which the CLI cannot
  tell apart from a declared no without a new function. The library keeps
  DEFAULT (yes) for an undeclared parameter; the QT4 driver, as a host, takes
  no (XQuery 4.0, 5.22.1 leaves it to the implementation).
- **Measured** (release drivers, whole runs, case by case, no case lost at any
  step): XP40 32,793 to 32,797 passed (40 to 36 failed); XQ40 46,070 to 46,101
  (138 to 107 failed, 49 to 44 wrong-error); XT40 12,207 to 12,220 from this
  packet's changes (12,239 in the final run, with 4.26's and 4.27's commits);
  XSD11 41,486 unchanged. CONFORMANCE.md is not regenerated: 4.28 commits XSLT
  changes while these runs were made, so no one commit matches them.
- **Not done**: Q{}N name tests on JNodes (frozen sxml_name_test); runtime
  constructors of named item types for fn:function-lookup (itemTypeDecl-058);
  function items fn:function-lookup makes (xqhof18, -19); format-number's
  decimal format name with a direct constructor's namespaces (eqname-007); two
  modules of one namespace without a location (modules-collide-var-001,
  -fn-001); the serialization singletons (adaptive 6, csv 1); deep-equal of
  partial applications (4); fn:transform 3; static typing (D263: not done).

**Sources**: XP40, XQ40 and XT40 passes at the start (`tools/run-qt4.sh`,
`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build, at 87686bc); XP40, XQ40, XT40 and XSD11
passes, whole runs, case by case, at each step (`tools/run-qt4.sh`,
`tools/run-xslt.sh`, `tools/run-xsd.sh`, release build).

### D276. XSLT conformance sweep: instruction locations, next-match in attribute sets, parameter and static error codes (packet 4.28)

**Summary**: Expressions an XSLT instruction adds take the span of its start
tag so its errors have a line, xsl:next-match and xsl:apply-imports work in
attribute sets, and defaults raise XTTE0600.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D245, D271, D273, D274. Verified as D181 asks: the
debug preset (the xslt*, xslt_declaration, xslt_key, xslt_read,
xslt_lower_control and cli tests), clang-tidy on the changed files, the
call-cycle check, the book examples (D257, 397 match), and the whole XT40 suite
with the release driver after each change, case by case. \**XT40 12,239 to
12,250 passed (107 to 104 wrong error), 279 to 268 failed, 0 errors, no case
lost\*\*, from a whole run at c238bc6 (with 2.25's commits up to it). Commits
8ea4281, 47981ac, d02aba3, ff27d21.

- **Locations of instruction errors** (D271's open item): the sequence
  constructor gives the expressions a child's lowering added without a span the
  span of the child's start tag (src/xslt_lower.c, locate_child_expressions);
  XPath text keeps its spans. A dynamic or type error an instruction raises
  (validation XTTE errors, XTDE1490, xsl:message terminate, streamed reads) now
  has its module and line: $err:module and $err:line-number in xsl:catch
  (try-004, try-021) and "file.xsl:LINE:COLUMN" in the CLI; the book's two XTTE
  examples (xsd-typed-data.md) and two CLI tests changed with it.
- **xsl:next-match and xsl:apply-imports in attribute sets** (6.11, 10.2:
  invoking an attribute set leaves the current template rule): lowered directly
  in a set's body with a focus, they apply templates to the set's focus slots
  with empty parameter maps, and the evaluator reads its current rule
  (next-match-012, attribute-set-0108). A template with context-item
  use="absent" has none: XTDE0560 (next-match-029). **Deviation**: a set
  invoked inside xsl:for-each (or another changed focus) of a template rule
  still sees that rule, which 6.11 clears; the lowering clears it lexically and
  the set is a function of its own. Fixing it would take a third variant of
  each attribute set function or an evaluator operation that clears the rule.
- **Parameter codes** (9.3, 7.2): an explicit default (select or content) that
  cannot be coerced is XTTE0600 for template and function parameters
  (sxml_xslt_default_value_mapping; error-0600a, function-40-903); the implicit
  () keeps XPTY0004 (function-40-904); an implicitly mandatory xsl:iterate
  parameter is XTSE3520 (error-3520a, iterate-902).
- **Static checks**: XTSE3088 (context-item as with use="absent"), XTSE1210
  (unknown key collation), XTSE0500 (visibility without name), XTSE0085
  (extension-element-prefixes on a reserved namespace; the suite's XTSE0800 for
  extension-functions-0105 is not in the draft), XTSE0010 for an xsl:fallback
  after the text of xsl:select (10.4.2).
- **Found for the XPath sweep** (src/xpath_lower.c, compatible_argument_row):
  XPath 1.0 compatibility mode converts arguments by fn:number only for
  xs:double parameters (XPath 4.0, 3.4.1), but F&O 4.0 types the XPath 1.0
  number parameters as xs:numeric (fn:round, fn:floor, fn:substring,
  fn:format-number), so format-number('foo', ...) in a 1.0 stylesheet is
  XPTY0004. Treating xs:numeric and xs:numeric? like xs:double, measured in a
  private build only, passes 8 cases (format-number-014, -035, -038 to -041,
  backwards-022, xpath-compat-0401) and is the reading the suite takes.
- **The draft decides, left** (D245): numerics compare exactly in 4.0
  (sx-gc-eq-016, -020, -021, -116, -120, -121); union patterns take the lowest
  priority and predicates +0.5 (next-match-025a, -026a, priority-002, -124,
  -141, -163, conflict-resolution-1901a); XPDY0002 for unparsed-entity
  functions without a focus (error-1370a, -1380a, context-item-016); XTDE0050,
  not XTDE0700, for a global parameter (error-0610d).
- **Left, with causes**: suite inconsistencies (package-location-001 to -005
  read a missing file and assert @q where @p is written; next-match-017 leaves
  out an xsl:text newline; whitespace-only assert-xml in sf-snapshot-0201 to
  -0209, attribute-set-1508/-1509); date-094e/f and 095e/f assume no processor
  supports years past 2^32 (sxml does); FORG0001 where a cast in a binding's
  coercion fails (as-1602, sequence-0132, variable-0115,
  call-template-ext-2102: a mapping would also catch FORG0001 of lazily
  evaluated values); XTTE0945 for xsl:copy with a dynamically absent focus
  (copy-4308, glob-cxt-item-013); D274's per-package strip-space for
  fn:document, fragment identifiers of xsl:source-document
  (implementation-defined), strip-space "none" of an available document,
  namespace-2606.
- The XT40 section of `docs/CONFORMANCE.md` was not regenerated.

**Sources**: XT40 passes, whole suite, case by case, after each change
(`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build, at c238bc6); book examples, 397 match
(`tools/check-book-examples.sh`); XT40 cases passed by treating xs:numeric like

### D277. XSD conformance sweep 3: XSD 1.1 component rules, content recovery (packet 5.13)

**Summary**: The XSD sweep fixes 21 cases by XSD 1.1 component rules and adds
`content_recovery`, so after a rejected child the validator goes on matching
the rest of the content.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D178, D180, D263, D270, D271, D275. No public header
changed; internal additions only (schema_internal.h:
sxml_schema_value_constraints_are_equal, sxml_schema_content_model_recover,
sxml_schema_type_definition.restricts_attribute_group; schema_read_internal.h:
sxml_schema_document_reference.needs_document; the validation frame's
is_after_rejection).

- **Start** (release sxml-xsd-test, whole run at 7277563): 41,486 of 41,518 in
  scope passed, 32 failed, 217 not run.
- **Fixed, 21, by what XSD 1.1 decides** (commit 3b037b0): src-attribute.5,
  fixed with use="prohibited" (4; QUEUE had it as a 1.0-only rule, but 3.2.3
  clause 5 is new in 1.1); an attribute's type must be simple, src-resolve (1);
  a required base attribute keeps a use in the restriction's {attribute uses},
  and the restriction that checks a redefined attribute group inherits none
  (2); src-redefine.1, a redefine with components whose document does not
  resolve (4); simple content restricting xs:anySimpleType or xs:anyAtomicType
  without facets, cos-st-restricts.1.1 (4); fixed values in restrictions
  compare as values, equal or identical (1); Element Declarations Consistent,
  wildcard paragraph: type tables of a local declaration and the top-level one
  a strict or lax wildcard matches (3); a restricting wildcard the union of the
  base's wildcards covers (1); xml:lang of schema documents is a language or
  empty (1). End: 41,507 passed, 11 failed, none lost; the slice 147/147.
- **Left, 11, not decided by XSD 1.1 as the tests expect**:

  - XSD 1.0 rules: particlesK006 (1.0's particle restriction; 1.1's is by
    language), particlesZ033_g (UPA between an element and a wildcard, allowed
    in 1.1, 3.8.6.4's note), annotF001 (xml:lang="" is invalid only with the
    2001 xml.xsd).
  - Against the 1.1 Rec: ibm s3_4_2_4si03 expects a circular attribute group
    reference to be an error; 3.6.2.1 says it is not.
  - xs:NOTATION used directly (github w3c/xsdtests issue 12): 1.1 makes
    validating a literal against xs:NOTATION the error; D171 keeps it a schema
    error, as MHK's 2026 revision of over027 does. Then particlesZ007 (schema
    valid, 2006) and particlesZ007.i fail, and so does over027.n01, whose
    schema is (rightly, by that reading) invalid while the instance test
    expects a verdict.
  - Instance tests of indeterminate schemas: schU3.i, schU4.i, schU5.i (a
    document redefined twice, bug 4136) and ste110.i (a circular union, bug
    4957, queried): sxml rejects the schema, the instance tests expect
    "invalid", and the driver counts an instance of a failed schema as a fail
    (D165).
  - XML 1.1 instances, named in QUEUE: none fail now; they are not run (XML-1.1
    is not a supported substrate token).
- **Not run** (217): the introspection set (92) validates the suite's own
  catalogs against xsts.xsd, which imports
  http://www.w3.org/XML/2008/06/xlink.xsd; with a local copy of that file all
  92 pass (measured with sxml validate). Cheap to run: the driver's resolver
  would serve that one file, as the stand-in xml.xsd is served (D180); it needs
  xlink.xsd in third_party, for the owner. "queried" (57): run as an
  experiment, 27 pass; their expectations are the ones the WG queried, so they
  stay out. "version 1.0" (50): XSD 1.0 behaviour, not an XSD 1.1 processor's;
  not cheap to judge, stay out. The rest (indeterminate 14, none applies 2,
  disputed 1, Unicode 4.0.0 1) have no expectation to compare with.
- **Content recovery** (D270's and D271's open item; commit 707ca3a; glossary
  content_recovery): after a child the content model rejects
  (cvc-complex-type.2.4), the validator moves to the nearest state the child is
  accepted from, as if the elements before it were missing (a breadth-first
  walk over the states, an explicit queue, D71; counter tests not applied on
  the way), or else skips the child and assesses it by a declaration of its
  name in the type's particles (else laxly); the rest of the content goes on
  being matched and checked. A missing element is one report, an extra one one,
  a swap two; "incomplete" is not repeated right after a rejection at the same
  state. Verdicts do not change (no attribution after the rejected child,
  3.4.4.2); empty, simple and nilled content keep the lax rest. The book's XSD
  chapters and apps/sxml/README.md show it.
- **xsi:schemaLocation in sxml validate: not added.** The library does not
  follow schema location hints (schema.h: "not followed (4.3.2 allows it)";
  fn:xsd-validator's use-xsi-schema-location=true is FODC0009), so a flag would

  its schema while it validates (hints may appear on any element), which is a

### D278. Schema location hints (packet 5.16)

**Summary**: A schema follows the `schema_location_hint` attributes of a node
named in `sxml_schema_configuration`, through the resolver, adding only
namespaces it does not yet have; `sxml validate` gets `--use-schema-location`.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D13, D99, D165, D174, D179, D270, D271, D277. sxml
follows xsi:schemaLocation and xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation when the host asks
for it (XSD 1.1 Part 1, 4.3.2: "Schema processors should provide an option to
control whether they do so").

- **API** (additive, schema.h; no substrate header changes): one field at the
  end of `sxml_schema_configuration`, `sxml_item schema_location_hint_node`.
  The zero item is today's behaviour. A document, element or attribute node
  names the instance: after the configured documents and everything they refer
  to, every hint of the node's subtree, in document order, is asked of the
  processor's resolver (kind SCHEMA_DOCUMENT, the location resolved against the
  base URI of the attribute's element, the hinted namespace as
  target_namespace_uri) and read with what it refers to before the next hint is
  weighed. No new resource kind, no file access of the library's own: what the
  resolver delivers is the trust rule, as for xs:import.
- **Why on the schema, not the validator.** Part 1, 4.1: an incremental
  assembly "must result in an assessment outcome that is the same as would be
  given if assessment were undertaken again with the final, fully assembled
  schema", and 4.3.2: hints on any element have a global effect. A validator
  that added documents while it validates could not promise that for content it
  already assessed; collecting the hints of the whole instance first and
  assembling one schema does, and it is the existing reader and assembly
  (src/schema_assemble.c: a hint is one more RESOLVED document in the work
  list; relation HINT, reported in itself as a configured document). A
  streaming host that wants hints parses the instance once to collect them
  (sxml validate does: two parses).
- **When a hint is ignored** (4.3.2, strategy 1 "do nothing ... a schema
  containing components for the given namespace name is already known"): when a
  document already read has the hinted namespace as target namespace (the
  configured schema, an earlier hint or what it imported), and for the XML
  Schema and XML Schema instance namespaces. So hints only add namespaces; they
  never replace, extend or redefine the configured ones. This is also XSLT 4.0,
  25.1.3's rule for hints ("must not override or redefine any schema components
  in the static context") and keeps 4.3.2's security note: a document cannot
  swap the schema of a namespace the host chose. A namespace without a location
  is ignored; a document the resolver does not deliver is no error ("It is not
  an error for such an attempt to fail"); a delivered one with another target
  namespace than its hint's is `schema_reference` (as a document that is not a
  schema document), and errors of hinted documents fail the compilation as
  configured ones do.
- **The languages.** `fn:xsd-validator` with use-xsi-schema-location=true (F&O
  4.0, 17.2.5) compiles its options' documents with the target's hints; with no
  documents option, the hints' schema comes after the in-scope schemas, so that
  an in-scope declaration wins. A failure of the hints (a document that is not
  a schema, a conflict) makes V return is-valid false with the error in
  error-details, "an invalidity, not a dynamic error" (17.2.5); FODC0009 for
  the option is gone. fn:doc, fn:doc-available, fn:parse-xml and XSLT's
  fn:document with use-xsi-schema-location=true (F&O 4.0, 17.1.1, 17.2.1; XSLT
  4.0, 20.1) validate against the in-scope schemas and then a schema of the
  document's hints. XQuery's validate expression keeps
  use-xsi-schema-location=false (XQuery 4.0, 4.25 recommends it) and XSLT
  validation attributes ignore hints (XSLT 4.0, 25.1.3 leaves it
  implementation-defined).
- **sxml validate** gets the flag `--use-schema-location` (D44: an explicit
  flag, never a mode guessed from the input or from a missing option; like
  `sxml check --external-entities`, it opts in to reading files a FILE names):
  each FILE's hints, relative to the FILE (standard input: the working
  directory), are read as local files through the CLI's resolver, never the
  network, and assembled with the `--schema` documents into the schema of that
  FILE. `--schema` is required unless the flag is given. A FILE is parsed twice
  then, once for its hints; errors of a hinted document are reported as schema
  errors of that FILE (`DOCUMENT:LINE:COLUMN: CONSTRAINT: description`, in JSON
  in its `errors` with `document`) and make it invalid.
- **xlink.xsd** (D277's introspection set): the W3C's
  http://www.w3.org/XML/2008/06/xlink.xsd is vendored in
  `third_party/w3c-xlink/` with its license (W3C Software and Document License)
  and served by the XSD driver's resolver for that URI, as the library serves
  its stand-in xml.xsd; the introspection set is run.
- **The XSD driver** follows hints through the library now (its own scan of
  xsi:schemaLocation pairs is gone): an instance with a hint attribute compiles
  the test's documents again with schema_location_hint_node, used when it
  compiles, as before.
- **QT4 driver**: the feature schema-location-hint ("at" hints of import schema
  resolved as relative URIs) is supported for XQuery; qischema041, 042 and 083
  pass.
- **Done** (commits d7e87f6, 6669c24, 67f313b, 9e86eec). Verified as D181 asks:
  debug preset (schema*, xquery_schema, xslt_schema, function_library*, json,
  qt4, xsd, cli tests: 296 passed), clang-tidy clean on the changed files,
  check-call-cycles 0 cycles, tools/check-book-examples.sh on the touched
  chapters.
- **Measured** (release drivers, HEAD 240bb83 before, the packet's files
  after): XSD11 whole run 41,507 -> 41,599 passed (the 92 introspection tests),
  11 failed unchanged (D277's 11), 217 -> 125 not run; QT4 XQ40 schema-aware
  sets (76) 11,691 -> 11,696 passed, 53 -> 51 failed (fn-doc-40-065 and
  fn-doc-available-40-065 by this packet, xml-to-json-057 by 4.29;
  fn-system-properties-supports-xinclude failed in the after snapshot only
  because it ran 2.27's uncommitted driver hunk without its code), 334 -> 331
  not run; parse-xml-440 passes; XT40 schema_aware sets (52) 4,084 -> 4,087
  passed (4.29's commits), none lost. CONFORMANCE.md not regenerated.

**Sources**: XSD11 whole run, QT4 XQ40 schema-aware sets and XT40 schema_aware
sets, HEAD 240bb83 before and the packet files after (`tools/run-xsd.sh`,
`tools/run-qt4.sh`, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); debug unit and CLI
tests touched, 296 passed (`ctest`, debug build).

### D281. XSLT conformance sweep: XSLT coercion casts, globals in xsl:iterate, deep-copy types, fixed-namespaces documents (packet 4.29)

**Summary**: A failed cast in an XSLT binding's coercion is a type error
through a new XSLT_BINDING coercion role, and closures in xsl:iterate read
globals where they read them instead of capturing them.

as D181 asks: the debug preset (the xslt*, ir*, evaluator*, json,
function_library*, serialize*, cli/transform* tests touched), clang-tidy on the
changed files, the call-cycle check, the book examples (D257, 399 match; no CLI
output the book shows changed), and the whole XT40 suite with the release
driver after each change, case by case. **XT40 12,250 to 12,261 passed (104 to
99 wrong error), 268 to 257 failed, 0 errors, no case lost**, from a whole run
at b97d939 (with 2.26's and 5.16's commits as they landed). Commits 86ad244,
240bb83, a6ec5ad, 4c7a872, 368f0e0, eb27ee8.

- **A failed cast in an XSLT binding's coercion** (D276's open item, 9.3: a
  value that "cannot be converted to the required type" is a type error): a new
  IR coercion role, SXML_IR_COERCION_ROLE_XSLT_BINDING, for the coercions whose
  XSLT lowering maps XPTY0004 to its own code (variables, explicit parameter
  defaults, template and function results, xsl:global-context-item); for it and
  TEMPLATE_PARAMETER the evaluator's coercion reports its type error where the
  cast of an untyped atomic item fails, not FORG0001. Only the coercion's own
  cast changes, so a FORG0001 of a lazily evaluated value stays (D276's
  concern). D262's reading (FORG0001 as the draft's) is replaced: the coercion
  rules cast (XPath 4.0, 3.4.3), and XSLT says what a failure to convert is
  (as-1602, sequence-0132, variable-0115, call-template-ext-2102).
- **Globals in xsl:iterate**: the closure captured every declared global by
  value, so an xsl:iterate in a global's initializer read that global while it
  was being computed (XTDE0640) and computed every other global first; globals
  are captured as GLOBAL_VARIABLE atoms and read where the closure reads them,
  as D275 does for inline functions (arrays-306, si-iterate-099).

### D282. The book's code-generation project (packet book-3)

**Summary**: The book gains Chapter 12, a project that generates a TypeScript
client, Node.js handler and OpenAPI document from an XSD schema and an API
description, with the generated files checked in sync.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D257 and D270. The owner asked for a chapter on
using XQuery, XSD and XSLT for code generation, such as RPC between the browser
and the backend in the manner of SvelteKit's remote functions.

- **Place.** A new top-level Chapter 12, "Project: Generating Code from a
  Schema", after Performance and before the appendices, so the numbers of
  Chapters 1 to 11 (cited elsewhere in the book) hold. Four sections:
  `codegen.md` (the sources and their validation), `codegen-typescript.md`,
  `codegen-running.md`, `codegen-pipeline.md`; examples in
  `docs/book/examples/codegen`. One sentence links to it from the XQuery, XSLT
  and XSD parts and the introduction; the book's glossary gains "Remote
  function" and "String constructor".
- **The example.** `library.xsd` (simple types with pattern, maxLength,
  enumeration and range facets; complex types read as JSON objects:
  minOccurs="0" is optional, maxOccurs="unbounded" an array) and `api.xml`
  (queries and commands), checked by `api.xsd` with `sxml validate`.
  `typescript.xqm` writes TypeScript with string constructors (types and
  checks, a fetch client, a Node.js handler) over a hand-written `runtime.ts`;
  `generate.xq` stores the files with `fn:put` and the text method;
  `openapi.xsl` writes OpenAPI 3.1 with template rules and `xsl:map`. Unknown
  facets and unknown type names are errors of the generators, not silently
  dropped. The generated files are kept in `generated/`, and the book's `diff
  -r` against a fresh run is the "in sync" check, so the book check also keeps
  them current: regenerate them (`sh generate.sh` in that directory) when the
  generator, the schema or the CLI's output changes.
- **Running the code.** `codegen-running.md` runs `node demo.ts` (Node.js 22.18
  or later strips the types; the generated code uses only erasable syntax). It
  is marked `<!-- requires: javascript -->`, so the check runs it only with
  SXML_JAVASCRIPT set, where Node.js is known to be present; the package link
  it makes is unused.
- **Finding for later** (QUEUE, not fixed here): a syntax error inside an
  enclosed expression of a string constructor (`` `{ ... }` ``) is reported at
  line 1, column 1 of the module instead of its own place.
- **Verified**: tools/check-book-examples.sh on a release build of a HEAD
  snapshot with SXML_JAVASCRIPT set: all 30 examples of the four files match;
  `mdbook build` succeeds; the generated TypeScript type-checks with `tsc
  --strict`.

### D283. Fast Invisible XML: Earley with lookahead sets and Leo items (packet 7.21)

**Summary**: Invisible XML keeps its one Earley parser and makes it fast with
16-byte items, FIRST and FOLLOW lookahead, Leo items for right recursion,
codepoint classes and grammar simplification.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D12, D53, D71, D189, D215, D224, D272. The owner: a
high-performance Invisible XML, book first, then the tests, then the
implementation. Done (commits ec3fd42, 4818dd3, 7a93dc7).

- **Book** (ec3fd42): the part "Parsing Text with Invisible XML", five
  chapters; the errors and performance chapters are drafts whose examples are
  the acceptance test. **Tests** (4818dd3): `tests/bench/run-ixml-bench.py`,
  whose `--check` holds the book's numbers.
- **Choice**: keep the one Earley parser of D215 and make it fast with (1)
  items in arrays of 16 bytes over numbered dotted rules, (2) one character of
  lookahead from the grammar's FIRST and FOLLOW sets, so an item is made only
  when the next character can continue it (Earley, 1970, used lookahead; global
  FOLLOW sets need no per-item lookahead), (3) Leo's items (Leo, "A general
  context-free parsing algorithm running in linear time on every LR(k) grammar
  without using lookahead", TCS 82, 1991) for right recursion, and (4) compiled
  codepoint classes: each codepoint is looked up once in a table of the
  grammar's distinct terminals. Rejected: an LR/LALR front end with a GLR
  fallback (Markup Blitz): grammars are run-time data, so the tables would be
  built per fn:invisible-xml call and could be large, and GLR needs a
  graph-structured stack and a packed forest beside the Earley sets, a second
  parser against D215; the LR(0) automaton of Aycock and Horspool ("Practical
  Earley Parsing", 2002) merges items into states but makes the first
  derivation, which sxml reads the tree from, harder to keep. Two notes from
  the orchestrator for the record: the "tables per call" objection is weaker
  than stated, since fn:invisible-xml returns a parse function and tables would
  be built once per grammar; and the largest constant factor left is lexical
  (regular nonterminals compiled to DFAs and matched in one step, not one
  Earley set per character).
- **Grammar simplification** (`src/ixml.c`, before productions are sorted): a
  hidden use of a rule of one production of one symbol uses that symbol in
  place (`-digit: ["0"-"9"]`, `-s: " "*`), and groups and options the compiler
  made, used once and hidden, are written out where used (at most 8 productions
  from one, alternatives in order). Parses, XML and ambiguity are unchanged;
  items per character fall by half to two thirds (Markdown-like text 5.6 to
  about 2).
- **Parser** (`src/ixml_earley.c`, `src/ixml_tables.c`): items of 16 bytes
  (dotted rule with the ambiguous and through-Leo flags, origin, predecessor,
  child) in blocks of 2^14 that never move; lookahead sets from FIRST/FOLLOW
  over distinct terminals plus end of input, tested against the next
  character's codepoint class (ASCII from a table, others computed once and
  cached); an item is made only when its set meets the class. Items left out
  are in no parse of the whole input, so the tree, its marks and the failure
  position are those without lookahead; the failing set is made again without
  lookahead for its expected terminals. Leo items only where one item waits as
  its last symbol and started earlier (no cycles), found down the chain and
  back without recursion; the chain's items are made when the tree reaches
  them. Tree nodes in blocks too. Steps: one per item, Leo item, chain item and
  tree node, as before; fewer items means fewer steps.
- **Errors**: FOIX0001 for grammar text says line, column and the character (or
  the end); S02 and S03 name the rule; D02 names the attribute and element, D03
  the name. Failure documents list each expected set once, sorted by notation;
  a quote is written '"'.
- **Numbers** (release, 1 MB inputs, processor s / MB, before -> after): log
  1.12/372 -> 0.18/91; csv 1.25/456 -> 0.28/120; calc 2.14/756 -> 0.53/204;
  markdown 3.21/1460 -> 0.30/125; right recursion fails at the step limit after
  5.4 GB -> 0.30/136; nesting 200 KB 0.16/64 -> 0.05/27; compiling a 5,800-rule
  grammar 1.07/410 -> 0.18/68; the ambiguous sum of 2,000 characters 2.41 ->
  1.4 to 1.8 (cubic; its book bound became 2 s). The book's targets are met
  (`--check` passes); linear benchmarks grow 3.8 to 4.2 times for 4 times the
  input; a 10 MB log takes 2.1 s within the default step limit. iXML suite 886
  of 907 unchanged (21 not run: 17 Unicode versions, 4 inputs with C0 controls
  that no xs:string holds; none decided by the specification for sxml; the
  vendored copy d1f37f6 is Codeberg's head); QT4 iXML sets unchanged. Native
  code +25 KB.
- **Memory** stays about 90 to 200 bytes per input character: every item set is
  kept until the tree is read out of the first derivations. An incrementally
  built shared packed forest, freeing sets behind the parse, would bound it by
  the forest; lexical DFAs for regular nonterminals would cut items per
  character further. Both are left for a later packet.

**Sources**: iXML benchmarks, processor seconds and MB, 1 MB inputs, before and
after (`tests/bench/run-ixml-bench.py`, release build); iXML suite passes and
not run (`tests/ixml/run-ixml-tests.sh`, from `third_party/ixml-tests`); QT4
iXML sets and native code growth.

### D285. Source code as XML: tree-sitter trees with highlights captures (packet 7.22)

**Summary**: `sxml:parse-code` parses source code with vendored tree-sitter
grammars into a document whose elements are named `syntax_node` kinds and whose
text is the source exactly, with highlight captures as attributes.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D12, D13, D44, D71, D99, D162, D189, D191, D208,
D215, D272. The owner's order: the book first (Chapter "Source Code as XML"),
then the grammars' own tests, then the implementation.

- **Shape** (glossary `syntax_node`, `syntax_node_kind`, `field_name`,
  `token_element`): a document node; one element per named syntax node, named
  by its kind, in no namespace; anonymous nodes (tokens) and the bytes between
  nodes are text, so `string()` of the document is the source exactly, and the
  document element holds the whole text, leading and trailing whitespace
  included. A child's field name is a `field` attribute. A token with a
  highlight or a field name becomes an `sxml:token` element so it can carry
  them; a named kind that is no NCName (an alias) an `sxml:node` element with
  `kind`. ERROR nodes are `ERROR` elements (tree-sitter's spelling); a node the
  parser inserted has `missing="true"`, and a missing token also `kind`. The
  option `positions` adds `line`, `column`, `end-line`, `end-column` (from 1,
  columns in characters, so they agree with XPath string positions); off by
  default, so documents compare without them. `sxml` is bound to `urn:sxml` on
  the document element. Like iXML (D215), syntax errors are part of the result,
  not an error: tree-sitter recovers, and a query can count `//ERROR`.
- **Highlights** (glossary `highlights_query`, `capture`): the grammar's
  `queries/highlights.scm` (the files its tree-sitter.json names, in that
  order) runs through the runtime's query API (ts_query_*). Text predicates are
  the host's job: `eq?`, `match?`, `any-of?`, their `not-` and `any-` forms;
  `match?` uses sxml's regex engine (F&O 4.0, 6.1, no flags; the queries' Rust
  regexes are in the common subset, and one that does not compile makes the
  predicate false); `#is-not? local` holds and `#is? local` does not (no locals
  query: no node is a local variable); directives (`#set!`) and unknown
  predicates are ignored. Captures named `_…` only serve predicates. When
  several patterns capture one node, the \**last\*\* pattern wins: the
  grammars' queries start with `(identifier) @variable` and refine it later,
  and their highlight tests expect the refinement (with the first pattern
  winning, the name in `function i() {}` would be `variable`, where the test
  says `function`). The winner is the `highlight` attribute; nested captures
  stay nested. Locals (locals.scm) and injections (injections.scm) are not run:
  a later packet can add them in the same place.
- **API**: `sxml:parse-code($source as xs:string?, $language as xs:string,
  $options as map(*)? := {}) as document-node()?` with options `highlights`
  (default true) and `positions` (default false), and `sxml:code-languages() as
  xs:string*`, in the new well-known namespace `urn:sxml` (`name.h`:
  SXML_NAMESPACE_SXML = 16, additive after D99, as D206 added EXSLT; sxml's own
  functions and errors go there). An unknown language is
  `sxml:unknown-language`. A direct function rather than fn:invisible-xml's
  function-returning shape: a grammar here is a compiled-in name, not run-time
  data, so there is nothing to compile once. Optional feature
  `sxml_source_code_feature()` ("source-code", `processor.h`, additive), whose
  library_functions hold the two rows (D191), in
  `sxml_all_optional_features()`, so every shipped build has it (D272). CLI
  (D44): no new command or flag; `sxml xpath` and `sxml xquery` bind the prefix
  `sxml` as they bind `bin` and `file`; a stylesheet declares it (D261).
- **Languages** (glossary `source_code_language`): option (a), vendored
  grammars compiled in: JSON, JavaScript (with JSX), Python, C, CSS, HTML and
  Go, from the tree-sitter organization's repositories (MIT), in
  `third_party/tree-sitter-grammars/LANGUAGE` (`LICENSE`, the generated `src/`,
  the highlights queries, `test/`, and `VERSION` with the commit), by
  `tools/vendor-tree-sitter-grammar.sh`. They join grammars/CMakeLists.txt's
  one grammar list as `sxml_source_grammar_LANGUAGE`, with the entry point
  renamed `sxml_source_language_LANGUAGE` (sxml's own JSON grammar keeps
  `tree_sitter_json`) and Clang's -fno-sanitize=function (upstream scanners
  declare `()`, compatible in C17). The language table and queries are
  generated into `src/source_code_languages.c` by
  `tools/generate-source-code-languages.py`; adding a language is vendor plus
  generate. Option (b), a host API to register a TSLanguage and a query, is not
  built: it would make tree-sitter's ABI part of sxml's public contract; it
  stays a proposal. Not shipped, by cost (native -O2 code and data of parser
  and scanner): TypeScript 1,413,409 and TSX 1,447,676 bytes, Rust 1,125,096,
  Bash 1,335,694, Markdown 368,665 plus its inline grammar 361,385; shipped:
  JSON 7,605, JavaScript 413,323, Python 459,815, C 618,257, CSS 114,067, HTML
  19,702, Go 222,353 (1,854,622 in all). sxml's own XPath, XQuery and XML
  grammars are not offered: they serve sxml's parsers (markers, external-subset
  entry points) and have no highlights queries.
- **Mechanism** (`src/source_code.c`, `src/source_code_internal.h`,
  `src/function_library_source_code.c`): tree-sitter parses (D12; its progress
  callback charges the bytes read to the call's step limit and cancels the
  parse past it); the query cursor's progress callback does the same; captures
  are recorded in allocator memory, sorted by node, one per node; one loop
  walks a TSTreeCursor with an explicit stack of "made an element" flags (D71)
  and writes tree builder events into an arena tree of the processor, text by
  byte offset, so nothing is lost or doubled. The D12 exemption (tree-sitter
  allocates with malloc) extends from the parse to the query step; parser,
  tree, query and cursors are freed before the function returns.
- **Tests** (D13): each shipped grammar's `test/corpus` (452 trees) and
  `test/highlight` (187 assertions) are vendored with it;
  `tests/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-driver.xq` runs them through `sxml xquery`
  (public API only): the document's S-expression against the corpus tree
  (normalized as tree-sitter normalizes; field names compared only when the
  expected tree has some), and each `<-`/`^` assertion against the highlight
  attributes covering its line and column. `tree-sitter/suite` keeps a baseline
  that only goes up.
- **Done** (commits e29713d book, 3b52502 tests, 33c225b implementation): the
  book's chapter, 18 examples, all match; tree-sitter/suite 630 of 639: corpus
  452 of 452, highlights 178 of 187 (7 need the locals query, 2 injections); a
  caret run is checked at its first column (the HTML tests run carets over
  `onclick=`). Sizes (stripped / gzipped): `sxml.wasm` 9,693,235 / 2,006,198,
  +1,990,621 in code and data since the D272 baseline (the grammars' parse
  tables 1,770,000 of it, tree-sitter's query code 43,579, the bridge 20,083),
  budget 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 / 2,800,000; the CLI module 11,289,043 /
  2,288,933, budget 9,500,000 / 2,100,000 to 11,500,000 / 2,500,000; the size
  baseline refreshed.

**Sources**: native -O2 code and data of each vendored grammar parser and
scanner (from `third_party/tree-sitter-grammars`); tree-sitter suite: corpus
trees and highlight assertions (`tests/tree-sitter/run-tree-sitter-tests.sh`,
`tests/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-driver.xq`, from
`third_party/tree-sitter-grammars`); book chapter examples, 18 match
(`tools/check-book-examples.sh`); sxml.wasm and the CLI module, stripped and
gzipped, against the D272 baseline (`bindings/javascript/test/size-budget.mjs`,
wasm build); configured: the sxml.wasm and CLI module budgets (from
`bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt`).

### D286. XPath and XQuery sweep: XInclude, ideographic numerals, place static contexts (packet 2.27)

**Summary**: fn:doc, fn:doc-available and fn:parse-xml gain `xinclude`
processing, fn:format-integer gains `ideographic_numerals`, and element()
selects no JNode, with namespaces recorded at static calls of a place.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D97, D162, D199, D263, D273, D275, D280, D281. No
public header changed; IR fields sxml_ir_step.is_xnode_type_test and
sxml_ir_static_call.namespace_bindings; a name role
SXML_XPATH_NAME_ROLE_CONSTRUCTED_ELEMENT. Verified as D181 asks: the debug
preset (every unit and CLI test but evaluator_stream; the tree-sitter suite
fails on 7.22's uncommitted baseline), clang-tidy on the changed files, the
call-cycle check, and whole XP40, XQ40 and XT40 runs with the release drivers,
case by case.

- **XInclude** (XInclude 1.0; F&O 4.0, 17.1.1, 17.2.1; glossary xinclude,
  inclusion_fixup; D280's cheapest not-run feature):
  src/function_library_xinclude.c copies a document into a new tree with each
  xi:include replaced by the document fn:doc gives for its href (resolved
  against the element's base URI: the loader's resolver, trust and stability),
  by text read as fn:unparsed-text reads it (parse="text", encoding), or by its
  xi:fallback's children after a resource error. One loop over an explicit
  stack of sibling cursors (D71); included documents are walked in the same
  loop; including a document already open is an inclusion loop. Top elements of
  an inclusion get xml:base (relative below the parent's directory) and
  xml:lang where they differ. Fatal errors are FODC0002 (F&O names no code), an
  include without trust-external FODC0016. Not supported: xpointer (a resource
  error, so a fallback applies), accept and accept-language (ignored). fn:doc,
  fn:doc-available and fn:parse-xml process after loading; XSLT's fn:document
  shares the option through sxml_function_library_read_document_options, so
  D273's FODC0013 is gone there too (one hunk in 4.29's file). A document
  without the XInclude namespace is returned as it is; with includes the result
  is a new tree per call, as strip-space "all" gives (the draft's doc(x,
  {xinclude}) is doc(x, {xinclude}) does not hold). supports-xinclude is true;
  the QT4 driver lists xinclude-option, so
  fn-system-properties-supports-xinclude-false is not run any more. The CLI's
  fn:doc has it (xquery_xinclude tests); the book no longer says XInclude is
  unsupported.
- **Ideographic numerals** (F&O 4.0, 4.6.1, implementation-defined sequences;
  glossary ideographic_numerals): the token U+4E00 numbers in Japanese
  numerals, as format-integer-052 expects; xsl:number shares it.
- **element() on JNodes** (XPath 4.0, 4.7.5.5; D281's item): element() and
  schema-element() select no JNode, \* every one; the step records the form, as
  D280's has_qualified_name_test.
- **Fixed default element namespace** (XQuery 4.0, 5.14.1, 5.11): fixed for
  name tests and types; xmlns="" in direct constructors changes only prefix 0,
  which constructed element names use (2.1.4).
- **Namespaces of a call's place** (D263 extended to static calls): an XQuery
  static call of a native row with USES_DYNAMIC_CONTEXT records the statically
  known namespaces of its place, which the callee reads; format-number's
  decimal format name in a direct constructor with xmlns:ex (eqname-007, D275's
  and D280's open item).
- **Smaller fixes**: XQST0034 for a declared function named as an in-scope
  schema type's constructor (5.18); strip-space "all" keeps the whitespace of
  elements XSD validation gives simple content (F&O 4.0, 17.2.1), with fn:doc
  validating before stripping and stripped copies keeping types;
  fn:build-dateTime atomizes field values; collection documents with a document
  URI are fn:doc's documents (17.1.3); xml-to-json's top element may have
  escaped-key without key (17.4.7).
- **Measured** (release drivers, whole runs; no case lost but the
  supports-xinclude-false case, now not run): start at 6236ab6, XP40 32,809
  passed (30 wrong error), 31 failed; XQ40 46,138 (44), 90. At 384040b, after
  the XInclude commits and 5.16's: XP40 32,814 (27 failed), XQ40 46,146 (86).
  At bc7a35e: XP40 32,815 (26 failed), XQ40 46,154 (78 failed); this packet's
  share XP40 +4, XQ40 +12. XT40 12,261 unchanged (at 384040b with and without
  the changes). CONFORMANCE.md is not regenerated.
- **Not done, with causes**: xqhof18 and xqhof19 (a function item that
  fn:function-lookup makes for a context-dependent row at run time, and
  fn:function-lookup#2 made in a library module, need a run-time closure that
  carries a module number and the reference's focus: an evaluator task bound to
  a module, medium); modules-43 (cyclic imports of named item types: modules
  are analyzed one at a time in reading order, so a module set needs a shared
  resolution round over all modules' types, medium); function-decl-40-060 (PR
  2941: a default value that does not depend on the focus is computed once; it
  would become a hidden global of the declaring module, small to medium);
  D281's record coercion cases (record-003, -005, -016): the draft rejects
  surplus entries (XPath 4.0, 3.4.2) and XDM 4.0, 8.3.2 makes a lookup of a
  non-field an error, which the tests contradict; fn-string-length-26 expects
  the string value of a validated element to be its text, where XDM 4.0,
  7.5.2.4 says the schema normalized value; map-to-element-014,
  serialize-xml-157 and serialize-csv-002/-003 fail in XP40 only, because they
  use XQuery's character references in string literals; xml-to-json-065
  (escaped on a map, which the schema of F&O 4.0, D.2 does not allow); XSLT's
  fn:document still strips before it validates (4.30's file); the kept groups
  of D280.

**Sources**: XP40 and XQ40 passes, whole runs at the start (`tools/run-qt4.sh`,
release build, at 6236ab6); XP40 and XQ40 passes after the XInclude commits and
5.16, and XT40 with and without the changes (`tools/run-qt4.sh`,
`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build, at 384040b); XP40 and XQ40 passes at the
end (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, release build, at bc7a35e).

### D287. XPath and XQuery sweep: syntax error places, run-time closures, globals after the evaluation, fixed defaults, cyclic item types (packet 2.28)

**Summary**: Syntax errors are reported at the innermost ERROR node,
context-dependent functions made at run time become a `run_time_closure`,
focus-free defaults become a `default_global`, and import cycles run an
`item_type_round`.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D55, D71, D154, D234, D263, D275, D280, D282, D286.
No public header changed; internal: sxml_function_parameter.
is_empty_without_focus, two fields of sxml_xquery_static_request, the evaluator
service sxml_evaluator_make_run_time_closure with its body operations and the
unlisted row sxml:run-time-closure. Glossary: run_time_closure, default_global,
item_type_round. Verified as D181 asks: the debug preset (every unit and CLI
test but evaluator_stream, under ASan and UBSan), clang-tidy on the changed
files, the call-cycle check, the book examples (472 match), and whole XP40,
XQ40 and XT40 runs with the release drivers, case by case against HEAD.

- **Syntax error places** (D282's finding): nothing is re-parsed; tree-sitter's
  recovery wraps a wide region, often from the module's start, in one ERROR and
  marks the token it could not take with an ERROR inside it.
  sxml_xpath_find_error now descends, while the node is an ERROR, to the first
  ERROR or MISSING node it holds, so a syntax error in a string constructor's
  `{ }` is reported at its place (4:44, was 1:1 or the clause's start). One
  path for XPath, XQuery and XSLT value templates (an attribute value template
  still maps through its normalized value). CLI tests
  xquery_string_constructor_syntax_error, xpath_string_template_syntax_error;
  the book shows no changed place.
- **Run-time closures** (glossary run_time_closure; XPath 4.0, 4.5.4; F&O 4.0,
  13.1.1; D275's and D286's open item, xqhof18, xqhof19): one closure
  representation for a context-dependent function made at run time, for XQuery
  and XSLT alike: a function item whose body operations are
  sxml_evaluator_run_time_closure_body_operations, whose state is the IR
  function of its place (retaining the unit) and whose captured values are the
  wrapped item, the place's expression index and, for a row that takes the
  caller's focus, the focus there. The machine calls the wrapped item in a CALL
  task made a task of the place, so sxml_dynamic_context_get_static_context and
  its kin read the place's module (D275's per-module static context) and the
  kept focus follows the arguments as a static call's caller focus. Two makers:
  a named reference to a context-dependent native row lowers to a static call
  of sxml:run-time-closure with the row's function item (and the caller's
  focus, dropped at run time when absent), replacing D275's IR closure of the
  module; fn:function-lookup wraps what it finds for a context-dependent row at
  the place of its call. So <lib/>/fn:function-lookup#2 made in a library
  module looks up in that module, with <lib/> as the focus.
- **Globals after the evaluation** (D154's limit; D55): a function item called
  after its evaluation ended, or from another evaluation, got no global table
  and failed with INVALID_ARGUMENT when its body read a global. Entering an IR
  function of a unit the run has no table for now adds one with every global
  absent: declared globals are computed again in that run on first read (D234),
  external variables and the context value read as absent (XPDY0002). A
  function item does not retain its evaluation's table: a global's value can
  hold the item, and values must not form cycles (D33). Unit test
  xquery_prolog/function_item_reads_globals_after_evaluation.
- **Fixed defaults** (XQuery 4.0, 5.18.3: a default "is evaluated in the same
  way as the initializing expression of a variable declaration" with the
  caller's focus; PR 2941; function-decl-40-060): a default function that reads
  no part of the focus becomes, through a function of arity 0, the initializer
  of a hidden global (glossary default_global, Q{urn:sxml:default}dN), and
  every call of it a read of that global, computed once per evaluation. XQuery
  only; XSLT's xsl:function defaults keep a call per use.
- **Cyclic imports of named item types** (5.12.4, 5.19; qt4 issue 1520;
  modules-43): with an import cycle the module set first runs an item type
  round (glossary item_type_round): every module's namespaces and named item
  types only (no schema imports or records), again and again with the public
  types its imports gave the last time, until no more are found; a module's own
  reading then has the found types of its imports not read yet. A set without a
  cycle reads as before.
- **"The context node, if any"** (4.30's D289 item, map-for-key-005):
  sxml_function_parameter.is_empty_without_focus makes an omitted context-value
  parameter the empty sequence where the focus is statically absent;
  xpath_lower.c supplies it, src/xslt_key.c (4.30's) is to set it on
  fn:map-for-key's parameter.
- **Measured** (release drivers, whole runs, case by case, no case lost): XQ40
  46,154 to 46,158 passed (78 to 74 failed, 44 wrong error); XP40 32,815
  unchanged (26 failed); XT40 12,268 unchanged (same cases). A fresh whole run
  at HEAD (2c91eaf, before this packet) found no new cluster: its failures are
  D286's (78 XQ40, 26 XP40), the kept groups and singletons.
- **Not done** (D286 stands): record-003, -005, -016 and fn-string-length-26
  (the draft decides against the tests); the kept groups of D280 and D286.

**Sources**: XQ40, XP40 and XT40 passes, whole runs, case by case, before and
after (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); fresh whole run
at HEAD before this packet (`tools/run-qt4.sh`, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, release
build, at 2c91eaf).

### D288. More source code languages, a registration API and run-time languages (packet 7.23)

**Summary**: TypeScript, TSX and Markdown become built-in source code
languages, locals and injections queries run, a public API registers a
`registered_language`, and the CLI loads each `language_library` with
`--code-language`.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D12, D44, D71, D99, D189, D191, D208, D272, D285.
The owner's answer to D285's proposal (2026-10-20): TypeScript, TSX and
Markdown built in, not Rust or Bash; a public registration API, with
tree-sitter's ABI part of the contract; languages supplied at run time from
tree-sitter language files, loaded by the host, never by src/. The owner's
order: the book (commit 0cad9a1), the tests (a40851e), the implementation
(c1a88af), the budgets (10487b2).

- **Built-in languages** (glossary `source_code_language`): typescript and tsx
  (tree-sitter-typescript 75b3874; their scanners include
  `../../common/scanner.h`, vendored to
  third_party/tree-sitter-grammars/common/; TypeScript's queries name
  JavaScript's package, taken from the vendored javascript grammar as
  queries/javascript-\*.scm), markdown and markdown_inline
  (tree-sitter-markdown a0a00f8). The vendor script also copies the locals and
  injections queries and the injection-regex of tree-sitter.json; the seven
  grammars of D285 were vendored again at their commits (JavaScript gains
  locals.scm and injections.scm, HTML injections.scm). sxml:code-languages()
  lists eleven.
- **Locals** (glossary `locals_query`; tree-sitter's highlight crate):
  local.scope, local.definition(.\*), local.reference captures in document
  order, a scope stack and a definition list (explicit, D71), `#set!
  local.scope-inherits false`; a reference finds the innermost earlier
  definition of its text; definitions and resolved references are local for
  `#is? local`/`#is-not? local`, and a reference takes its definition's
  highlight (D285's "no node is local" is gone).
- **Injections** (glossary `injection`, `injections_query`, `injection_regex`):
  injection.content with injection.language (a capture's text or `#set!`),
  injection.self, injection.include-children. The node's range without its
  *named* children's (as Neovim and the highlight crate: Markdown's inline
  nodes hold anonymous tokens of the block grammar) is parsed through
  tree-sitter's included ranges, so positions are the document's. The language
  is found by name (registered first), then by the first injection regex that
  matches (XPath regex, registered first); unknown languages leave the node as
  it is. The injected tree is written inside the node's element; its document
  element has `language`. The option `injections` (default true) turns it off;
  the corpus driver parses without injections. One loop over an explicit stack
  of layers (one per tree), at most 8 injections deep. Not supported:
  injection.combined (each node is its own document), injection.parent.
- **Registration API** (`processor.h`, additive after D99; glossary
  `registered_language`): `sxml_source_code_language` (name, `const struct
  TSLanguage *grammar`, highlights, locals and injections query texts,
  injection regex), `sxml_processor_configuration. source_code_languages`
  (appended, so earlier fields keep their places),
  `sxml_source_code_check_language` with `sxml_source_code_language_report`
  (problem: name, ABI, which query and its byte offset), and
  `SXML_SOURCE_CODE_MINIMUM_LANGUAGE_ABI` 13 to `..._MAXIMUM_...` 15, the range
  tree-sitter 0.27's runtime reads (tree-sitter 0.20 and later). A registered
  language replaces a built-in one of its name. sxml_processor_initialize
  refuses empty or odd names (letters, digits, `_-+.`), NULL grammars, other
  ABIs and a name twice (cheap: no query is compiled there); a query that does
  not compile raises `sxml:invalid-query` when the language is used (an
  injected language's bad query only drops its highlights). The checks are in
  src/source_code_check.c, so the processor does not link the grammars.
  Lifetime: the array, grammars and texts outlive the processor. A TSLanguage
  is immutable, so a host may share one.
- **Run-time language files: what works**. Native shared libraries (glossary
  `language_library`: `libtree-sitter-NAME.so`, `.dylib`, `.dll`, or `NAME.so`
  as `tree-sitter build` writes, exporting `tree_sitter_NAME()`), loaded by the
  CLI: `--code-language=LIBRARY` (repeatable) for `sxml xpath`, `sxml xquery`
  and `sxml transform` (D44: one flag; it works on Linux, macOS and Windows;
  under WASI the platform has no loader and the flag reports "this platform
  loads no libraries", exit 3, as `--allow-file-access` has no Windows file
  system). The name is the file name without directory, extension, `lib` and
  `tree-sitter-`, with `-` made `_`; the queries are `queries/` beside the
  library (a grammar repository after `tree-sitter build`), else
  `../queries/NAME/` (Neovim's parser/ and queries/ layout); without
  highlights.scm there, no queries. Errors: a name that names no language (2),
  a library that does not load or lacks the function (3, with dlerror's text),
  another ABI or a query that does not fit (1, with the byte offset and the
  file). The CLI framework gains `sxml_cli_library_loader` (cli_command.h), the
  platform layer `apps/sxml/platform_library_loader.c` (dlopen RTLD_NOW |
  RTLD_LOCAL, dlsym; LoadLibraryW, GetProcAddress), which the platform-layer
  lint rule names; libraries stay loaded until exit. Test:
  tree-sitter/run-time-language builds the vendored JSON grammar as a module
  with the entry point tree_sitter_testjson, no network.
- **Run-time language files: delayed, with reasons**. (a) tree-sitter's
  WebAssembly language files (`tree-sitter-NAME.wasm`, web-tree-sitter's) in
  the JavaScript package: each is a dylink side module that imports the main
  module's memory, indirect function table, stack pointer,
  `__memory_base`/`__table_base` and libc (malloc, iswspace, ...). sxml.wasm is
  a WASI SDK static module (not `-fPIC`/`--experimental-pic`), exports no table
  or stack pointer, and its tree-sitter is C inside it, so a language file
  cannot be linked into it. Doing it means building sxml.wasm as a PIC main
  module and a small dynamic linker in the package's JavaScript (what
  web-tree-sitter does): a later packet, medium to large, with its own size
  cost. (b) The same files natively, through tree-sitter's wasm store
  (`ts_wasm_store_new`): it needs wasmtime's C API, a JIT runtime of several MB
  built with Rust; rejected for sxml, which is a small embeddable C library
  with no JIT (D12's spirit), and native hosts have shared libraries anyway.
  (c) The host shim (bindings/host) and so Kotlin and Swift: the shim's
  configuration would pass languages through; Phase 6 is paused (D255), so it
  waits for 6.12; a grammar pointer across JNI needs its own design.
- **Not shipped**: Rust and Bash as built-ins (the owner), D285's sizes; they
  are one `--code-language` away. markdown_inline's wiki_link and tag
  extensions are not in the generated parser (upstream generates them only with
  EXTENSION_WIKI_LINK/EXTENSION_TAGS), so their 8 corpus tests fail; one spec
  test has no divider (an error of the corpus).
- **Measured** (debug ASan/UBSan): tree-sitter/suite 630 of 639 to 1,410 of
  1,438 (corpus 1,223 of 1,251, 19 not run; highlights 187 of 187: the 7 locals
  and 2 injections assertions pass); the baseline is 1,410. The book's chapter:
  32 examples, all match (D285's 18 updated: a reference to a parameter is
  `variable.parameter`). source_code_test gains the checks and registered
  languages; CLI help goldens show the flag. Sizes: sxml.wasm 9,693,235 /
  2,006,198 to 13,425,285 / 2,411,765 (+3,730,635 code and data, 3,671,000 of
  it the four grammars, 95 % parse tables), budget 14,000,000 / 2,800,000; the
  CLI module 15,026,404 / 2,696,842, budget 15,500,000 / 2,900,000.

**Sources**: tree-sitter/suite passes before and after (corpus and highlights

### D290. Invisible XML for large inputs: regular tokens, sparse item sets, text runs (packet 7.24)

**Summary**: Invisible XML handles inputs of hundreds of MB by matching each
`regular_token` with a `token_automaton`, keeping item sets only where items
are, using byte offsets and storing kept characters as one `text_run`.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D71, D99, D215, D283. The owner: sxml's iXML usable
on tens to hundreds of MB; the book first (f560fdf), then the tests (ef46866),
then the implementation (fdff1ee); one parser (D215). Done; the chapter is no
longer a draft (d46f559).

- **Regular tokens** (`src/ixml_tokens.c`, glossary `regular_token`,
  `token_automaton`): a nonterminal whose language is regular (no recursion but
  a repetition's left recursion, through every nonterminal it uses) and whose
  XML is its text or nothing (every use inside hidden, no insertion, its
  terminals all kept or all hidden) is compiled with the grammar, so once per
  parse function: Thompson's construction, then the subset construction, each
  state keeping the number of paths, 1 or 2+, that reach each NFA state. Paths
  are derivations, so an end reached two ways is an ambiguous completion, as
  Earley marks it; an empty loop counts as many, as Earley's items do. Limits:
  512 NFA states, 8 distinct terminals (a column is a set of them), 1,024 DFA
  states; a nonterminal over them stays an ordinary rule, and the tokens it
  uses get automata in turn. Only tokens used by a rule that is not one get an
  automaton.
- **The rule for ends**: predicting a token runs its automaton, and every end
  it reaches is a completed item there; longest match is not iXML's semantics.
  An end is kept when the next character can follow one of the token's uses
  outside its own rules (the lookahead sets of the dotted rules after its uses,
  which a left recursion's own FOLLOW would not filter); later ends wait in a
  heap and are added at the start of their set, in origin order, ahead of the
  scanned items. So the items a successful parse reads, its tree and its XML
  are those of the parser without tokens, and its ambiguity too: the token's
  item is marked exactly when its rules' items would mark a derivation of the
  same text. A parse that fails with tokens is parsed again without them, so
  the failure document (where, what was expected) is the same; failures pay
  twice. An ambiguous parse may show another of its trees than 7.21 did (any is
  allowed, the Specification, "Parsing"); the suite's listed trees still match.
- **Memory** (measured, then chosen): at the end of a parse 85 to 97 % of the
  items are on the first derivation (log, csv, calc, markdown, numbers), so a
  collector freeing sets behind the parse would save at most 15 %; the
  derivation itself had to shrink. Item sets exist only where items are,
  numbered (glossary `item_set_number`), and an item's origin is a set number;
  positions are byte offsets in the UTF-8 input, which is borrowed (copied only
  to normalize a CR), not decoded into 4-byte codepoints; the parse tree has no
  nodes for hidden nonterminals (their children are the parent's) or hidden
  terminals, and kept characters next to each other are one `text_run` (a node
  grows 24 to 28 bytes); waiting entries, hash tables, the heap and the sets
  but their positions are released before the tree is read out; Leo chains are
  recorded in two passes without a frame stack. Internal header only
  (`src/ixml_internal.h`); no public header changed.
- **Steps**: one per token run and one per 16 characters it reads (a character
  costs an automaton a few instructions, an item some hundred); items, Leo
  items and tree symbols one each, as before.
- **Numbers** (release, 1 MB, before -> after, s / MB / MB per further MB): log
  0.196/90/84 -> 0.059/21/9.9; csv 0.32/120/113 -> 0.22/61/53; calc
  0.54/204/195 -> 0.33/95/86; markdown 0.34/119/111 -> 0.22/65/57; right
  recursion 0.36/136/128 -> 0.14/46/38; log 10 MB 2.0 s/831 MB -> 0.61 s/124
  MB; log 100 MB beyond the default step limit (about 8 GB) -> 6.2 s/1.17 GB
  within it. Of the log's 9.9 MB per MB, about 8.4 are the XML tree itself (the
  arena tree, not this packet's): the parser's own share fell from about 75 to
  under 2. The ambiguous sum misses D283's 2 s bound on this machine before and
  after (3.7 and 3.1 s; a marked item's hash slot now says so).
- **Verified**: iXML suite 886 of 907 unchanged (21 not run, as D283); QT4
  fn-invisible-xml 16/16 (XP40, XQ40), app-spec-examples' iXML cases; the debug
  preset's ixml, ixml/suite, cli and function_library tests (ASan, UBSan, every
  allocation failure); clang-tidy on the changed files; no call cycles;
  ixml_fuzz 600 s, 51,351 runs, no finding; the five iXML chapters' 42
  examples.
- **Left**: tokens whose terminals are mixed (`-quoted: -'"', (~['"']; -'"',
  '"')*, -'"'` in csv) could be read by an automaton too, the kept characters
  found by walking the unique path back at tree time; csv met its bound without
  it.

**Sources**: iXML parse time, peak memory and memory per further MB of log,
csv, calc, markdown and right recursion at 1 MB, log at 10 and 100 MB, and the
ambiguous sum, before and after (`tests/bench/run-ixml-bench.py`, release
build); share of items on the first derivation at the end of a parse (log, csv,
calc, markdown, numbers); iXML suite passes, unchanged
(`tests/ixml/run-ixml-tests.sh`, `ctest`, debug build); QT4 fn-invisible-xml
(XP40, XQ40) and app-spec-examples iXML cases (`tools/run-qt4.sh`); ixml_fuzz
for 600 s, 51,351 runs (`tools/fuzz.sh`); the five iXML chapters' 42 examples
(`tools/check-book-examples.sh`).

### D291. XSLT per-package items, an absent global focus through call-template, namespace undeclarations (packet 4.31)

**Summary**: An element that does not inherit namespaces needs no tree change,
call-template from a global passes an absent focus, and accumulators,
strip-space and fn:function-lookup visibility work per package.

Recorded 2026-10-20, after D69, D99, D163, D245, D287, D289. Verified as D181
asks: the debug preset (xslt*, cli, function_library*, processor, xquery*,
xpath*, evaluator*, ir* tests), clang-tidy on the changed files, the call-cycle
check, the QT4 sets the loader and fn:function-lookup touch (XQ40/XP40
fn-function-lookup, fn-doc, fn-doc-available, fn-collection, prod-ModuleImport:
equal to docs/CONFORMANCE.md), and the whole XT40 suite with the release driver
after each change, case by case. **XT40 12,268 to 12,273 passed (99 to 98 wrong
error), 250 to 245 failed, 0 errors, no case lost**, from a whole run at
fdff1ee. No public header changed. Commits 4df51df, bb89091.

- **Namespace undeclarations need no tree change**: D289's sketch was wrong.
  The tree has stored an element that does not inherit its parent's namespaces
  since D69 (sxml_element_start_event's ignores_parent_namespaces; copies send
  undeclarations for the descendants, sxml_tree_builder_copy_node), and XSLT's
  inherit-namespaces="no" (xsl:element, xsl:copy, literal result elements;
  5.7.1, 11.1.2) and XQuery's copy-namespaces no-inherit use it. Probed:
  in-scope-prefixes of namespace-2606's b and c are right, and its
  serialization (XML 1.1, undeclare-prefixes) is the expected file's byte for
  byte except whitespace. namespace-2606 fails only because its expected file
  is indented while the stylesheet does not indent (assert-xml compares
  whitespace text nodes): **the suite decides**, left. So does document-2402
  (its overriding template "a" has no visibility, so it is private, 3.4.5.3,
  and no initial template: XTDE0040, 2.4.4; document-2401, which says public,
  passes).
- **An absent global focus through xsl:call-template** (3.4.9, 10.1.2, 11.9.1):
  a call from a global, whose focus is the global context item, is `if
  (exists(try { item } catch err:XPDY0002 { () })) then template(item, 1, 1,
  ...) else template-absent((), 0, 0, ...)`, the template's absent-focus
  function (D144) chosen at run time; an XSLT error mapping with no raised code
  catches to the empty sequence (copy-4308: XTTE0945).
- **fn:map-for-key#2** (20.2.3: "If the argument is omitted or empty, the
  selected subtree is the document containing the context node"): $top is
  node()? and the caller's context value is passed after it, the empty sequence
  where the focus is statically absent (D287's is_empty_without_focus); none
  gives XTDE1270 (map-for-key-005). Left: in a global whose global context item
  is absent at run time, reading it for the hidden argument raises XPDY0002

- **Accumulators per package** (3.5.3.1, 19.8): an accumulator's definition
  records its package; XTSE3350 compares declarations of one package; each
  package has its own fn:accumulator-before and -after (as fn:key, D163), which

- **The package of a static context**: sxml_ir_static_context gains
  package_number (the index of the package's top module,
  sxml_xslt_package_top_module; 0 outside XSLT), set on each XSLT module. Two
  uses:

  - *fn:document and fn:doc strip by their package's xsl:strip-space* (4.2.2):

  - *fn:function-lookup by visibility* (10.3.5: only a function in the static
