matches (release build); QT4 XP40 and XQ40 regex sets and XT40 regex groups,
release drivers, before and after, case by case (`tools/run-qt4.sh`,
`tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); 14,400 random regexes over random inputs
through fn:analyze-string, before and after; configured: the start filter walk,
a stack of 32 and at most 256 visits (from `src/regex.c`).

### D311. Required literals in regex search (packet perf-9)

**Summary**: A compiled regex records a `required_literal` that every match
contains, and a search finds its next occurrence with memchr and memcmp and
skips the start positions no match can begin at.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D53, D71, D105, D308, D310. No public header
changed.

- **Whom it serves**: callers of the regex functions whose regex must spell a
  literal that the input seldom holds, above all SchXslt: its expansion of
  abstract patterns calls `replace($s, "(\W*)\$name(\W*)", ...)` for every
  parameter on every test expression. Such a regex can match the empty string
  before a "$", so D310's start filter skipped nothing and every position was
  attempted, though no match exists without "$name": `sxml_regex_matcher_scan`
  was 12.9 % of the expand stage.
- **Mechanism** (glossary `required_literal`, `read_set`; all in
  `src/regex.c`): when a regex is compiled, a CODEPOINT instruction is required
  when MATCH cannot be reached from the first instruction while avoiding it
  (the successors the matcher can take: both ways of a split, a counted loop's
  choice and a character repetition); the CODEPOINT instructions after it then
  run right after it, so their run is in every match, contiguous. Of the first
  16 candidates the longest required run is kept, its first 32 bytes as UTF-8.
  The instructions reachable without the run read every character a match reads
  before its first occurrence; their read set is the literal's prefix (a
  back-reference or "." with s: anything). At search time the scan finds the
  literal's next occurrence (memchr, memcmp), walks back from it while the
  characters are in the prefix read set, and skips the positions before that;
  when the literal does not occur, it skips every position left. A position
  skipped counts one step within the step limit, as D310 settled (skipped
  positions of an ASCII string are counted from bytes, otherwise from
  codepoints). The start filter's first characters became a read set too.
  Correct because a match starting at p reads the literal at some q' at or
  after the first occurrence q found from p, and every character in [p, q') is
  read by a prefix instruction.
- **What is not required, or not analysed**: a regex with lookahead or
  lookbehind (their regexes read characters a match does not consume) or more
  than 256 instructions gets none, and the analysis walks a fixed stack (D71).
  Alternations, optional parts, repetitions and counted loops follow from the
  graph (a counted loop's body is never required: its choice may leave). Under
  flag i a character with case variants is a class, so only characters without
  variants form a literal; q and x are compiled away first; anchors, \\b and
  multi-line mode read nothing, so they do not change the literal and only
  restrict the attempts made. `sxml_regex_matcher_match_at` (XSD pattern
  facets) is unchanged.
- **Measured** (release, x86_64; valgrind instructions of the process, 10^6,
  and processor seconds, the fastest runs on a shared machine), before / after:

  - SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931 (step bound raised in a scratch build
    only): 75,266.6 / 65,844.7 (-12.5 %), scan 12.87 % / 0.42 % of it,
    inclusive; 10.68 / 9.14 s; the same output;
  - bench-real.xsl (n=50, mode=regex): 2,626.5 / 2,221.5; 0.320 / 0.256 s;
  - `tests/bench/regex-literal.xq` (new, registered in `run-bench.py`): 5,482.3
    / 1,781.7; 0.458 / 0.186 s;
  - `tests/bench/regex-reuse.xq`: 1,417.3 / 1,180.3; 0.145 / 0.130 s;
  - `tests/bench/regex-match.xq`: 6,152.4 / 6,174.5 (+0.36 %: its literals are
    found where the start filter already skipped); 0.595 / 0.600 s;
  - 5,000 distinct regexes compiled: 199.6 / 201.8, about 440 instructions more
    a compile; `"(\W*)\$PARAMn(\W*)"`: 250.5 / 256.8.
- **Checked**: QT4 XP40 and XQ40 fn-analyze-string, fn-matches, fn-matches.re,
  fn-matching-segments, fn-regex, fn-replace, fn-tokenize and XT40
  analyze-string, regex, regex-syntax, regex-syntax-xslt20 with the release
  drivers: 4,405 pass, 10 fail, 1 wrong error, 1,154 not run, before and after,
  0 outcomes differ case by case. 14,400 random regexes (literals, classes,
  groups, back-references, assertions, anchors, quantifiers; flags i, m, s, q,
  x) on random inputs of up to 40 characters through fn:analyze-string, and
  3,600 in SchXslt's shape through fn:analyze-string, fn:tokenize and
  fn:replace: the same output, except one search that reached the step limit
  before and now ends with the right result (`[^a].(.+?)+?A\S`: the positions
  after the last "A" are skipped).
- **Left**: a literal inside a counted loop or an assertion is not used; the
  step limit of a search can now be reached later than before, never sooner.

**Sources**: valgrind instructions and processor seconds before / after:
SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931 (scratch build, step bound raised) with
sxml_regex_matcher_scan's share, bench-real.xsl, regex-literal.xq,
regex-reuse.xq, regex-match.xq, 5,000 distinct regexes (`valgrind`,
`tests/bench/run-bench.py`, release build); QT4 XP40 and XQ40 regex sets and
XT40 regex groups, release drivers, before and after, case by case
(`tools/run-qt4.sh`, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); 14,400 random regexes
and 3,600 in SchXslt's shape on random inputs, before and after; configured:
the first 16 candidates, 32 bytes of literal, 256 instructions analysed (from
`src/regex.c`).

### D313. The owner's decisions of 2026-10-28: Schematron, source locations, the CLI's step limit

**Summary**: The owner fixes Schematron's edition, query bindings, outputs and
exit status, makes source locations of parsed documents a processor setting
AUTOMATIC, ALWAYS or NEVER, and removes the CLI's step limit.

Recorded 2026-10-28 by the orchestrator, from the owner's answers to the open
points of packet 7.27 and of the "Source locations for parsed input documents"
item that was under "## Proposed" (moved here).

**Schematron (packet 7.27, its design follows these):**

1. The edition is ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025 (4th edition, with `group`, `library`
   and `rules`, and the XSLT 3.1 and XQuery 3.1 binding); older schemas are
   read as the 4th edition reads them.
2. Query bindings: `xslt`, `xslt2`, `xslt3`, `xslt4` and `xpath`, `xpath2`,
   `xpath3`, `xpath31`, `xpath4` are accepted. A schema without `queryBinding`,
   and `xslt`, `xpath` and the reserved `xslt4` and `xpath4`, are read as XSLT
   4.0 and XPath 4.0, the versions sxml implements (D315, points B and 2a; as
   first recorded on 2026-10-28, a missing attribute was read as `xslt3`, never
   as XSLT 1.0, whose stylesheets sxml refuses with XTDE0160). `xquery3` is
   rejected in one place with the error the standard gives.
3. Outputs: text and `--format=json` as for XSD, and `--format=svrl`.
4. Exit status 1 for a failed `assert` or a fired `report` whose role or flag
   is `fatal` or `error`, or that has neither; findings with other roles
   (warning, info) are printed and leave the status 0.
5. `--schema` with `--schematron`: XSD validation first, then the Schematron
   rules over the typed result; both reported, also when XSD validation fails.
6. SchXslt 1.10.1 (MIT) is vendored in `third_party/` as the reference of a
   differential test only; nothing of it ships.

**Source locations for parsed input documents** (the owner's direction:
optional, and on by default where it matters):

- A processor setting with three values, `AUTOMATIC` (the zero value),
  `ALWAYS`, `NEVER`, for the documents sxml parses: by
  `sxml_processor_parse_document`, `fn:doc`, `fn:parse-xml`, `fn:collection`.
- 7. Under `AUTOMATIC` a document that a host parses before any program is
     compiled keeps its locations. Where sxml parses on a program's behalf, the
     compiled program decides: locations are kept when it calls `fn:location`,
     can reach functions dynamically (`fn:function-lookup`,
     `fn:load-xquery-module`, `fn:transform`, `xsl:evaluate`), or is a
     Schematron or XSD validation. `xpath` and `xquery` in the sxml command
     compile before they parse `--context-item`.
- 8. A dynamic error that names an input node prints its line and column when
     the node's document kept its locations.
- `--locations=always|never|automatic` in the sxml command; the same three
  values in the JavaScript package.
- Cost measured: 32 bytes a node; a 26 MB document of about 2.5 million nodes,
  release build, x86_64 Xeon 2.1 GHz: peak memory 171 MB without, 248 MB with
  (+45 %), time 3.0–3.2 s against 3.2–3.3 s. Streamed input builds no tree and
  pays nothing. Packet 7.29.

**The sxml command's step limit** (9): the sxml command sets no evaluation step
limit; a long run is stopped by the person running it. The library's default
(D89, D259) stays for embedders and the JavaScript package; the conformance
drivers keep their own bounds (D166, D178). Packet cli-4.

**SchXslt upstream** (10): the sort-once fix for `schxslt:replace-params` is
not offered upstream.

**Sources**: cost of source locations: bytes a node, peak memory and time of a
26 MB document of about 2.5 million nodes, without and with (x86_64 Xeon 2.1
GHz) (release build).

### D314. The sxml command asks for no step bound (packet cli-4)

**Summary**: The sxml command sets `maximum_evaluation_step_count` to
`UINT64_MAX`, so its runs have no step bound in practice, while embedders and
the JavaScript package keep the library default.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D313 (9), D89, D259.

- **Mechanism**: the command's one processor configuration
  (`apps/sxml/query_command.c`, shared by xpath, xquery, transform, serialize,
  validate and check) sets
  `sxml_processor_limits.maximum_evaluation_step_count` to `UINT64_MAX`
  (`SXML_QUERY_MAXIMUM_EVALUATION_STEP_COUNT`). The header has no value for "no
  bound": 0 means the library's default of 10^8. The largest count is no bound
  in practice (about 585 years at a step a nanosecond), and the charge in
  `sxml_dynamic_context_charge_steps` cannot overflow at it. No named constant
  is proposed: the header's interface stays as it is (D99), and an embedder
  that wants no bound writes the same value.
- **Kept**: the library's default for embedders and the JavaScript package; the
  conformance drivers' bounds (D166, D178); entity expansion stays bounded to 4
  MiB; a run is stopped with Ctrl-C.
- **Test**: `cli/xpath_no_step_limit`, `(1 to 20000) = (1 to 20000)`: a general
  comparison is charged a step per pair up front (D89), 4 x 10^8, and finds its
  match at once. It gave LIMIT_EXCEEDED (exit 4) before and gives true() now,
  in milliseconds under every preset; a loop of 10^8 real steps takes 25 s in a
  loaded release build and far longer under the sanitizers, so no test runs
  one.
- **Book**: "The step limit" (performance.md) shows the command running past
  the default and says how to stop a run; appendix-differences.md,
  ixml-performance.md and javascript.md cite it; c.md still shows the default
  for a C program. `docs/CLI.md` has a "Limits" rule.

### D315. Schematron as a front end to the XSLT AST: the design (packet 7.27)

**Summary**: Schematron compiles as a front end to the XSLT AST: a reader
resolves inclusions, a builder emits one mode per pattern with template rules
for rules, and XSLT's compiler collects every error.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D24, D44, D52, D99, D102, D162, D165, D183 and the
owner's answers in D313, which this record follows. Brings Schematron into
Phase 7 (PLAN.md names XSD only) as packets 7.27 (this design, for the owner's
review) and 7.28 (the implementation). The public header is
`include/sxml/schematron.h` (new, additive; implemented by nothing until 7.28).
Glossary: the Schematron terms of 2026-10-28 (`schematron` to `svrl`).
**Revised 2026-10-28** after the owner's review of the first version (points A
to D below) and against the text of ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025, which the owner
bought. "Where the standard overturned the first version" lists what changed
and why. **Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-28**, with the answers to the
revision's eight choices under "The owner's answers".

**Sources.** ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025 (the fourth edition), cited by clause and
annex (5.4.x elements, 5.5.x ancillary elements and attributes, 6.x semantics,
Annex A the grammar, B the additional constraints, C and H to N the query
bindings, D SVRL, informative). Where the standard leaves behaviour
implementation-defined, SchXslt 1.10.1 (`2.0/include.xsl`, `expand.xsl`,
`compile/compile-2.0.xsl`, `compile/templates.xsl`, `svrl.xsl`, named where
used), which implements the third edition, is the precedent, and the choice is
said to be sxml's.

**The owner's review** (2026-10-28), applied here:

- A. Compiling reports every error of the `.sch` through a report sink, as XSD
  compilation does, instead of stopping at the first.
- B, amending D313 point 2: an explicit `queryBinding="xslt"` or `"xpath"`, and
  a schema without the attribute, are read as XSLT 4.0 and XPath 4.0, the
  versions sxml implements (not as `xslt3`, which D313 read a missing attribute
  as). The 1.0 differences this accepts are listed under "Query bindings".
- C. A schema with an unsupported binding gives exit status 1 in the sxml
  command, not 4, with an error code naming the construct.
- D. The 2025 constructs the first version rejected or left unverified are
  designed from the text, below. Nothing of the 2025 edition is rejected now;
  `schematron:unsupported` is gone.

**Whom it serves, who pays.** First the maintainer of a rule set (every error
at `rules.sch:LINE:COLUMN` in one run, also inside abstract patterns) and the
person reading a finding (the document's line and column beside the XPath);
then hosts in C and JavaScript that validate many documents without a
third-party stylesheet or its 10 s compile. They pay: a reader, an expander and
a builder in C (six source files), one public header, the `validate` command's
options, the JavaScript API, a book chapter, and two small entries in existing
files (`src/xslt_read.c` reads one foreign declaration into a given AST;
`src/xslt.c` compiles a given AST). Nothing per event of XPath, XQuery or XSLT:
no IR kind, no evaluator change, no generated XSLT text. Validation costs one
walk of the document per active pattern (EN 16931: 3, XRechnung: 4).

**The path.**

1. *Read* (`src/schematron_read.c`): the schematron document is parsed by the
   processor's XML parser into an arena tree with locations; one walk with an
   explicit stack (D71) resolves inclusions in place (6.2): `sch:include`
   (5.4.6) and `sch:extends href` (5.4.4), each document parsed once, by
   absolute URI; a document on the path of inclusions is `schematron:include`.
   It checks the query binding first (see "Query bindings"), and records the
   *index*: the `ns`, schema `param`, `let`, `phase`, `pattern` and `group`
   (abstract or not), `rules`, `diagnostics`, `properties`, `title` and foreign
   XSLT children of the schema, those an external declaration brings included,
   in order, as (tree, node) pairs, with tables of ids for patterns, abstract
   rules, diagnostics, properties and phases. Every error found goes to the
   report sink and reading goes on (A).
2. *Choose*: the phase (`#DEFAULT` gives `defaultPhase`, else `#ALL`; `#ANY`
   keeps every phase with a `when` and every pattern; an unknown id is
   `schematron:phase`) and the patterns it can make active, in schema order.
3. *Build* (`src/schematron_build.c`, placeholders in
   `src/schematron_expand.c`): one walk per compiled pattern over its elements
   (for a pattern instance, over its abstract pattern's, with the instance's
   parameter table in force; `sch:extends rule` pushes the abstract rule's
   children), emitting stylesheet AST nodes (`sxml_xslt_ast_add_node`,
   `_add_attribute`, `_append_child`, `_take_expression`) with `source_node`
   the Schematron element and its location. Each expression and rule context is
   parsed alone, so a syntax error in one is reported and the walk goes on. Two
   walks rather than one because an instance may precede its abstract pattern
   and phases follow patterns; both are linear.
4. *Compile*: only when steps 1 to 3 found no error, the sealed AST goes
   through what `sxml_xslt_compile` does after reading (in-scope schemas,
   lowering, outputs), split out of `src/xslt.c` as an internal entry that
   takes an AST and the report sink. 7.28 gives XSLT's compiler that sink (the
   owner, 7b): its errors (an unknown variable or function, a type error, an
   error in an XSLT declaration) are all collected too (see "Compile errors").
5. *Validate*: one transformation per call, in the initial mode
   `Q{urn:sxml:schematron}validate`, initial match selection the node, global
   context item `root(node)` (the instance document root of 5.4.7, 5.4.12,
   5.5.7, 5.5.22), raw delivery. Its raw result is the sequence of finding
   items (under `#ANY`, first an item naming the phase chosen);
   `src/schematron.c` turns each into an `sxml_schematron_report`, counts it,
   gives it to the sink and the SVRL writer.

**The stylesheet the builder makes**, shown as XSLT text for reading only (none
is ever written; `s` is `urn:sxml:schematron`, which keeps synthesized names
apart from the schema's):

<xsl:stylesheet version="4.0"> one synthesized root per schematron document;
version by binding <xsl:variable name="L" select="V" as="T"/> schema lets, the
phase's lets, pattern lets <xsl:variable name="s:phase"> #ANY only: the first
phase whose when is true <xsl:choose><xsl:when
test="WHEN-1">1</xsl:when>...<xsl:otherwise>0</xsl:otherwise></xsl:choose>
</xsl:variable> <xsl:param name="s:fired-rules" select="false()"/> ...foreign
XSLT declarations, read by src/xslt_read.c... <xsl:template match="."
mode="s:validate"> <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="s:pattern-1"/> each
active pattern, in order <xsl:variable name="s:from" select="FROM"/> a phase
with from= (5.5.7) <xsl:apply-templates select="$s:from except
$s:from/descendant::node()" mode="s:pattern-1"/> <xsl:variable name="s:base"
select="base-uri(root(.))"/> <xsl:for-each select="DOCUMENTS"> a pattern with
documents= <xsl:apply-templates select="doc(resolve-uri(string(.), $s:base))"
mode="s:pattern-2"/> </xsl:for-each> </xsl:template> <xsl:template
match="document-node() | element()" mode="s:pattern-1" priority="-1">
<xsl:apply-templates select="@\* | node()" mode="#current"/> </xsl:template>
<xsl:template match="attribute() | text() | comment() |
processing-instruction()" mode="s:pattern-1" priority="-1"/> <xsl:template
match="CONTEXT" mode="s:pattern-1" priority="N-K"> rule K of N <xsl:variable
name="L" select="V"/> the rule's lets, those of extends in place <xsl:if
test="$s:fired-rules"> FIRED-RULE ITEM </xsl:if> <xsl:for-each
select="VISIT-EACH"> a rule with visit-each= (5.5.21); else none
<xsl:choose><xsl:when test="TEST"/><xsl:otherwise> FINDING ITEM
</xsl:otherwise></xsl:choose> <xsl:if test="TEST"> FINDING ITEM </xsl:if> a
report </xsl:for-each> <xsl:apply-templates select="@\* | node()"
mode="#current"/> in a pattern <xsl:next-match/> in a group, instead
</xsl:template> </xsl:stylesheet>

Under `#ANY` the validate template is an `xsl:choose` on `$s:phase`, one branch
per phase with a `when` (its from and its active patterns), the last applying
every pattern.

- *User text is never spliced into synthesized text*: each `context`, `test`,
  `subject`, `select`, `path`, `value`, `documents`, `from`, `when`,
  `visit-each` and the expressions of a dynamic attribute value is parsed alone
  into its own expression AST (pattern AST for `context`) with the spans of its
  attribute, and the synthesized expressions (`.`, `base-uri(root(.))`,
  `$s:fired-rules`, `$s:from except ...`) are fixed texts. So an assert's
  negation is `xsl:choose` with an empty `xsl:when`, not `not(TEST)` (6.2
  allows either), and `sch:name path="P"` is `xsl:for-each select="P"` over
  `xsl:value-of select="node-name(.)"` (Annex J: fn:node-name of the result, as
  a string).
- *A finding item* (glossary `finding_item`, internal): an `xsl:array` whose
  members are the assertion's index in the schematron's table (an integer
  literal), the subject node, the values of the dynamic attribute values (role,
  flag, severity) that are not static, the message, then one member per
  diagnostic and per property it names, in order. A fired-rule item is the
  rule's index, `.` and its dynamic role and flag. The table holds everything
  static of each assertion and rule (ids, static role, flag and severity, see,
  icon, fpi, xml:lang, test, context and visit-each texts, rule title, the
  pattern, the element's location), so an item carries only what evaluation
  gives.
- *Subject and message context*: the subject (5.5.19) is what the assertion's
  `subject`, else the rule's, selects with the rule's context node as context
  item (a `xsl:for-each` over a variable bound to the context node, so a
  visit-each item does not change it); else the context item when it is a node;
  else, for a visit-each item that is not a node, the rule's context node. A
  subject attribute that gives other than one node is XPTY0004 at its location.
  The message's `value-of` and `name` are evaluated with the *message context*
  (6.3): the subject node when a subject attribute applies, else the context
  item (the visit-each item, as 5.5.21's example needs). Diagnostics and
  properties are evaluated with the context item: 6.3 names only the message,
  and 5.5.1 and 5.5.13 only the variables.
- *Priorities*: rule K of N in a pattern has priority N - K, so the first
  matching rule wins (6.3, 6.6: a rule fires unless a previous rule of the
  pattern matched the item; XSLT's own rule, distinct priorities never
  conflict), and the traversal templates at -1 come last. In a pattern the rule
  template walks on itself; in a group it ends with `xsl:next-match`, so every
  matching rule fires (5.4.5, 6.6) and the chain ends at the traversal
  template. The traversal templates are explicit, not
  `on-no-match="shallow-skip"`, because built-in rules pass parameters on and
  the walk must not carry any. Text nodes reach rule templates whose context
  matches them (the bindings allow it at user option, Annexes C, H, J; sxml
  always does).
- *Modes per pattern, not per documents group*: SchXslt puts every pattern
  without `documents` into one mode and lets each rule template check a
  sequence of "patterns matched" passed along `xsl:next-match`
  (`compile-2.0.xsl`, `schxslt:rule`). A mode per pattern makes XSLT's own rule
  selection do Schematron's, needs no parameter per node, and gives the reports
  grouped by pattern without buffering (6.6 leaves the order to the
  implementation); it costs a walk per pattern. Rejected SchXslt's form for
  that reason.
- *from* (5.5.7): evaluated at the instance root; its nodes, less those inside
  another of them (so no node is visited twice), are where the phase's patterns
  start instead of the node; an item that is not a node is XPTY0004. Not for
  patterns with `documents` (5.5.7). Variables outside rules are unaffected
  (5.5.7), being globals.

**The mapping, construct by construct.**

- `schema` (5.4.17): `queryBinding` (see "Query bindings"); `defaultPhase` (an
  id that names no phase is `schematron:reference`); `title`, `schemaVersion`
  and `schematronEdition` go to SVRL and to `sxml_schematron_describe`; `id` is
  not used. `schematronEdition` (5.5.15): any value is accepted, never an error
  (the owner, 8b; the "shall be 2025" binds schema authors), and its value or
  absence is reported at user option, as 5.5.15 requires, by
  `sxml_schematron_describe`, the CLI's JSON and SVRL's attribute. `ns prefix
  uri` (5.4.10) are the statically known namespaces of every Schematron
  expression, besides XPath's predeclared ones; the XML namespace declarations
  of the documents are not (5.4.10 says so; SchXslt's generated templates
  agree). *Amended 2026-10-29 (D331):* "XPath's predeclared ones" are the
  prefixes of the function library, `xs`, `fn`, `math`, `map`, `array` and
  `err`, which every binding makes available (Annexes H to L) and which 7.28
  had left out; they are bound without `sch:ns`, an `sch:ns` of one of them
  wins, and `xml` is XPath's own. `sch:p` is not used.
- `pattern` (5.4.12): a mode; `id` names it in reports, `title` gives SVRL's
  `name`, `role` SVRL's `role`; `documents` is evaluated at the instance root,
  its relative IRIs resolved against the instance's base URI, and the pattern
  is applied to those documents and not to the instance (5.4.12); a document
  that cannot be read is a dynamic error that stops the validation (FODC0002;
  5.4.12 makes termination implementation-defined). The pattern's own variables
  are not in scope in `documents` (5.4.12): the builder walks that expression's
  variable references and reports XPST0008 for one.
- `group` (5.4.5): as `pattern`, except that every rule whose context matches
  fires (6.6); SVRL `active-group`.
- `rule` (5.4.15): a template rule; `context` its match pattern: an XSLT 4.0
  pattern, or an *expression rule context* wrapped as one (the owner's
  amendment of 3a, see "Query bindings"); `visit-each` (5.5.21) a
  `xsl:for-each` around the rule's assertions, after its lets and the
  fired-rule item: its items are the context items of the assertions; an empty
  result still counts as fired and evaluates no assertion. The rule's lets are
  evaluated once per context node, before the loop (the owner, 6b: 5.4.7 scopes
  them to the rule and its context, and 5.5.21 replaces the context for
  assertions only), so the visit-each expression and the assertions see them.
  `id`, `role`, `flag`, `see`, `icon`, `fpi` and `title` go to fired-rule
  reports and SVRL; `subject` as above; `abstract="true"` makes it an abstract
  rule.
- `rules` (5.4.16): a container of abstract rules at the top of a schema or a
  library. Abstract rules in a pattern, as the third edition and Annex D.4's
  own schema write them, are read too (the Introduction promises older schemas
  the same results); `extends rule` finds an abstract rule anywhere in the
  schema (Annex B).
- `extends rule="ID"` (5.4.4): the abstract rule's `let`, `assert`, `report`
  and `extends` children in its place, in order (6.2); an id that names no
  abstract rule is `schematron:reference` (Annex B).
- `extends href="IRI"` (5.4.4): the children of the *external declaration* it
  names (the document element without a fragment, else the element the fragment
  names) in its place, not its attributes. Under a rule the declaration must be
  a rule (abstract or not, 5.4.4's note); under a schema or a library, a schema
  or a library (5.4.8: libraries are included this way). Allowed at the top of
  a schema (the foreword; Annex A). Another kind is `schematron:include`. The
  inserted children count as the schema's: their `ns`, `param`, `let`, `phase`,
  patterns, groups, `rules`, `diagnostics`, `properties`; a second `title` is
  not used. The declaration's `queryBinding` is not read (only contents are
  inserted, 5.4.4).
- `include href="IRI"` (5.4.6): the element it names in its place, which must
  be one the grammar allows there (a library never is); otherwise
  `schematron:include`.
- `library` (5.4.8): an allowed document element (Annex A's start) reached only
  by `extends href`; it cannot be compiled alone (`schematron:not-schematron`).
- Inclusion errors (5.4.4, 5.4.6: reported; termination
  implementation-defined): each goes to the sink and reading goes on without
  that element.
- Fixups (6.7, 6.8, XInclude 4.5.5 and 4.5.6): every element is read in its own
  document's tree, so its base URI and its `xml:lang` in scope are those of its
  own document, which is what the fixups give; the same for elements of
  abstract patterns, abstract rules, diagnostics and properties.
- `assert`, `report` (5.4.3, 5.4.14): a condition in the rule template;
  attributes as for `rule`, plus `severity`, `diagnostics` and `properties`
  (lists of ids looked up in the schema's `diagnostics` and `properties`, those
  of included libraries among them; an unknown id is `schematron:reference`).
  Content: text as written, `value-of select` as the string of `string(SELECT)`
  in the message (the select's expression AST as the argument of a static call
  to fn:string, nothing spliced; every binding defines the value-of query as
  fn:string of the result, Annexes C, H to N, corrected after 7.30's suite,
  D317), so a result of more than one item is XPTY0004: a dynamic error that
  stops the validation, located at the `value-of`'s `select` in its schematron
  document, with the instance node (the message context) in the error's
  description. SchXslt and the ISO skeleton use `xsl:value-of`, which joins the
  items with spaces: 7.28's differential test may show findings whose message
  sxml refuses where SchXslt joins, an expected, explained difference (D315),
  not a bug. `name` as above, `emph`, `dir`, `span` and foreign elements by
  their text; whitespace collapsed (5.3) unless `xml:space="preserve"` is in
  scope. Text value templates in messages (Annex J leaves their extent
  implementation-defined) are not read: braces are literal text, as every
  edition before wrote them (the owner, 4a, with the evidence under "The
  owner's answers").
- `let name value as` (5.4.7): `value` is an expression; without it, the
  content is the value (a temporary tree, as `templates.xsl`'s
  `schxslt:let-variable`); `as` is applied as XSLT's (Annexes H, J, 9.1 of
  XSLT) under every binding (Annex C would ignore it). Scopes under
  "Variables".
- `param` (5.4.11): of a schema or library, a schema parameter; of an abstract
  pattern, a declared parameter with an optional default; of an instance, a
  value. Under "Abstract patterns, schema parameters and placeholders".
- `phase` (5.4.13): `id`, `active pattern` (a pattern or group id; otherwise
  `schematron:reference`, Annex B), `let`; `from` (5.5.7) as above; `when`
  (5.5.22) only under `#ANY`: each is evaluated at the instance root, in schema
  order, and the first true one is the phase (`$s:phase`); none true makes
  every pattern active (5.4.13). A phase id `#ALL`, `#ANY` or `#DEFAULT` in a
  schema is `schematron:syntax` (5.4.13).
- `diagnostics/diagnostic`, `properties/property` (5.5.1, 5.5.13): evaluated in
  the rule template for the same context item, with the assertion's variables
  and the instance's parameters in force; `xsl:copy-of` inside a property is
  read as an instruction under the xslt bindings.
- `value-of`, `name`, `emph`, `dir`, `span`, `title`, `p`: as above.
- `flag`, `role`, `severity` (5.5.6, 5.5.14, 5.5.16), *dynamic attribute
  values*: a value that is a variable reference (`$name`, after placeholders
  are replaced, leading and trailing whitespace stripped) is evaluated for the
  context item under every binding; under the xslt bindings the value is an
  attribute value template (Annexes C, H, J), of which a lone `{$name}` is the
  same. Otherwise the value is static, as written. Reports carry the value for
  the finding; SVRL too. A flag "becomes true" when an assertion with it fails
  or a rule with it fires (5.5.6): reports carry each flag, and a host derives
  the set raised; the outcome keeps no set.
- *Error findings* (D313 item 4, extended by 5.5.16; the owner, 1a): a finding
  whose severity is `fatal` or `error` is an error; one with another severity
  is not; without a severity, D313's rule: role or one of the flag's tokens is
  `fatal` or `error`, or it has neither role nor flag. Values compared
  case-sensitively, after evaluation. The assertion's own attributes only, not
  the rule's (5.5.14; Annex D maps only the assertion's to failed-assert and
  successful-report).
- An element or attribute of the Schematron namespace where Annex A does not
  allow it, a missing required attribute, or a value the grammar refuses is
  `schematron:syntax`; foreign elements and attributes are ignored (5.2).

**Variables** (5.4.7, 3.23; 7.2 one definition in scope). Every variable
outside a rule is evaluated at the instance root:

- schema lets: global variables;
- the chosen phase's lets: global variables. Under `#ANY`, one global per name
  the candidate phases define, an `xsl:choose` on `$s:phase` whose branches
  bind each defining phase's value (with its `as` through an inner variable),
  the empty sequence otherwise;
- pattern lets: global variables, so XSLT functions see them as SchXslt makes
  them (XRechnung's `variable-pattern` holds `$XR-IBAN-REGEX`, which
  `xr:checkIBAN` reads). A pattern's variables are scoped to the pattern
  (3.23): when two compiled patterns define one name, each becomes a global
  under a synthesized name and each of its rule templates binds the written
  name to it first (a local variable referring to the global: no second
  evaluation);
- rule lets: template variables, in document order, evaluated once per context
  node before the visit-each loop and the assertions (XRechnung writes some
  after the asserts that do not use them; 6.6 makes let order significant).
- A name defined twice among the scopes around one rule (its schema, the phase,
  its pattern, the rule) is `schematron:variable` (5.4.7), a rule let that
  would shadow an outer variable included; a let and a schema parameter of one
  name too (both are variables, 3.23); a let with the name of an abstract
  pattern's parameter is `schematron:variable` as Annex B asks. A reference to
  an undefined variable is XPST0008 (5.4.7).
- Values from outside: the schema parameters (5.4.11, 6.1's "name-value
  pairs"), given at compile time; lets are not external (the owner, 5a;
  evidence under "The owner's answers").

**Abstract patterns, schema parameters and placeholders** (5.4.11, 6.2, 6.4;
the `$` convention of Annexes C, H, J). A pattern instance's `sch:param`
elements form a table by name; the abstract pattern's own `sch:param` elements
declare its parameters, with their `value` as default. An instance parameter
the abstract pattern does not declare, an instance or abstract pattern naming
one parameter twice, and a declared parameter with no value from either is
`schematron:parameter` (5.4.11, Annex B); an abstract pattern that declares
none (as third-edition schemas write) takes the instance's table as it is.
Schema parameters (`sch:param` of the schema or a library) form a second table;
each needs a `value` (Annex B) unless the configuration gives one, and a
configured name that is no schema parameter is `schematron:parameter`. While
the builder emits an expression attribute (`context`, `test`, `subject`,
`visit-each`, `select` of `value-of` and of `xsl:copy-of` in a property,
`path`, `value` of `let`, `documents`, `from`, `when`, an instance parameter's
`value`, and a dynamic `flag`, `role` or `severity`), one left-to-right scan
copies the text and, at each `$`, takes the run of NCName characters after it,
the *parameter name token*, looks it up whole in the instance's table, then in
the schema's, and copies the value instead; a token that names no parameter
stays as it is, a variable reference or a literal `$` (Annexes C, H, J: a `$`
not followed by the name of a parameter in scope is not a delimiter). EN
16931's 269 and 780 parameters cost one hash lookup per `$`, not 780 regex
passes per attribute (SchXslt's `schxslt:replace-params`, D309's 10 s). A value
is not scanned again, except that an instance parameter's value is itself
scanned once for schema parameters where it is written; SchXslt, which replaces
one name after another over the whole text, also replaces a placeholder that an
earlier value brought in. The differential test of 7.28 shows whether a real
rule set has it. SchXslt does not replace in `subject`; 6.2 replaces in "all
enclosed attributes that contain queries", and this design does (no difference
for EN 16931 or XRechnung, which have no subject). The scan records the
expression's *expansion segments*: a syntax error inside text that a value
brought in is reported at that `sch:param`'s `value` attribute (or "the
configured value of parameter NAME"), with the offset inside it; elsewhere at
the attribute.

**Foreign XSLT.** Under the xslt bindings (`xslt`, `xslt2`, `xslt3`, `xslt4`),
the `xsl:function`, `xsl:key`, `xsl:include`, `xsl:import` and
`xsl:import-schema` children of `sch:schema` (Annex H), and except under
`xslt2` also `xsl:accumulator` and `xsl:use-package` (Annex J), are read by
`src/xslt_read.c` into the same AST, as declarations of the schematron
document's module, through a new internal entry that reads one element subtree
under a given parent: the nodes are exactly those a stylesheet would give.
Annexes place them "before the pattern elements"; sxml reads them wherever they
stand among the schema's children (no result depends on it). Their static
context is their own XML in-scope namespaces plus the `sch:ns` bindings (and,
D331, the function library's prefixes) for prefixes they leave unbound (in
SchXslt the copied element sits under a root that declares every `sch:ns`;
XRechnung's `name="xr:checkIBAN"` needs it). `xsl:include` and `xsl:import`
read their modules as XSLT does (an imported module has lower precedence than
the Schematron rules). Other XSLT children are ignored, as SchXslt ignores
them; under the xpath bindings all are (Annexes I, K, L: no user-written
functions).

**Query bindings** (6.5, Annexes C, H to N; D313 point 2 as the owner amended
it). One function in `src/schematron_read.c` reads `queryBinding` before
anything else of the schema, compares it ignoring case (6.5 and each annex
permit any mix of cases), and maps:

- none, `xslt`, `xslt4`, `xpath`, `xpath4` to XSLT 4.0 and XPath 4.0 (the AST's
  version 4.0). `xslt4` and `xpath4` are reserved by 6.5 without definition;
  sxml reads them as the languages it implements (the owner, 2a);
- `xslt2` and `xpath2` to version 2.0, `xslt3`, `xpath3` and `xpath31` to 3.0
  (the AST's version, which changes nothing a 4.0 processor does: D197, XSLT
  2.0 and 3.0 behaviour is 4.0's);
- every other value (`xquery`, `xquery3`, `xquery31`, `xquery4`, `stx`,
  `exslt`, unknown names) to `schematron:query-binding` at the attribute: "the
  query binding 'xquery3' is not supported; sxml reads xslt, xslt2, xslt3,
  xslt4, xpath, xpath2, xpath3, xpath31 and xpath4" (6.5: an implementation
  that does not support the binding shall fail with an error; the code is
  sxml's, the standard names none). In the sxml command it exits 1 (C). An
  XQuery binding would read expressions with the XQuery front end in this
  function's place.

*What reading `xslt` (and no attribute) as 4.0 accepts* (Annex C defines the
default binding as XSLT 1.0's XPath; sxml has XPath 1.0 compatibility mode,
D197, and does not use it here). A schema written for 1.0 can observe:

1. a function given several nodes where 1.0 took the first (`string(a)`,
   `contains(a, 'x')`, `number(a)`): XPTY0004;
2. `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` between two untyped values compare as strings, not as
   numbers (`@a < @b` with "10" and "9" is true, false in 1.0);
3. `=` between a string and a number, or a value and a boolean: the operand is
   cast or the comparison is XPTY0004 (`'1' = 1`), where 1.0 converted (`@a =
   true()` was `boolean(@a)`, now a cast that fails for "yes" with FORG0001);
4. arithmetic on a non-numeric string or untyped value is an error (XPTY0004,
   FORG0001), not NaN; on the empty sequence it gives (), not NaN;
5. numeric literals with a point are xs:decimal: `1 div 0` is FOAR0001 (1.0:
   Infinity), and string forms differ (`string(1 div 3)`; doubles of 1e6 and
   above print with an exponent);
6. `value-of` over several nodes is XPTY0004 (fn:string, as every binding
   defines it; 1.0 took the first node's value);
7. a `let` keeps its value's type (Annex C makes it a string) and its `as` is
   applied (Annex C ignores it);
8. names, syntax and functions 1.0 lacks are available. The same holds for
   `xpath` (no annex of its own; 6.5 reserves it) read as XPath 4.0.

*What a 2.0 or 3.x schema can observe on sxml's 4.0 processor*: none of the 1.0
differences; what XPath 4.0 and XSLT 4.0 list as incompatible with 3.1, of
which sxml's records name: `fn:doc` and `documents` refuse a document that
refers to an external DTD or entity (FODC0016; trust-external defaults to
false, F&O 4.0 17.1.1, D199); `xsl:key` compares by fn:atomic-equal, so
`key('k', 3.7)` no longer finds the string "3.7" (XSLT 4.0 20.2.2, D289); 4.0's
coercion rules accept some calls that failed in 3.1 (an error can become a
value, never the reverse). 7.28's differential test cannot show these: SchXslt
runs on sxml's 4.0 processor too.

*Rule contexts* (the owner's amendment of 3a). Under every binding a `context`
is parsed first as an XSLT 4.0 pattern and, when it is one, used as one. Under
the xslt bindings that is the standard's reading (Annexes C, H, J name XSLT's
pattern production). Under the xpath bindings it is sxml's choice: Annexes I, K
and L say only that the context is interpreted as an XPath expression, and 6.3
leaves its evaluation context to the binding, which does not define it. The two
readings differ for relative paths: `context="item"` as a pattern matches every
`item` element, as an expression evaluated from the instance root only the
`item` children of the document node. sxml reads such a context as a pattern
because that is what schema authors write and what every implementation does. A
context that is no pattern but a valid XPath 4.0 expression (Annexes I, K, L
define xpath-binding contexts as expressions: `(//item)[1]`, `../x`, `$doc//x`)
is an *expression rule context*: the builder wraps its expression AST,
unchanged and spliced into no text, in the predicate pattern `.[. intersect
$s:context-K]` (K the rule), where `$s:context-K` is a global variable holding
the expression's value evaluated with each *start node* as context item,
`$s:start ! (EXPRESSION)`. The start nodes are those the pattern is applied to:
the instance root (`root(node)`, the root of the validated node's tree), or
under a phase with `from` the nodes `from` selects (`$s:start` is one global,
under `#ANY` an `xsl:choose` on `$s:phase`, 5.5.7). So the context matches
exactly the nodes the expression selects from the instance root, or from the
`from` nodes. In a pattern with `documents` the start is each subordinate
document's root, which a global cannot hold: there the pattern is `.[.
intersect root(.) ! (EXPRESSION)]`. A value with an item that is not a node is
XPTY0004 (intersect). Variables in the expression are the globals (schema,
phase, pattern lets), as for any match pattern. *Cost*, paid only by expression
rule contexts: the expression is evaluated once per validation (per start,
through the global; per tested node in a `documents` pattern), and each node
the mode tests against the rule (nodes no rule of higher priority matched
first) pays one `intersect`, which sxml evaluates as a merge walk over both
operands in document order (`src/evaluator_path.c`): up to m document-order
comparisons for a context selecting m nodes, so O(n·m) per validation over n
tested nodes at worst; negligible for the usual `(//item)[1]`, large for a
context selecting most of a big document (a hash of the selected nodes would
make it O(n + m), a later optimisation, not designed). A context that is
neither a pattern nor an expression gets the expression parser's error
(XPST0003) under the xpath bindings and the pattern parser's (XTSE0340) under
the xslt bindings. XTSE0340 is no longer raised for a valid expression.

**Findings and their two locations.** Each report has `schema_location`, the
assertion's element in its schematron document (absolute URI, line, column of
its start tag; for an abstract pattern, the element in the abstract pattern's
document, with `pattern_id` naming the instance), and the subject node with
`node_location` (its tree's location: the instance's line and column, when the
tree keeps locations, which D313's AUTOMATIC setting does for a validation) and
`node_path` (`fn:path`, SVRL's `location`). Static errors carry the location of
the element or attribute, or of the position inside an expression (through the
expansion segments for placeholders). Dynamic errors carry the location the
XSLT machinery gives the expression: exact for unsubstituted text; for an
expression with placeholders, the spans are placed at the attribute's start
(D169's moved spans would otherwise point past the abstract text), so the line
and column are those of the attribute.

**Compile errors** (A). `sxml_schematron_configuration.report_sink` is
`sxml_schema_report_sink` of `include/sxml/schema.h`, reused: one report of a
compile error (code, description, location) for both schema languages, not a
second kind; its code here is a `schematron:`, XPath or XSLT code, not an XSD
constraint name. Reading, structure, references, variables, parameters and
every expression's syntax are all checked and every error reported (each
expression is parsed alone, so one error per expression); then, when none was
found, the XSLT compile stage reports its errors to the same sink (the owner,
7b). The null sink stops at the first error, as XSD's. The error record keeps
the first error. *XSLT gains the sink* (7.28, the owner's 7b):
`sxml_xslt_configuration` gets a `report_sink` field of the same type
(`include/sxml/xslt.h` includes `schema.h`; additive, its own record in 7.28).
With the null sink a stylesheet compile stops at its first error as today; with
a sink, reading reports every syntax error (one per attribute or expression,
each parsed alone) and goes on, and static analysis reports one error per
declaration or template and goes on with the next; nothing is lowered once an
error was reported. `sxml transform` compiles with a sink that writes each
error as today's one line, `FILE:LINE:COLUMN: CODE: description`, in the order
found, on standard error, and exits 1 after the compile as it does now for the
first; the JavaScript `compileStylesheet` throws an `SxmlError` for the first
as today, with every report in a new `reports` member. Shown in the book where
it shows a stylesheet error.

**SVRL** (D313: one output, made from reports; Annex D, informative). Written
by `src/schematron_svrl.c` from the reports and the compiled schema's static
table (title, `schemaVersion`, `schematronEdition`, phase, `ns`, patterns,
rules): `svrl:schematron-output` (`title`, `phase` the phase in force,
`schemaVersion`, `schematronEdition`), `svrl:ns-prefix-in-attribute-values`,
then for each active pattern `svrl:active-pattern` or for a group
`svrl:active-group` (id, name, role, documents), followed by its
`svrl:fired-rule` (id, name from the rule's title, context, visit-each, role,
flag, document for a subordinate document), `svrl:failed-assert` and
`svrl:successful-report` (id, location, test, role, flag, severity) with
`svrl:diagnostic-reference`, `svrl:property-reference` and `svrl:text` (Annex
D.2 and D.3). `location` is `fn:path` of the subject, as SchXslt's XSLT 3.0
output. Reports arrive pattern by pattern, so SVRL is written as the validation
goes. SVRL asks for the fired rules; they are not counted as findings. Choices:
the message's markup (`emph`, `dir`, `span`) is reduced to its text, in SVRL
too, although D.2 maps them to `svrl:emph`, `svrl:dir` and `svrl:span` (reports
carry text only; Annex D is informative); `sch:p` is not written as
`svrl:text`; no line or column in SVRL, which has no place for them (an
attribute in `urn:sxml` would break SVRL's schema); `svrl:error` is not written
(a dynamic error stops the validation); SchXslt's `svrl:suppressed-rule` and
`svrl:metadata` are not written.

**The C API** (`include/sxml/schematron.h`; golden file
`include/sxml/schema.h`): `sxml_schematron` with `memory_requirements`,
`initialize`, `finalize`, `create`, `destroy`; `sxml_schematron_describe`;
`sxml_schematron_validate_node`; a report sink of `sxml_schematron_report`s.
Choices beyond D313:

- The phase is chosen at compile time (it decides the modes); `#ANY` compiles
  every pattern and its choice in one stylesheet, and the outcome names the
  phase each validation used.
- Compiling reports every error through the report sink, the XSLT compile
  stage's included (A, 7b; first version: stopped at the first).
- Schema parameters are given at compile time as text
  (`sxml_schematron_parameter`: name, query fragment), since they are fragments
  of queries put into expressions (5.4.11); the validation request has no
  parameters (first version: schema lets as stylesheet parameters per
  validation; 5.4.11 makes params, not lets, the values a user overrides; the
  owner, 5a).
- Validation returns `SXML_STATUS_OK` whatever it finds; the outcome counts
  findings and error findings and names the phase. A failed assert is data, not
  a failure of the call (XSD's `sxml_schema_validate_node`, which makes a copy,
  returns an error instead).
- The null sink counts and discards; SVRL is an optional output stream in the
  request rather than an object of its own (one field instead of a writer with
  a lifecycle).
- `FIRED_RULE` reports go to the sink only when asked (`reports_fired_rules`);
  the compiled stylesheet tests one boolean parameter per fired rule otherwise.
- `sch:include` and `extends href` documents are asked of the resolver as
  `SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_XML_DOCUMENT` (they are XML documents; no new kind in
  `processor.h`).
- Error codes in `urn:sxml:schematron`, prefix `schematron`, listed in the
  header: the standard requires errors (5.4.4, 5.4.6, 5.4.7, 6.5, Annex B) and
  names no codes. Annex B's assertion ids are not codes.

**The CLI** (written here; `docs/CLI.md`'s `validate` section belongs to cli-4
now, and 7.28 updates it; D44: no new command):

- `sxml validate --schematron=FILE [--phase=NAME]
  [--schematron-param=NAME=VALUE]... [--schema=XSD]...
  [--format=text|json|svrl] FILE...`. `--schematron` at most once ("-" reads
  standard input, as `--schema`); `--schema` is no longer required when
  `--schematron` is given; `--phase` (an id, `#ALL`, `#ANY`, `#DEFAULT`) or
  `--schematron-param` without `--schematron` is a usage error (2), and so are
  `--format=svrl` without `--schematron` and `--format=svrl` with more than one
  FILE. `--schematron-param` is repeatable and collecting (CLI.md's rule for
  `--param`); a name given twice is a usage error.
- The `.sch` is compiled first (after the XSD schema); every error is reported
  as `SCH:LINE:COLUMN: CODE: description` on standard error, and then no FILE
  is read.
- Each FILE is parsed into a tree with locations. With `--schema`, it is
  validated against the XSD schema first (D313, item 5); when valid, the
  Schematron rules run over the validated copy (typed), otherwise over the
  document as parsed (an invalid document has no validated copy), and both are
  reported.
- Text: each finding on standard error, as XSD errors are, one line:
  `FILE:LINE:COLUMN: ID LEVEL: MESSAGE (SCH:LINE:COLUMN)`, where ID is the
  assertion's id (else `assert` or `report`), LEVEL its severity, else its
  flag, else its role (nothing when it has none), MESSAGE the message, SCH the
  schematron document as XSD names schema documents (relative to the current
  directory). A subject without a line gives its path in place of
  `LINE:COLUMN`. Nothing is printed for a FILE without findings.
- JSON: the one object of today's command gains a `"schematron"` member
  (`{"document":"rules.sch","phase":"#ALL","edition":"2025",
  "status":"valid"}`, `"edition"` the schematronEdition as written, any value,
  null when absent (5.5.15's report at user option; the text form does not show
  it), with `"errors"` when it does not compile) and each file a `"findings"`
  array of objects with `"kind"` (`failed-assert`, `successful-report`),
  `"id"`, `"role"`, `"flag"`, `"severity"`, `"error"` (D313), `"message"`,
  `"line"`, `"column"`, `"byte_offset"`, `"path"`, `"pattern"`, `"test"`,
  `"assertion"` (`{"document","line","column"}`), `"diagnostics"` and
  `"properties"`, and a `"phase"` (the phase in force, which differs from the
  schema's under `#ANY`); a file's `"status"` is `invalid` when the XSD
  validation failed or a finding is an error. Fields are only ever added.
- SVRL: the SVRL document of the one FILE on standard output; errors of the XSD
  schema, of the FILE and of the `.sch` on standard error as in text form.
- Exit status (D313, item 4, with D44's codes): 1 when the `.sch` does not
  compile, an unsupported query binding included (C: `schematron:query-binding`
  names it), when a FILE has an error finding, or as today (XSD invalid, not
  well-formed); findings that are not errors leave 0; 3 when the `.sch` or a
  FILE cannot be read; 4 only when sxml fails (a limit, out of memory). The CLI
  sets no step limit (D313, item 9; cli-4).

**JavaScript** (the same compile-once, validate-many shape as
`Processor.compileSchema` and `Schema.validate`):
`processor.compileSchematron(schema: string | {text?: string | Uint8Array,
uri?: string}, options?: {phase?: string, baseUri?: string, parameters?:
Record<string, string>}): Schematron`, throwing a `SchemaError` with every
report when the schema has errors, as `compileSchema` does; `schematron.title`,
`.schemaVersion`, `.schematronEdition`, `.queryBinding`, `.phase`;
`schematron.validate(input: Value | string | Uint8Array, options?: {uri?:
string, firedRules?: boolean, svrl?: boolean}): SchematronResult`, where
`SchematronResult` is `{valid: boolean, phase: string, findings:
SchematronFinding[], svrl?: string}` and a finding has `kind`, `id`, `role`,
`flag`, `severity`, `isError`, `message`, `diagnostics` (`{id, language,
text}`), `properties` (`{id, role, scheme, text}`), `patternId`, `test`,
`path`, `sourceName`, `lineNumber`, `columnNumber` (the instance) and
`schemaSourceName`, `schemaLineNumber`, `schemaColumnNumber` (the assertion).
Text input is parsed with locations. `dispose()` as for `Schema`. Field names
follow the package's (`lineNumber`, `sourceName`).

**Where the standard overturned the first version.**

- Binding names are compared ignoring case (6.5, every annex), not
  case-sensitively.
- `group` (5.4.5, 6.6): confirmed as designed; SVRL writes `active-group`, not
  `active-pattern`.
- `library` (5.4.8, 5.4.4): reached by `extends href`, not by `include`;
  `include` of a library is an error.
- `extends href` at the top of a schema or library (the foreword, 5.4.4)
  inserts a schema's or library's children.
- Placeholders match the whole parameter name token (Annexes C, H, J), not the
  longest prefix of the name run that is a parameter: `$rowx` is not `$row`
  followed by `x`.
- Abstract patterns declare parameters with defaults, checked against the
  instance (5.4.11, Annex B); schema-level `sch:param` is a schema parameter,
  not rejected.
- A rule let may not shadow a schema, phase or pattern variable (5.4.7); two
  patterns may define one name (3.23), where the first version made it an
  error.
- The message's `value-of` and `name` are evaluated with the subject node when
  a subject applies (6.3), not always with the context node.
- `role`, `flag` (and `severity`) can be dynamic (5.5.6, 5.5.14, 5.5.16; AVTs,
  Annexes C, H, J), not always as written.
- Schema lets are not external values; schema parameters are (5.4.11, 6.1),
  given at compile time.
- `documents` is evaluated at the instance root without the pattern's variables
  (5.4.12), not with the validated node as context.
- `visit-each`, `severity`, `phase/@from`, `phase/@when` with `#ANY`,
  `schematronEdition` and `let/@as` (with the bindings' rules) are designed
  above, not rejected.
- Exit status 1, not 4, for an unsupported binding (the owner, C); `xslt`,
  `xpath` and no attribute read as 4.0 (the owner, B).

**Rejected.**

- Generating XSLT text and compiling it (the owner, 7.27): the cost is in the
  text, and errors point into generated text.
- Lowering Schematron to IR directly (7.27): it would duplicate modes, patterns
  and priorities.
- SchXslt's one mode per documents group (above).
- Findings through `xsl:message` and the trace sink: they would mix with the
  messages of the schema's own XSLT and need a marker; the raw result is the
  transformation's own output.
- An expanded copy of the schematron documents (what `include.xsl` and
  `expand.xsl` build): a second tree and a second location map for nothing the
  builder cannot do while it walks.
- Placeholder replacement by one regex per parameter (SchXslt's): 780 passes
  per attribute.
- SVRL with sxml attributes for line and column (above).
- One compiled stylesheet per phase for `#ANY`: N compilations for a choice one
  `xsl:choose` makes.
- A compile report kind of Schematron's own beside XSD's: the same three
  fields.

**The owner's answers** (2026-10-28) to the revision's eight choices, applied
above:

- 1a. A present severity decides whether a finding is an error; otherwise role
  and flag, as D313 point 4.
- 2a. `xslt4` and `xpath4` (reserved, 6.5) are read as 4.0.
- 3a. Rule contexts are XSLT patterns under the `xpath*` bindings too.
- 4a. Braces in messages are literal text: no text value templates (Annex J
  leaves their extent implementation-defined).
- 5a (decided by the orchestrator at the owner's request, after checking real
  rule sets): schema parameters are compile-time text substitution,
  `--schematron-param` in the CLI. Evidence: EN 16931 (UBL, CII, EDIFACT) and
  XRechnung declare no schema-level `param` (new in 2025); their thousands of
  params are all pattern params, substituted at compile time; XRechnung's 20
  global `let`s are not meant to be overridden, and what users vary is the
  phase; the pre-compiled EN 16931 stylesheet exposes only the skeleton's
  unused file-name parameters. 5.4.11 makes the override mechanism
  implementation-defined, and a schema parameter's value is a query fragment as
  a pattern parameter's is.
- 6b. A rule's `let` is evaluated once per rule context node, not per
  visit-each item (5.4.7, 5.5.21).
- 7b. 7.28 gives `src/xslt.c` a compile report sink, so errors of the XSLT
  compile stage are collected too; XSLT users gain the same sink ("Compile
  errors").
- 8b. Any `schematronEdition` value is accepted and reported (5.5.15), never an
  error. Confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-28, after the conformance suite
  (D317) read 5.5.15's "shall be 2025" as making another value a schema error:
  sxml validates best-effort, since the editions are largely backward
  compatible. The suite keeps its neutral case (`edition-other-value`); 7.28's
  driver lists it as a deliberate deviation with this record's reason, not as a
  failure.

**The owner's amendments** (2026-10-28, after acceptance):

- 3a amended: a context that parses as an XSLT pattern is used as one under
  every binding; a valid expression that is no pattern is wrapped as an
  expression rule context (see "Query bindings": the form, the start nodes and
  the cost). One mechanism, the match pattern; only those contexts pay for the
  expression.
- 4a confirmed with evidence: none of six real rule sets uses braces in assert,
  report, diagnostic, property, title or p text: EN 16931 UBL, CII and EDIFACT;
  XRechnung UBL and CII; Peppol BIS Billing 3 UBL and CII (branch 2026-Q2-QA2).
  EN 16931 and XRechnung insert values with `value-of`; Peppol's messages are
  fixed text. SchXslt does not evaluate text value templates in messages
  either. Text value templates may come later as an opt-in for `xslt4` and
  `xpath4` schemas only; out of scope now.

### D316. Cheap coercion of one item: single-item shortcuts (packet perf-8)

**Summary**: A `single_item_shortcut` matches and coerces one item against a
plain atomic item type without the coercion engine, and the matcher's frames
move out of its struct, cutting coercion costs.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D71, D85, D224, D229, D259, D281, D309. No public
header changed.

- **Whom it serves**: every function call with typed parameters, built-in or
  user-defined, above all XSLT that passes attribute values to string
  functions. A callgrind profile of SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931 (75.3 x
  10^9 instructions, 10.5 s, step bound raised in a scratch build) put 33 % in
  `sxml_evaluator_coerce`: 8.1 million coercions from COERCE leaves, about
  3,000 instructions each. 4.8 million returned after a whole match (537
  instructions a match, most of it making the matcher and its frames); 3.4
  million ran the coercion engine, which made 4.1 million sequence builders,
  atomized 2.7 million nodes, cast 1.4 million xs:untypedAtomic values to
  xs:string and matched the value again before and after.
- **Mechanism** (glossary `single_item_shortcut`; `src/evaluator_function.c`),
  the one coercion and the one matcher, without new machinery:

  1. *Matching*: `sxml_evaluator_match_sequence_type` decides no item by the
     occurrence and one item by the occurrence and the matcher's own item rules
     (`sxml_type_matcher_advance_item`), with no frames; whatever those rules
     do not decide at once (choices, typed maps, arrays and records, JNode
     value types) runs the matcher as before. One atomic item against
     xs:anyAtomicType matches at once (XPath 4.0, 3.2.3), as against its own
     annotation did (D229).
  2. *Coercion*: one item against a plain atomic item type (variety atomic, not
     a union, choice or enumeration; not under the cast rules of D281's
     composite casts) is coerced without the engine (3.4, 3.4.3): an instance
     of its type stays, before the type is read; else the item, or a node's
     typed value when it is one atomic item, goes through
     `sxml_coerce_atomic_item` once; an unchanged item needs no final match, a
     cast one still gets it. Atomized values of no item or several, and every
     other value and type, go to the engine from the beginning; atomizing again
     there raises what the first atomization would have.
  3. The matcher's and the engine's four inline frames are an array of the
     caller's, not part of the struct, so making either writes no frames; the
     frame structs' fields are ordered for padding (clang-analyzer's
     optin.performance.Padding).
- **Not changed**: outcomes, error codes (XPTY0004, the role's code, XPTY0117,
  FORG0001 and the XSLT roles' type errors of D281), the order in which errors
  arise, and steps (coercion charges none; D89). D71 holds: no new loops over
  nested structure.
- **Measured** (callgrind instructions x 10^9, release, before at e82b48d2e,
  after 44f8d546b): SchXslt expand 75.27 to 61.68 (-18 %), of which coercion
  24.88 to 11.21 (about 1,380 instructions a coercion), the same output byte
  for byte; `tests/bench/coercion.xq` (new, in run-bench.py) 3.775 to 2.847
  (-25 %); recursion.xq 5.268 to 5.114; xmark-all 8.737 to 8.735. By change,
  coercion.xq: matching and coercion shortcuts 3.775 to 3.190, frames out of
  the structs 2.999, xs:anyAtomicType 2.901, instances before the type is read
  2.847 (recursion.xq had risen 0.8 % before that last step). Processor seconds
  (fastest of seven, a shared machine): coercion.xq 0.463 to 0.332, xmark-all
  1.12 to 1.09; expand about 10.5 to 8.5. QT4 XP40 (32,785 passed), XQ40
  (46,114) and XT40 (12,185), whole, release, case by case against the base
  commit built the same way: 0 outcomes differ.
- **Left**: in the expand profile coercion is still 18 %: node atomization
  (3.1, the typed value's string), casts of xs:untypedAtomic to xs:string (2.2,
  about 1,600 instructions each through the cast pipeline: a relabelling of the
  same string would halve it, but belongs in `src/cast.c`), 0.7 million single
  items against unions, choices and enumerations still run the engine, and 0.7
  million multi-item values run the whole matcher (some twice: a vector of 16
  items or more whose slice base fails D309's base match is matched again item
  by item). Multi-item values coerced to atomic types still match every item
  before, during and after the engine.

**Sources**: callgrind profile of SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931 (step
bound raised in a scratch build): coercions, matches, builders, atomizations,
casts (`callgrind`, release build); callgrind instructions, before at e82b48d2e
and after 44f8d546b: SchXslt expand and its coercion, coercion.xq by change,
recursion.xq, xmark-all (`callgrind`, `tests/bench/run-bench.py`, release
build); processor seconds, fastest of seven: coercion.xq, xmark-all, expand
(`tests/bench/run-bench.py`, release build); QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 passes,
whole, case by case against the base commit built the same way
(`tools/run-qt4.sh`, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build).

### D317. A Schematron conformance suite of sxml's own (packet 7.30)

**Summary**: sxml has its own Schematron conformance suite,
`tests/schematron/`, for ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025, with neutral expected results,
recorded readings, a SchXslt cross-check and an independent check of the 2025
cases.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D313 and D315 (as revised and accepted).

- **What**: `tests/schematron/`, 332 cases in 18 test sets for ISO/IEC
  19757-3:2025, in a catalog format of its own (namespace
  `urn:sxml:schematron-test-suite`, golden file `third_party/qt4tests`), with
  `catalog.xsd`, `coverage.xml` (139 requirements of clauses 3 to 7 and the
  normative annexes, 131 with cases, 8 with the reason none can test them) and
  a README. Every schema, instance and expected result was written for the
  suite; the standard's text is cited by clause only.
- **Expected results are neutral**: a multiset of findings (kind, subject as
  `fn:path`, id, role, flag, severity, subordinate document, message after
  whitespace normalization, diagnostics and properties), the set of raised
  flags, optional XPath assertions over SVRL; or `schema-error`, `error` (6.1's
  third outcome) or `implementation-defined`, each with its clause. No sxml API
  or error code appears. `since="2025"` marks the 67 cases that need
  fourth-edition constructs; query-binding and feature dependencies mark what a
  processor may lack.
- **Readings taken** (the README lists them): whole-token parameter references;
  Annex B's param-names-match only for abstract patterns that declare
  parameters (read literally it fails every third-edition instance); one
  definition per variable name over schema, phase, pattern and rule, pattern
  variables scoped to the pattern; the subject as message context (6.3);
  `value-of` through `fn:string()` (several items are an error); relative rule
  contexts under the xpath bindings implementation-defined (the orchestrator's
  direction), as is how the default `xslt` binding is read when a result
  depends on it.
- **Cross-check**: the 265 cases with `since="2020"` ran through SchXslt 1.10.1
  on a release build of sxml (`tools/crosscheck.py`, report in
  `tools/schxslt-crosscheck.txt`): 198 agree, 5 implementation-defined, 13 need
  a binding SchXslt lacks (xslt, xpath\*), 49 disagree, each with the clause
  that decides it (27 unchecked static errors; SchXslt's global pattern
  variables, shadowing, `name path` as a value, rule context for messages,
  prefix placeholders, no placeholders in `subject`, no base URI fixup, empty
  phases, joined `value-of`, and three SVRL omissions). The 67 2025-only cases
  wait for the independent check.
- **Against D315**: two points differ from the standard as the suite reads it:
  `value-of` as `xsl:value-of` joins several items, where Annexes H to N define
  it with `fn:string()` (`value-of-several-items`); any `schematronEdition` is
  accepted (D315, 8b), where 5.5.15 requires 2025 (`edition-other-value`).
  Reading no queryBinding and `xslt` as 4.0 is D313's choice; the suite keeps
  those cases dependent on the `xslt` binding or implementation-defined.
- **Existing suites**: schematron/schematron-conformance (49 cases, 2016
  edition, no licence: not reused), SchXslt's unit tests (MIT, not reused),
  XQS's BaseX tests (Apache-2.0, not reused); none covers the 2025 edition.
- **Addendum (2026-10-28): the independent check of the 67 2025-only cases.** A
  separate agent derived each result from the standard alone, on copies with
  `result` and `description` removed; it never saw the suite, D315 or D317 and
  ran no implementation. 52 identical; the other 15 agree in substance
  (fired-rule listings against `flags` and `assert-svrl`, `@n` against `@Q{}n`,
  the conditional findings of the five optional-binding cases,
  `let-as-mismatch` an error either way, `visit-each-atomic`'s uncompared
  location, `edition-reported` at user option). No case changed.
- **Addendum (2026-10-28): the edge-case pass.** 182 cases more (514 in 18
  sets; 104 `since="2020"`, 78 `since="2025"`), each construct varied by
  cardinality, order, static and dynamic errors, namespaces, text (non-ASCII,
  astral, combining, whitespace-only, mixed), node kinds and interaction with
  phases, group, documents, from, visit-each, subject, abstract patterns and
  extends; the README's "Edge cases" table marks each pair covered,
  implementation-defined or not applicable (22 reasons). New readings, in the
  README's "Ambiguities in the standard": dynamic role/flag/severity that are
  empty, several or not names, static role and severity that are not names,
  `role="$undefined"` (5.4.7 against Annex J), parameters in role and severity
  (6.2), subject and rule variables under visit-each, the context of
  diagnostics and properties with a subject, subjects selecting none or
  several, overlapping and attribute `from`, later `when` under `#ANY`,
  duplicate documents and rule-context items, two `ns` for one prefix, a
  library as the schema, `active` naming an abstract pattern, whitespace in
  queryBinding and schematronEdition: all implementation-defined. Normative
  readings: include and extends-href cycles are schema errors (6.2),
  `visit-each` duplicates are evaluated twice, a role from an attribute node is
  its string value, syntax errors in unused abstract rules and inactive phases
  still make the schema incorrect (7.2). Every case on the `xslt3` binding now
  declares the dependency (485 cases): only the default binding is mandatory
  (6.5). `crosscheck.py` collapses only 5.3's four whitespace characters.
  SchXslt cross-check of the 369 2020 cases: 281 agree, 55 disagree (6 new,
  each by the clauses already recorded: Annex A, 7.2, 6.3, Annexes H and J), 18
  implementation-defined, 15 need a binding SchXslt lacks. The 78 new 2025-only

- **Addendum (2026-10-28, the orchestrator): the independent check of the 78
  new 2025-only cases.** The same separate agent derived each from the standard
  alone, on copies without results or descriptions, and without this record,
  D315 or the suite. 39 identical; 39 agree in substance: 21 the suite calls

  severity that are empty, several or not names; errors in `when` and `from`;
  overlapping or attribute `from` results; `visit-each` with variables and
  subject; schema parameters; a library as schema), 6 dynamic errors on both
  sides (the check notes that 6.1's result "error" and D.2's svrl:error fit no
  finding), 1 on the optional `xquery31` binding with the same conditional
  findings, and notation (fired-rule listings, `@n` against `@Q{}n`, no
  location for atomic `visit-each` items). One judgement call:
  `edition-whitespace` stays implementation-defined, because 5.3's stripping is
  a "should"; the check read Annex A's `xsd:token` as deciding it. No case
  changed. Both rounds together: all 145 2025-only cases checked. Packet 7.30

### D318. Source locations for parsed input documents (packet 7.29)

**Summary**: A processor's `source_location_policy` decides whether parsed
documents keep locations; under AUTOMATIC a compiled program that
`reads_source_locations` asks for them, and copies keep what they copy.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D313 (7, 8), D87, D88, D99.

- **Header** (additive after D99, packet 7.29): `include/sxml/processor.h`
  gains `sxml_source_location_policy` (`AUTOMATIC` = 0, `ALWAYS`, `NEVER`) and,
  at the end of `sxml_processor_configuration`, `sxml_source_location_policy
  source_location_policy;` (another value makes the configuration invalid).
  `include/sxml/tree.h` (frozen) gains one function,
  `sxml_node_get_location(node, &location)`: dm:location over the tree's
  `get_location`, line 0 when unknown, for hosts (the CLI's error report, which
  uses the public API only) and for sxml's own copies. Nothing else in a frozen
  header changes.
- **The program's flag** (glossary `reads_source_locations`): one bool per IR
  unit, set by `sxml_ir_unit_add_expression` and `_replace_expression` when a
  STATIC_CALL or FUNCTION_REFERENCE names a native row with the new property
  `SXML_NATIVE_FUNCTION_READS_SOURCE_LOCATIONS`: fn:location,
  fn:function-lookup, fn:load-xquery-module, fn:transform and xsl:evaluate's
  row. One place for XPath, XQuery and XSLT, no pass and no new IR kind.
  `sxml_ir_unit_set_reads_source_locations` is for a front end whose reports
  need locations (Schematron, 7.28: D315's `node_location`). A unit whose
  in-scope schemas include any but the processor's built-in ones also reads
  them (it can validate, `sxml_processor_unit_reads_source_locations`).
- **What AUTOMATIC decides by** (glossary `location_demand`, in the processor):
  whether a program has been compiled, whether one of those reads locations
  (noted by the public compile functions of XPath, XQuery and XSLT, and by
  `sxml_schema_initialize`: a schema is a validation; the processor's built-in
  schemas leave it as it was), and the evaluation in progress.
  `sxml_evaluate_unit` begins and ends each evaluation with its unit's answer,
  or'ed with the enclosing evaluation's (fn:transform, fn:load-xquery-module, a
  host function). `sxml_processor_parse_document`, the one parse behind fn:doc,
  fn:document, fn:parse-xml, the CLI's fn:collection and a resolver's
  DOCUMENT_NODE, keeps locations when: ALWAYS; never under NEVER; under
  AUTOMATIC, during an evaluation as it says, otherwise when no program has
  been compiled or one compiled reads them (D313, 7).
- **Copies keep what they copy**: `sxml_tree_builder_copy_node` passes each
  node's location in its events when the copied root has one (one question per
  copy, so a copy of a tree without locations costs nothing more), and XSLT's
  whitespace-stripped source documents (`src/xslt_whitespace.c`) keep locations
  when the document did; so `location(.)` answers for a stylesheet's input
  under xsl:strip-space, and a validated copy keeps its input's lines.
- **Errors** (D313, 8): an error "names an input node" when its value
  (`$err:value`: fn:error's third argument, an xsl:message's select) holds a
  node; the record's own location stays the expression's (the frozen
  `sxml_error_record` has one), and the CLI prints a second line
  `FILE:LINE:COLUMN: the node the error names` for the first node of the value
  whose document kept locations (`sxml_query_run_fail`). `src/evaluator.c` is
  unchanged. fn:error is not a reason to keep locations (D313's list is the
  owner's); `--locations=always` gives them to a program that cannot ask.
- **CLI**: `--locations=automatic|always|never` for xpath, xquery and transform
  (`SXML_QUERY_LOCATIONS_OPTION`); xpath and xquery compile before they parse
  `--context-item` (`sxml_query_run_read_context_item`), so a static error is
  now reported before a context document that does not parse. 9 CLI tests, 21
  goldens with the new usage line.
- **Measured** (release, the 26 MB, 2.5 million node document of D313, peak
  RSS): `xpath --context-item count(//line)` 173 MB under automatic and never,
  249 MB under always; `location((//line)[last()])` 249 MB under automatic;
  xquery `count(doc(...)//line)` 175 MB automatic, 251 MB always; transform
  with `count(//line)` 174 MB automatic, 250 MB with `location()`. Before the
  change every case was 171-175 MB.

### D319. Casts that keep the string, choices of one item, untyped items cast at once (packet perf-10)

**Summary**: A `relabelled_cast` keeps the source's string cell under the
target type, one item against a choice takes the first alternative it matches,
and untyped items are cast without a prior match.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D71, D85, D281, D309, D316. No public header
changed.

- **Whom it serves**: every coercion of an untyped value to xs:string (XSLT
  passing attribute values to string functions, SchXslt first), every call
  whose parameter is a choice type (fn:replace's `$replacement`), and every
  cast of a string to a supertype. A callgrind profile of SchXslt's expand
  stage of EN 16931 at a05385eb4 (52.19 x 10^9 instructions) put 21.3 % in
  `sxml_evaluator_coerce`: 2.7 million node atomizations (3.19), 1.36 million
  casts of xs:untypedAtomic to xs:string through the whole cast pipeline (2.25,
  about 1,650 instructions each: describe the target, parse, validate and copy
  the same text), 676,000 single items against a choice type through the engine
  and the whole matcher (about 1.8), and the matches before each of those casts
  (0.37).
- **Mechanism**, in the one cast (`src/cast.c`) and the one coercion
  (`src/evaluator_function.c`), no new machinery:

  1. *Relabelled casts* (glossary `relabelled_cast`): a cast whose result has
     the source's own text is the source's string cell under the target's
     annotation and primitive type, retained: an xs:string, xs:untypedAtomic or
     xs:anyURI item cast to xs:string or xs:untypedAtomic (F&O 4.0, 19.1.2.1
     and 19.2: their canonical text is the string; whitespace preserved; every
     string in the value space), or an item cast to an atomic type it is
     derived from (19.3.1; XSD 1.1 Part 2, 4.3.6: whiteSpace only strengthens
     by restriction, facets only narrow). Casts to xs:string and
     xs:untypedAtomic are decided before the target is described. The item
     struct carries the annotation and the primitive type beside the cell
     (D34), so nothing in the cell changes.
  2. *One item against a choice* (`single_item_shortcut`): the first
     alternative the item matches decides, as the engine's CHOICE rule does
     (XPath 4.0, 3.4.2); when that alternative never changes the items that
     match it (not a typed function, record, array or map type), the item stays
     and the final match holds. No match, or a first match that converts, goes
     to the engine from the beginning.
  3. *Untyped items cast at once*: an xs:untypedAtomic item coerced to an
     atomic type of another primitive type is cast without a match first; its
     only supertypes are xs:anyAtomicType and above (XPath 4.0, 3.2.3).
- **Not changed**: outcomes, error codes and their order, steps (coercion and
  matching charge none), D71 (no new loop over nested structure). Unions and
  enumerations of one item still take the engine: the profiles here have none
  that do not match at once.
- **Measured** (callgrind instructions x 10^9, release, before at a05385eb4;
  commits 53ede6754 and f58ed07f2): SchXslt expand 52.19 to 50.23 (relabelled
  casts; a cast 1,650 to 240 instructions) to 48.44 (choices) to 47.78
  (untyped), -8.5 % in all, coercion 21.3 % to 13.9 % (11.14 to 6.63), the same
  output byte for byte; `tests/bench/coercion.xq` 2.845 to 2.753 to 2.755 to
