### D320. A compile report sink for XSLT (packet 7.28)

**Summary**: `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_configuration` gains a `report_sink`, a
`compile_report_sink` that receives every static and type error of a stylesheet
compile while reading and lowering go on; the null sink keeps first-error
behaviour.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D315 ("Compile errors", the owner's 7b), D99 and
D139. The header change D315 announced for 7.28.

- **Header** (additive): `include/sxml/xslt.h` includes `sxml/schema.h` and
  `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_configuration` gains, at its end,
  `sxml_schema_report_sink report_sink;` (XSD's sink type, reused: one report
  of a compile error, code, description and location, for every language). The
  null sink, the zero value, keeps the first-error behaviour exactly.
- **Mechanism** (glossary `compile_report_sink`, `error_collector`): one
  internal collector (`sxml_xslt_error_collector`, src/xslt_ast.c) that the
  reader and lowering write each error into and ask whether to go on. With a
  sink a static or type error goes there and the work goes on: the reader
  leaves out the attribute in error (and the element's whole-element checks,
  which would report what follows from that), or the element when the element
  itself is wrong, and reads the rest; lowering goes on with the next template
  rule, stylesheet function or global variable (each lowering enters and leaves
  its own function, so nothing is left half-open). Nothing is lowered once
  reading reported an error, and no unit is made once lowering did. An error
  that stops a stage (a dynamic error of a static expression, the in-scope
  schemas, outputs, streamability) goes to the sink too, once. The record holds
  the first error.
- **Users**: `sxml transform` gives the sink a receiver that writes each error
  as the one line it always wrote (`FILE:LINE:COLUMN: CODE: description`) and
  exits 1 after the compilation; Schematron (D315) passes its own sink to
  `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_create_from_ast`; the JavaScript `compileStylesheet`
  keeps throwing the first error and adds every report (`reports`).
- **Not done**: errors inside one template rule after its first (a template is
  one unit of lowering); errors of included modules that are not well-formed
  stop reading as before.
- **Evidence**: `xslt_test` `report_sink_receives_every_compile_error` (four
  reading errors in three declarations, three analysis errors in two template
  rules and a function, the null sink giving the first); CLI tests
  `transform_compile_errors`, `transform_analysis_errors`. XT40, release, case
  by case against the base commit built the same way: 0 outcomes differ (12,185
  passed).

**Sources**: xslt_test report_sink_receives_every_compile_error and CLI tests
transform_compile_errors, transform_analysis_errors (`ctest`); XT40 passes,
case by case against the base commit built the same way (`tools/run-xslt.sh`,
release build).

### D321. Choices try every alternative; a caught error leaves the error record (packet fix-4)

**Summary**: A choice coercion accepts an attempt only when its result matches
the alternative, so every alternative is tried, and a caught error is cleared
from the error record once handled.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D85, D310, D314, D316, D319. No public header
changed. Commit 5a47d8a68.

- **Choice coercion** (D319's engine gap): XPath 4.0, 3.4.2 coerces an item
  that matches no alternative of a choice or union "to each of the alternatives
  in turn, until an alternative is found that does not result in a type error",
  and the item coercion rules end with a type error when the resulting item
  does not match the required item type (3.4.2, last rule). The engine's CHOICE
  took an attempt that left the item unchanged (no rule applies:
  xs:untypedAtomic against element(a)) as the first alternative's success, so
  `(element(a) | xs:string)` given `xs:untypedAtomic("v")` ended in XPTY0004 at
  the final match. Now an attempt succeeds only when its result matches the
  alternative (`sxml_coercion_accept_attempt`, src/evaluator_function.c); an
  unchanged item never does, since the CHOICE tries alternatives only for an
  item that matches none, so it is not matched again. A failed attempt reports
  the role's type error in its record and counts as an error raised above the
  CHOICE: the first attempt's error still stands when all fail (`(xs:integer |
  element(a))` and "v": FORG0001). An accepted later attempt clears the first
  failure from the request's record, which the coercion succeeded without.
- **Stale error record** (D310): reproduced with the CLI, a regex error caught
  and then a depth limit, `declare function local:f($n) { 1 + local:f($n + 1)
  }; (try { matches("a", "(") } catch * { 0 }), local:f(1)`: exit 4 with the
  regex error's description and place (since D314 the step limit is not
  reached, and it writes its own description, so it hid the bug except for the
  code and place). The catching task read the record and left it filled. New
  machine call `sxml_evaluator_machine_forget_caught_error`
  (src/evaluator_machine_internal.h, "Catching") clears it once a catching task
  has read the error and handles it: a catch clause, after its details map is
  made; an error kept for a finally clause (raised again from the try state); a
  template rule's pattern error, which is no match (XSLT 4.0, 6.5); the filter
  index giving up. A step limit hit between the catch and its handling keeps
  its own description and drops the rest. Streaming accumulators keep their
  caught error for the reads (19.5), as before.
- **Evidence**: `evaluator_test` `choices_try_every_alternative` (a node
  alternative first, an atomic one first, a union inside a choice, maps and
  arrays, several items, the first attempt's error); `evaluator_try_test`
  `caught_errors_leave_the_record` (every step bound across a caught error: the
  record holds no code, value or place, and the limit's own description).
  debug-gcc: 437 tests pass; clang-tidy clean; no call cycle.
- **Conformance**, release, whole, case by case against 47a1d9a33 built the
  same way: XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114, XT40 12,185 passed before and after, 0
  outcomes differ, no gains. The brief's figures (32,815, 46,158, 12,283) are
  not what HEAD gives with these drivers here. SchXslt's expand stage: output
  identical to s2.sch; 47,779,606,081 to 47,779,606,157 instructions
  (callgrind).
- **Left**: code that tries something and drops its error without a catching
  task (outside the machine's catching) was not audited; such a place would
  leave the record filled the same way, visible only through a later failure
  that writes no record.

**Sources**: the whole test suite, 437 tests (`ctest`, debug-gcc build); XP40,
XQ40 and XT40 passes, whole, case by case against 47a1d9a33 built the same way
(`tools/run-qt4.sh`, `tools/run-xslt.sh`, release build); SchXslt's expand
stage: instructions before and after (`callgrind`).

### D322. Node atomization describes once; the costs left are the atomic cell's (packet perf-11)

**Summary**: Node atomization describes its node once and skips attributes by
count when walking text descendants; the cost left is the atomic cell's
allocation, validation and type resolution.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D39, D71, D229, D316, D319. No public header
changed.

- **Whom it serves**: every atomization of a node (coercion of node arguments
  to atomic types, comparisons, fn:data, string functions given nodes), first
  SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931, where D319 left node atomization at 3.19
  x 10^9 instructions (6.7 %).
- **Profile** (callgrind, release, at 47a1d9a33; 47.78 x 10^9): 2.71 million
  atomizations, every one of an untyped node: 2.03 million attributes and 0.68
  million text nodes, but only 4,903 distinct nodes, most of them parentless
  (node 0 of a tree of their own), each atomized about 550 times. One
  atomization cost about 1,010 instructions in `sxml_node_make_typed_value`:
  two node descriptions (113 each), the content (54) and
  `sxml_atomic_item_make` (590: the cell from the allocator 283, UTF-8
  validation 178, type resolution through the registry about 70), and later the
  cell's free. The common case the packet names was confirmed: one
  xs:untypedAtomic from the string value, without a sequence builder (D229 had
  removed it).
- **Mechanism** (`src/xdm_node.c`, no new machinery): the string value takes
  the caller's described node, so a typed value describes its node once (the
  public `sxml_node_make_string_value` describes it itself); the walk over the
  text descendants of a document or element steps over each element's
  attributes by `attribute_count` (they are stored right after it, D39) instead
  of describing them, never past the last descendant.
- **Not changed**: outcomes, error codes, steps (atomization charges none), D71
  (the walk is the same loop).
- **Measured** (callgrind instructions x 10^9, release, before at 47a1d9a33,
  after 365e4257b): SchXslt expand 47.780 to 47.463 (one description) to 47.452
  (attributes skipped), -0.7 %, output byte-identical to `s2.sch`;
  `tests/bench/coercion.xq` 2.716 to 2.697 to 2.695 (-0.8 %); xmark-all 8.747
  to 8.646 to 8.643 (-1.2 %; its 0.86 million atomizations are mostly text-only
  elements). Processor seconds (fastest of seven, interleaved, a shared
  machine): expand 6.28 to 6.40, coercion.xq 0.303 to 0.367, xmark-all 1.205 to
  1.043, within the machine's noise. **Conformance setup**: the base commit and
  the change built alike (`git archive` snapshots, preset `release`), run one
  after the other on the same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset (UTC, the
  C locale), from the snapshot root: `sxml-qt4 run --spec=XP40 --format=json`,
  `sxml-qt4 run --spec=XQ40 --format=json`, `sxml-xslt-test run --format=json`
  (default catalogs, no test list). XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114 and XT40 12,185
  passed in both: 0 outcomes differ, case by case. debug-gcc: 437 of 437 tests
  pass; clang-tidy clean.
- **Left**, outside this packet's files (see "## Proposed"): the atomic cell
  itself, about 70 % of what an atomization still costs. A scratch experiment
  that resolved xs:string and xs:untypedAtomic without the registry in
  `sxml_atomic_item_make` (`src/xdm_atomic.c`) took the expand stage from 47.45
  to 46.98 (-1.0 %, 6.8 million calls of about 70 instructions); UTF-8

  %); cell allocation through the allocator 2.04 (4.3 %) plus the frees. A memo
  of typed values per item heap would remove most of the 3.2, since SchXslt

**Sources**: callgrind profile of SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931 at

### D323. Schematron implemented: what 7.28 built and the readings it took (packet 7.28)

**Summary**: Implements `schematron.h` as D315 designs it, with `sxml validate
--schematron`, host shim and JavaScript entry points, and records the readings
taken, such as pattern variables scoped to their pattern.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D313, D315 (revised and accepted), D317, D318 and
D320. Implements `include/sxml/schematron.h` as D315 designs it; no public
header changes beyond D320's.

- **Whom it serves**: the embedder and the user of the sxml command, who
  validate documents against Schematron rules (EN 16931, XRechnung, their own)
  with both places of each finding. **Pays**: about 9,500 lines of library C
  (`src/schematron*`), a driver, a CLI option set, five host-shim entry points.
- **What was built**: reading (documents, `sch:include`, `sch:extends` href and
  rule, libraries, Annex A's grammar and Annex B's constraints, every error to
  the compile report sink, the query binding), the placeholder scan with
  expansion segments, the stylesheet AST (one mode per active pattern, groups,
  visit-each, phases with from, when and `#ANY`, expression rule contexts,
  dynamic flag, role and severity, variables and their scopes), compile,
  describe, validate, SVRL. `sxml validate --schematron` (D315 "The CLI"); the
  host shim's `sxml_host_schematron_*` and `sxml_host_compile_reports_of`, the
  package's `Processor.compileSchematron` and `Schematron.validate`, and
  `compileStylesheet` throwing a `SchemaError` with every error (D320).
- **Readings and choices made on the way** (none changes the header):

  1. *Pattern variables are in scope in their pattern only* (3.23, 5.4.7):
     every `let` of a compiled pattern is a global under a synthesized name;
     the pattern's expressions reach it as a placeholder is replaced (the
     rename table follows the instance and schema parameter tables in the one
     scan), its templates through a local binding of the written name; the
     `documents` attribute sees none of them (5.4.12). SVRL and reports show
     the text as written.
  2. *Errors of the grammar and of the expressions in one compile*: with a
     report sink, building runs after reading errors and reports the
     expressions' syntax errors too; the XSLT compile then does not run (its
     static analysis needs a correct schema).
  3. *An include where the grammar has none* (Annex A, `inclusion`; in `rules`,
     `properties`) and an `ns` of a library that `extends href` inserts are
     syntax errors; an abstract rule with `visit-each` too (Annex A).
  4. *`name path` selecting more than one item* raises XPTY0004, as
     `fn:node-name` would (Annexes H, J).
  5. *An expression rule context is typed `node()*`*: a context such as
     `count(item)` fails at validation (XTTE0570) instead of matching nothing.
  6. *A validation of a document node uses the compiled unit*: the default
     initial match selection, not a given one, which lowered the stylesheet
     once per validation (EN 16931's 1,131 unit tests: 281 s before, 9.4 s
     after).
  7. *Documents through a byte reader* (D233, the sxml command's resolver) are
     read whole, then parsed.
- **Deviations** of 7.30's suite (the driver's list,
  `tests/schematron/driver/deviations.txt`): `edition-other-value` (D315 8b);
  `binding-xpath2-no-maps` (D315 "Query bindings": xpath2 is read by the 4.0
  front end); `error-context-is-expression` (D315 3a as amended: a context that
  is an expression is wrapped under every binding, so the error is dynamic).
  One suite case changed, a 2020 case: `abstract-in-phase` gave its phase the
  id of its pattern instance, which Annex A's `xsd:ID` forbids; the phase is
  now `tables-phase`, the expected findings unchanged.
- **Evidence**: suite 463 of 463 applicable normative cases, 3 deviations, 43
  implementation-defined, 5 refused bindings (xquery\*); `schematron_test`
  (placeholders, errors with places, bindings, parameters, both locations, 2025
  constructs, SVRL, every allocation failure); EN 16931 UBL 1,133 of 1,133

### D324. Compiling large stylesheets in linear time (packet perf-12)

**Summary**: Large units compile in linear time: the descendant pass groups
expressions by function once, the global-read pass finds each chain head once,
and the XPath lowerer checks a declaration view for duplicates once.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D46, D71, D223, D224, D229, D259, D322. No public
header changed; the IR after the passes is the same.

- **Whom it serves**: every compile of a large unit, first the pre-compiled
  Schematron stylesheets (EN 16931, 900 KB of XSLT) that `sxml transform` and,
  after 7.28, every Schematron compile pay for.
- **Profile** (callgrind, release, at 5bd945281): one EN 16931 invoice 2.680 x
  10^9 instructions, 79 % the compile; the descendant pass 12.5 % and the
  global-read pass 8.6 % self. A growth series of generated stylesheets (N
  blocks of 8 template rules with 3 Schematron-style assertions and 8 globals,
  N = 8 to 128; and 2 blocks whose templates hold 6 to 384 assertions; the
  generator was a scratch script) found three costs that grow faster than the
  unit:

  - the descendant pass scanned every expression of the unit once per function
    for the ones it owns (functions times expressions);
  - the global-read pass climbed each expression's LET chain to its head (chain
    length times expressions), and searched a chain's list of globals for each
    global read;
  - the XPath lowerer checked an embedding's variable declarations for
    duplicate names on every embedded expression, every global against every
    other (globals squared times expressions; `src/xpath_lower.c`).
- **Mechanism**, no new machinery: the descendant pass groups the expressions
  of `owners` by function once (a counting sort, each group in index order, so
  the visit order is the one before); the global-read pass finds each chain
  head once along the path climbed and marks a global per chain head; the
  lowerer keeps the variable declaration view it last found free of duplicates
  (`sxml_xpath_lowerer.checked_declarations`, `src/xpath_lower_internal.h`) and
  checks only another view: a stylesheet's expressions share their package's
  view. A view's array must not change while a lowerer uses it, as the static
  context's other parts already must not.
- **The next costs in these files** (on the invoice after the above): the
  fusion pass (D259) made a slot census and the demand members of every
  function; a plain walk now finds whether the body holds a QUANTIFIED, without
  which nothing fuses (73.6 to 41.7 x 10^6). The XPath front end found each
  node's AST kind by binary search over the type names, twice per node; the
  kind is now kept per grammar symbol for the parse (`sxml_xpath_parse` 662.2
  to 639.9 x 10^6). `push_every_child` reads expressions in place (-6 x 10^6).
- **Measured**, instructions x 10^9 (callgrind, release; base 5bd945281 and the
  change built alike from `git archive` snapshots): invoice 2.680 to 2.135 (the
  three linear fixes) to 2.076 (the rest), -22.5 %; growth N = 8, 16, 32, 64,
  128: 0.472, 1.143, 3.305, 12.101, 57.091 to 0.357, 0.704, 1.413, 2.908, 6.192
  (each doubling x 2.0 to 2.1, was x 2.4 to 4.7); in it the descendant pass
  0.089 to 21.569 becomes 0.0017 to 0.027, the declaration check 0.0075 to
  29.054 becomes 0.0002 to 0.0033; templates of 6, 24, 96, 384 assertions
  0.188, 0.647, 2.582, 11.833 to 0.167, 0.566, 2.164, 8.534, the global-read
  pass 0.0023, 0.015, 0.162, 2.281 to 0.0019, 0.0068, 0.027, 0.106; xmark-all
  8.641 to 8.639; SchXslt expand 47.452 to 47.450, its output equal to
  `s2.sch`. Processor seconds (fastest of five, interleaved, a shared machine):
  invoice 0.386 to 0.305; N = 128 4.34 to 0.91; 384 assertions 2.18 to 1.36;
  expand and xmark-all within the machine's noise (instructions equal).
- **Same result**: the IR text form after the passes (`src/ir.c`'s printer,
  dumped by a scratch-only hook in `sxml_ir_run_passes`) is byte-identical on
  the EN 16931 stylesheet (141 MB of text) and the growth stylesheets, and on
  all 414,483 units the XT40 suite compiles (a hash per unit, in order). The
  VEFA harness: EN 16931's 1,133 UBL checks pass. **Conformance setup**: base
  and change built alike (preset `release`), run one after the other on the
  same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset, from each snapshot's root:
  `sxml-qt4 run --spec=XP40 --format=json`, `sxml-qt4 run --spec=XQ40
  --format=json`, `sxml-xslt-test run --format=json` (default catalogs, no test
  list). XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114 and XT40 12,185 passed in both: 0 outcomes
  differ, case by case. debug-gcc: 439 of 439 tests pass; clang-tidy clean on
  the changed files. D71 holds (loops only).
- **Deviation**: `src/xpath_lower_internal.h` (one field of the lowerer) is
  outside the packet's list; no other packet owns it.
- **Left** (see "## Proposed"): on the growth series the XSLT component graph
  (`add_named_edges`, `sxml_xslt_package_bind`, `src/xslt_lower_control.c`,
  `src/xslt_package.c`) is now the largest cost that grows with the square of
  the unit (0.120 to 0.480 x 10^9 from N = 64 to 128). On the invoice the
  compile is 72 %: tree-sitter parses of XPath 31 % (a parser made and deleted
  per expression, 1.6 %), the XML read 19 %, value templates 6.3 % (attributes
  of literal result elements without "{" are parsed too), the IR passes 13.6 %,
  of which the demand pass 5.4 % and the four walks that make `owners` 3.8 %.

**Sources**: callgrind profile of one EN 16931 invoice at 5bd945281, the passes
self (`callgrind`, release build, at 5bd945281); instructions, base 5bd945281
and the change from snapshots: invoice, the growth series (generated by a

parse instructions (`callgrind`, release build); processor seconds, fastest of

### D325. Compiling XSLT and Schematron: the component graph, value templates, the Schematron front end (packet perf-13)

**Summary**: XSLT compiles find components through sorted indexes and node
maps, value templates without braces skip the parser, and the Schematron
builder parses each synthesized text once through a hash table.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D224, D315, D320, D323 and D324 (its proposal "XSLT
compile costs that grow with the square of a stylesheet"). No public header
changed; the IR after the passes is the same, and compiled Schematron gives the
same findings.

- **Whom it serves**: every compile of a large stylesheet and every Schematron
  compile, first EN 16931's (900 KB of pre-compiled XSLT; the `.sch` sources
  compiled by `sxml validate --schematron`). **Pays**: three sorted indexes
  made once per lowering, a node map for the templates and the globals, a hash
  table of parsed texts per Schematron compile; no new mechanism (sorting is
  `src/sort_internal.h`'s).
- **Profile** (callgrind, release, at 3919bc7ce): the invoice transform 2.077 x
  10^9 instructions, value templates 6.3 % (each attribute of a literal result
  element parsed, braces or not); the invoice `validate --schematron` 3.366, of
  which the Schematron compile 2.138: building the AST 1.102 (XPath parses of
  the schema's expressions 0.391; of synthesized texts 0.627: 4,567 tree-sitter
  parses of a dozen texts such as "$Q{urn:sxml:schematron}subject", one set per
  assertion), reading 0.355 (5.4.11's check that parameter names are distinct
  compared each of a pattern instance's 780 parameters with every earlier one:
  0.185; the included documents' XML 0.138), the XSLT compile 0.681. The growth
  series of D324 (regenerated: N blocks of 8 template rules with 3
  Schematron-style assertions, 8 globals, a function and a named template; and
  2 blocks whose templates hold 6 to 384 assertions) grew x 2.46 per doubling
  at N = 256: a component found by name walked all declarations
  (`add_named_edges`, 4.17 at N = 256) or its package's instances
  (`find_instance` under `sxml_xslt_package_bind`, 1.17); an expression's
  owning global walked the globals, a variable reference the declaration view
  (1.17 with the rest of the globals' ordering), `find_template_entry` the
  templates (0.20), `check_conflicts` every pair of a package's instances.
- **Mechanism**:

  1. *Indexes made by sorting, searched by binary search*, each giving what the
     walk gave, in its order: the component graph's named declarations by kind,
     name and declaration order (the edges in declaration order); the package
     table's instances by package, kind, name and index (`find_instance`
     chooses the first of the highest precedence whose arity range fits, as
     before); the names of each declaration view (one index per view, shared by
     the static contexts that have it) for the first declaration of a name; for
     `check_conflicts`, a package's instances by kind and name, the first pair
     in index order reported. Node maps: AST node to global (the owner of an
     expression), AST node to template entry. A package that accepts no mode
     skips XTSE3050's search of rules.
  2. *A value template without "{" or "}" is its text* (XSLT 4.0, 5.6.1): built
     directly as the AST the parser made: the XPATH root, the STRING_TEMPLATE
     body, one fixed part (none for an empty text), every span the whole text
     at 1:1, the parser's capacities. A text the fixed part scanner rejects
     (NUL, U+FFFE, U+FFFF, invalid UTF-8) or a depth limit below 3 goes to the
     parser.
  3. *The Schematron builder parses each synthesized text once*: a hash table
     (FNV-1a, open addressing) keeps the AST of each fixed text by value kind
     and text, and each use takes a copy, node for node and the text store byte
     for byte, what the front end would build; the spans are placed as before.
     5.4.11's distinct names: the parameters sorted by name and position, a
     name equal to the one before it repeated, reported in parameter order as
     before.
- **Measured**, instructions x 10^9 (callgrind, release; base 3919bc7ce and
  each step built alike from snapshots): invoice transform 2.077 to 2.070
  (indexes) to 1.958 (value templates; -5.7 % in all); invoice validate 3.366
  to 3.358 to 3.358 to 2.633 (Schematron; -21.8 %), its compile 2.138 to 1.405
  (build 1.102 to 0.556, read 0.355 to 0.176); growth N = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128,
  256: 0.397, 0.769, 1.556, 3.290, 7.392, 18.165 to 0.371, 0.706, 1.380, 2.731,
  5.460, 11.039 (each doubling x 1.90 to 2.02, was x 1.94 to 2.46); at N = 256
  `add_named_edges` 4.173 to 0.009, `sxml_xslt_package_bind` 1.167 to 0.015,
  ordering the globals 5.343 to 0.101 (with `add_named_edges`), the value
  template builder 0.779 to 0.057; templates of 6, 24, 96, 384 assertions
  0.197, 0.663, 2.527, 9.982 to 0.186, 0.621, 2.358, 9.304; xmark-all 8.638 to
  8.638 (output equal). Processor seconds (fastest of 15, interleaved, a shared
  machine): invoice transform 0.274 to 0.263, validate 0.442 to 0.380; fastest
  of 5: N = 128 0.89 to 0.74, N = 256 2.39 to 1.62, 384 assertions 1.39 to
  1.29; the XT40 run (its 414,483 compiles and the transforms) 354.0 to 353.9
  (its stylesheets are small).
- **Same result**: the IR text form after the passes (dumped by a scratch-only
  hook in `sxml_ir_run_passes`, as in D324) is byte-identical on
  `EN16931-UBL-validation.xslt` (141 MB of text), on the growth stylesheets,
  and on all 414,470 units the XT40 suite compiles (an FNV-1a hash and length
  per unit, in order). Schematron: `sxml validate --format=json` over EN
  16931's 1,131 UBL unit tests and 19 examples gives byte-identical output (6.3
  MB, every finding with its location); 7.30's suite through
  `sxml-schematron-test` 463 of 463 applicable cases, 3 deviations, 43
  implementation-defined, 5 not applicable, as before; EN 16931 UBL 1,133 of
  1,133 checks from the `.sch` sources. **Conformance setup**: base and change
  built alike (preset `release`, snapshots of 3919bc7ce and of the change), run
  one after the other on the same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset, from
  each snapshot's root: `sxml-qt4 run --spec=XP40 --format=json`, `sxml-qt4 run
  --spec=XQ40 --format=json`, `sxml-xslt-test run --format=json` (default
  catalogs, no test list). XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114 and XT40 12,185 passed in
  both: 0 outcomes differ, case by case. debug-gcc: the whole suite passes (459
  tests; kotlin/jvm and swift/linux skipped); clang-tidy clean on the changed
  files; `tools/check-call-cycles.py` finds no cycle (D71).
- **Deviation**: `src/xslt_value_template.c` (the packet's mechanism names it;
  its Owns list does not) is changed; no other packet owns it.
- **Left** (see "## Proposed"): at N = 256 the costs that still grow with the
  square of the stylesheet are about 0.29 x 10^9 of 11.04: XSLT streamability's
  `is_streamable_mode` (`src/xslt_streamability.c`) walks the declarations for
  each template rule (0.18); the XPath lowerer's `look_up_variable`
  (`src/xpath_lower.c`) walks the declaration view for each variable reference
  (0.05); the duplicate searches as declarations are added
  (`add_own_instances`, `find_global`, 0.05). In the Schematron compile the
  XPath front end on the schema's own expressions (0.37) and the entry numbers,
  one parse each (0.06, 1,086 texts), remain; the validation of the compiled
  schema (1.21) costs twice what the pre-compiled XSLT's transform (0.55) does
  on the same invoice, an evaluation cost outside this packet.

### D326. Running compiled Schematron: the pattern walk visits only what a rule may match (packet perf-14)

**Summary**: A compiled Schematron pattern's `pattern_walk` visits element
children always and other node kinds only when a rule context of the pattern
may match them.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D315, D323 and D325 ("Left": validating the compiled
schema costs twice what the pre-compiled XSLT's transform does on the same
invoice). No public header changed; no shared file changed (only
`src/schematron_build.c` and `tests/schematron_test.c`). Glossary:
`pattern_walk`.

- **Whom it serves**: every Schematron validation, first EN 16931's (`sxml
  validate --schematron`, the host's `Schematron.validate`). **Pays**: one loop
  over each rule context's pattern AST at compile time; no new mechanism (the
  walk is still xsl:apply-templates in the current mode).
- **Profile** (callgrind, release, at a7a8d50ee; the invoice
  `ubl-tc434-example1.xml`): `sxml_schematron_validate_node` 1.208 x 10^9
  instructions, the official stylesheet's `sxml_xslt_stylesheet_transform`
  0.548. The C profiles have the same shape (`sxml_machine_step_expression` 16
  % of each, the rest the machine's tasks and values), so the difference is in
  how much IR runs. Counted by a scratch-only hook in the evaluator (not
  committed), by function: steps in match functions 2,503,052 against 928,554,
  in template functions 73,075 against 71,402 (the rule templates, with their
  finding items and fired-rule checks, cost the same); calls of match functions
  123,282 against 44,422, of template functions 3,541 against 1,321. By IR kind
  the steps scale alike (LET 1.49 M against 0.59 M, ATOM 0.35 M against 0.13 M,
  CONDITIONAL 0.58 M against 0.21 M, STATIC_CALL 0.13 M against 0.05 M). The
  match functions themselves are the same IR in both (the same patterns lowered
  alike).
- **Explanation**: the evaluator chooses a template rule by calling the mode's
  match functions in rule order until one is true (6.8), so a visit costs about
  one call per rule of the mode for a node no rule matches. D315's walk applied
  templates to `@* | node()`, so each of the three modes visited 1,177 nodes of
  the invoice (369 elements, 70 attributes, 738 text nodes, 516 of them
  whitespace only) and every text node tried every rule in vain; the ISO
  skeleton walks `@* | *`, 439 nodes per mode. 2.7 times the visits gave 2.8
  times the match calls and the factor 2.2.
- **Mechanism** (`src/schematron_build.c`): the *pattern walk* selects the
  element children always, and attributes, text, comment and
  processing-instruction children only when a rule context of the pattern may
  match that node kind; other nodes are unobservable, as no rule of the pattern
  can match them. The kinds come from the context's pattern AST, read as XSLT
  4.0, 6.3 matches: the last step of a path (after "/", "//", a rooted
  variable), both sides of a union, the left of intersect and except, the value
  of a filter, the inside of parentheses; an axis step's node test gives its
  kind, a name test or wildcard the principal node kind of its axis (XPath 4.0,
  4.6.4.1); "/" a document node; every other pattern (node(), `$v`, `id()`,
  `key()`, `.`, simple patterns, an expression rule context wrapped as
  `.[...]`) may match any kind. A loop over the nodes and their ancestors
  (D71). The walks are added after the pattern's rules, once every context is
  known: the traversal templates are now declared after the rules (priority -1
  orders them last, as before), and each rule template's walk is appended as
  its last instruction. D315's semantics are unchanged: a rule that can match a
  node still sees it, the first matching rule wins in a pattern, every rule of
  a group fires, phases, `from` and `documents` choose the start as before,
  `let` once per context node, both locations, `value-of` as `fn:string`. EN
  16931's contexts are all elements: its walk is `*`.
- **Measured** (callgrind, release; base a7a8d50ee and the change built alike
  from snapshots). Invoice: validation 1.208 to 0.479 x 10^9 (the official
  stylesheet's transform 0.548), the whole `validate --schematron` 2.633 to
  1.903, the compile unchanged (1.405 to 1.404); template calls 3,541 to 1,111,
  match calls 123,282 to 36,612. The 1,131 VEFA instances
  (`sxml-schematron-test vefa`, compile and all validations): 49.90 to 29.03 x
  10^9, validation 47.14 to 26.27. Seconds (processor, a shared 4-CPU machine):
  invoice fastest of 15, interleaved, 0.362 to 0.296 (the official stylesheet's
  transform 0.258, its compile included); VEFA validation 7.51 to 4.65 s; the
  1,150 files of D325's comparison in one `sxml validate` run 9.8 to 5.3 s.
- **Same result**: `sxml validate --format=json` over EN 16931's 1,131 UBL unit
  test instances (each `<test>`'s document, extracted as the VEFA harness does)
  and the 19 UBL examples, all in one run: 14.8 MB, byte-identical. 7.30's
  suite through `sxml-schematron-test`: 463 of 463 applicable, 3 deviations, 43
  implementation-defined, 5 not applicable, as before; EN 16931 UBL 1,133 of
  1,133 checks. A new unit test,
  `pattern_walk_reaches_every_kind_a_rule_matches`, has a pattern per kind
  (elements, `@n`, `text()`, a comment step after a parenthesized step, a
  processing instruction, `node() except *`, an expression rule context) and
  checks every report in order. debug-gcc: the whole suite passes (459 tests;
  kotlin/jvm and swift/linux skipped); clang-tidy clean on both files;
  `tools/check-call-cycles.py` finds no cycle. QT4 and XT40 were not run: no
  shared file changed.
- **Left** (see "## Proposed"): a rule search that skips rules whose pattern
  cannot match the item's node kind or name would help every stylesheet with
  many rules, the official EN 16931 one as much as this.

### D327. Template rules chosen from rule buckets by node kind and name (packet perf-15)

**Summary**: Each mode keeps its template rules in buckets by node kind and
name, so an item tries only the rules whose pattern can match its kind and
name.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D144, D149, D223, D224, D326 (its Proposed entry,
now done and removed). No public header changed. Glossary: `item_category`,
`item_requirement`, `rule_bucket`.

- **Whom it serves**: every stylesheet with many template rules, first EN
  16931's (the official XSLT and sxml's compiled Schematron). **Pays**: at
  compile time one pass over each pattern AST and a sort of each mode's names;
  per mode at most eight buckets of rule numbers plus one per element or
  attribute name its rules test (4 bytes per rule number); at run time one node
  description and two binary searches per item applied.
- **Profile** (base 29719119c, release; a scratch-only hook in
  `src/evaluator_template.c`, not committed, counted the steps taken between a
  match function's call and its return): the invoice transform 1,359,249
  evaluation steps, 1,201,091 of them (88 %) in 44,422 match calls for 1,324
  items; `validate --schematron` 1,176,633, 1,031,291 (88 %) in 36,612 match
  calls for 1,111 items. An item tried 34 rules on average, nearly all of which
  could not match its kind or name.
- **Mechanism**: `sxml_xslt_pattern_find_requirement` (`src/xslt_pattern.c`)
  reads what a pattern may match from its AST, as D326's walked kinds did and
  now in one place: the last step of a path, both sides of a union, the left of
  intersect and except, the value of a filter, parentheses (XSLT 4.0, 6.3); an
  axis step gives its kind test's kind, or for a name test or wildcard the
  principal node kind of its axis (XPath 4.0, 4.6.4.1), and for an EQName of an
  element or attribute its expanded name, resolved as the lowerer resolves it;
  "##any" and typed modes (6.9.4, substitution groups) give elements of any
  name; "/" a document node; every other pattern (`$v`, id(), key(), doc(),
  simple patterns, `.`) any item. Every pattern may match items that are not
  XNodes (category OTHER: JNodes are not decided), so OTHER's bucket holds
  every rule. The lowering (`src/xslt_lower_template.c`) gives each mode its
  rule buckets (`sxml_ir_rule_bucket`, `src/ir_internal.h`): per category the
  rules that may match it whatever the name, and per name the rules that may
  match only some names of that category, the name among them; a typed mode's
  XTTE3100 rule is in every bucket. Buckets hold the unit's rule numbers, so
  each is in the mode's order (6.8: precedence, priority, the later
  declaration). APPLY_TEMPLATES (`src/evaluator_template.c`) describes the
  item, takes the bucket of its category and name and the bucket of its
  category, skips numbers below the first candidate (next-match) by binary
  search and merges the two in rule order; the precedence filter of
  apply-imports, on-multiple-match="fail" (ties among the candidates, which
  hold every rule that can match) and the built-in templates' apply-templates
  are unchanged, and streamed modes go through the same choice (D223: a
  streamed node is an XNode of its window; `evaluator_stream`'s template rules
  applied node by node and XT40's streaming sets are unchanged). An item that
  is not an XNode or cannot be described takes OTHER's bucket: every rule, as
  before. The verifier checks the buckets (ordered by category and name, names
  only for elements and attributes, rules of the mode in increasing order). Not
  done: element() and attribute() tests with a name,
  processing-instruction(name) and JNode keys are indexed by kind only.
- **Measured** (callgrind, release; base 29719119c and the change built alike
  from snapshots). Invoice transform 1.957 to 1.618 x 10^9 instructions, the
  transform itself 0.548 to 0.208 (the compile is unchanged, 1.409); steps
  1,359,249 to 324,824, match calls 44,422 to 2,739. `validate --schematron`
  1.903 to 1.613, validation 0.479 to 0.189; steps 1,176,633 to 287,135, match
  calls 36,612 to 2,526. The new benchmark `tests/bench/xslt-many-rules.xsl`
  (87 rules, one per XMark element name and for attributes and text, over every
  node of the XMark document, 152,795 items) 55.84 to 3.36 x 10^9; steps 165.2
  M to 4.04 M, match calls 10,857,281 to 153,558. Processor seconds (a shared
  4-CPU machine): invoice transform 0.262 to 0.222, validate 0.288 to 0.254
  (fastest of 15, interleaved); `run-bench.py --repeat 5`: xslt-many-rules
  6.972 to 0.463, xmark-all 1.075 to 1.093, xslt-key and xslt-match-variable
  within noise (interleaved reruns 0.465-0.507 against 0.459-0.475, 0.287-0.299
  against 0.285-0.326); VEFA (`sxml-schematron-test vefa`, 1,131 tests) 4.36 to
  3.10 s; the XT40 run 363.5 to 364.0 s (its stylesheets are small; compiles
  dominate).
- **Same result**: the rule chosen is the one the whole mode in order would
  give (a skipped rule's match function returns false). Checked: the official
  EN 16931 XSLT's SVRL over the 1,131 UBL unit test documents (extracted from
  each VEFA `<test>`) and the 17 UBL examples, per document, identical; `sxml
  validate --format=json` with the `.sch` over the same 1,148 files in one run,
  14.7 MB, byte-identical; xslt-many-rules and the other benchmarks' outputs
  equal. 7.30's suite through `sxml-schematron-test run`: 463 passed, 3 failed,
  43 implementation-defined, 5 not applicable, as base; EN 16931 UBL 1,133 of
  1,133 checks. New tests in `tests/evaluator_template_test.c`: `rule_buckets`
  (names and kinds interleaved by priority, a named rule below a kind-wide one,
  next-match from one bucket into the other, atomic items, on-multiple-match
  across buckets, the default element namespace) and `rule_bucket_contents`
  (the buckets a small stylesheet gets). **Conformance setup**: base and change
  built alike (preset `release`, snapshots of 29719119c and of the change), run
  one after the other on the same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset, from
  each snapshot's root: `sxml-xslt-test run --format=json`, `sxml-qt4 run
  --spec=XP40 --format=json`, `sxml-qt4 run --spec=XQ40 --format=json` (default
  catalogs; XP40 and XQ40 because `src/ir.c` and `src/ir_internal.h` changed).
  XT40 12,185, XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114 passed in both: 0 outcomes differ, case
  by case (13,867, 47,313 and 47,313 cases). debug-gcc: the whole suite passed
  (459 tests; kotlin/jvm and swift/linux skipped) except `evaluator_template`,
  whose one wrong expectation (a union's default priority) was then corrected;
  at the commit the 329 tests matching evaluator_template, ir, xslt, schematron
  and cli pass. clang-tidy clean on the changed files;
  `tools/check-call-cycles.py` finds no cycle (D71).

### D328. Union patterns keep one default priority, the lowest of their alternatives' (packet fix-5)

**Summary**: A union pattern is one template rule whose default priority is the
lowest of its alternatives', as XSLT 4.0 says; sxml already does this, and
nothing changes.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D118, D144, D245, D276, D327. No source change and
no public header; one new unit test case.

- **Question** (perf-15 found it): `<xsl:template match="a[@n] | b">` with a
  later `<xsl:template match="a">`, applied to `<r><a n="1"/><a/></r>`, prints
  "plain plain" in sxml; XSLT 3.0 (6.5 of 3.0) makes the union one rule per
  alternative, `a[@n]` at 0.5, and gives "union plain".
- **What 4.0 says** (the editor's draft of 28 October 2026, the same text as
  qtspecs master's `specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml`): 6.4.1, "If the
  pattern is a UnionExprP then the default priority is the minimum of the
  default priorities of the alternatives", with a note calling it "a backwards
  incompatible change from XSLT 3.0 and earlier versions, which treated a
  template rule using a union pattern as equivalent to multiple template rules
  with different priorities"; a union rule is one rule, so next-match never
  runs it twice for an item both branches match. 6.4's changes list and the
  changes appendix (Issue 1770, PR 1772, 2025-02-11): "The default priority for
  a template rule using a union pattern has changed." 3.8.3 defines no
  difference for an effective version of 3.0, so `version="3.0"` gets the same
  answer. sxml already computes this (D118,
  `sxml_xslt_pattern_compute_default_priority`), and D327's rule buckets put
  the one rule under both alternatives' kinds and names: the reproduction's
  "plain plain" is 4.0's answer. Nothing to change.
- **Reading taken** (D208): 6.4 also says "The default priority of a pattern
  containing one or more predicates is +0.5"; read literally of the whole
  pattern it would make `a[@n] | b` 0.5 (and "union plain"). sxml reads it of a
  pattern whose own form has predicates (a predicated step, `.[p]`), with the
  union rule applied first, as 6.4.1's note requires: `A | B` "always has the
  same or lower priority as either alternative", and a branch's priority is
  "lowered to that of the other branch".
- **XT40** (the cases covering PR 1772): next-match-021a, -023a and -039a pass;
  next-match-025a and -026a (`node()|element(x)` against `*:x`) and
  conflict-resolution-1901a fail, as D276 recorded: their expectations need the
  union above its lowest alternative (0.5 would give all three), against
  6.4.1's text; the draft decides (D245).
- **Test**: `union_priority` in `tests/evaluator_template_test.c`: the
  reproduction under versions 3.0 and 4.0 ("plain plain"), the union declared
  after `a` ("union plain": the tie at 0 goes to the later rule), `node() |
  element(a)` below `*:a`, and next-match from an item both branches match
  running the rule once. `rule_buckets`' comment cites 6.4.1.
- **Verified**: debug-gcc and release, evaluator_template 10 of 10; clang-tidy
  clean. XT40 whole, base e4d928c2e and the change built alike (preset
  `release`, snapshots), run one after the other on the same machine with TZ,
  LANG and LC_ALL unset, from each snapshot's root, `sxml-xslt-test run
  --format=json` (default catalog): 12,185 passed, 235 failed, 98 wrong error,
  1,349 not run (13,867 cases) in both, 0 outcomes differ case by case; no
  gains (no source change). 7.30's suite (`sxml-schematron-test run`): 463
  passed, 3 failed, 43 implementation-defined, 5 not applicable, as before;
  VEFA (`run_vefa.py` with the official EN 16931 UBL XSLT over the Invoice and
  CreditNote unit tests) 1,133 of 1,133 checks.

### D329. Parsing XPath: fewer reductions, each text once per compilation (packet perf-17)

**Summary**: The XPath grammar inlines its hidden choice rules so a primary
expression is reduced once, not once per precedence level, and an `ast_memo`
parses each distinct expression text once per compilation.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D12, D232, D324 and D325. No public header changed;
the ASTs and the IR are the same.

- **Whom it serves**: every compile of a stylesheet or a Schematron schema,
  first EN 16931's, where XPath parsing was 32 % of the invoice transform and
  30 % of the invoice validate from the `.sch`. **Pays**: about 206 KB of parse
  tables (the `sxml` command 16.93 to 17.14 MB), an AST copy per expression met
  again, a hash table per compilation.
- **Profile** (callgrind, release, at ae61af90e): transform 1.618 x 10^9
  instructions, `sxml_xpath_parse` 0.517, tree-sitter's parse of XPath 0.299
  over 2,418 parses; validate 1.613, `sxml_xpath_parse` 0.483. The cost was per
  reduction, not per character: a typical assertion of 552 bytes and 116 tokens
  took 676 reductions, because each primary expression was reduced once per
  precedence level (22 hidden choice rules, A.5) on its way to an operand, each
  reduction a hidden subtree node the walk's cursor then passed through.
  Repeated texts matter less than their count says: the official stylesheet's
  2,246 select, test, match and use attributes are 1,042 distinct texts, but
  the repeated ones are short (the distinct texts hold 93 % of the bytes).
- **Grammar** (`grammars/xpath`, as D232 cut XML's tokens and nodes): the
  hidden choice rules of the operator levels, the steps, primaries, literals,
  node tests and names are inlined (tree-sitter `inline`). They make no node,
  so `node-types.json`, every named node and field and the AST are unchanged;
  that assertion takes 132 reductions. `_expression_single` and `_expression`
  stay rules: inlining them doubled the states for 10 % fewer reductions.
  Regenerated with `tools/generate-grammars.sh`: xpath 1,179 to 1,609 states,
  xslt_pattern 1,275 to 1,706, value_template 1,166 to 1,596, xpath_full_text
  1,559 to 2,117 (+48, +47, +48, +63 KB of tables). XQuery does not take them
  (`inline` is its Full Text rules only, its parser byte-identical to before):
  they gave it 5,647 to 9,518 states, +558 KB, for a parse a query makes once
  (xmark-all -0.15 %). The corpus tests of the five grammars pass.
- **The AST memo** (`sxml_ast_memo`, `src/xpath_ast.c`; glossary `ast_memo`):
  an open-addressing table (FNV-1a, at most half full) of the ASTs a
  compilation parsed, keyed by the front end's entry point, the text and the
  parse's limits (expression depth, XML 1.1 reading), which are all a front
  end's AST depends on besides the source name; the static context does not
  enter a parse. A text met again takes a copy (`sxml_ast_copy`: the same
  capacities, node entries and text store, its own source name); a text in
  error is not kept, so each use reports its own error. The XSLT reader
  (`src/xslt_read.c`, one memo per read) and the Schematron builder
  (`src/schematron_build.c`, one per compile) parse every expression through
  it; it replaces perf-13's table of fixed texts and its node-by-node copy
  (D325, mechanism 3). Memory: one AST per distinct text more during a read,
  from the same allocator and limits; no recursion (D71).
- **The walk** (`src/xpath_parse.c`): a named child's AST field is kept per
  grammar field identifier, a terminal's delimitation (A.3.2) per symbol, as
  D324 kept kinds per symbol (-1.4 % of the parse).
- **Measured**, instructions x 10^9 (callgrind, release; base ae61af90e and the
  change built alike from snapshots): invoice transform 1.618 to 1.323
  (grammar) to 1.294 (memo) to 1.291 (walk), -20.2 %, `sxml_xpath_parse` 0.517
  to 0.185 (14.4 % of the run), XPath parses 2,418 to 1,210; invoice validate
  1.613 to 1.332 to 1.323 to 1.321, -18.1 %, `sxml_xpath_parse` 0.483 to 0.202,
  parses 2,323 to 2,248; the new benchmark `xpath-parse`
  (`tests/bench/xpath-parse.xsl`, 250 Schematron-style assertions,
  compile-bound) 0.947 to 0.649; xmark-all 8.641 to 8.638 (output equal).
  Processor seconds (fastest of 15, interleaved, a shared 4-CPU machine with
  other builds running): transform 0.212 to 0.185, validate 0.246 to 0.219,
  xpath-parse 0.121 to 0.093; the XT40 run (its compiles and transforms) 340.3
  to 330.9, one run each, under other load.
- **Same result**: a scratch harness parsed 133,165 texts with both builds
  (each QT4 test expression as XPath and as XQuery, the XT40 suite's select,
  test, match, as and value template attributes, the EN 16931 XSLT's and `.sch`
  files' attributes): the 119,276 that parse give identical node entries, text
  stores, capacities and roots; the 13,889 in error give the same status and

  recovery follows the tables (often at the "(" or "[" before the old place, or

  early or misses a token" for "The text is not valid XPath 4.0 syntax".
  tests/schematron_test.c's two pattern errors move from 4:16 to 4:20 and 15:46

### D330. IR passes walk each body once, with a cheaper child walk (packet perf-16)

**Summary**: The IR passes walk each function body once: `push_every_child`
writes child indices in place, the demand pass makes no owners and counts its
census while collecting members, cutting compile instructions by up to 12 %.

Recorded 2026-10-28, after D224, D259, D324, D325, D327. No header changed; the
IR after the passes is the same, item demands included.

- **Whom it serves**: every compile, first large ones (EN 16931's Schematron
  and pre-compiled XSLT). **Pays**: two arrays lent across functions in the
  demand and fusion passes, two slot arrays per function in the demand pass, a
  byte per function in the fusion pass.
- **Profile** (callgrind, release, base ae61af90e): `validate --schematron` of
  one invoice 1.613 x 10^9 instructions, the IR passes 0.502 of it (demand
  0.200, descendant 0.074, fusion 0.066, hoist 0.064, filter-index 0.041,
  verify 0.030, global-read 0.028). No cost grew faster than the unit (the
  growth series of D324 and D325 doubled x 1.97 to 2.02 per doubling before and
  after); the constants were large. The unit (about 155,000 expressions) was
  walked about ten times: `make_owners` in five passes (0.135), a slot census
  per function in the descendant, demand and fusion passes (0.081), the demand
  members (0.061), a plain walk per function in fusion (0.020). Each step of a
  walk went through `children_of` into a local array, then `pass_array_append`,
  a call and a memcpy of a variable size per child: `push_every_child` cost
  about 130 instructions per expression. The demand pass also allocated its
  member arrays per function (230 functions, the largest with most of the unit)
  and, in each settling round, noted every member's reads again, looking up
  native function names with strlen.
- **Mechanism**, no new machinery (`src/ir_loop_passes.c`): `push_every_child`
  switches on the kind and writes the indices in place, room made once per
  expression (`pass_array_reserve`; catch clauses, sort keys and merge streams
  in `push_listed_children`). The demand pass makes no owners: a function's
  body is a tree (the verifier's invariant), so a member is inside a STREAM or
  MERGE when its parent is one or is inside one, as `make_owners` marked it;
  the census is counted as the members are collected (one walk of the body),
  and a FILTER predicate's role, which needs the whole census, is decided after
  the walk. The descendant pass counts each function's census from the
  expressions `owners` gives it (grouped once, D324), without a walk. The
  fusion pass finds the functions that hold a QUANTIFIED in one scan of
  `owners` (fusion only makes a QUANTIFIED of one). The demand pass notes the
  reads that do not depend on a member's demand once per function (all but a
  DOCUMENT_ORDER's), and each round adds the DOCUMENT_ORDER reads to them. The
  other passes' walks (hoist, filter-index, the owners of fusion and
  descendant) keep their place and gain from the cheaper step. Golden file:
  `src/ir_verify.c`.
- **Measured**, instructions x 10^9 (callgrind, release; base ae61af90e and the
  change built alike from snapshots): invoice `validate --schematron` 1.613 to
  1.413 (-12.4 %), the IR passes 0.502 to 0.302 (demand 0.200 to 0.100,
  descendant 0.074 to 0.042, fusion 0.066 to 0.028, hoist 0.064 to 0.047,
  filter-index 0.041 to 0.027, `make_owners` 0.135 for five to 0.057 for four);
  invoice transform 1.618 to 1.506 (-6.9 %), the passes 0.282 to 0.171; growth
  N = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256: 0.553, 1.089, 2.163, 4.319, 8.681, 17.496 to
  0.517, 1.018, 2.021, 4.034, 8.111, 16.355 (at N = 256 the passes 2.757 to
  1.615, demand 0.939 to 0.442); templates of 6, 24, 96, 384 assertions 0.266,
  0.956, 3.708, 14.719 to 0.249, 0.894, 3.467, 13.757; xmark-all 8.638 to
  8.637. Processor seconds (interleaved, a shared 4-CPU machine; fastest of
  15): validate 0.246 to 0.221, transform 0.214 to 0.202; fastest of 5: N = 128
  1.190 to 1.137, N = 256 2.461 to 2.293, 384 assertions 2.063 to 1.906,
  xmark-all 1.002 to 1.007 (noise); the XT40 run (its 414,470 compiles and the
  transforms) 338.6 to 333.9. Outputs equal byte for byte on every run above.
- **Same result**: the IR text form after the passes and a hash of every
  expression's item demand (which the text form does not show), dumped by a
  scratch-only hook in `sxml_ir_run_passes`, are identical on the EN 16931
  `.sch` compile (286 MB of text), the EN 16931 XSLT (141 MB), the growth
  stylesheets, and all 414,470 units the XT40 suite compiles (a text hash and a
  demand hash per unit, in order). **Conformance setup**: base and change built
  alike (preset `release`, snapshots of ae61af90e and of the change), run side
  by side on the same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset, from each
  snapshot's root: `sxml-qt4 run --spec=XP40 --format=json`, `sxml-qt4 run
  --spec=XQ40 --format=json`, `sxml-xslt-test run --format=json` (default
  catalogs). XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114, XT40 12,185 passed in both: 0 outcomes
  differ, case by case (47,313, 47,313 and 13,867 cases). 7.30's suite through
  `sxml-schematron-test run`: 463 passed, 3 failed, 43 implementation-defined,
  5 not applicable, as before; VEFA (`run_vefa.py`, the official UBL XSLT over
  the Invoice and CreditNote unit tests) 1,133 of 1,133. debug-gcc: 459 of 459
  tests pass (kotlin/jvm and swift/linux skipped); clang-tidy clean on the
  file; `tools/check-call-cycles.py` finds no cycle (D71).
- **Left**: on the invoice the passes are 21 % of `validate --schematron`: the
  demand pass 0.100 (its member walk with the census 0.061, of which growing
  the members array 0.014: the allocator zeroes each new block), `make_owners`
  0.014 in each of four passes (each pass needs the owners of the unit as it
  starts it; keeping them across passes would need every pass to give owners to
  what it adds), the hoist pass's `analyse_let` 0.020, verify 0.030,
  global-read 0.028.

### D331. Schematron: the function library's prefixes, the document of each finding, real rule sets read with warnings (packet fix-7)

**Summary**: Schematron resolves `xs`, `fn`, `math`, `map`, `array` and `err`
without `sch:ns`, reports name each finding's document in `document_uri`, and
three deviations of real rule sets compile with `schematron:compatibility`
warnings.

Recorded 2026-10-29, after D315, D323, D326, D327 and the owner's three
requests of 2026-10-29 (the third his choice of option a on D323's Proposed
entry, which this record replaces). Sources: ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025 by clause;
nothing of its text copied.

- **Whom it serves**: the user of `sxml validate --schematron` and the embedder
  who run real rule sets (EN 16931, XRechnung) from their sources, and the
  author of a pattern with `documents`. **Pays**: a field of the report, one
  internal walk of the stylesheet AST's variable references per compile that
  has pattern variables, one warning path in the reader, a JSON member, the
  book's pages.
- **1. Prefixes.** 5.4.10 says the prefixes of query expressions are defined by
  `ns`; every binding annex adds that all namespaces, prefixes, functions and
  operators its functions specification defines shall be available (Annexes H,
  I, J, K, L; M and N for the XQuery bindings sxml refuses; Annex C, XPath 1.0,
  defines none, and sxml reads `xslt` and no binding as 4.0, D315 B). Read
  together: `xs`, `fn`, `math`, `map`, `array` and `err` resolve without `ns`
  in every query expression, and in the XSLT declarations the xslt bindings
  read, for a prefix they leave unbound; an `sch:ns` may bind any of them and
  then wins; `xml` is XPath's own; every other prefix still needs `sch:ns`;
  SVRL lists the `sch:ns` bindings only. D315's wording is amended. The 7.30
  suite's `rules-predeclared-xs-prefix` becomes normative (no findings) and
  five cases join `schema-structure` (`ns-predeclared-*`,
  `ns-undeclared-other-prefix`).
- **2. The document of a finding.** A finding of a pattern with `documents`
  (5.4.12) was printed with the validated file's name and the other document's
  lines, and JSON did not say which document. `sxml_schematron_report` gains
  `document_uri` (additive, at its end): the document URI of the tree the
  subject node is in, so a subordinate document's, one `fn:doc` read, else the
  validated document's; `node_location` is that document's. The command shows
  it where it showed FILE, by its path from the working directory, and JSON
  findings gain `document`; the host shim and the package give `document`. SVRL
  already said it as Annex D asks: each `fired-rule` of such a pattern carries
  the subordinate document's URI (Table D.1, note c), and the findings follow
  their fired rule.
- **3. Real rule sets read with warnings** (option a). Three deviations are
  accepted by default, each occurrence a report with the code
  `schematron:compatibility` through the compile report sink, naming the
  clause: a parameter named twice in one pattern instance (the first value is
  used, as SchXslt does; 5.4.11, Annex B); a pattern's `let` read by another
  pattern, a variable outside patterns or an XSLT declaration (3.23 scopes it
  to its pattern; a global of the written name refers to the first compiled
  pattern's `let`; references are found in the stylesheet AST, XSLT's scoping
  and the expression's own bindings respected); a rule's `let` after its
  assertions (Annex A; evaluated before them as every rule let is). A warning
  is not counted as an error, never fills the error record, and the null sink
  drops it; the command prints `warning:` before the code, keeps the exit
  status and lists them in `schematron.warnings` of its JSON; the package has
  `Schematron.warnings`. The undeclared `xs` in XRechnung's `xsl:function` is
  no deviation after 1. Anything else stays an error (a `let` after a rule in a
  pattern, a parameter twice in a schema, ...). The suite's
  `abstract-param-duplicate`, `let-pattern-not-visible-elsewhere` and the new
  `let-after-assertion` are deviations with this record's reason (they are
  errors by the standard).
- **Not done**: no option to make the warnings errors (nothing asked for one);
  a pattern's `let` defined only in a pattern the phase does not compile is not
  shared (XPST0008 as before).
- **Evidence**: suite 520 cases, pass 467, fail 0, deviations 6 (3 of D315, 3
  of this record), implementation-defined 42, not applicable 5; EN 16931 UBL
  1,133 of 1,133 and CII 9 of 9 checks from the sources (ctest
  `schematron/en16931-ubl`, `-cii`); XRechnung UBL and CII compile from the
  unpatched sources and run their 354 instances (`schematron/xrechnung-*`); the
  differential against SchXslt 1.10.1 on the unpatched sources identical: EN
  16931 UBL 255 instances (274 findings, 23,099 fired rules), CII 128,
  XRechnung UBL 226, CII 128 (ctest `schematron/differential-*` with
  `SXML_SCHEMATRON_DIFFERENTIAL`, about ten minutes or more). Unit tests
  `reports_name_their_document`, `compatibility_warnings`; CLI tests for
  documents and warnings, text and JSON; debug-gcc and release. The book's
  Schematron chapters match (rules: the prefixes; documents: a pattern over
  `vane-api.xsd`; reports: Warnings with `older.sch`, written for the book) and
  it builds. No shared XSLT file changed. The package's additions typecheck;
  `sxml.wasm` was not built (no WASI SDK here).

## Proposed

- **Cheaper atomic string cells** (D322, perf-11; for a later perf packet
  owning `src/xdm_atomic.c` and `src/xdm.c`): (1) resolve the built-in atomic
  types in `sxml_atomic_item_make` from a table instead of describing them
  through the registry (measured: SchXslt expand -1.0 %); (2) let a caller that
  already holds validated text, such as a tree's content (tree.h: trees hold
  well-formed UTF-8), pass its codepoint count or skip the second validation
  (2.5 % of expand); (3) small-cell reuse in the item heap, kept out of the
  live counts only if the tests' leak checks are redefined (cells 4.3 % plus
  frees); (4) a typed-value memo per evaluation for untyped nodes, which needs
  the dynamic context to reach `src/xdm_node.c`.

  Proposed default: the perf packet does (1) and (2), which stay inside those
  two files and save about 3.5 % of expand together. (3) and (4) wait: (3)
  changes what the tests' leak checks count, and (4) needs node atomization to
  reach the dynamic context, which the public `sxml_node_value_request` cannot
  carry (D99, D322).

- **Compile costs that still grow with the square of a stylesheet** (D325,
  perf-13; for the packets that own the files). With XSLT's component graph
  linear, at 2,048 template rules and 2,048 globals (D325's N = 256) about 0.29
  x 10^9 of 11.04 still grow four times per doubling: `is_streamable_mode`
  (`src/xslt_streamability.c`) walks every declaration for each template rule's
  modes (0.18); `look_up_variable` (`src/xpath_lower.c`) walks the declaration
  view for each variable reference (0.05); `add_own_instances`
  (`src/xslt_package.c`) and `find_global` (`src/xslt_lower_control.c`) search
  the instances or globals made so far for each declaration (0.05). Proposed
  default: a mode index made once for streamability, and the sorted name index
  of D325 for the lowerer's variable lookup; the duplicate searches by a sort
  of the declarations when they show in a profile.

- **Outward-facing choices** (D208; for the owner): tagging and publishing
  releases (0.2.0 and after, `docs/RELEASE.md`, the archives of `mise run
  dist`, D256), macOS and Windows code signing, and when the repository moves
  to tinyactors-dev. The license (MIT) and the npm name (`@tinyactors/sxml`)
  are settled in D239. The proposed defaults, which hold until the owner
  decides:

  - Releases: agents prepare everything up to the tag (`docs/RELEASE.md`,
    D138); nothing is tagged or published until the owner does it.
  - Signing: the archives ship unsigned, the arm64 macOS program signed ad hoc
    by zig, and README.md says how to lift macOS's quarantine (D256); Developer
    ID signing, notarization and Authenticode wait for the owner's
    certificates.
  - The repository stays where it is until the owner says it moves (D239).
